Really nice professor! Midterms and final are easy which they are based on the labs and cases in class! One of the best accounting professor that I ever had!! :)

A slow grader. Finals week and she wants us to revise slides we did around midterms that she left us notes on, yet never graded them or shared those notes.

Avoid Professor Illaria at all cost! The only reason I chose this class was that it was the only landscape architecture studio available in person. Complete joke of a class. Avoid at all costs, she has no interest in teaching her students. Pretentious subject matter taught by an egotistical pseudo-intellectual. What a bore...

Ilaria is very unorganized. The semester is paced horribly and she focuses a lot on pointless details. Ilaria's studio is quite a mess. She is aloof, incredibly disorganized, will rarely give any constructive feedback on your work, is rude at times, and the semester's pacing is pretty horrendous. She shows an extreme lack of care, planning, and effort. In my opinion, she does not live up to the standard I expect of CPP's architecture faculty.

In my 4 years in the architecture program here at Cal Poly Pomona, Ilaria has by far been the most disorganized professor. This led to a FRANTIC dash to complete our final.

Snarky. Makes you change your project a lot and never seem totally happy with it. During critiques, shes often on their phone and doesn't give clear instructions, just general advice. The concept board helps, but it's hard to know exactly what she want. Cool as a person.

Claudia is actually a nice professor, if you do work that shows you are putting in effort. If you show up with work that could have been done within the hour, she would be reasonably disappointed. She is honestly the worst teacher ive had in my life.
Assigns so much work, almost has no understanding of workload. difficult to follow lectures, usually a lot of information given at once. snarky and rude personality

Very lecture heavy class but isn't good at explaining concepts. Explains concepts like you are supposed to know them already. Pairs with another professor for lectures so usually not the one teaching the class, when asked questions, doesn't know what topics were talked about and you have to explain the topic back to her to get an answer.

Claudia as a studio professor was very helpful, especially for somebody like me who had little exposure to the field beforehand. She is a little off-putting at first but as the semester goes on and the studio gets to know one another better, it gets more enjoyable. She does assign a lot of deliverables, but I am honestly grateful for that.

Professor Wainer teaches Rhino like you already know how to use it. When students ask questions, she usually answers in a belittling way like how do you not know how to do this? or obviously you use this command. She doesnt record the lectures but that doesnt matter because her lectures are confusing. Youtube tutorials are easier to follow.

Claudia pushes you to your limits but if you show her that you're putting in effort she'll provide great and helpful critique . As a person though she seems chill.

Claudia was the push I needed to really elevate my architectural skills! She is very caring towards her students and gives great feedback specific to your project. Her class is packed with deliverables every session but it helps you to time manage well. for your future years. Overall great experience and improved greatly.
She didn't teach students how to use the program at all, she simply dove right in to homework assignments, and then pushed you off to TA's and googling if you didn't understand. Super frustrating.

If you don't know how to work the app, you won't understand the class. It's click after click w little to no explanation. Also, you might get some attitude if u don't hear the first time. YT will be ur Bestie for this class. Won't improve your skills. Class is not recorded for the mere purpose of you making your own research.

This studio is definitely work dense and time management is crucial. That said, it did push me out of my comfort zone which made me into a better designer and student. Claudia gives amazing feedback and truly cares about everyones project and wellbeings. She will give you the time and feedback as long as you put in your best effort each week.

(COVID Edition) Seeing Claudia's Studios' work from last semester, I thought taking her would improve my skills. I was wrong. I barely learned anything. The professor didnt answer any of my emails until three months into the semester. Professor Wainer really has a grasp of Rhino (the modeling program). It is really important that you pay attention during her half of the lecture time to get all the tips to complete the week's modeling assignment. Sometimes, she can be a little cold towards the students, but overall I had a positive experience.

Professor Wainer really makes her students work for their grades. Her tough criticism may make her seem to have a snarky and condescending attitude at first, but as the semester continues she'll warm up and provide really intuitive feedback. Also, she was very understanding if you occasionally couldn't meet all the requirements for class sometimes.

(Claudia's Portion of ARC1010, COVID Edition) 2/3 of this class would be the foundational design portion (Rhino V6). I don't blame her since she has to teach 120 people, but you better pay attention. Claudia is a perfectly fine studio instructor. That being said I don't think I learned as much from her as from other instructors. You'll do totally fine in her studio as long as you show up to every studio meeting (duh!) and give her class some effort. If you have problems with these two things then maybe you should re-asses your major.

Claudia gives amazing feedback and I learned a lot from her! Even though she does make you do some extra works, but it is worth it. I will recommend her if you are willing to work hard. Remember to utilize your individual discussion for questions or for help, she will really help you out.
Ms. Wainer made class interesting to learn and related classwork to the real world. I would recommend her to other classmates!

Claudia is a great studio instructor, I learned so much! Shes very knowledgeable, caring and wants her students to succeed. Occasionally hard to understand what she is looking for but she is always willing to answer questions. Take advantage of studio to get individual discussions and ask specific questions because then shell know how to help :)
She is one of the best first year teacher that I have , she cool, very knowledge and helpful

Learned a lot in one semester. She is a fair and dedicated professors who rewards those that work hard. Some of my student peers did not take studio seriously, showed up late without any work and expected to do well. She is far more knowledgeable in the latest software then some of the older professors.

Do yourself a favor and avoid like the coronavirus. Kills passion for architecture. Half of our studio dropped the major because of her. From what I know, Claudia grades the easiest out of all the first year studio instructors. He cares about participation, definitely gets passive aggressive when there isn't any participation.

Passive aggressive with students. If you want him to repeat questions during zoom, you can't, because he said he doesn't like repeating questions. His lectures were long and unorganized. There was a lot of information that was not needed to completed assignments. It was a little daunting to look at most weeks. Homework was simple and he gave opportunities to improve your scores before putting final grades in. He offered the option to participate via Zoom for our evening class. complete

Lazy grader, he literally will not submit the grade until 30 minutes before the grade is due and u can't even argue with him about the grade bc by that time it was already too late. Marc is definitely a character. However, it's not always the best for a borderline physics class. Marc's Structures 2 class was bittersweet. Although he was willing to go over homework problems, lectures were hard to follow. Be sure to come to class; if not enough of the class shows up, Marc will take participation attendance.

Very chill! Marc is willing to spend time with his students to ensure students understand the principles and develop their projects. Be sure to come to class with physical deliverables or Conceptboard drawings as he won't accept looking at Rhino.

great studio professor. expectations are clear from the beginning. he encourages participation and group work. he keeps things real so you might get some harsh feedback sometimes because he wont sugar coat things, but he will help you improve the projects. he provided us with great outside resources to understand the projects better.

Marc's Structures 1 class could be described as an outright dumpster fire. Marc was the best studio instructor I have had. He is super knowledgeable and insightful while being supportive and giving good (sometimes harsh) feedback. He will push you to make your project the best it can be and he appreciates it when you put in the effort to do the same. I have never learned more from a single instructor as I did from Marc.

he goes through about 1-2 lectures every 2-hour class. does check-in quizzes over zoom to make sure ur paying attention. group project is thicc but its semester-long and u can split the work. lots of hw but easy to do in a group and u get many attempts, ez enough class but hard to listen to in lecture and isn't helpful with hw until after u do it

Sasha is so good that I made my account to give this rating. She does a great job teaching the course material; very helpful feedback and digestible instructions. She understands that students are here to learn, and truly cares about their education. She's also empathetic and knows students have lives outside studio. Truly the perfect 1st yr prof.

Sasha is the perfect first year architecture professor, and I found myself comparing my other professors to her. She is SO DETAILED with assignment instructions and feedback, something that you get less and less of as the years go on. Everyone loves her!!

Sasha was my first architecture prof at CPP, and she set the foundation extremely well. Gives great and direct feedback which is something most arc profs don't do. One of the biggest highlights for me is that she explains assignments, concepts, and drawing conventions well so there was no confusion in the air (again, smth not many arc profs do).

Such a great first year professor. Very kind and clear with her expectations and feedback. Wanted prints pretty much weekly which was very expensive. If you put in the effort, and willing to discuss your work, you will succeed in her studio. If you can, take her!
Sasha is a very caring instructor and will work with you to make sure that you are making the best possible design. She helpful, gives good feedback, and it's easy to talk to her and ask questions.

For anyone like me who didn't end hs on such a good note, Sasha is the professor you want to take either fall/spring semester of your 1st year. She is super caring, would go way beyond in terms of effort towards her students, and was never the type of person to put down your work. Plus, she allows a resub if you submitted at least something on time
Provides thoughtful feedback on students' work. Very inspirational during challenging parts of the course and appreciated by students.

Sasha is a great studio instructor that gives great advice and direction for projects. She can help guide you in a direction that will make your studio project more cohesive and overall put together. They give great feedback and is pretty lenient and understanding when it comes to deadlines.

Best architecture teacher so far. She understands the creative process and is very flexible with studio work and projects. She gives very clear feedback, explains concepts very well and never makes you feel dumb for not knowing something. Wonderful teacher overall.

Sasha gives you a lot of freedom on your projects and also gives helpful feedback. She is super nice and always willing to help. She would look at your work outside of class and give feedback if you email her. Sometimes we go over time for presenting but if you already presented then you are free to leave. Definitely would take again.
Shes incredibly arrogant and i cried everyday i had her. Shes always makinf suggestions and if we dont follow them she'll mark us down.

I took Sona's studio a few semesters ago, and I can say she is the most difficult studio professor I am yet to have. I regret taking her.

DONT TAKE HER!TAKE THE ALTERNATIVE THIS WOMAN IS THE DEFINITION OF MEAN.Only excuses for health emergencies with notes from doctors, wont care that hospitals are expensive & spending a day at the clinic won't help you.DOESNT RESPOND to emails,will redirect to Canvas for questions even though she knows the answer.She thinks we're trust fund kids????

Sona has been my favorite studio professor so far. Mostly just plays prerecorded videos during class and asks for questions afterwards. Very strict about what kind of questions can be asked to the professors, would rather guide you to ask other students, TA's, or the internet instead.

Based on my first run in with Garet, I thought he was going to be a mean professor, but he was completely the opposite. Solid speaker. Values student's independence - isn't big on hand-holding. If you want to do well in his studio definitely shoot for a Star Wars/Blade Runner aesthetic. He went to Sci-Arc and it shows.

He is alright. has an off vibe to him but was fine overall. Studio is not his main priority. Has a little bit of an ego. Does not give very good feedback but rather tries to let you do your own thing, but then gets frustrated when you won't create what he wanted. Overall, he was just an alright teacher. Not terrible

This class was mainly an asynchronous for the most part, which can be either a blessing or a curse. The class met for an hour to critique people's work, but that's where the positives end. Garet was a great studio professor. I personally saw him unlock and inspire students that had a rough start to the semester. He gave redlines in a respectful manner and knew where to be firm with a student who needed it. I would take him again if I could. He had us ahead of both other sections in our cohort/made critics stress-free.

Katrin overall is a great professor who gives great feedback without attempting to take over your project too much. There are some things she will be adamant about you changing, but it's not common. Although she is a smart and respectful professor, she is also not the most empathetic of professors and will not sympathize much for your issues.

Katrin overall was a very caring professor that does seem very interested in what she does. But things could have been better. Through sitting in studio, I felt that those who naturally excelled tended to get more attention. She would give general advice, but seemed to "tell" and not "show". Favoritism? Maybe. Overall? Decently good.

She is one of the best studio instructors I have ever had. She listens to students and really takes their thoughts and opinion seriously. Studio classes will always be difficult and come with an insane amount of work, but she is incredibly understanding and gives great feedback on projects, making the class so much easier and less stressful.

Pick a different professor. George makes his section stay for the entire 6 hours studio is allotted for. And during this time, he'll only get through 5 or 6 of the 21 students in the class. George does not give constructive feedback and will go off on tangents often. Will spend more time with certain students than others which bottlenecks crits.

ABSOLUTELY TAKE THIS PROF! Very direct with his feedback and not vague like most studio profs. He emphasizes section drawings and highly encourages using Illustrator. He's relaxed and approachable yet respectful. I'm grateful that he drifted from the main curriculum at some points because he prepared us & helped develop our final project more.

He is such a great professor! He gives great feedback and helps students understand what is expected for class. He is also very respectful in critiques and proposes ideas that can help students improve in their designs.
David is great, he's nice and the feedback is good, though his instructions are sometimes unclear. Might send the list of deliverables fairly late but he's lenient.

Really great instructor. Despite this past year being his first at Cal Poly, he taught the material very well and guided us in the right direction. He always really clear about instructions and expectations. Critiques are very helpful and he's really nice about them. Very understanding as well. Highly recommend lol.
THIS IS FOR 1502. Graded by TA's which could be harsh on little things such as file naming conventions such as .PDF1 thats 1 will give you a -1. QUizzes every week and assingmnet due every 2 week.

Mostly just plays prerecorded videos and asks for follow up questions, but overall explains well. Drew is a top-tier studio instructor. His feedback is heavily reliant on what you show him, and he's good at reciprocating the same energy you give back to him. its not that he requires attendance but u r gonna wanna attend. His feedback is really good and he wont stop explaining something to you until he knows you get what you are doing. really awesome and its open to creativity

DONT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR IF YOUR A FIRST YEAR!!!! if you are a first year do not take this professor, not only will he not assign you what really needs to be completed but will assign that work at the last minute. Mitchell has an incredibly kind heart and absolutely cares about his students. He knows how to guide and critique students with respect and class - every bit of advice he gives is meaningful. Insanely wise and knows what he's talking about. He isn't the most communicative man, and sometimes doesn't know what's going on, but is so so caring and kind. You have to manage your own time in his studio - he isn't good at giving deadlines. He lets everyone work at their own pace, which means some people don't do well.

Mitchell was the best professor I've had, as other comments said he recognizes your strengths and instead of telling you what to do he pushes you in the right direction. He is patient and understanding and grades fairly. He is respected by students for his experience and takes time giving you good feedback!

Mitchell really cares about his students and their growth. He is full of knowledge and wisdom gathered over a long career of teaching and practicing architecture, and he is eager to share that with his students. He will crit your project hard, but he is never unkind or condescending. Though he expects much from you, he will meet your where you are.

When you have a question, he won't tell you exactly where to like put a wall or a door. Instead, he will explain to you the problem so that you understand it and fix it yourself. You will def understand your project and how it develops. Also, he loves enthusiasm and he reciprocates it. Show interest and he will stay as long as he needs to to help u

Mitchell is a great professor. He allows creative liberty and is great at honing in on each student's strengths. He definitely grades based on how much effort and work you put into your projects and how much progress you make overall, but as long as you work hard he is a caring professor that'll help you progress.

Mitchell is the best! He is very inspirational and is a very skilled teacher. He really cares for his students. I was so glad to have him for studio this semester. As with any class, you get out what you put in, but he really helped motivate me to give my all and I have learned so much about design as a result. Take him, you won't regret it!

Mitchell is a great person and gives really clear instructions. However, he doesn't really push you to produce good work since he believes that everyone has their own pace. If you are really good at motivating yourself and have good time management, then Mitchell is a good teacher to provide extra feedback. Also, text him instead of email.

Interactive feedback received, good communicator, and open to creative ideas. He paints what students are thinking with the broad brush and fills in the details with the fine brush. he's ok

mitchell loves learning with you, and therefore you love learning with him

Ever was a great professor. He was super good at giving constructive feedback and was always able to compare your project to an existing one. I would 100% take Ever again.

Really good foundational professor, explains concepts for beginners easily using a different number of diagrams, metaphors, and examples. Ever is a great person and professor. He is understanding but still pushes you to get your things done. Will give great feedback on your work. Like all studio professors, he has his flaws. Lectures are really boring. When trying to reach out, it's impossible to reach this instructor. With all due respect, this class was incredibly boring. I was really excited for this class too. Bob is one of my favorite professors. He gives such good feedback although he can occasionally be slightly harsh. Bob cares a lot about his students and makes an effort to get to know everyone. I did not like Bob for the very reason that he gives off know it all vibes, and for the fact he once called me sassy for asking a question. He shows favoritism towards his studio class. Very sassy and comes off as passive aggressive. Lecture heavy but gets sidetracked and rambles a lot. 2-3 assignments per week which are mostly discussion related, easy A if you follow the pace of the work, but you need strict time management. Slow grader.
Long lectures but gets sidetracked a lot with his own stories and studio. 2-3 assignments every week including reading his book and quizzes.

IN MY OPINION... he's alright i guess. Wouldn't take him again, he's really passive aggressive. Plus I've heard other people say he's scary during critique. Also kinda a big ego tbh he only posts his studio on the insta and like that so rude to the other 170 students in architecture lol.

Robert (Bob) Alexander is a pretty good professor. His lectures are engaging for being online and his activity section ends early. However, he charges over $100 for his e-book that he wrote. His organization skills are a mess. He reused the previous year's Canvas for this year which makes sense. All of the past assignments in 2021 are still there. Overall this was one of the easier Architecture classes. He gives weekly film/reading assignments and had us sketch during every class. Easy A if you do all your work, but he's a slow grader. I had the class online in 2020, and this professor was super easy to get a long with and just had such a great energy. What an amusing man. Bob's fount of architecture references will set you off on the right foot as a first-year with a hilarious sense of humor to boot. Half of ARC1010 (online) was for Bob to lecture about the week's topic. The workload itself isn't too bad as it was only a small project, a chapter reading, and a movie for the week. Bob is caring and likes to interact with his students, especially with the people in his studio. Some may start disliking Bob and ended up liking him after taking his studio. Bob is hilarious and once you get to know him is a super great professor. Hes very smart and gives great advice and resources to help in studio. I cannot fit all in just this. Extremely hypocritical to make his section look best. Tries to explain in lectures, most students left not knowing the assignment. Bob is a unique professor. He is great at giving lectures and to talk to you just need to get the courage to speak up. He gives feedback if asked for, and be open to any suggestions. You will be lost during the course, but don't be discouraged; use your peers and his office hours.

His style of teaching is not clear. It's hard to follow up with him. Her grading criteria are clear and help you prepare well for the essays. The test seems to be a bit difficult, but if you study carefully, you will do well. Highly recommend this class

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Croteau is by far my favorite professor at CPP! She is extremely knowledgeable, caring, and understanding. Her class structure and grading system is very straightforward. As long as youre taking notes in class, participating in discussion posts, and completing the written assignment you should pass this class! I absolutely love her!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I love professor Croteau, her class was my favorite for Spring 2022! There is a book required but I would just watch her lectures instead. once a week we had a quiz with 20 questions and a discussion board. This class was fully asynchronous which was nice, she was always able to accommodate. 3 exams and one paper which were not too bad! Take her!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Her lectures are very well constructed, and the slides she gives us to study for the exams are extremely valuable. The papers we had to write were not difficult and she allows a lot of freedom when writing.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Her lectures are very long and heavy for an online course. One discussion and quiz for each week. If you take notes you should be prepared for all 14 quizzes and 3 exams. All quizzes and exams are 100 points each. Also an art paper halfway through the semester on a piece from the met museum which wasn't difficult.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Even though class was asynchronous, she seemed caring and kind with enthusiasm and motivation throughout emails during semester. Weekly lectures, quizzes, discussion post. Three exams and one paper. Lectures can be long and somewhat dull, but criteria is easy. Wish I had this class in person, as it would seem more engaging. Overall, recommend.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Class was suppose to be synchronous only to find out once class started that it was asynchronous. It wasn't up to the class to vote which mode they wanted either. I'm not too good with my time management skills and found myself having a hard time managing her 1.5-2hrs worth of lectures every week... Just felt that her weekly work was too much.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Croteau was an amazing professor, and her class was enjoyable and easy to follow. She is always available to help, and she genuinely cares about her students. The workload was reasonable. We had weekly lectures and quizzes and discussion boards that followed the lectures. The exams are based off the quizzes. We also had one paper.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Susan Croteau is honestly one of the sweetest professors I've ever had, she really cares about her students and wants us all to pass. There's 1 hr long lectures twice a week, one quiz (all from lecture) and discussion post every week, one 5-7 page essay, and 3 noncumulative exams consisting of 100 questions. You don't need the textbook :) .

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Croteau is so sweet. Her lectures are fast paced, yet very important. Extremely organized and has a clear grading scale. Online quizzes aren't due until the night before the test, and very helpful to study because they are exactly like her test. The class material is hard to memorize, but she really knows what she is talking about.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very lecture heavy. Simple grading throughout the class - quizzes for each section, 2 midterms and a final (sometimes she'll throw in a paper or she'll just have you do an essay question after each test) She really cares about her students too.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Croteau was so nice and cool. You do not need buy the book just come to class ready to take notes. Try to print out the slides and take notes from there so it would be easier to remember. She has weekly quizzes but she recycles that for the test. Her weekly quizzes is about 30% and test are 40% then the rest is participation etc.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: without a doubt the greatest professor at cal poly. she is beyond knowledgeable about the material and really makes you love it as much as she does.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Class was easy if you study. Lectures are just pictures so you have to go to class to hear what she has to say. Attendance matters, easy class but can get boring

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She reads directly from the textbook and has no problem repeating or clarifying if you don't understand. Her slides are on blackboard but they just have the bare minimum for each piece, so either pay attention in class or get it directly from the textbook. STUDY for tests and quizzes. There is one extra credit opportunity.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's a really chill professor, I took him for Winter 2025 and considering the fires and all he was very mindful of due dates. As long as you complete the assignments (discussions/ homework/ few quizzes)and detailed on the final using the lectures you'll do well!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Super sweet professor. Attendance counts towards grade and there's one final group project, but overall an easy class with a really easy-going professor!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dudes super cool and its a super nice class to take for a humanities. Go out of your way to take this class with him.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This was one of the greatest classes I've taken so far at CPP. Professor Manny is so supportive and understanding. The big assignment is a very fun group project where you choose a style of dance and take a class for it. Seriously one of the best teachers, and super understanding of any personal issues you may have.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's a great instructor, attendance is mandatory and will count towards your grade but he is very lenient if you are in a tough situation, and very understanding. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Griffith really knows her stuff but get ready to read a lot, new chapter every week. Be sure to read it beforehand and have a discussion ready for class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

It is about 10 minutes in length and you will present in front of a small class, he then asks you questions on the subject. Mr. McCabe is a very brilliant professor, who knows everything about Biology. I really enjoy his lectures. He is up to date on blackboard, with powerpoints and other materials because he also teaches online courses. One big tip: attend class the week before an exam, he reviews the study guide.

The syllabus is pretty straightforward. Quizzes/exams are based on lecture notes and articles he may assign. One final presentation at the end of the semester that is easy to get full points if turned in on time. Attendance isn't necessary but can help you understand the material better.

Dr. Carpenter is incredibly knowledgeable about biology, he is basically a library of information. He encouraged student questions, and he would happily explain. Quizzes are graded based on completion. Exams were conducted online and were open book/note during class, about 20 MCQ's. He would sometimes throw some EC too! One poster due at the end.

I took his async bio class and it was a snoozfest. Just do the assignments and you'll pass. He constantly send emails reminding everyone of the upcoming quizzes and exams, which r all ez. If u want an easy ge then take this class
Lectures are very in-depth and informational. He is very interested in his subject and it shows. Expect to be studying a lot.

Fall 2023. He a cool guy who's very passionate about biology but honestly you dont ever need to show up to a lecture. This is the easiest class you could ever take. Take this class if you want a free A but are okay with not learning AS MUCH as you could from a more strict professor. Tests were online and quizzes were graded on completion not score.
3 exams and one big assignment due at the end of the semester. Exams are easy if you read the presentations he posts on canvas. Make sure you watch the TedTalks he uploads.

Mr. Carpenter is a great professor with plenty of experience in what he does. He cares for the students and teaches his class in a clear manner. However, his class does become dull from time to time. The exams are difficult if you don't take any notes nor pay attention. You are graded by a few things, but if you try in his class you will be fine.
pretty easy, only one assignment. some quizzes and 3 exams but very doable.
All quizzes and tests are online. The book isn't mandatory to read and he posts all lectures online. There is one project that is a poster board. However, the board can be done online.

Could easily be an online class as attendance doesn't matter (he posts lecture videos online). LOTS of lectures and 3 total tests (no final, tests are online). The only points you really receive are from tests and they can be difficult and answers cant be found online. Just make sure to know where things are at in the slides & you should be good.

Professor Carpenter was a great professor. He is a bit monotone, but he does give breaks in between. He has quizzes, but they are full credit no matter the score. The exams were a bit hard if notes are not organized. The worst part was the project, but it was doable. We met once a week, and rest of the class was asynchronous lectures. I recommend!!

Medical parasitology hybrid async, met 1x/week in person but the lectures are posted online anyways. Quiz almost every week. No final. All the tests are based on his notes and sometimes from online-assigned videos and readings, so beware. Expect a solo or group presentation. He is OK...really boring but the class is not hard. I recommend!

Decent professor, his quizzes are automatic 100% no matter what grade you get. He uploads the notes through canvas. The only thing diffcult would probably be the exams yet they are at home and open notes.

The exams are easy, they are literally open internet and open notes. Also, the quizzes are automatic 100's since he gives full credit for just doing them. The only difficult part is the project and that's about it.

Decent professor. The material is hard, but hsi exams were open note and open internet. Honestly manageable and a good professor to keep in contact with. Just make sure you actually understand the material before leaving lecture. ASK QUESTIONS!

Forgot to leave a review earlier but I had him in Spring 2021. This class (by him) is always asynch online before COVID. Quizzes and exams are open-book and untimed. His lectures are really boring because he talks fast and is boring. The quizzes are tricky because you don't get partial credit. It's all or none. I recommend though cuz it's doable!

Dr. Carpenter is a decent professor. You can tell he knows his stuff from his lectures. My only complaints, however, is that it is hard to stay on track with this class. This class depends on you making sure you are keeping up with the lectures, which are quite boring at times. However, other than that the class is easy with quizzes being particip.

Asynch class, even before COVID. Quizzes are easy bc u get full credit regardless of your score, no HW, 1 easy poster assignment, 3 exams. His class had 3 exams, 3 quizzes, & 1 poster. His tests consist of multiple answer questions and he doesn't give partial credit for those. Other than that the class is good. I loves that his quizzes you get full credit for attempting. but theirs not a lot of assignments so better do good. doesnt update his grading till right before semester ends

This is by far the easiest environment class I have taken! He has no actual assignments. All lectures are pre-recorded on YouTube. There are some articles and videos to watch. No homework. Professor Carpenter is an amazing prof! His quizzes and exams were not timed and are open for about 3 days. There are a lot of lectures and powerpoints, but overall the course was doable. Make sure to double-check your work though and carefully read the questions on the exams. DO take your time. We also had a bio poster project, but it was easy.
Professor Carpenter is a solid instructor. There will be a lot of lectures but its not too bad. Easy exams and quizzes, and one assignment.

Professor Carpenter is very knowledgable in Biology and you can tell he knows what he's talking about. Our class got switched to virtual from the COVID-19 pandemic, so he made video lectures which weren't too long. All his exams and quizzes are online and not timed. His class isn't too hard if you don't slack off and become lazy. Easy A if you try!

Professor Carpenter is probably one of my favorite biology professors! Although hes monotone during lecture, hes very knowledgeable about biology. Very knowledgeable and chill, but his lectures can be boring since his voice is sort of monotone. Fell asleep in every lecture, but I suggest attending each one bc he sometimes gives out 5 point activities. His tests/quizzes are online but hard. I have to say I really am glad I chose Prof. Carpenter. He is a very good teacher, though a little boring at times mainly the tone of his voice. Prof Carpenter is an amazing professor! I don't understand why people complained about his class. Exams are online and not timed, doesn't expect you to memorize anything. Attendance isn't mandatory but still show up since he does random in class assignments that are put into your grade. He does extra credit! Do yourself a favor & take him!

This class is very easy and it's an easy A if you do your work. Lectures are assigned through youtube and class sessions are mostly used for activities (quizzes, short assignments, or jeopardy). Kevin Carpenter was one of my favorite classes. His class is so easy and we got out early almost every time. Just show up so you don't miss any quizzes, which he allows you to work on with everyone as well as with open notes.

He's a cool dude. Attendance matters because you either had to turn in an in-class worksheet or a quiz. He let us work together on the quizzes making it easy. Two tests, both online. Homework is just watching videos. Easy class to pass.

His lecture is uploaded on Youtube, however, his voice is kinda boring and make you fell asleep. There are pop quizzes and worksheets every week. However the exams will be all online and easy to cooperate with your friends.

Took professor Carpenter for Bio and it was one of the easiest classes I've taken. All tests are online and quizzes are taken in class and you are allowed to work with others. He's a funny, sort of awkward guy who makes the course simple to complete. Attendance isn't taken but you may miss a quiz or worksheet if you skip.

This should have been an easy. IN-PERSON class. All of our exams and quizzes are online and open book basically. The lecture is heavy/monotone/boring/ read the book. I can't speak for his in-person classes, but his BIO 1110 online class was very reasonable and had very clear expectations. His online lectures are great! Watch the lectures and youll pass! The test answer are taken straight from the lectures and online powerpoints. Solid class!

One of the easiest classes I've ever taken. The class consists of 2 midterms and a final, 3 quizzes, and a written assignment. extremely easy course. There's two online exams. A few quizzes, he'll give you the points for them if you just attempt them. One poster project which counts as the final. It felt more like an online class.

Easiest class Ive ever had. I stopped showing up half way through the semester since we never got any assignments. (2) Quizzes and (2) Midterms (no final) are online, PowerPoint based. As long as you try on the quizzes you get 100%. Then you have 1 easy group project. Take him. Dont show up. Take the online tests. Youll pass.

Attendance is not mandatory but he gives three assignments in class and if absent for all three your grade will plummet. He is passionate about Biology- cool, but this was a class I just needed as my general. Super hard grader. Unless you are a great test taker and have a laptop with you to cheat, stay away. Midterm and final make up your grade.

Never went to class, never studied, still got a B. How? Open note exams (computers, tablets, notes, his lecture slides). I literally just googled every question. Thatll get you a C. He gives extra credit at the end which bumped me up. he grade is midterm, final, and a few in class assignments, thatss it. Dont get textbook, you dont need it!

I don't see why everyone is complaining about this class. By far the easiest bio class I have ever taken. He literally lets you use your laptop, along with his slides, during his tests. Just download the slides and use Ctrl+F to find the answer. You're golden after that.

Super overqualified... I never skipped a day, and I ended up with a B-. Take someone else. The tests are too hard. Your grade is basically a midterm and a final. I do not recommend him at all, unless you are really good at taking tests his class is challenging. If you bomb one test out of the two, there is basically no way for you to pass with an A. DO NOT TAKE HIM! Terrible unless you have mastered biology already. I took him thinking I knew what I was getting into but soon after realized it was a terrible idea. Search easier professors unless you want to torture yourself for ten weeks.

Your grade is only based on a midterm and final. Which both are open book and you can use your computer. Aside from that, his tests are hard. He's super boring too btw.

I really disliked this class; it was open book open note tests but, not worth it. Attendance is not mandatory because he never takes attendance. Professor Carpenter was dull teaching, so it was very difficult to stay awake during his class. A plus side though is that his tests are open note and open book, but then all you hear during the test are people rummaging through slides and pages. Another thing, DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK, you never use it.

Pros: 1) You basically don't have to show up to class because all he does is go over the powerpoint notes. 2) Exams are open note/book/you can use the lecture notes on your computer but don't be fooled because the exam is still super difficult. Cons: 1) He's soooooo boring. 2) His exams are hard and your grade is based off of two exams Midterm

This professor wasn't the most exciting but our very first class he said that he understands a lot of people are only taking the class to fulfill a GE requirement so all quizzes and tests are open note and open book. For the exams, save all the slideshows on your laptop it's a big help.
This has to be one of the most boring professors of all time.

This professor is ridiculous. He makes the class easy by having the midterm open book and 10% of our grade is through quizzes taken in class (that you receive full credit for as long as you take it). She was very sweet and respectful and would always help you if you asked. Never made you feel bad if you did need help. She would grade you for attendance. Dr.Beardsley was a good professor. He made the class very lively and just overall good vibes. He has a good personality and sense of humor. He wasn't the best at teaching the class, instead would just go off the slides pretty fast. He did give a lot of work that was very time consuming. Beside that, I would take him again.

Professor Beardsley is an outstanding teacher who makes his lectures engaging and enjoyable. He genuinely cares about your success and offers flexible office hours to help. His extra credit opportunities are straightforward and manageable. While his tests are comprehensive, they closely follow the information provided in the study guide.

Beardsley is passionate and ready to help! His lectures are engaging and easy to read/understand. He offers a few extra credit opportunities. If you're struggling, his office hours great. Study guides are the key to the test, but don't do them last minute.

The textbook is easy to pirate. Encourages students to create a study group. If you study for at least 2 hours with this group, he allows you to take the test again with your study group, which really pads your test score. Has one quiz every week, but allows you to take it multiple times and the questions are the same.

Paul's lectures are alright. Very hard to take notes during lectures because he teaches fast. His lectures do get very boring but they're very detailed. MasteringBio saved my grade. Workload is good, and not stressful. Exams were easy thanks to the cheat sheets he allowed. Better than Brandon King so it's a win.

Greatest professor ever! I was really struggling in the beginning of the semester yet I ended up with an A in his class due to his determination towards helping students. He allows one lowest exam to be dropped as well as an opportunity to gain more points on exams through forming study groups and correcting your wrongs on the test. TAKE HIM!

Professor Beardsley was a great teacher. He's very invested and interested in biology which makes the class fun and enjoyable. His tests are not too hard and the homework is very manageable. Would definitely take him as a professor again!

He was a great teacher with lots of energy and clearly loves teaching biology. He offered several extra credit opportunities and test corrections to help build your grade. He gave study guides for each topic which are really similar to the exams.

Professor Beardsley has a bubbly personality. It shows in all his lectures. Although his teaching style was not right for me, his lectures were fun and he does not assign too much homework. Make sure to study for exams.

Personally, professor Beardsley's teaching style is not for me. What really helped me was going to office hours with the TA(I only went to one office hours session with the TA but had I gone to all, I'm confident I could have gotten an A ). Basically he lectures, and then you take the midterms, and he offers midterm corrections 4 credit.

One of the best professors at Cal Poly Pomona. Had him for BIO1040 Evolution. He cares about the success of his students, and grades fairly. Especially good transition to online format during the Covid19 crisis. Absolutely would recommend taking if possible!

Prof. is a nice man however his way of teaching does not work for a lot of people. He often assumes you know the material, just because he does. He rushes through lectures. His tests were insanely hard and even when I studied for days I would end up with a bad score. Some questions had multiple correct answers but he wanted a specific one.

Mr. Beardsley's class was very interesting and his excitement for biology is the main reason I was excited to learn in his class. His tests are graded very fairly and he accounts for questions that may be difficult to understand and grades on a curve. Very animated at anytime of the day. Would definitely take a class with him again.

Easiest class so far, an AMAZING professor that truly cares about his work. Will always be available to help. Study guides. USE THEM they help so much on the test and ALWAYS do the homework because there's a lot of concepts on the hw that help on the test. Take notes of what he says in case it's not on the powerpoint, he posts powerpoints.

Professor Beardsley is a really great person and professor. He is super passionate about biology. Having him in the morning, he really tried to make that 8:30 a.m class fun and exciting because he knew all of us were tired. Beware because he is lecture heavy and just shows you powerpoints and I didn't know what to write down half the time.

Very helpful and willing to answer any questions you might have. He really made himself available after class through office hours, study sessions, and email. He offered extra credit opportunities and group exams to earn a few extra points! I loved that he was passionate about biology and tried to make it as interesting as he could!

I really like Dr. Beardsley. He's extremely kind, caring, and funny. He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities which really helps a lot. His lectures are very thorough and he makes sure everyone understands. I highly recommend him.
He's a super funny guy. Reading the book and going over his lectures will give you most of what he covers on the tests.

You have to read to get a good grade in this class! And do the homework yourself, don't just google the answers! If you fall behind, look for resources other than him because he just tells you to look at your book anyways. He's a nice guy but I am glad I don't have to take any other classes with him!

I Love Dr. Beardsley! He is a great teacher. 2 midterms and 1 cumulative final. Test come straight from study guides and mastering bio. In class participation a must. In class group assignments. Lots of extra credit. Heavy textbook usage. He loves his students and it shows. Read the book, study mastering bio, DO THE STUDY GUIDE. Easy A.

PAUL IS AWESOME! I WISH HE WOULD TEACH ALL OF THE BIO SERIES. To pass his class I say just read the chapters he assigns and you should get an A. Great Class, not too difficult! The professor is nice and understanding. Class material consisted of a few quizzes and two midterms. It was a simple class, and the lectures were detailed.
I actually had her for BIO 1100L. The class was super easy. She was very kind and very lenient when grading.

I've always hated science classes but this was the first science class where I was intrigued. I loved asking questions because she loved answering all questions. Optional textbook, worksheets, assignments, quizzes, and 2 midterms based on her PowerPoint lecturers. Show up to class and study the material before taking the quiz or exam.

Professor Sanchez is by far one of the best professors on campus. Very Understanding! If you put in the work will pass. Such an amazing and understanding professor, wish more of them were like her. Very Interesting class that she's so passionate about too, would definitely take her again.
Her classes are very easy and she provides lots of great material for her curriculum. She also provides a lot of extra credit so you can improve your grades. Highly recommend taking her class!

This class was definitely one of my favorites. Professor Sanchez is very knowledgeable in the subject which makes the lectures interesting. the professor is really nice. she gives extra credit by attending classes. she wants you to learn and try your best, helping you to get an A in this class.

Super sweet and caring professor. She is really passionate about the subject and makes everyone feel very comfortable. She does not take attendance. Three quizzes, one midterm, only like 5 homework assignments. Highly recommend, I love her!
Professor Sanchez does an amazing job at her lectures. Her quizzes and exams are only based on the lectures. There's about 5 homework assignments and 4 quizzes and two exams. She offers extra credit.
Really easy and laid back class.

She is very passionate about the subjects in class and will genuinely try and find out any information she doesn't know. There are lots of extra credit opportunities, show up to class and do the work and you will pass as well as maybe learn a thing or two.
Highly recommend this professor, an interesting class. Few assignments & quizzes, lots of extra credit. Few discussion posts as well.

Take her for an easy GE. We didn't do half of the assignments that she had on the syllabus and was a bit disorganized. She gave a ton of extra credit opportunities. She is caring and a nice person. Take her class!!!! I loved how she gives time for you to do assignments so you can work on your own pace and don't feel pressured. Super easy but you learn! Could even do a whole module on a Saturday to get it out the way in one day which is what i've been doing. BUT TAKE HER I LOVEEEEEE HERRR
This is a good and easy class and the professor is understanding. She got behind in the middle of the course and that was very frustrating. But overall, just do the work and you'll get an A

I took Prof Sanchez for Bio 3010 for Fall 2020. Fully asynchronous. She was kind of behind.... we were supposed to go over like 10 chapters and we only did about 4. Nonetheless, class was easy. Few quizzes, discussions, assignments and a 1 page paper. All easy :)

This class was extremely easy for me, and she gives you PowerPoints that help with your exams. She truly tried her best to accomadate us students during the transition to online learning. Her exams are easy since you have the slides to reference to. Also she gives soooo much extra credit!!! I highly recommend this professor :)

Really easy class if you want something to compliment a tough semester. 6 modules. Not many answers are on quizlet, and ctrl+f will find you most answers on the slides for the tests. Best if you sign up for this class with a friend and do the tests together. Quite a bit of extra credit too if you do poorly on a test.

Professor Sanchez is amazing! She is super dedicated and educated on her class studies. She really does want her students to learn. Never had a professor that accommodates as she does with students. The Class is straight forward. She provides a syllabus with clear instructions and due dates. She provides PowerPoints with audio. Gives lots of extra credit. I took her for Fall 2023. I didn't have her for lecture, but I highly recommend her for lab. She explains everything, so you'll be fine if your lecture prof is bad. Professor Jones wasn't great nor bad. All of her videos are videos of some dude covering this course from 2013. Her supplemental notes did help, and she does have discussion boards before quizzes and test. Her due dates for both quizzes and exams are very flexible. And was open notes too.

She treats the class like a GE and doesn't give a lot of homework. Her lecture notes are fill in the blank and are easy to follow. she was really cool! Honestly highly recommend taking her for her lecture and lab, she's really open to extensions and gives a good amount of extra credit at the end of the course. Only the in-person exams were difficult rather than the online exams since it was open note, open lecture, and open internet.
She was alright, passing her exams were hard (I only passed like 2). Her homework is easy and if majority of the class is failing then shell give extra credit.

Decent professor is all I can mostly say. Took for lab and the only work was from the manual you have to buy at the bookstore. Pretty easy and straightforward class. Extra credit offered and one of the last assignments is a project which is relatively easy.

This class felt like a waste of time. Students are better off teaching themselves as she is inaccessible and basically just reads off slides. You really have to study for exams bc a majority of your grade is exams.

I took her biology class and it was nothing special. She was good at giving the information out, however her lectures can be a little boring and there isn't much room for questions. In general not a very interactive course, it's just homework assignments, tests and lectures.

A mediocre professor at best. I had her during COVID and she seemed rather unorganized and confused over using her own computer. Lab reports and pre-lab quizzes/activities are easy but she doesn't put in grades until the end of the semester.

Easy A for me, but AVOID if exams aren't your thing.

There is just no way to coast through without Biology knowledge. To even pass the class, she makes you work for it and there is still a good chance that you may not pass no matter how hard you work for.

Professor Jones is a very straight forward professor. I took her human sexuality class and it was an interesting class. Also, Professor Jones is the best!

She gives so much extra credit. Her tests are super straightforward--straight from ppts. She really cares and tries her best to help her students. Ignore the previous reviews. Please take her.

One of the easiest college classes I've ever taken. Honestly, as long as you go to class daily and write down / review your notes, you should get good grades on exams. Lectured very clearly about everything on tests. Tests were only two or three chapters and multiple choice.

She believes a lot in collaborative work and is a great lecturer. The homework website she uses can be frustrating sometimes because it makes you do the same topic over and over again until you get it right, but it does help you learn in the long run.

Great professor. Incredibly understanding (I had to take the final a few days late because of a school trip). Very lenient and allowed for test corrections that add to your total test score. Allowed a notecard for every test as well (including final). All quizzes open note. If you struggle in chem she is the right choice. =)

1220 is a more difficult, less considered side of chemistry that is math focused. This class was difficult, but she made it very easy to follow along and do well. She gives you every chance to make your grade better. Homework is long and difficult, but if you do it, the exams are no problem. Take notes on how to solve homework problems.

Incredible experience on every level. Attendance isnt technically mandatory, but you get extra credit if you come. Homework is tough, but it makes the exams a breeze. It is not difficult to do well, and it is even easier to learn and remember the material. One of the best professors I've ever had.

Literally the worst chem Professor Ive encountered. Beware of ALEKS, its the worst program thatll have u spending 6+ hours on unnecessary material. Disregards your questions and tells you to figure it out yourself. She doesnt post the study guide until A DAY before the final.

Probably one of the best professors I have ever had. Tests were very easy as she gave a very detailed study guide before each one and gave retake opportunities after each midterm. ALEKS hw was time consuming but overall very easy to get through when you put enough time aside for it. 10/10 professor!!

Her lectures are very easy to understand, and she is very patient with any and all questions. Quizzes every week, but it all helps in the end. Her grading is very fair and clear, and she does her best so you can succeed in her class. Couldn't recommend her enough.

Her class is not difficult at all. Her lectures are online and need to be watched before class. There are activities done in class that help you learn the material. She does homework through the ALEKS system. There are 3 exams in the semester, and pre-quizzes on canvas that prepare you for the Monday class quizzes. A few EC points are given.

My favorite prof! She really cares. Weekly pre-quizzes due Sunday. Weekly Monday quizzes. 3 Exams and a final. Pre quiz and quizzes basically explain the whole exam. Video lectures so she can use class to go over examples. Only thing is there's a lot of ALEKS, but they're 3 questions per section. She goes over how to do it all. Take her!

My grade doesn't actually reflect how well I could've done in this class. Hirakawa is an amazing professor and genuinely cares about her students. She wants you to succeed and will help you immensely in doing that. I had a medical issue about halfway through the semester and she was the only professor who was accommodating and actually cared.

(FALL 2019) Homework is done through ALEKS and Extra Credit opportunities are available through a program called TopHat, both of which you have to pay for. If you dont wanna hurt your wallet I wouldnt recommend her, haha. Other than that, a great professor who really cares about her students.

Professor Hirakawa is really nice and lenient. She allows you to take as many attempts as you want for your homework and gives you until the last day of the semester to finish it all. Her lectures and tests really coincide with one another and I really learned a lot.

The best lab professor to take. She is very caring and loves to help her students. She supplies lab videos which helped understand the lab very clearly. Her quizzes were not too bad, and sometimes she decided not to give them. She grades leniently as long as you work hard on the lab reports. Definitely make sure to get a serious lab partner!!!!!!!!

Weekly labs, weekly quizzes on the lab video she gives us. WATCH the lab video will help A LOT with the procedure of the lab. Labs are done in partners, so register with a friend. Make sure to show up to every lab. If you mess up on one of the parts u prob have to restart the lab. Labs usually take at least 1 hr + 30 min. ASK for help, if needed.

3 exams, 1 final, weekly quizzes. ALEKS weekly hw, was a bit tedious (80-140 Questions a week). DO NOT wait till the last minute to do ALEKS you will be overwhelmed. ALEKS helps ur grade A LOT. In general, a caring, and understanding professor so don't be afraid to ask questions even if it's simple ones.

Professor Hirakawa was a great professor as she always made sure we were prepared for the exams. In addition to her lectures, she posted videos of herself further explaining topics and added links to other websites we may have found useful. Her lectures were interactive, encouraging students to work through problems. Definitely recommend!

Easily the best chem professor to take. Drops lowest quiz grade. Goes over the labs live in class and also in recorded lectures. Caring and has multiple office hours to ask her for help. Quizzes are exactly like the lab material of the week being tested. Highly recommend to anyone. Easy A if you just do all the work and come to class.
best chem prof. just take her. very understanding and willing to explain everything clearly.

On top of synchronous lectures, she provides videos in the module to help you further understand content. The most difficult thing about this class is probably ALEKS (hw system) but the videos give a really straightforward explanation how to do them. She's a very chill teacher and is pretty lenient on things.

No doubt she's of the best chem profs at CPP. She's always willing to explain even the smallest detail and work w/ u till u get it. She's also really nice and lectures really really well. There is a good amount of online hw on Aleks (not busy work), and it is a chem class so ofc u have to put in an effort but trust me she's the prof you want!

There is a pre quiz and a quiz every week, except when there is an exam. There is weekly homework through ALEKS. The exams are based on the ALEKS problems. The lecture videos contain the textbook discussion and practice ALEKS problems. The professor would sometimes upload the lecture videos a day late.

To me, I think her videos aren't very organized and are super shaky, I can't focus if the camera keeps moving. For a while, I did watch them but it got so annoying lol so I stopped. There are prequizzes & quizzes, easy points, don't miss them. Tests aren't hard, some are from Aleks hw. Could be better though, it was hard self-learning most times.

It's been virtual learning all semester and I don't know what I'd do without Hirakawa's patient explanations and examples. She doesn't make you feel bad for not understanding something. I feel during this pandemic, chem is SO much harder, but she has been doing exceptionally well in supporting her students with care and supplemental info. A+

Hirakawa makes chem bearable!! She is personable, caring of students, and explains labs patiently and thoroughly. My struggle with chem has always been the intimidation of the work and approaching professors about it. This isn't a problem with her because she is welcoming of stumped students. Highly recommend! Great energy too!- which is rare imo.

LOVE THIS PROFESSOR!! She's probably one of the best chemistry professors on campus. Chemistry in general is a difficult/time consuming subject, you definitely have to work for your grade. But Hirokawa is sooo helpful! Go to all of her office hours and she's amazing at explaining everything without making you feel dumb :)

Professor Hirokawa was super easy to reach out to for help. I definitely recommend attending all of her office hours or as many as you possibly can just because chem is a time consuming class that requires more attention. She also offers extra credit!

She's an excellent professor and makes things easy to understand. Classes were moved online due to COVID-19 so she adjusted her grading. ALEKS homework made up a large part of your grade. Her online quizzes were open book and open notes so they were pretty easy. She does her best to make sure that you understand the material and get a good grade.

One of the best chem 121 teachers! Highly recommend for students who struggle with chem. She tries her best to keep things simple. She doesnt take attendance but you need to go to lectures to understand the material. Take notes. Hw is based on ALEKS, which can be frustrating if you dont keep up with it. Gives out EC via Tophat or essay

Her lectures were easily understandable and her organization of the course really helps her students succeed. She uses ALEKS rather than mastering chemistry and I liked it a lot better. Her grading is straight forward and she's very caring and understanding. Half of our semester was online due to covid but she was still able to teach effectively

She is the nicest professor ever. She is so helpful and caring and wants everyone to do well. She is really helpful during office hours and can help you with the lab or anything really. Her tests are pretty straightforward if you follow the study guide and your notes. Overall, shes great.

She really wants you to pass and do well. Quiz and exam questions are often the same or similar to homework. Lots of online homework. Great extra credit opportunities. Chemistry was not my subject but if you read the textbook and do plenty of the practice problems, you should at least get a B.

Very kind and sweet to her students. 6 quizzes, 3 MTs, 1 final, and some homework. Quizzes are after every couple concepts, and are a good check of what you learned. MT builds off quizzes. Tests are word problems/application with no m/c. ALEKS homework is long, and she doesn't even test from it (get ahead and forget about it) You can ask about lab!

She is very nice, but her lectures are very unorganized. Tests often do not resemble the homework she assigns which is ALEKs. Often has points in her lectures that are on quizzes that you must listen carefully for. Allows for two opportunities of extra credit, and replacement of exam if you do better on that section of the final. Fine experience.

She's a nice person. BUT A TERRIBLE TEACHER. Goes off topic in class A LOT and you have to listen very closely to her for get information on tests. Assigned HW on THE WORST PROGRAM EVER. BEWARE ALEKS!! Wasted $100 on HW, plus an extra $30 on extra credit. SKIPS A LOT OF MATERIAL IN CLASS THAT'S ON HW AND SKIPS CHAPTERS!! DO NOT TAKE HER!

Chemistry is hard. You cant expect any professor to make it easy if the subject itself isnt. Jennifer is one of the most caring and nicest professor in the department. Be persistent, go to office hours and make yourself present. She will honestly tell you what is on the quiz, test, with great detail. You just have to put in the actual effort.

3 weeks in she told us attendance is not mandatory, I went up to ask questions after class and every time it seemed like someone else's problems were far more important than mine since she would never recognize my presence as a student. Ill just go to my next class 50 minutes early, so I can actually talk to my professor.

Prof was amazing and took so much time to make sure that we were able to understand the materials. She makes the lectures relatable for everyone for all non-science majors. We had a few quizzes throughout here and there as well as essays and no textbook required, so you could use your notes for the quizzes and final.

She is an ok professor, she did teach us how to do problems in class and went over it to make sure everyone got it. However, she was always very unorganized. She does allow extra credit and her exams very easy. She does online homework on masteringchemistry or aleks.

Professor Jennifer is a very kind and nice professor. She tries her best to engage a large crowd of students. Her lectures are pretty helpful. Only con is that she is not very accessible during office hours. The one thing that is annoying about her class is hw. She uses a website called ALEKS, worse homework site. Overall pretty decent Professor.

Tried her best to get over 100 students engaged in class. Homework was online, and I hated every minute of that dumb ALEKS program, but you could do it in class as she was explaining it, and you could go to office hours and get help on it.

One of the best professors, if not the best, Ive had at CPP. Extremely helpful and approachable. I went to her office hours because I needed help with my study guide from my chemistry lecture ( with Joelle O), and she explained everything to easily. Shes the best!!

She should be given such high standing at Cal Poly Pomona, she cares about all of her students and wants everyone to understand the material. If you go to office hours you'll be able to get help on the online homework and prepare for the exams. Gives lots of opportunities to raise your grade and returns quizzes and exams quickly. 12/10 professor.
BEST chem professor I've ever had. She is very nice, patient, and fair. I love that she utilizes the white board and has nice writing. She is always available outside of class to help!!

Great professor who explains concepts that you can easily understand. Her grading is forgiving. If you do better on the final than the midterms, your midterm grades can be replaced with the final. Homework is online, using Aleks. It's a stupid program, but it's manageable. Overall, Harikawa was pretty good. Easiest of the CHM 121 professors.
Lab lecture is just explaining the lab. She's very caring and explains everything clearly and even allows omissions of parts she thinks is not important.

Professor Hirakawa is an amazing professor. Very nice and is always willing to help as much as she can. Make sure to complete her homework and study for her exams. Her exams are derived from her lecture notes so try not to skip class. Drops lowest quiz and her final exam is cummulative and heklps replace your lowest exam score.

Professor Hirakawa is amazing! She is very enthusiastic and her voice never puts you to sleep! She explains everything very well and will always answer your questions. If you take notes and follow along you will get an A!! She also bumps people up who have borderline grades! She is a must take!!

This was a great professor. She mainly wrote on the board instead of power points, which worked well for me since I am a visual learner. She takes time to explain concepts and goes at good pace since there is a lot of complicated material to cover. The grading scale she also uses is very clear and helpful and she offers moments for extra credit.

Professor Hirakawa is the best! She's really friendly, approachable, and helpful. Even though attendance is not mandatory, show up for her lectures because it'll help prepare you for the exams. I'd definitely take her again!
Professor Hirakawa is amazing! Attendance isnt mandatory but its not a good idea to skip the lecture, she gives good notes that are very relevant to the exams. Would definitely take again.
Amazing professor! If you took chemistry in high school, you should have no problem passing this class. If you didn't, she really cares and is always available to help you understand.

Best chemistry professor ever. In high school I came out of chemistry with a C- and i thought I was horrible at chemistry but with Professor Hirakawa my test score average was an A at all times. Show up to lectures, do the in class participation, do all the online homework and you will pass. What you put in is what you get out. Be willing to learn.

She really cares about the success of her students. There was about 100 people in the class yet she takes the time to get to know as many people as she can. If you need help with anything she'll stay after class or you can go to her office hours. She has a very clear teaching style and tells you what to prepare for on quizzes/exams.

She is a great professor. I loved her class. Her lectures were great. She was ALWAYS available during office hours and helped you with every question you had until you understood. She really cares! NOTE:when i say easy A, people think show up and get an A. No, it's chemistry, you'll get an A but only if you show up and pay attention and do the HW

Super sweet professor, really knows chemistry and actually explains it in a clear-cut way. Pretty big amount of online homework. Had 6 quizzes, two midterms, and a cumulative final. Don't buy the ($250+) book, no one used it!

So helpful, she genuinely wants you to succeed. Attendance is not mandatory but come to class and go to office hours if you don't understand something, and you will do well! I never understood chemistry before her class, but her in-class explanations and use of the Aleks homework program have left me confident in my chem abilites. Amazing teacher.

She is the nicest professor I've ever had and is extremely helpful. As long as you show up to class, you'll understand the material. She gives a lot of examples that really help with the homework. I never once had to use my book. She doesn't use Mastering Chemistry so don't buy it!

She's great. I didn't really listen too well in class because she was very organized but she was always willing to help. Just know that you will need Aleks for her and not Mastering Chemistry, so have fun with that. I know I didn't.

Lecturers are not well organized. Her lectures are slightly confusing because of the lack of organization. Her tests are on the difficult side if you are trying to get a good grade. Miss one question and its good bye good grades... and your hard work!

WORST professor tried to communicate and ask for help but only his way was correct. Had favorites in the class which did not help. Multiple people failed this course. Only take him if you are good at chemistry and like to teach yourself
very very nice

This professor was straight-up rude when you asked questions or seemed confused. He thought his way was the only way and didn't try and help you in a different way if you didn't understand.
