GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! Chem lab is hard regardless of the professor but Corcoran definitely does his best to help you out. I asked him for help during pretty much every lab and although the class was a pain and reports suck, if you ask for help he will explain and make sure you understand for the quizzes - doesn't ask much about the pre-lab (1 of 6)

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Any other professor honestly is gonna be a better choice. Informal communication over emails, he likes some more than others, and he is also a very hard grader. Won't know your grade til week 12, office hours are pointless he doesn't stay the entire time he has his office hours, passive aggressive, nice guy bad teacher
Dr. Corcoran clearly loves and is passionate for Chem. He made me realize how much I love chemistry and had so much patience when I would ask questions.

Corcoran's lab is absolute profound gobbidge!!! P-Chem lab, although the most challenging class I've ever taken, has to be the best class I've taken so far. I've learned so much about life through Corcoran and his witty talks. Super helpful guy, wise as his age says. Really talented cook as well.

Tough grader? Absolutely. Kind with your grade? Even more! Corcoran is hilarious, constantly on your back in lab, and really pushes you to the limit. He MAKES SURE that besides suffering, you really learn from the lab and apply it outside. He loves the stuff he does. Incredible. The effort he expects from you is the same that he puts it to you.

Homework done through Mastering Chemistry. Quizzes every week. 3 exams and a final. 3% extra credit for each exam and the final. Lectures were live and pre-recorded and are 99% of the tested material. Has a curved scale for an A (100-80). Easy to get an A if you do all your work and watch the lectures. Caring person and lenient if you need help.

His lectures cover some things but he says he mainly uses them for questions and class discussion. The rest of the time you are learning by mastering chemistry or the textbook so have fun teaching yourself
Pay attention to his lecture videos he put quiz questions on those and be prepared to teach yourself a lot.
He has weekly quizzes and has a ton of homework. His lectures are okay but he post the powerpoints as well as reccorded lectures.

He is caring and makes lectures interesting, that being said ONLY take this class if you are confident that you can teach yourself the subject matter. He gave easy examples in lecture and much harder conceptual and calculation problems on test and quizzes that he never covered. Mastering Chemistry will be your professor for this course.

Did not like his teaching style at all, made the subject much harder than it needed to be. He doesn't give answers back to you once exams are over, but still expects you to learn from mistakes. Doesn't give partial credit on quizzes and final is worth 41% of grade.

He's a great professor, but be ready to use MasteringChemistry like crazy. This class can be very frustrating, but with the homework helps. Studying was quite difficult, but if you know how to study, this professor is for you. Be ready for quizzes and using clickers (Fall 2018).

He tries to keep lectures interesting. Always available during office hours if you need more help. I found it helpful to study his lectures and the book. I had him for 1210 lecture, and liked him so much I took him for 1220L. Would recommend taking him for both.

I took Corcoran because he was the only option for CHM 115. Overall his class isn't bad, but his lectures were boring and you could learn the same material faster with a textbook. Also, you have to buy a clicker and show up to class for participation which is a waste of time. The class is graded on a curve because its harder than it needs to be.

Professor Corcoran is okay as a professor, but his standard for a chemistry class engineers are forced to take is kind of high. His lectures are very broad on purpose because his goal is to "guide your inquiry", which basically means learn from the homework. His syllabus mentions where each letter grade is, but he ended up giving pluses and minuses

I didn't do so well in the class but I understand there's a strict criteria that they have to follow. I had him for CHM121 Lab and he was very helpful. I had difficulty setting up an apparatus even though we found it was broken he kept helping us over and over again until it was set up correctly. He explains labs well and is really accessible.

This man is a beast. Great professor for my first quarter of college. Going to lectures are crucial. Great Professor overall, but get ready to work.

Very passionate about what he teaches about. His grading curve is an 80% and above is an A, which is awesome. The daily quizzes were not hard, but his midterms and final were a bit of a struggle. A very funny guy that applies Chemistry to real life.

No quizzes, final was just cleaning the lab room. Super helpful, caring, lots of examples and important info written on the board. Labs are partner assignments, due the following lab day at midnight. Wish I could take him again, real good guy.

Chemistry is not my strong suit so I struggled a bit, but he has office hours and will answer your questions. He gets off-topic quite a bit. He doesn't provide study guides, so its hard to know what's on the test. Make study groups before the tests. Amazing professor. Very passionate about Ochem and made sure that all of the students understood the material before moving on to a new topic. Homework assigned is worth a decent percent of your grade (so not super exam heavy), quizzes & exams accurately reflect what we learn. Very clear with due dates. Gives opportunity to earn back some points from missed questions on exams. Coming from someone with heavy anxiety, she was super nice & helpful. Study ahead of time! Memorization is key.

I'm so glad I started my Ochem journey with Dr. Thane. She's the GOAT! Super nice and understanding. Her notes are well-organized, and her lectures are engaging. No real study guides were given, just chapter concepts. The class is fast paced, but she wants you to understand and is willing to meet outside of set office hours. The lowest exam is dropped and there is one group quiz. Lots of homework and teaching/practicing outside of class is necessary.

Dr. Thane is an amazing professor who cares about her students and goes above and beyond to make sure her student understand this difficult material. Her notes are very detailed and explain everything. Tests do have harder problems than the homework assignments so prepare for this by doing as many textbook problems as you can.

Genuinely the best professor I've had at cpp. Takes the time to learn every students name & makes sure everyone understands the material. Lectures are in person but are recorded & posted on canvas. 3 midterms and 4 quizzes, lowest midterm is dropped, & allows test corrections. Accessible outside of class. No words to describe how great she is!

One of the best professors to take for Ochem! I like that she actually lectures during class time and we don't have to watch pre recorded videos before class. She gives practice questions after a concept which really help in understanding. She grades fairly and gives points where she can. I would most definitely take 3150 with her after.

Dr. Thane was definitely the best prof to take. Class was very tough because of the insane amount of material to know. She records lec and breaks everything down. Quizzes and exams were fair as long as you study daily. STUDY EVERY DAY because material keeps building up and it's easy to fall behind. Go to office hours. 3150 is way harder than 3140!!

I am going back to my past professors I have taken and cannot believe I never wrote a review. Dr. Thane is a great teacher. I took her my first semester and it was her first semester teaching. Ochem is tough, but with her knowledge, you can do it. There are a good amount of chemistry professors, so make sure to have her on the list.

Dr. Thane is wonderful. O chem is already hard and she knows that so she does her absolute best to help in any way she can. super accessible outside of class and very willing to go over topics if you're confused. she goes the extra mile and genuinely cares that everyone learns the material and does well.

Dr.Thane is AMAZING! She makes Ochem very digestible and understandable. She has so many resources that allow for you to succeed. Her office hours are so helpful and she creates thoughtful study guides along with having a review session. Her homework is also very doable. "You just have to be a little bit better today than you were yesterday"

Dr. Thane was definitely the perfect prof to teach O-Chem. Class was tough but O-Chem is hard no matter who you take it with. She records lec and breaks everything down. I love her. Her lectures are super organized, its easy she chews everything for you like if you were a little baby and explains everything well. I took mahendran and failed because it was so hard to learn for me but o my God she made me not hate and detest ochem. I feel that im learning and retaining everything. She is an amazing teacher.

Dr. Thane is the best professor I've ever had! Her lectures are so organized and I was able to get As on every exam and even a 100% on the final! She is a great professor. She cares about every one of her students and is very helpful. Definitely take her if you can!

she is SO great, very accessible outside of class and helpful! she is extremely approachable as well. ochem is a very difficult course, you need to be prepared to put in the work, though she is extremely fair and helpful in helping you succeed. i would take her for the entire series of ochem if i could in a heartbeat.

Dr. Thane is great. I have no idea why she got a few bad reviews. She is the kindest, most caring, and most amazing professor. She truly cares about you and acknowledges that this course is hard. She is so so accessible outside of class and very willing to help. tbh, if you didn't pass this class, it's probably your fault for not getting extra help

The subject is tough, but Thane made efforts to make sure students passed. accessible outside of class, patient, and understanding. Lecutures go fast and have lots of info. Dr. Thane is one of the best organic chemistry teacher I have had at Cal Poly. She provides scaffold notes in which gets filled out during lecture. She uploads them after each week to Canvas. Practice problems, quizzes, multiple exams, HW, short surveys are all part of your grade. As long as you study and do all the assignments you will be ok!

Dr. Thane is an angel. She makes organic chemistry easy to understand. Drops lowest midterm. Gives extra credit opportunities. Exams are reflective of practice problems and homework. Take her, you will not regret it!

The BEST orgo professor at Cal Poly. Organic chemistry is definitely hard, but she has this way of teaching that helps you understand the material so much butter. Actually cares about you and is patient. Gives you opportunities to correct mistakes on quizzes/tests so you're actually learning from them. Take her class if you get the chance!

My favorite professor ever. I've had her for 3140 and her 3150 class is incredibly easy. Incredibly organized and has a perfect style of teaching. I recommend her to everyone. Good class, but I have gone to almost every single office hour and she gets frustrated if I still don't understand something.I'm putting in the time and doing all of the practice problems she assigns + hwk problems. This class was definitely hard, but this professor puts a lot of work in to make the information understandable. Multiple group quizzes, three midterms with lowest midterm dropped, and test corrections to re-gain missed points.

She is great! Extremely helpful in and out of class. Although she does go a bit fast while teaching, she is someone who is willing to help you go through the material if you do not understand it. DrThane is a tough grader but shes accesible during Office hrs but her office does fill up. Ochem is a well known weed out class, but Dr. Thane somehow made it fun. Professor is knowledgeable, truly cares about student success, and is easily accessible. Gives no feedback on assignments, not everyone has time to go to office hours, not very approachable. Makes the material harder than it has to be.e

Exams are a lot tougher than hwk material and class problems. She goes way too fast during lecture, no extra credit at all, no study guides, not a good professor overall, especially with such a hard class.

Good at explaining concepts, but does go really fast during lecture. Test material is harder than the hwk and class problems. Amazing lab professor. Made sure each student understood the lab conceptually and made sure everyone was safe and aware of the dangers present in each lab. Best lab professor ever!!! She pretty much holds your hand through each lab, making sure you're doing everything right at each step. She's also super understanding and sweet! Dr. Priya was an excellent professor! She made the material clear and easy to understand. She gave a final exam sample and went through each question and explained it very well. She was an amazing professor, very approachable, and she made you feel safe.

Professor Priya was amazing. She helped us through any difficulties in lab, whether it be the actual lab or the report. She usually responded to emails within three hours. She gave several study guides for the lab final.

He won't submit grades for a while. Participation matters. Show up for every speech (and class if possible) for 15pts extra credit. He's weird about respect.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He can be intimidating but is very helpful when it comes to getting over public speaking fears. There are only 3 speeches for the semester, and he gives you an outline of the speech. There are two tests but they're online.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: DO NOT take this teacher if you are taking a communications course. I made the mistake of taking it, baumwirt is an egotistical a-hole who prides himself on "making students cry" in class which I found very odd. Felt like nothing was retained or relevant. He just shouted at students in my class and even cursed at us. I also felt very uncomfortable.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Gave good advice after speeches and his lectures went over how to write the speech outlines. The workload is not insane but there are some discussion posts, quizzes, and a final exam. Speech outline takes the longest to write, and you have to basically memorize the speech since he doesn't want you looking at notecards that much.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Baumwirt was surely an experience like no other. He was a good public speaker who brought a lot for us to learn and take from to improve our own public speaking. However, he was terribly strict with his grading and was slow at grading. I still don't know two of my speech grades because he only inputted them at the end. If you take him, GOOD LUCK.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He isn't bad, but very insincere. He will tell you that your presentation was good, but still give you a C.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Overall Baumwirt is a good prof, his lectures were entertaining and most of the assignments are all online but weren't too difficult. For speeches, he is a tough grader and has a strict criteria for what he looks for, but if you follow what he wants you'll do well. Though, if you don't like his personality early on, get out because he doesnt change

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Baumwirt made me realize the best qualities in myself, even the flaws, if I didn't really like who he was as a person, or assumed him to be. Him playing devil's advocate helped me to realize that everything is a lot more neutral, and to be the best you can be, you just have to let go of all inhibition and fear to communicate what you want

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He looks intimidating but all he wants to do is help you. We had 3 speeches done through video upload, one speech live, midterm, no final. Though he is a bit of a tough grader when it comes to the speech outline. Also some classes were zoom/in person and he'd cancel some classes which was funky but whatever, epic class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Baumwirt was a horrible professor. He expects way too much from students and his jokes were never funny. His exams were based on the textbook which he barely covered and you are pretty much on your own. Communication with him was difficult as he took every word/question students emailed him to heart. Overall, stay away from him.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is a tough grader, but he gives good feedback so you can improve. He pointed out what I was doing wrong and once I fixed it, he gave me a high grade. Really good professor. I would say he is excessively tough, but can occasionally be lenient if you can adapt. Not flawless, but pretty good honestly.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Baumwirt is an acquired taste. He genuinely cares about his students and their success. He has a blunt sense of humor, so you need thick skin, but he is very funny as long as you understand that he's joking. I think professor Baumwirt is a great professor and person, he just may not be the teacher for everyone out there.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: If you're good at speaking this is an easy A, he really just wants you to seem like you know what you're doing. The textbook is only needed for the midterm and final. If you take it online HAVE YOUR CAMERA ON!! It's a huge deal in this class. You just need to know how to deliver, if you're bad at writing you can get by on being confident.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Baumwirt was my last resort for a COMM 1100 class,this is an intro to public speaking and overall his class became unenjoyable fast. He seems like a good professor on the first day then in the next class he expects too much from students who are taking a GE course. If you try you will survive, he is very nit picky with certain things.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Baumwirt was a great choice for COM1100 because he was clear of what he wanted from students. I think that he was pretty lenient when it came to grading speeches, especially the live ones. I think that he also gave extra credit that boosted everyone's grade. His exams are hard, but he gave what chapters to study from the ebook.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is a good, caring professor and is very clear about what you need to know and learn. However, he is a tough grader and doesn't give the best criticizm. He expects A LOT from students. This class was harder than my actual major classes...

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He sucks don't take him

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: (SPRING 2020) Prof. Baumwirt is HILARIOUS and goes to great lengths to keep students engaged. Public speaking can be very intimidating. However, his teaching style made it feel less so and really brought the class closer together.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Baumwirt is a very interesting man. Although, his speech presentations and assignments are rather intimidating, his grading is very reasonable and worth it. His lectures are entertaining and rather enlightening. He's honest and brings real world aspects into his lessons. If you had to choose a communications class, I recommend his course.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I've never had a professor be so understanding. He really wants his students to find improvement in themselves. The speeches can be tough to produce, but for myself at least its just been a problem of time management. All the speeches you do in class are very interesting, and if your a stem major finding something for speeches should come easy 4 u.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He lets his emotions get the best of him and can be hard and rude at times because of this. We all get a textbook and the final does not cover it like he mentions and have to read on your own. He doesnt mention this until half of the semester is over.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took this class online so my review may be a little unusual, but Baumwirt is somewhat a tough grader although he gives great feedback. We had 4 main speeches that ranged from 5-7 minutes long, and my whole class seemed to be stressed by it. The tests aren't too hard and he does curve some assignments. Beware of the stress this class will give!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Baumwirt is a great choice for a GE COM class. You only give 4 speeches and there is barely any other work than a couple tests and peer reviews of speeches. The only thing is that in his class it is completely up to you to keep up with what is due (those due dates sneak up on you, so beware). He gives lots of feedback and wants to see you improve!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He has clear standards and expectations. Grading is a little hard but overall good lectures and really helpful. He's funny and knows the material.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He likes to help his student be successful; he allows you to speak up and ask for help. He tries his best to make the class be interactive even through the pandemic, which is great. His speeches are easy if you follow the outline and practice, but since that's the most of your grade, you really need to spend time on it because he's a tough grader.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took his class during the Pandemic and I enjoyed his lectures because he will make you laugh but don't take his class if you take things too personally. He is a teacher that wants you to pass and tells you to come to ask him for help if you need it.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: 4 speeches. Its a really quick class due to the fact that its all speeches. Textbook is available online for free. Follow his outline instructions & you will be fine. Final was open book & taken at home. If your the type to get offended easily, he might not be the right professor for you.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Do not take him. He cannot control his emotions in class and it leads to you fearing hun and learning absolutely nothing. Good luck on that final without having a single productive class lecture.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He was not organized about giving back scores and feedback. His extra credit opportunities did not help at all. He was very goofy but not a good teacher and then his tests were hard with material we never covered because he was too busy making jokes. He never responded to one email I sent him the entire class. He only works with students in class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Baumwirt was by far one of the best professors I've taken at CPP. I was not ready for public speaking if were being honest. But Baumwirt's class made it that much easier, and throughout his class I could see both myself and others improving.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Hands down one of the best professors I've taken a class from! Professor Baumwirt makes the class fun and engaging (I was terrified of public speaking, but I loved his class), and is very clear about what is expected. He really cares about his students, teaches life skills, and will take time to work with you. Amazing teacher; highly recommend!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I don't know why he has such low reviews, he was a very good teacher with clear instructions, I got a B+ 88% and could have got an A if i put a little more effort in practicing my speeches so that was totally my fault. The people complaining are just lazy and use chat gpt for their speeches or don't practice at all He is a very nice man

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Ruh was a tough grader, I got an A in this class so it is definitely possible. Even when I felt like my speech was good he always had something negative to say. His midterm and final were not too bad since they were online and you can use notes. He did give the class extra credit at the end if you followed his phone policy.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: His sour attitude doesn't make him a bad teacher. Grading criteria is VERY clear, and as long as you outline your speeches EXACTLY as he tells you to (and practice!), you'll pass with flying colors. The only reason I didn't get an A+ in this class is that I failed one of my speeches because I waited until the last second to write it.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Was scared by his low rating at first, but he's a really good professor. Is super clear about how he wants speeches and assignments done, if you just read the rubric you'll do well. Most people who got D's just did their speeches at the last minute. Give the class a little effort and you'll do well.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: DO NOT listen to the 1-star reviews. He's amazing and those who got lower than a B honestly were not listening to any of his announcements, lectures, and emails. PLEASE practice your speech, the amount of people who read off their outline is insane. I'm terrible at speeches but I ended with a solid A. Just listen to what he says and you're good.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Nice guy idk why people are leaving such negative reviews. One thing is that he can be pretty tough with grading but if you listen to his feedback and do your work you'll be fine.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Please, for the love of god, don't be tricked into his funny charismatic persona on the first few days; these reviews by others are entirely accurate of his teaching skills and performance. He turned into a monster when grading. He did nothing but nit pick. He is by far the absolute worst professor I've ever taken.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Had this professor fall of 21. Checked his reviews, still unfairly rated even after 3 years. Great professor will meet with you during office hours/after. Respects students who need help, always with a hilarious attitude. Unfair reviews, would vouch any day for this professor. Grading-wise hard beware, out of all the classes at CPP he's the easiest

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: No clear grading criteria. His progess meetings were pointless, as he'd approve my ideas & even read over my speeches but never got higher than a B. Accused me for cheating on my notes in class and gave me a 0, which lowered me a whole letter grade. Didn't respond to emails. Made fun of me giving him a penny in class instead of a quarter.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The class was very lecture-heavy and quizzes were somewhat difficult of what they were asking for in the questions. The speech portions I felt were alright if you were able to pick a good topic for the prompt. Gave the tools to succeed in the class. I liked his character overall and I personally don't see all the hate for him.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Don't listen to his charisma at the beginning of his lectures; these reviews are entirely accurate of his performance. I've been at cal poly for 2 years and this is the worst professor I've ever taken. He irreparably harms students careers and does their education no good.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Do not take this professor. I made the mistake of not checking Rate My Professor before enrolling for this class as it was my first semester: what a horrendous mistake. Please if you care about grades, do not take this Professor Ruh. Way too critical... turned me off from any sort of public speaking in the future- killed my motivation.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Horrible professor, if you can choose an alternate professor, please do so. Gives useless feedback and harshly critiques people who are barely starting out. His jokes are not funny whatsoever, so if you're one for awkward moments where the professor makes a joke and receives blank stares from the rest of the class...then this is the class for you.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I always felt so disconnected and discouraged from this professor and while he has a great attitude and a great speaker, but honestly a poor listener to the point every time I went to office hours I would only get 3 to 5 words for my topic to only be bombarded by a lecture what I should do with out fully explaining my ideas

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Unfortunately didn't get a full semester with Ruh but he was a great professor if you really want to learn. Not harsh grading, but you get what you earn and he gives great feedback - always willing to work with you

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Ruh is not a bad teacher in terms of his depth of knowledge and the material he teaches. He actually gives good feedback on the speeches presented. The gripe many students have is that he seems overly strict on grading criteria. If he loosened his grading and gave the same feedback, I think many people would find him fun.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is just the worst, I couldn't stand his teaching style. His anger issues are through the roof! if you take him, just make sure you agree with his point of view on every topic because he will get angry if you don't. He also yells at students in front of the class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: All of the Ratings are true about professor Ruh. At first, he seems like a really cool professor and his lectures make sense. towards the end of the semester, it just goes downhill. He will start to stress out and not care about you he just wants to finish grading and he becomes a rude person.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I was iffy taking him at first but in my opinion, he was an average proff. He was very strict on his rubric and if its not what he wants he WILL take points off. Grade changes drastically with presentations and it went from an A to a C in the last week. Overall, hes alright.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: HORRIBLE profesor, grades things last minute before grades are due. Messes up a lot of the time. Does not answer any emails, and the assignment itself are easy but his grading is just so strict and wants everything done his way. When it comes to speeches even if the speech is very good he will always find a way to criticize it even when not needed

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Takes forever to grade. Tough grader. At the beginning of the class he said that rate my professor was wrong but here we are. Assignments are relatively easy but he makes them difficult. Stay away at all costs.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Honestly the worst professor I could imagine. Grades extremely late for assignments that build off one another. Overly critical about work, just "bc its not how he would have done it." Feels like I'm back in High School being hounded over every little thing. Also doesn't understand how to teach general classes bc he does not apply class to all.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I honestly dont understand why professor Ruh has a lot of bad ratings. Yes, he is a bit critical with speeches, but its only to help make you better. He's also very understanding. I missed an important assignment due to personal reasons, and he was more than happy to help me make it up when I explained to him what was going on. Just do the work :/

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Insufferable. The worst instructor I've ever had the displeasure of attending. His feedback would often be condescending. He once had an erotica tab open and visible in a corner of his browser, while sharing his screen. He dislikes any deviation from his formulaic speech template and any student who attempts to is met with harsh, poor scores.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Horrible professor. Incredibly petty. Gives grades back months later. Helps you but gets frustrated easily.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: One of the things that I heard most from Prof. Ruh was " we have to move on, we're running out of time". One thing that I prefer, is a Professor that makes time for his/her students. This was not the case. Prof. Ruh was also one of the strictest graders I've had in college. It seems like an A is close to impossible in this class. Do not recomend

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very lazy when it comes to grading so you never know what your grade actually is. His feedback to you will more than likely be very harsh and make you feel bad about your abilities if you didn't do perfect. Very Strict about what he wants and how he wants it. Lost interest in the course. Not really inspirational, so don't expect anything special.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Ruh was not as bad as people on here made him out to be. He was late with grading, a bit tough with grading but I did not think it was a bad class. He's pretty understanding, gives good feedback and it was not too much work. If you put in the effort and try to enjoy the class, its pretty easy and not bad.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Ruh is one of the worst I've had. He is so picky with your assignments there is no room for creativity. Your outlines are more important than your speech. I thought the reviews were wrong but they were perfectly accurate. He likes things a certain way and if you do it not that way then your probably screwed no matter what.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Would not take again. He doesnt grade anything until the very end so make sure you try your best from the beginning because if all your assignments are bad, you wont know until youre done with the entire semester since the grade book only shows the first 2 assignments. Hes also extremely unorganized and doesnt give details on work. Stay away

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: It actually surprises me that he has low ratings considering that his grading criteria is pretty solid and although he is critical with his speech grading, he isn't bad by any stretch. Despite what others say, I'd say give him a chance.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is very insensitive of his students even if you engage in class topics and turn in all assignments. He will belittle your opinions and disregard your questions. Along with the fact that he constantly mocks a student with disabilities in our online class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Rue expects perfect performance, while he does the bare minimum explaining the assignments. His grading is very odd, as he often gives Cs to students who gave great speeches, but cited sources incorrectly. He is also very behind on grading, so you can expect to see your grade drop by 20% during the last day of classes. He's also rude.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Despite the quizzes, midterm and final being easy, he is a really tough grader on speeches (the majority of your grade). You miss one or two things and you're looking at a B as your grade on that speech. Also, his grading system is hard as a 93.99% is an A-. Lastly, you can never get in touch with him as he doesn't respond to emails.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: By far the worse professor I've ever had at Cal Poly. He is incredibly rude and condescending to students, and constantly is racist to students who don't speak English. He has terrible temper issues and the slightest thing sets him off. Virtually unreachable by email he constantly complains that his email is full. Incredibly heavy workload for GE.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Ruh enters the class with a certain charisma in the first day of class that is misleading. doesnt allow any cell phones during class. He makes you buy the text books for 3 uses the entire sem. And he gives really unspecific prompts then grades extremely harsh. After speeches he critiques in front the entire class. He will tear ur arguments apart.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I would give a 0 if I could. This is easily the worst professor I have ever had at Cal Poly Pomona. He is inconsistent and unnecessarily harsh with grading for an intro class, he is condescending and EXTREMELY nit-picky. You will NOT get an A. Also doesnt grade work all semester because he says puts him in a bad mood..... Avoid him at all costs.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: avoid avoid AVOID this professor at all costs. condescending and rude. He will make snarky comments and if oftentimes in a bad mood coming into class. His speech expectations are not entry-level standards. He expects perfection and bulletproof research. Half a letter grade will be taken off for each absence, which is excessive and ridiculous.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The Good: Passionate. Allowed to use notes on quizzes. The Bad: Often times subjective. Make sure to stay away from political topics for your speech. When asking for class feedback, he'll often interrupt you. The Ugly: The PowerPoints are annoying because he doesn't take out the things you won't be quizzed on. He needs to make them concise.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Teaches the class as though it were an upper division course. Oftentimes, rude, condescending, and stand offish. Talks over you constantly, went to office hours to discuss my grade on a speech and next class he told my peers about it. Gives confusing instructions, overall very rude!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Horrible professor that doesn't teach you anything. Don't bother taking her class if you want to learn something. No actual thought behind any of her assignments. Surprised Cal Poly hasn't fired her for being so incompetent. Also she loves using lies/excuses to cancel class, specifically the third week. She does it to every class every year.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Terrible, that's the only word to describe this course. She doesn't teach you anything about how to be better at public speaking. She forces you up onto the stage and makes you talk, that's her way of making you learn. There is a horrendous amount of work but she grades so insanely hard, so don't expect an A cause you won't get it

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Jaimes is unfortunately one of the worst professors I have had at CPP. Her canvas is a maze, the grading scale is extremely tough, and her grade updates are late. Her deadlines are extremely confusing as well and when trying to email or communicate with her, there is no way to get an answer until after a week. Bottom line, DO NOT TAKE.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She acts like she cares about you, but she doesn't. She says she should be fair to everyone but she isn't. If you finish an assignment even a bit late, she won't let you turn it in. For an intro to public speaking class, she shouldn't even be teaching. Her format in Canvas is bad, & she's also always late to respond to any messages.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Not very understanding, I did all my speeches. I had trouble turning them in online and she gave me 0 on some even if I emailed them to her days before the due date. Ended up failing (I pride myself as a good public speaker). Redid this class over the summer w/ Rebecca Franco (exact same speech scripts) and passed with a A in half the time.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Her teaching style is very confusing. She does not respond to emails. She does NOT accept late work, no matter what. If your internet went out during an online assignment, she won't let you make it up. The way she formats her assignments is very confusing. She is a very hard grader, public speaking should not be this hard.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Way too much for a public speaking class. Strict guidelines for how she wants things done and strict due dates no matter the circumstance. No late work accepted. If anything the speaking part was the easiest part of the course.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Was very very strict about the exact way anything should be done, also the amount of homework for a public speaking class was ridiculous. Would not take her if you have difficult classes because your time will be taken by this

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Speeches and homework lack clarity and she is a tough grader, she does have some extra credit which is nice. I didn't do it but I would recommend peer tutors as finessing her assignments is hard. If you need this GE take her class but I would recommend going to another teacher.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Not a particularly hard class but effort needed to do well. Lectures are standard, although a lot to keep track for speech preparation and keeping up with assignments. Doable as long as you pay attention to major speech requirements which are generally explained clearly. Prof is a little hard to reach outside of class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: By far one of the HARDEST GE's I have taken here at CPP. So much prep work that goes into a speech and very very hard to meet all the standards on her rubric. Once you finish your speech you will oftentimes immediately start preparing for another one. Last few speeches are difficult to do because she asks for a lot of citations which is hard to do.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Jaimes is a teacher that you should take if you are a communications major or close to it, not anything else trying to pass a GE. I felt like I did more work for this class than any of my major classes. I found myself preparing for new speeches while I had past speeches to present still. She is a tough grader for an introductory level class as well

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She assigns so much for a ge class and doesn't give a lot of time to prepare for speeches. She is hard to reach by email and won't answer right away.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She was not easy to reach, the only time they ever read Emails is during office hours. There are no acceptions or redos for missing speeches, practice ones, or quizzes. Only way you could get excused or redo it is if you have a school sanctioned absence. She doesnt have lectures you just need to read the slides and the books to learn.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took this speech class online spring 2021 and it was my worst decision ever. Her zoom sessions are solely for speeches and not for questions, concerns, or even conversations with her students. She is not good at answering emails, nor being clear about assignments and deadlines. I did not have a good experience in the class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Zooms are only for speeches. Sucks at getting back to you through email. Quizzes are easy. Topics easy to write about. Main problem is no time to prepare for speeches. After the speech is assigned be ready to present the following week. Never throughly explains things, reads off her power points in video lectures that you need to watch on your own.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: 5-6 quizzes. 4 speeches. 2 exams. Pretty simple if you follow all instructions/ the syllabus. IMO she doesn't give enough time between speeches to prepare for the next, so make sure you stay on top of your work. All the speech topics were pretty easy to write about. Make sure you go to class on speech days, otherwise have fun trying to pass

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: 5-6 quizzes based on textbook, but I didn't buy the textbook and did alright on the quizzes. 2 exams. 4 speeches: memorable experience, informative, movie review, persuasive. You'll have about a week to prepare the speeches, as she tends to post outlines pretty late. Instructions on how to develop speeches are pretty clear in the syllabus.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This class is all about following directions, turning things in on time and showing up to the speeches. If you follow her directions on the syllabus, posted lectures, and do your speech as she asks, you will pass the class. There are 4 speeches, each one with peer reviews. There are 5 to 6 quizzes, all of the material is from the book.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: such an unorganized person. Everything is all over the place. Small things include her handouts or website layout is terrible. Big things include she will give you a very very arbitrary date for submissions. Half of the time doesn't even post a link like 10 minutes before an assignment is due. All over the place, just all over the place.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She's Mediocre. Took her class online due to COVID, she's alright but sucked at keeping due dates clear and didn't allow late work. Quiz almost every week based off text book, one midterm based off quizzes. Four speeches but doesn't gives the grades until end so you can't see how you're doing. Takes forever to respond to emails, and busy work.
