Class wasn't too difficult. May be more difficult for no programming experience at all, but I think for most people in my class it was rather easy. Drops lowest lab, assignment, and exam grade so I didn't even have to take the final. Assignments/labs usually every week but they aren't too difficult and he will help you in office hours. Chill guy.

Super nice and interesting professor! Class is extremely easy -- the whole point is to get GPT to do things for you more efficiently. The baseline to get an A is very low, but he encourages students to go deeper and explore everything related to NLP.

For his prompt engineering course, he was great, other than sometimes when it would feel as though he is making up the course as he goes along. Despite that, you will learn a lot and he does not grade too harshly, with the projects and topics being generally pretty interesting. Great professor!

Class material isn't that hard. Its mainly just asynchronous with him posting certain youtube videos for you to watch. What makes him difficult is how he never responds to any emails nor is available for any help. Overall seems like a nice professor and it is an easy A as long as you submit the assignments.

Like others point out, his lectures are him just talking about "the industry". He gives very little guidance for the semester long projects but requires you to implement specific features. This class pretty much relies on your group. No exams and attendance not required unless you have to present a part of your project.

No quizzes or exams only 3 solo projects ( 2 big ones and the 3rd project builds off of the 2nd one) and 1 group presentation. Attendance isn't required and the material covered is just design patterns for Java. The class is easy enough and he/ his TA is an easy grader.

More like a motivational speaker than a professor. My friend and I were struggling to understand how to start the class project and went to talk to him during office hours. He give us the same rant he gave in class. We went online and signed up for a couple of online courses on web dev and started studying to do the project and barely made it work.

Just very uninteresting classes. He spends most of his time talking about the industry, which I can summarize for you as "apply to a lot of places" and doesn't teach much. There was some guidance for the big semester long project, but not as much as I would like for what might be considered the most important class in the major. Very skippable prof

One of the only professors in the CS department that focuses on trying to prepare you for the outside world after graduation. If you don't care and don't attend you'll pass but it's one of the only classes actually worth going to sometimes. CS4800 was a semester-long group project to develop a web-based application. Actually learned useful stuff.

This class is very easy. The first assignment may be slightly tricky, but the remaining two are a breeze. Only three assignments and a group presentation on a topic that should be an individual assignment. No midterm or final. If you have any questions, his office hour is always open.

The difficulty of the course depends on how much you want to work on for your project. I like how Prof. Sun pushed everyone to push the app to Google Play, which adds a very nice record to my resume. A lot of self-learning for the topic but that's exactly how developers should do their work.

This professor is the embodiment of mediocre. Basically took him for winter class and he doesn't teach, just gives you pre-recorded lectures to watch. Problem is, some of the stuff from the videos is outdated, so you have to look up a lot of things yourself. It also doesn't help that he doesn't really respond to emails that much.

One of the few classes I've taken that focused on practical experience and advice instead of grinding through assignments. There is little stress and passing the class isn't an issue if you work on the semester-long project regularly. I was able to just pay attention to the (helpful!) lectures and advice professor gave and actually learn something.

Professor Sun's lectures are very hands-on and practical. He always adapts to use the latest technology and his top priority is to prepare students to get ready for their careers. Besides the course content, I learned a lot about job application and career planning. He is a true mentor for students, because he always thinks for students.

Great professor to learn about the industry from. No tests. Main issue you may face in this class is learning how to build a web service (especially if you have had no prior experience). Make sure to sit next to people that are smart / hard working, because you are put into groups on the first day for your semester-long project.

Dr Sun is knowledgeable about the subject and communicates clearly, both verbally and through presentation materials. Live coding demos in class and energetic lecture keep the class interesting. Workload, however, is as much as you want to put in. If you are motivated to learn a lot about Software Engineering quickly, he is a good choice.
Best Software Engineering professor at CPP. Only class you'll take that means anything outside of college.

Not too difficult, just basically a quiz each week, a (not too long) paper, and a group presentation on whatever topic you choose. Showing up to class can be annoying since attendance is mandatory, and most grading is done on a C/NC basis despite the class itself being on the A-F scale. Not too bad though.

This class was easy but he is not a good professor. Grades off a complete or incomplete system but still has a letter grade. Basically, pass at least 9/10 quizzes for an A, 8/10 for a B and etc. Quizzes are poorly written, he gives one-sentence essay prompts for 6 page papers, and gives very boring and annoying lectures. I do not recommend him.

So this class was easy, and is for the most part a light workload until he decides to assign a 6-page essay to be completed in a week and a half. Class consists of watching youtube videos and taking terribly worded quizzes on canvas. There is a group presentation that he gives no clear instructions on. He changes his syllabus during the semester.

The only thing I liked was how easy his class was to cheese. The material itself is very boring and his syllabus changes due to him not being able to keep up with his own pace. Very easy but very boring, which is good for people who just want to get a requirement done. Also, forces you to buy Packback, which is a very funny discussion board.
He changes his syllabus midway through the year. His grading system is pass or fail for each assignment. If you fail one assignment your grade drops by a whole letter. Avoid him at all costs.

The class is mostly Prezi slides and interesting documentaries. This quizzes aren't bad and there's only 4 essays. The essays are kind of tough to write because the prompts aren't great, and the grader can be harsh. But, he usually will give you back points if you complain to him about being graded too harshly. Also, all assignments are pass fail.

This was one of my favorite classes I have taken at CPP. Professor has clear grading criteria. Lectures are unique, they are mostly based off discussion and aren't tested on. If your trying to get an A as fast as possible you can do homework in class and ignore lecture. If you enjoy the course material you can engage. Fun, balanced workload

If you want a headache then this is the professor for you. He does not care about you whatsoever. Attendance is mandatory. He is always unprepared for lectures. He has no knowledge of the course material and cannot answer the questions you have for him. If you are taking his class you are studying on your own. Harsh grading structure. Do not take.

You have to learn by yourself. The professor is literally learning along with the students. He quite possibly be the worst teacher I have taken at any school I have been at. He is very unprepared for every class. It seems like he hasn't even looked at the material before entering class. Do yourself a favor and do not take this teacher.
Horrible at teaching

This professor literally doesn't know the topics that he's supposed to teach. You become responsible for ingesting all of the textbook material on your own, as every lecture was a session of him trying to learn the topic on the spot in front of a full class. He rarely has meaningful answers to questions and often gets stuck doing example problems.

Grading system was a bit unorthodox but really not that difficult to understand. You do all the work, which was not tough at all, and you got an A. You won't really learn much though. Other professors who teach this course make you do more work I think so he is probably your best option.

Really boring class overall, but not very difficult either. He wanted people to show up to class, but his lectures were mostly useless. Class consisted of 4 essays, 6 quizzes based on movies, using a site called Packback, and a group project. Everything was turned in online. Relatively easy class, but you won't really learn anything.

The class is easy, but the work is degrading and the professor is very frustrating. The only lecture I attended was the worst presentation I've ever been in. The grading system is incomprehensible and he changed it from the syllabus on the last day, after we turned in work, to make the requirement for passing higher. Not difficult, worse: annoying.
The class has a very weird grading system that takes a while to understand. There are 3 essays, but as long as you hit the page count, you're all good.

The class was interesting, but the grading system was very unusual, with each assignment being graded complete or not and a chart to determine your grade depending on the number and type of assignment completed, so you can't skip a single assignment to get an A. Essays were pretty easy to pass if you hit the requirements. Not great communication

Pretty easy class but professionalism for an undergrad lecturer is not there. Weird email responses, takes forever to respond if he does at all. Unclear grading. Video quizzes were easy, great recommendations on movie selections. Just do the work and he welcomes the effort. Appreciate laidbackness but didn't really learn except we have no privacy.

This was the professor's first semester using Canvas. He had no idea how any of it worked and struggled the entire semester, even deleting a quiz once and having us retake it. Hopefully he learned from it and will be more organized next semester. Course information (350 character limit): pastebin/DDdzQUeh

This class grading system is pass or no pass. Therefore, you must get like a 80% to pass for quizzes and 90% for essays. The quizzes are based on a movie you watch. Also, I feel the quizzes questions are unfair which makes it very hard to pass. Overall, this class is more stressful than it should have been. If you don't want stress avoid.

This guy is super unorganized and has an unfair grading system. He does assign movies to watch which are interesting but the quizzes often ask ambiguous questions that can be very opinionated. His prompts for essays are also confusing. He also has a dumb thing called Packback which you gotta do every week . The AI grades it and is terrible at it.

It is hard to imagine that this professor got into his position from his teaching abilities. His organization was terrible, he gave quizzes where the answers were not part of the lecture material, or were wrong, the lecture content comes from his opinions, and he has an unreasonable grading system. don't take his class online if you don't have to.
Class is a total disaster, but i found it entertaining and incredibly easy.

There are quizzes where the material wasn't even covered within the lecture. He's super disorganized with using Blackboard; although I don't blame him since it's a bad LMS. Usually throws about due dates and assignments and are due by the end of the week.

Weekly discussion boards and quizzes on movies/videos. A lot of the quizzes had weirdly worded questions and many of them had questions that werent even in the weeks material. Try the best you can on them and just complain to him and he will try to fix it. 3 essays and they are easy and around 3.5 pages. Kind of a throwaway/dated class.

Try to avoid this guy at all cost, his quizzes literally make no sense whatsoever; I feel like they're actually designed to make you fail. A lot of confusing questions, some answers that he's never even mentioned in lecture material or they're just inaccurate answers. The coursework isn't too bad but sometimes can get confusing on what you gotta do

Simple course, but very unorganized online. There's no structure, at times I find myself wondering what's due. Also slow email responses. He also assigned 2 essays on less than a weeks notice. There's a group presentation and several films/tests you will watch. Take this class online if you can.

He's really simple but I didn't like the discussions that was due every week. His movie quizzes were easy but some of them were like tricky questions. We got lucky and only had to do 2/3 essays. Presentations were super easy. I think he's more lenient online than in person.

Ever notice how the most worthless classes are the ones that require attendance? Yeah. Your grade will depend on your showing up to a class in which you could just stay home, watch whatever documentary he posts and do his dumb little quiz, weekly discussion boards, group projects, essays, all the usual GE suspects. He also injects politics. Fun.

AVOID AVOID! The teacher has a grading policy where very hard to get an A in the class. Here is his criteria copied from his syllabus: You may have no more than two unexcused absences Of the two essays your score on each must be at least 17/20 Your group presentation score must be at least 8/10 This is just 3 of the 5 req he has 4 an A in the class

It seems that Eller changed his grading policy (for the worse) since none of these reviews are valid anymore The class is graded on quizzes drawn from tediously long documentaries. If you enjoy spending HOURS scrolling through videos for answers, you'll love him (you won't). This class has absolutely no business being as difficult as it is

Teacher definitely has passion for the subject. Shows a lot of relevant videos in class that can sometimes be boring depending on your interest. 4 easy essays and 1 group project as final. Class is more of a discussion than it is a lecture.

I took this class to complete my general ed requirements. This class is super easy, but boring. We watch a lot of movies and youtube clips; we rarely have lectures, maybe 2 lectures the whole quarter. There are no daily homework assignments, you get points for attendance, and for your midterm and final your group does a quick and easy presentation
there are a lot of group work (after each quiz and exam, group project). there are quizes before each chapter (RAT). try to teach, but most of the time looses his own place. all exame are open book
he is trying hard... a lot fo group work. kind boring in the class.
Didn't like teaching style & he was inconsistent with answers. Took & received A in formal logic just before taking class with him and found his methods of indirect proofs were invalid.
No Comments

I really enjoyed taking Salloum for both Architecture and Database Systems. He is definitely not for everyone because his lectures go at a snail's pace, but overall he does provide a ton of examples to learn from. He is also a very caring professor that will definitely provide extensions and exceptions to grading rules if needed.

This class is passible, but he makes it difficult. The homework, quizzes, and tests get exponentially harder as the semester goes on and he will increase the difficulty of quizzes if the class is doing too well. If you pay attention and use chatGPT you should be able to pass. Everything is open note and internet but sometimes that doesn't help.

This professor is caring and a bit funny but he doesn't really teach anymore. He'd just kind of ask if we had any questions but was pretty bad at explaining things, often explain examples w/o drawing them and then he'd forget/get lost in his own example. The actual content is pretty standard,needs a touch of modernity but overall material was good.

Professor Salloum's class is overall decent. The lectures can be slow and he sometimes rambles about CS topics not related to the lecture material. His homework is pretty similar to problems on lecture slides and the test/quizzes are very similar to the homework.

Honestly a really caring professor who's really knowledgeable about what he teaches. He assigns a lot of homework but also gives a lot of extra credit. He cares way more that you learn the content than anything else. He will give out extensions often if multiple people ask and is very understanding.

As others have stated, while Prof. Salloum is caring and will give extensions and is overall very passive, his ability to teach leaves some things desired. He definitely does know his stuff, but how well that information translates to the student depends on if you're willing to do the extra work and teach yourself in parallel to the lessons.

One of the most kind professors I have ever taken. Extremely empathetic and caring, offers extensions and office hours to fit your schedule, takes criticism well, and will genuinely appreciate if you teach him something. A very humble professor. The class itself isn't too bad, just make sure to stay on top of it and ask questions.

The class is ridiculously unorganized and talking to the professor just creates more questions. None of the rubrics are clear and he just adds things to projects/assignments during lectures. He tries to help but at the end of the day he comes off very rude and has a very entitled air to him. If possible, don't take him.

Salloum focuses on his Power-points instead of the textbook, making them seem random. The course is concept based but not hard to understand, but it gets dry quick. Apply the concepts yourself to practice. He provides ample time for review. Tests are usually based on homework. Do the extra credit. He means well, so try to work with him.

Lectures are boring and difficult to understand. He seems like he just picks up the lecture from whatever point he feels like and sometimes contradicts himself. Explains poorly, Tests and projects are pretty tricky but he lets you redo the projects as many times as you want for full points, and he's a pretty nice grader.

Not as bad as people say but not great. People don't like him because he makes a lot of mistakes, etc. You only learn a little, so learn databases and SQL on your own. However, he's a lenient grader and his assignments/tests aren't that hard. Two midterms were just SQL statements, final was database normalization, SQL statements, and ER diagram.

One of the worst CS professors. His tests online are impossible to finish in the amount of time and are extremely difficult. The final was impossible. He's not a good teacher at all (extremely hard to follow and doesn't explain things well). My entire class used online videos to teach themselves the concepts instead. Don't take this guy.

His class and what you gain from it is very average at best. Does not like to record lectures and post them, so you have to show up. If you focus on the homework assignments and put in a mild amount of effort, you should be alright. Lectures can be very boring. Take a look at MIPS before you take this and the course should be a little easier.

I would definitely avoid this prof if possible, but also he is not one of the worst professors I have had. The class is not too much work, but he has a student grader, and I felt like I lost points I should not have. If you complain about your grade it may get fixed, but you have to ask him to check it. He is a nice guy, but lectures can get boring

Made mistake taking his class twice. His knowledge is outdated. He should retire. His assignments are Joke. He doesn't grade well. Even though I performed really well in his class still gave me a 2nd grade. You cant maintain good performance in his class. Because you will definitely sleep. Make sure you don't take his class.

1/10. Avoid this professor! 1) His lectures involve him scrolling quickly through his PPT w/o actually teaching us. You then get tested on this via quizzes that are 45% of your grade 2) For our project, he cared more about diagrams & documentation rather than the program itself. He expects you to turn in a 100-page binder. No programming was taught
Easy. Lots of grade improvement opportunities. Graders mess up often. Final is difficult. You won't learn anything. If you fail, save your work. Funny to see how he moves. He's so strange.

This is probably the only class and prof that i learned anything from that helped me get a job later. You just need to know your data structures to get a job after college and you get to learn this backwards from Prof. Salloum... and thats all that matters.

Can be difficult to understand due to accent and lack of explanation. Homeworks/projects lack clear requirement, but grading is not strict. Notes are allowed on quizzes/tests. Would not be my first choice of teacher but would not mind taking for future classes.
Overall, not bad. A bit boring teaching method but you do learn the material well. I would prefer more clarifications through illustrations. Tests weren't that easy.
Class is incredibly easy, open book / open note tests. However, he's incredibly boring, and tends to assign labs using an obsolete program without explaining how to do it all.

Professor is very knowledgeable, and available outside of class. Rate of speed class goes at is fast. He marks you off most of a question in written exams for missing syntax details. Getting an A requires lots of experimentation with the programming systems outside of class. Share your goals with him and he will help you accomplish them

Professor is cool but when it comes to test there is little to no partial credit. The point distributions for the questions aren't even and one little mistake can be the difference between getting the full points for the question or getting 0. The class is lecture heavy mostly off the slides. He'll tell you whats on the tests but be ready to study.

Lectures are just him reading off slides which rarely help when doing the homework. Tests are extremely difficult and expect you to memorize/understand every little thing. Don't trust the good ratings. Last month of the course was awful he gave up on homework and expected us to learn everything from the slides, which were useless and complicated.

We have two exams plus a final and he said that he would give partial, but didn't. He releases students early out of class and says that we are behind schedule and rushed to teach some topics like C. Assignments are based on effort, while exams are graded on correctness. The correct answers for assignments aren't released. Nice guy, but not great.
Take him for 2600! Workload was very manageable, exams are relatively fair. Very nice professor and makes lectures enjoyable. He cares for his students and always encourages questions

Professor is very knowledgeable in the subject and knows what is important to learn for industry but is often irritable and impatient. Also goes off topic a lot. Definitely possible to get an A and learn from the class but I would advise another professor if given the opportunity.

Have very mixed feelings about him. He knows a quite a lot about unix and C programming. Explains interesting concepts at times. However, his assignments and exams are stressful. For a 2000 level course makes it feel like 3000 at times. He's not gonna teach here anymore tho. #packwatch

Funny and cool guy but ok professor. He teaches as if he's just reviewing material everyone is already familiar with, so you'll probably have to teach yourself. However, he is helpful and not too strict on grading from my experience, he wants everyone to pass.

Professor seems very knowledgable but often rushes through some material during class. Exams are difficult and he expects you to know a lot of things not taught during class. Also gives difficult problems on assignment that make you want to pull your hair out. Probably one of the worst CS professors I've had.

If you have prior programming experience with Java/C++, this class will be a breeze. Just make sure to follow instructions of assignments to the T because you may lose 10% on VERY LITTLE things. Must use VSC. Sometimes he's quite unprepared when coding to explain a concept, try to be patient with him, he's kind, but VERY STRICT with instructions.

Definitely attend his lectures, he gives a lot of information that's not on the slides and that you'll need for the projects. He's super knowledgeable about the subject he teaches. If you don't have prior programming experience you'll probably struggle in this class but you will learn a lot. Make sure you follow proper conventions in assignments.

Dom is pretty good and a nice guy. Two midterms and a final. Strict deadlines, expects you to study pretty hard if you don't have experience. Makes his own organized slides but expects you to go a little beyond them on your own. Know the *nix shell well, C programming (linked lists, pointers, even matrix multiplication), regular expressions.

Honestly, I was really scared coming into this class when reading his previous reviews. But, he is a really good prof. Knows his stuff and will help you 1000%. He is the first prof I went to office hrs for, and he will see ur trying. Really chill n easy to get along with. Wont judge you on ur questions. I ACTUALLY learned a lot from him. Very real.

CS4600 is an interesting class learned about the concepts used behind asymmetric, symmetric, digital sigs, hashes etc. I enjoyed the class many people did not since he did not upload slides. Attendance is required and you must write notes as well unless you share with a group. Also, listen and pay attention since his lecture contains a lot of info!

His lectures are good and he knows what he's talking about. There weren't too many projects, the tests were straightforward and correlated to his in-class reviews. He's also really friendly and funny, and I had problems with miscalculated grades but he always fixed it. I would recommend going to class regularly as he doesn't post slides online.

His class wasn't too hard, but I feel like I learned nothing useful. His lectures consisted of him explaining very broad overviews of complex subjects and drawing a bunch of diagrams. We did one project the whole semester, had a group presentation instead of a final, and tests were mostly like his lectures. Not hard, just felt like a waste of time.

Unless you have some previous exams, avoid at all costs. He will very lightly go over a complex problem then he will give a very different question on the topic. He also does not explain well during office hours since it feels like he was too tired all the time. Also, the tests were unfairly graded.

Pros: Has an amazing sense of humor Cons: His lectures are incredibly rushed and the slides he provides are incredibly bare-bones. He ignored my emails regarding points on a test question that I rightfully deserved. I managed to get an A and yet I feel like I've learned nothing. Due to the word limit I'll leave a detailed review on Koofers

A bit late in reviewing - just wanted to say he is a very helpful teacher and tries to be entertaining even though the subjects might be dull. He takes attendance through a Raspberry Pi setup, which is pretty cool. He is quite knowledgeable and is able to answer questions without trouble. The tests can be difficult if you don't study slides/book.

He is not a bad choice for 264. 5 projects total. He grades them very generously so dont worry if you cant get yours to work correctly. STUDY FOR THE TESTS. The midterm was mostly definitions and number system conversions. The final is very hard, we had 4 coding problems and 3 other kinds of problems that we had to do within the two hour time.

Pretty easy class. Made the assignments reasonable. For the tests, study the slides he posts on blackboard and watch a few videos on youtube to further understand the concepts. The lectures are pretty boring and he teaches until the end (but if you dont pay attention in the lectures it wont hurt you much so long as you read the slides later).

Good professor overall. We had 4 assignments and 1 project. Lectures are heavy but he makes it fun. Pay attention and use the book as a reference. Consider using online resources if needed make sure you understand and grasp the concepts do not simply CTRL+PASTE. Midterms and final have definitions/concepts/programs.

We have only a few (easy) homeworks, a midterm and a final. The midterm gets a full 8.5x11 sheet of paper, both sides. Finals gets 2 sheets. I got 100% on the midterm with no notes. He makes this class really easy. Highly recommend.
40% FINAL 20% HW 40% PROJECTS AND PRESENTATIONS bunch of homework, labs, projects, presentations, and exam is in person. he does not curve and said he will not curve

When doing the work pace yourself. It is a LOT of homework but the good thing is that it is all due at once and you'll know months in advance of when the due date is. You just have to worry about procrastination. My class met online the very first day of school and that was it, the class is very easy to pass but Professor is not easy to reach.

Pace yourself when doing the work for this class instead of procrastinating. Instructions from this professor were a bit unclear at times, but as long as you follow the syllabus and do all the work you will pass.

He is just a robot. Reads off slides. Its a 8-9:50pm class, so you can imagine how bad it is. His slides are outdated, his examples are boring. Teach yourself. He doesn't respond to questions well. He flips it on you. "Look at your book and the assignment, you will find your answer there".
Class was uber-easy. There is only class when there is an exam. Homework is fairly easy being that many students already utilize many Microsoft platforms. Easiest course I've ever taken.

Fall 2016 & Passed. CR/NO CR. EASY! Programs: Windows 10, Word, Powerpoint, Excel, & Access. Class: 5 trainings, 4 projects, & 5 exams. Only Projects(all programs except Windows 10) & exams(all) are GRADED. Excel & Access projects are difficult, so use your resources. Don't have Final if pass exams. U go to class once every 2 weeks for exams :)

He is the worst programming teacher I have ever had. He makes you hate this subject. Super hard Midterm and Final exam. His lectures are useless. He goes through some useless powerpoint slides. 70 percent of the class get an F on his exams. Avoid taking CIS 304 or any programming classes with Him.

CIS 101 is a pass/fail class. Just do the projects and trainings then go to class every other week to take a test on excel, word, powerpoint, access, and windows 10. 70%+ passes. Super easy class just don't get lazy. Sam Cengage (the program you have to buy) can tell if you're using another person's projects so don't even try many have been screwed

Professor is terrible at teaching. If you can avoid taking him, I would do so at all costs. He is not easily available unless you make an appointment with him beforehand. He does not grade fairly at all and gives off so much attitude when you try to ask him a simple question. He obviously does not respect his students and thinks he is above them.
pretty good choice for 3310, had review before exams that was basically exactly what was on the test. very nice and approachable

Really great choice for 3310. Nice & caring professor who made an effort to help students learn. Mostly lectured off the slides. Worked through exercises to make concepts easier to grasp. Fair midterms & graded leniently - curved too. Even dedicated a review class before each exam. Not a cakewalk but very doable with practice.

One of the easier profs but I dont think the quality of education was there. He wasnt good at explaining things and only covered HALF of the material we were supposed to. A strong foundational knowledge of DM is extremely important for cs which is why I am so disappointed. Take him if you want to pass. If you want to learn, take someone else.
not the best. reads off the slides and bad at explaining things. 8 homework and 3 midterms. midterms are similar to homework. allows notecard too.

He seems like a nice and genuine dude that wants you to pass. Although his lectures are boring, you will likely have to teach yourself. He makes up for this with his lenient grading. Exams are very fair as they reflect the material in the homework and review slides. He also allows a notecard. He's not a bad option in my opinion, take him.

Extremely nice professor and really lenient grading on exams and assignments. He gives plenty of time to finish coding assignments, but do not procrastinate. His lectures are kinda boring since he just reads off the slides. I recommend reading the textbook. Just wished there was more collaboration with other students in class.

Had him for CS1300. I had him this semester and his class was awesome. Lecture for most of the time, besides going over homework or past exams. He has 3 exams and lets you use a flashcard for the exams. Had 8 homework assignments. His grading scale is awesome. If you can understand basic concepts in relation to math take him!
He's a nice professor who wants to help and listen to students. His homework challenged me a bit but they end up helping me understand the material better.

Solid professor. One thing I liked is that he gives real world advice on how C++ is used, how to better your code, and career advice. He would often talk about the industry or his experiences which would always make the class a bit more interesting. He's a fair grader and lets you resubmit labs/projects if you get a 0 due to compilation errors.

Homework is too non specific, have to go and find out everything on your own. If the homework does not compile correctly for the grader, they will give you a 0 on that assignment. Even if the program compiles correctly for you WITH THE SAME INSTRUCTIONS.
He barely explains anything and has no care at all. He is way too old to be teaching this class still. His Exams are insane and there is no extra material outside class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

He stands in front of his notes half of the time and his handwriting is barely legible. If your not sitting upfront it's hard to note things down Homework is rare, which is a shame because the little homework he does give helps out for the tests. The lectures are really misguided and you pretty much have to learn on your own.

Lectures are very hard to follow and understand. He copies an example problem down from a piece of paper and does it on the board with no explanation. If you ask a question on the example hes's doing he will tell you to read the textbook or will give a very vague answer. Class often becomes time consuming since the professor does not always provide many examples or access to his slides when some aren't covered. The class' pacing is poor. The course doesn't have time appropriately distributed according to subject. To get the most out of this professor, ask questions immediately if you don't understand something.

Lectures are lengthy with not many example problems, but otherwise this professor cares for students. He will push back homework due dates if most students request it. Quite a few quizzes and tests, they are all open book/closed notes, and are pulled from examples or homework.

Prof.Ganapathy is pretty good and teaches well. If you don't understand something, going through Coburn's YT videos will assist as well. He's generally caring and makes sure that all students are able to submit their homework. He does do occasional quizzes, but as long as you understand the homework you'll be fine.

A very respectful, caring, and helpful professor, his lectures might feel lengthy and off the slides, but his class is quite easy otherwise. Make sure to attend or else you'll get a surprise quiz. HW can be due before exams. If you want to learn and pursue structures, take Dr. Coburn. If you want a easy grader and low workload, take Prof Ganapathy.

He is a prof who tends to just lecture. You have to work to follow along and pay attention, but even if you do, it's not easy to understand the material. I mean structures is a difficult concept overall, but you will not understand anything unless you read and watch Coburn's material (yt). Ganapathy for an "easier" pass, Coburn to learn.

Ganapathy is a super chill professor. If you are on top of the readings or lecture videos and do your homework before quizzes or exams you will very likely be fine. He is great in office hours and is happy to answer any question you have. Make sure to attend class, because he will give out pop quizzes if he notices students aren't showing up.
Professor's lectures can be a bit dry. If attendance is low he gives pop quizzes but typically with warning. Tests are like the homework and are open book.

Lectures aren't bad but they aren't posted online. If you didn't understand something, the book will have it. The book for this class is clear, conscious, and to the point, so its not a hard read unlike most textbooks. Professor is understanding if you need more time for hw. Tests aren't bad, very much like the homework. Some quizzes, not hard.

Great professor who can teach this subject to students as best as he can. Willing to explain concepts and solutions in depth if asked to clarify in class or during office hours. Expects us to know the material well enough for each exam. The whole material may be too much to get in a 1:15 hr lecture, so watching lecture videos is highly encouraged.
This professor is very understanding and if you need another day for an assignment, do not hesitate to ask. He genuinely wants you to do your best.

Essentially if you read the handbook and take notes you will do well. Tests reflect the material in the handbook and homework with some changes. Well designed course and this professor delivers it well. Most of the lecture is repeating what is in the videos/slides. Mostly be ready to take good notes because they come in very handy.

Compared to the other professors teaching this course, you will CERTAINLY have an easier time passing with Ganapathy. His tests are simple and taken from homework. He uses the same lectures slides and homework as Coburn. Overall good dude who knows what he's doing and will help you if you ask.
The professor is very knowledgeable when it comes to the material. Lectures can get dry at some parts but for the most part, he keeps you engaged.
The professor mostly just reads off of the lecture slides. If you understand the homework and the examples in the lecture then you can do well on the tests. Overall, he is an average professor.
He lectures pretty well and will answer any questions. The class is pretty straightforward if you do the homework accurately.

This class was one of the easier classes to understand, the professor made an effort constantly to make the class engaged with questions. Lectures and quizzes are pretty quick, not very much time to prepare between homework assignments and quizzes/tests.

The class subject is difficult. Its hard to get someone that can teach this proficiently. He reads of the lecture slide a majority of the time. Watching the lectures on youtube provides more information on the subject.

Ganapathy mostly reads off the lecture slides in class and occasionally goes into more detail when asked a question or for basic examples. You will probably have to review Coburn's lecture videos to get a better understanding of the material. Tests are open book and open note so they are not too difficult.

Professor Ganapathy is a part-time professor, and taught a night structures course in this case. Class setup (Powerpoints), HW, and tests all from another professor, Todd Coburn. Grading criteria is extremely clear, and you will do fine if you keep up with the homework/lectures. Ganapathy is an alright lecturer, and gets his points across clearly.

Lots of people imply that Ganapathy is a really poor lecturer, but I wouldn't say that's the case. He lectures pretty well for most topics in the class, there are a few which he isn't very clear on and you need to go watch Coburns videos but for the most part he's a decent lecturer, a fair grader, and very friendly.

I couldn't follow along with his lectures at all. When I'd try to ask questions or ask for more example problems he'd say we have no time. So I stopped listening to his lectures to just read the book and do the homework. He's nice enough to extend homework often, but gives pop quizzes for low attendance. Exams are open book usually.

Professor Ganapathy is a really nice person. He cares about what he teaches, however, his teaching method and style are not the best. His class is fairly easy compared to other professors that teach the same class, however, it will not fully prepare you for the second structures class.

Prof. Ganapathy is a nice guy! I'm sure he is a better professor when class isn't over zoom. This class moved at a very fast pace and the content used to teach us students was not his own, so his in depth knowledge of the material was at a minimum. If you are good at statics, you will be fine in this class if you need a lot of help don't take
You won't learn much, but he's an easy pass. In all honesty, just watch Prof Coburn's lectures on YouTube if you want to do well in 3271.

As a person, Ganapathy is really chill. He just wants you to try your best and understand the material. As a professor, he is not the greatest. Doesn't know the slides completely, mainly because they are Coburn's slides. Expect to see him reading off the screen and making mistakes here and there. If you can get Coburn, do it. If not, Ganapathy's ok

Professor Ganapathy is extremely passionate for what he does and he offers great advice in this class; it is necessary to stay on top of the workload as it is challenging, and since he reads directly off of the powerpoint slide. While he is great for asking questions during his office hours, it is necessary to do some prep-work before the class.
MINION PAPOI MUAK MUAK MUAK

Professor Mannion is a decent professor, however, his grading criteria can be unclear at times. He will take off points for things he never mentioned in class. He can also be quite insensitive at times (putting it generously) making comments that are completely inappropriate for an academic setting. He's not the worst option out there I guess.

He gives a lot of work for ME 1001L and I struggled a lot to keep up as someone new to solidworks. Our section was doing a lot more advanced work compared to other sections, which was good because I learned a lot, but I was also spending around 8-10 hours on homework a week. But, he's a very lenient grader, although slow.

Chill guy with easy class. Lectures can get boring but sometimes his jokes get everyone chuckling, even at 8AM on a Friday. Random, but gives good career and life advice. Homework can take a bit of time. Final group project modeling a real object with 40+ parts. Still shocked I made part of a nerf gun shell for that. Actually learned SolidWorks.
This guy is amazing, take him for anything you can. All I gotta say. Very approachable in class and a great guy to have a conversation with. Ask him his thoughts on daylight savings time!

Most chill professor on the planet. Labs aren't too tough to get through and really helps explain the concepts from controls. It's the fourth class I've taken him for and every class has been great. Please take if possible. Cheers!

Really chill dude. If your going to take a Solidworks class, do not take any other professor besides professor mannion. Dude knows his stuff, and is the best CAD prof on campus. Compared to the other classes, you will be set up for industry after taking this class. Great class and great professor.

Hilarious and amazing professor. Down to Earth dude who'll speak his mind on the school. I've never used SOLIDWORKS, but his lectures were very well structured and his HW was challenging but doable and never felt like busywork.

He really does care for people and he will always help you if you need it. He is very good at what he does, so at times it feels like if you ask him a question you should feel stupid for asking it, because he fixes the problem in a literal second. But good a teaching and the coursework that he assigned is fun to do, His T.A. grades a lot of thing

Had previous modeling experience which helped me, but this class maybe tougher if you are new. Time consuming but manageable. Finals is a group project, so it would be helpful to get to know some people in the class that you can rely on.

Very nice man, makes jokes and is not afraid of saying how he really feels about the school (ask him about how much he makes). Grades nicely, you will get an A from doing the work, make sure you get a good group. The final lab is hard but passable, he also is very willing to help if you ask.

Really nice prof. This class gave me a run for my money just because of tech issues, but I made it through in one piece. Really great lectures and does care. Felt a little bad for him because it was mostly first-term freshman class so he was cracking jokes to a nearly silent room. Take him! You won't regret it.

He will easily be one of your favorite professors. His lectures are engaging and teach you the core concepts, and he's extremely willing to help students with any questions--whether it be related to the class, or the major in general. You can tell he wants you to succeed. And he's got a great sense of humor to top it off.

Professor Mannion is extremely helpful and funny. His lectures are not long at all and he explains them in a very easy way to understand. He is also a light grader and tells you exactly how to do each assignment.
Man has more chill than a disabled diglett on route 2

Great professor, very chill and really good at giving feedback. His class is not too difficult except for a big group work final project, so just make sure you get together a good group. Very lenient on grading and deadlines. If you can take him I highly recommend taking him.

10/10. Makes the labs fun and easy to do. He walks around during the lab to answer questions and provides feedback. Just a chill professor to have, he is easy to talk to and creates a good environment in the lab.

Went in with sketchy matlab skills and even with that this class was fun. I really enjoyed the way he related the experimental and simulation trials that were tested throughout the semester. Tied the lab work to the lecture portion of the class very well

He is a great professor. I took him for ME 1001L which is basically a introduction to SolidWorks. if you're taking the class online, he posts the lectures on youtube. I was new to solidworks so I did struggle in the first 2 or 3 weeks, but once you understand SW, the class gets a lot easier. There is one midterm project and one final project.

Great professor and made the most of the half online, half in person aspect of this class. He really tries hard to make a thermo-fluids lab that is generally pretty boring fun and interseting for the students

He was great. I went into this class knowing nothing about solidworks but, he was a great professor. He explained things well and is a very understanding guy. I added the class 3 weeks late and he gave me plenty of time to catch up and was very helpful.

Probably an easier course online than in person. Lab reports are very straightforward and the data is typically not hard to wrap your head around. He is not a strict grader as long as you're not extremely lazy while writing the reports. Gives great feedback when asked questions

Mannion is a relatively chill lab professor. He can grade pretty harsh if you are really lazy on your lab report, but otherwise is very fair and doesn't nitpick super minor details like other professors. He is happy to help you if you ask for help on any troubles you have for the lab whether it be in the classroom or email. I recommend him!

Young dude that is really good at explaining the intricacies of SolidWorks. I went into the class with prior exp. and still learned. Its honestly a lot of work in the software especially for the midterm. I highly recommend spacing out your work and not waiting till the last minute because modeling correctly with the exact requirements takes time

A really cool guy. Fun to talk to. Will give his thoughts on life and scenarios regarding the class material. If you are unclear about anything just ask! You will do bad on the first report but if you listen to his feedback you will do good on the rest of them. Quizzes contain a free response math question so review strengths for those.

I like Mannion as a person, but he tests us before every quiz, and he is a pretty harsh grader on the labs. sometimes we would go to his office hours, ask him what we need to do, and he would just kinda be like vague, then give us a 50% on the lab and make us redo it.... like if were coming to you with questions just help us out the first time!

Nice and young professor, he's patient and willing to sit with you for as long as he can to make sure you understand the logic behind coding. The final seems overkill, but he curved in the end (I think).

Mannion is funny, he has no filter and he seems like he just graduated college so he gets a lot of the bs. I already knew the content going into the class but he covered all the stuff that will actually help you not just tick off boxes. Fun to go to class, and you'll probably never be there the full three hours.

He is super chill. Took him for the statics lab since I am an ME. He gives homework and quiz every week that is take home. The practice final exam was challenging but not tough. He is super straightforward with grading and lecturing. He lectures for at most one hour and the rest of class is to work on the hw. Truly is caring and approachable.

Patrick is a really cool guy. Really down to earth and easy to talk to. He seems a little new to teaching but he does know his stuff. Hes very helpful with any questions in class or office hours. His classes dont have very serious feel to them though

I think he is a brand new prof since I couldn't find any reviews on him prior to registering. He is a great professor. All you do is solidworks. He has weekly quizzes and you pretty much follow instructions out of the solidworks book during the lab. Its a lecture/lab combo so you have to be in the same section and prof for both. Take him, good prof

Coburn's a very entertaining and passionate guy, fun to listen to. Steady flow of homework, typically for each two-lecture week there will be 2-3 assignments. Wonderful playlist for each course on his YouTube channel, which he updates regularly. Quiz nearly every class. Read up on Statics and 3261. Do your best not to fall behind!
Amazing lecturer, does a great job at teaching the course material. Can be a harsh grader when it comes to exams but he is very clear with his expectations and accessible when you need help.
Fair in his grading, unrelenting in his homework and quizzes so if you are not on top of work in this class it is easy to get overwhelmed.

He's great at teaching structures. Goes on unrelated rants a lot but it makes the class fun. Pretend to be offended for more extra credit lol. Only sometimes will his rants cause him to rush through lecture and miss some important details needed for the homework but just watch his YouTube videos or go to office hours and you'll be fine.
High quality lecture videos and textbook that match his in person lectures 1:1 which helps review topics you don't get the first time. Tough class but I learned a lot.
High quality video lectures and textbook that match 1:1 with his in-person lectures which makes it super easy to follow at home and review what I didn't understand. Tough class but I learned a lot.

The professor can be a tough grader, but it's because he cares. He is also available during office hours. His teaching has been among the best at this school. I wish I had taken him for Statics and ARO 3261. His passion for teaching is evident.

He is a tough grader and you have to stay on top of the class. The amount of time you study will show on test scores. Always a line at office ours and they are not very long. The required text book is poor quality and falling apart.

Dr. Coburn is a very good lecturer, he does his best to teach the concepts as simply as possible; he also records and posts lectures on his YouTube to rewatch if needed. He is a somewhat tough grader in terms of notation and detail, but it's manageable once understood. There are quizzes every class. He also has a strong personality but good intent.

Amazing professor, provides lots of insight into the Aerospace industry. Wants you to succeed but makes you work really hard. Expect a quiz every lecture and expect to be tested to your critical stress level... had too. Great professor would take again.

I'm going to mention two out of three things you can clearly perceive from him. - He really knows the material and concepts he is teaching. Almost no question you have will stay without answer. -By improving the in class and homework activities he clearly cares about students success and improving his teaching style. Get ready for overtime!

I am rating Professor Jonathan Nguyen, who is also teaching this class but is using Dr. Coburn's textbook and homework. Overall, the class is taught pretty well, and Professor Nguyen answers any questions we have. He also explains examples well. Dr. Coburn's YouTube channel is definitely a useful supplement to the class as well.

I definitely feel like there's too much homework (not a full week to complete them. And no I'm not being a pansy). But Dr Coburn is such a nice guy and loves what he's doing. He's clear of what he expects from you and his tests aren't horrible. His textbook is really helpful too. If you end up taking another professor, Coburns YT vids will help.

Overall most interesting class I have taken so far at cpp topics can get quite confusing but having the textbook and reviewing the professors youtube channel really helps. Lots of homework and can be overwhelming sometimes but practice makes perfect.

In order to do well in the class you really have to pay attention and do the homework, Coburn gives you a lot of resources that you need to take advantage of. He is a tough grader but very fair when it comes to the material that he expects you to know. Also, don't be afraid to ask questions or go to his office hours, he is very helpful.

Great lectures, really good at explaining things intuitively. He also wrote the textbook and does in-depth youtube lectures. Be careful to read the syllabus so that you don't get negative points on anything! Lots of homework, it's tedious but you end up learning the material. He lectures fast, so read or skim over the book ahead of time.
pretty cool guy

To get a good grade in the class you really have to understand the homework. I don't know any other professor that uses his free time to create study material for students. Watch his Youtube lectures, read the book, take good notes and you'll pass. Its a very demanding class but you will get the most out of it.

Professor Coburn is honestly one of the best and most engaging professors I've ever taken. He's very nitpicky with work, and its for good reason. Once you get used to it, it becomes really good work habits. It might seem like a lot at times, but all the work that we are assigned really pays off for understanding the mechanics of structures.

Coburn is a brilliant engineer with a plethora of knowledge to share with his students. He genuinely wants the best for all and works hard to give them the best education he can, but he expects the same level of work from his students. There are a lot of points to be made so utilize them well. Grading is rigorous, be vigilant. Don't freak out.

Professor Coburn is an amazing professor who cares about his students' success. He explains the concepts fairly well, and for whatever the student does not understand, Professor Coburn posts YouTube videos for students to review. He's funny, keeps the students engaged throughout the lecture time, and is knowledgeable in his area.

Coburn is strict but only in the way that he wants students to excel and succeed not only in his class, but in future classes and careers. He is funny and plenty loud enough to be able to wake up in the mornings. The lectures are explained extremely well. The only problem I have had is with online communication.

Dr. Coburn does a great job of covering and explaining topics. The textbook does a good job of going over topics in greater detail. Lectures are energetic and enthusiastic but often go over time. Quizzes at the beginning of almost every class are easy if you know statics and content from previous lectures.

Obviously puts in lots of time to support students and ensure they learn content well. Explains concepts very well. Homework heavy class but topics are explained very well. All lectures are also posted on YouTube and the handbook (written by Coburn) aligns perfectly with the class.
A great teacher and professor with some funny quirks and moments. A rough grader with a lot of emphasis on key points, pay attention to what he iterates on and you'll be fine.

Dr. Coburn's class is a mixture of pain and fun. His lectures are hilarious and packed with valuable information and insights. His classes are rarely easy, but always worth the hard work. If you do the work and commit to the material you will come out industry ready. Dr. Coburn makes mistakes but cares about his students.

Dr. Coburn brings a lot of passion to his lectures and will inspire you to complete your work! Completing the homework and preparing for pop quizzes will absolutely prepare you for the exams. His grading criteria is very clear and his syllabus is clear as well (schedule, HW, exams, etc.) He will keep you on your toes, so stay ahead!

This is easily the most challenging class I have taken. The lectures are organized, the book is clear, and the subject is hard, but Dr Coburn is there to help. Beware, you will pay for easy mistakes. Double-check and triple-check your work! So far I have learned a lot from Dr Coburns classes and I hope to learn much more!
One of the best lectures I have taken. He makes the class interesting and makes the content easy to digest.

Prof. Coburn cares immensely about the student's experience in his class, and it shows in every aspect imaginable. His handbook is simple to understand, he explains concepts using simple analogies, he rewards student's extra effort to understand material with extra credit, and he makes time to get your questions answered during office hours.

I haven't taken his classes ever before and am enjoying the lectures as well as the materials covered. I am not an ARO student but Dr. Coburn was pretty eager to give me an add code to enroll in the course and I'm not regretting it!

Dr. Coburn is a wonderful professor and great role model. He is a tough professor, not out of meanness, but because he wants you to become the best engineer you can be. Engineering should be hard, and should be done correctly, and these are values that Coburn teaches well. His lectures are entertaining, and his textbook is clear and easy to read.

Professor Coburn is a great professor! He is very passionate and energetic in his lectures. He is a tough but fair grader. I wished I could have taken him for ARO3261 and 3271. He is very glad to help his students in understanding the material and is very accessible outside of class times.

Professor Coburn is a very interesting professor. He makes things as simple as possible, and the lecture is very dynamic. I was a little hesitant to choose this course when I read all the reviews that said it was very hard and a lot of work, but I'm not regretting taking this class (for now). Also, professor Coburn's anecdotes are great!

Coburn is a tough professor but he cares about how well his students are understanding the material. Composites is a hard subject, but you can trust Coburn to make it as simple as possible. Best professor I've ever had, everyone should take him but be prepared to put in the work. Ask questions, go to office hours, email him... he wants to help you.

Professor Coburn is a great professor. His class is challenging but he pushes you to become a great engineer. He really simplifies the material and the quizzes really help keep you in check. Overall, composites is a fun subject and he is very knowledgeable about it. This class is early but he will definitely wake you up to start your morning right.

Professor Coburn is one of the best at Cal Poly Pomona. His class is tough, but he pushes students to become great engineers. The workload is heavy, and the material is challenging, but he teaches clearly and uses the best textbook for real-world application. If you're willing to work hard, take himyou won't regret it.

Coburn is an amazing lecturer and knows his stuff! He keeps the class entertained with his funny stories while also having the ability to quickly redirect back to the topic of the lecture. His simplification of the material coupled with his textbook makes this class fairly understandable and easy to follow.

One of the best Aerospace professors at CPP, without a doubt. Coburn's teaching style may not be for the light-hearted, but he really prepares you for the real world in the aerospace industry. Be prepared to get humbled, but in an encouraging and supportive way.

Coburn may be a bit of a tough (but fair) grader, if you want to really learn the subject and prepare yourself for the aerospace structures industry, he is the professor to take. Do the homework, annotate his book, ask questions when you are confused, and you will pass the class. Also, be ready for lots of lively in-class stories!
Top-notch teaching skills and technical knowledge. His classes are tough but he'll make you a better engineer. Take his class.

Dr. Coburn's class can be challenging but that makes it worth working through. His quizzes are frequent and his tests can be long but they are not unfair. If a student reads the textbook and takes time to practice they should not fail. Ultimately I think a student who puts in the work will come out stronger than they would with an easier professor.

He literally had part of the homework assignment be to go grade him after he got super upset someone left a bad rating. It's not that deep. And all these reviews started flooding in after that. Hes hard but passionate so I give it to him for care, everyone is a "pansy" (his words) for not going after it on homework assignments that take 8-12 hours.

Professor Coburn genuinely cares about the success of his students and that is very apparent in every lecture. You must put in the time/work for this class to succeed. You will leave feeling like you learned and earned your grade.

The professor is a good and interesting lecturer, he often goes over time but I usually don't care cause he gives extra credit for going over time. Even if he didn't, he's interesting enough that I'm engaged with the material. I gave him average difficulty because I've taken this professor too many times and I've grown numb to his difficulty.

Coburn is a great lecturer, and he gives extra credit often for participating in class or staying on top of your work. He gives quizzes almost every class and can be a tough grader when it comes to missing small details on quizzes or tests. Overall, he cares about his students, and you will succeed if you keep up with all the homework he gives.

The class and content can be difficult, but as long as you do the homework and attend class genuinely, you will succeed in this class. Professor Coburn is an amazing professor that will set you up for success, you will be doing yourself a disservice if you were to avoid taking him.
Tough class but you will definitely learn the material!

Professor Coburn can be viewed as a tough grader, but in truth his grading is fair and encourages you to really learn the material rather than fumbling through the class. If you enjoy structures, Coburn is the right professor for you and the difficulty is worth it for the knowledge you will receive.

Keeps you awake during class. If you want to discuss the HW during office hours he tends to be hasty in his feedback the later you arrive in his office hours. Expect a line at his OH. Gives extra-credit for corrections on HW/tests/book/lecture slides, useful participation in class, and for fastest completed (correctly) exams/quizzes.
Tallest guy in aero department

This is a Professor that will make you work and prove yourself in his classes. This is my third class I have taken with him, and every time I am glad I did. He is truly one of the best professors you can take because he truly cares about his students learning experience and wants success first in our education. Take if you want to learn.

FEA is my 3rd class with this professor. If you take the time to do the homework and understand the process for each problem then you will be fine. Don't just copy answers. Compared to his other classes, FEA has the most confusion as he uses a 3rd party textbook causing some differences in nomenclature between the lectures and the equations.

This is my second course with Coburn. The class is really straight forward and following along with the two textbooks really helps. Along as you honestly complete the homework and attend class, you will definitely pass.

Coburn is a tough professor but he is very knowledgeable and willing to help students who put in the effort. If you don't do the homework, you won't pass the class since tests are very similar to the homework. Take Coburn if you WANT to learn, take another professor if you want to pass. He cares and wants future graduates to be great engineers.
He is the lord of structures in the department

He's a great professor who knows what he is talking about. His class is always fun to be a part of, and he is great at teaching the material to his students. If you had to take a morning class, his class is worth waking up early for.

Great professor, really ensures that you earn your grade and understand the material. Heavy HW class, which gets rewarded if you are diligent. If you want to succeed, pay attention in the lectures, and supplement with the books/YT videos. Comprehensive NASTRAN primer that simplifies FEA. Plenty of resources to make sure you learn FEA very well.

He grades quizzes same day and tests within a few days. He goes over them in class. He has many resources available: a YouTube channel, his website, even audio files. He offers extra credit to balance out his harsh grading. If you can't wake up early don't take this class. A passing grade means you know more than A students with other professors.

This is an amazing class with a professor who provides the resources to learn the material in the best way possible. This class is demanding, so I would suggest taking this class when you have the time to focus on it. :)

Professor Coburn lectures very well and provides good online lectures for things not covered in class. Pop quizzes will make or ruin grades and midterms are graded based on answers rather than process. Overall lectures make Coburn worth it.

Dr. Coburn is a really good professor. He walks you through the lectures, he doesn't just read off of lecture slides. Does a really good job at explaining what each concept means in 3D space which is really helpful. Material definitely is not "easy" but teaches it in a way that makes it easy to understand for the most amount of people.

Dr. Coburn is a very effective lecturer. He is very engaging and knowledgeable with many years in industry. Loves to go on tangents but they make the class much more enjoyable. Lots of tests, but that means more chances to raise your grade after you inevitably fail the first few quizzes reviewing statics.

Professor Coburn has lecture videos on his youtube that were extremely useful to me, and without them I would be lost in this class. Everything coincides with what we learn in class and all of his resources are organized and easy to find. Class is difficult, but he is an easy grader for tests.

This professor is by far my favorite in all of university. He is very attentive to each student and so long as you put in the effort he will recognize that and that is something that he values for sure. He is always available to talk and he is easy to approach with anything. Problems at home/class, he is a great listener and gives great advice.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He really cares about his students' success, but he is a tough grader so you must be meticulous. Goes on tangents that aren't related to the class, and while funny and can keep you awake and engaged, it can make it a little hard to follow at times. Just make sure you would be okay with that teaching style.

This class is a prime example of how an Engineering class should be taught. Dr. Coburn also gives amazing lectures that are very understandable and digestible. On top of that, he is very accessible and willing to help students further in his office hours. For students who want to actually learn the material, you should take Dr. Coburn.

Dr. Coburn teaches in a way that is simple and easy at every step, until you take an exam and realize you've learned an entire section of structures analysis. He quizzes on small concepts, lectures on tools/equations to use, and combines it all in the HW after each class session. No one thing is difficult if you stay on top of things.

This Professor is a harsh grader, but you will learn from this course. He offers supplemental lessons online and his lectures are engaging.

Pay attention to homework concepts as and questions. Tell him you don't understand his answer if you really don't understand and he'll try to explain further. And especially review the shorter supplementary lectures on Youtube as they were uploaded after we bombed those test questions teehee :D

Pop quizzes!!! Normally worth 30% of grade. Graded by 5 exams and a final. Lots of homework. If you attend lectures and do the homework then the class should be doable. If you want to really learn, Coburn is you guy!

Coburn's class is a great experience; you're almost guaranteed to hear a tangent each lecture, but they're entertaining and he provides good resources to help with the subject. Professor Coburn is an expert at structures and his handbook and supplementary videos make concepts easy to understand. Be prepared for pop quizzes and do a lot of excel in this class.

Very consistent and structured class. If you follow along and integrate that mother you'll do fine.

Dr. Coburn is a highly skilled professional in Structural Mechanics and gets straight to the point with related tangents on the topic, along with being the author of the required textbook. Professor Coburn is a great teacher who really knows what he is talking about. A lot of content in this class but it's scheduled at a nice pace. Be ready to learn and always do the hw.

Very enthusiastic teacher. He grades hard and is very particular but he's a good teacher and you won't have a problem falling asleep in class bc of all the jokes

Prof. Coburn is a very engaging lecturer and has a ton of online resources if you didn't understand or need extra help on a section. In my honest opinion, I believe the professor has done a phenomenal job in making his students understand the concepts and material covered in this class. Coburn is a great professor although he can go on random tangents. However I still find his lecture very informational and fun to attend. If you're up for a challenge then take him! You'll definitely learn and grow better work ethics.

As energetic as a golden retriever on steroids, entertaining like your friend with ADHD, smarter than an IBM supercomputer from the future. Lecture never boring! A professor with an impressive discipline, always on top of his class. You stay on top of your pop-quizzes for they will kill your grade, they weight 30% of the overall grade.
