A challenging part about the online environment is that the grade is only based off of tests and quizzes, and there is no partial credit on quizzes.

Amazing Professor expects many things from you but only because he wants you to better yourself as a student. Test and quizzes are reflective of what is taught in the lectures. His handbook and lectures make the difficult material much easier to understand. Be ready to spend a good amount of time sitting down to understand the material.

Grading is tough, especially with online classes but going back to review your errors is critical as similar problems can/will come back in in future exams or quizzes. In the end, his grading helps you be more careful with your work. Overall, Professor Coburn is a great choice. Class is well organized and structured.

I had Coburn for structures 1 right before online and he was great. He gives tons of extra credit and homework feedback in addition to his lectures being super informative. But online in this class is super rough. The whole grade is half test half quizzes and they are graded off only the inputted answer. Basically no partial credit

Taking him online is rough. It's hard to get a good grade even if you learn the material, because he grades you on just your answer. He gave partial credit at the beginning but stopped. My BIGGEST advice is: DO THE HOMEWORK and really master it. If you know how to do the homework, you are good. Also, read the Beer & Johnson book. "Enjoy"

Professor Coburn was a great professor to have. He is the type of Professor that really wants you to understand the material, and will do so by allowing you to try and understand what's going on yourself before answering your question. His class is not boring, he likes to crack jokes and has an voice that won't make you lose focus

Coburn is an amazing professor that is passionate about his teachings and his work. While this is an elective class, be prepared for a lot of work. If you stay on top of it, this class can provide great intro experience to FE analysis.
Prof Coburn is a great person and the class isn't too bad, show up to his office hours to get questions answered. Would recommend if you really want to learn the material

I had the experience of taking Professor Coburn in person for ARO 3261, and then online for ARO 3271. In person he was one of my favorite professors and would recommend taking him. However, online was a slightly different story, as the only way you can reach him is through office hours since he doesn't reply to emails, and the grading is tough.

This man is good at his job. Listen and do the homework, and you will get the material. The reason I struggled was because we were online, and his office hours often get over crowded, but otherwise he is fantastic. Watch out for tests and quizzes though. There is no partial credit, so the smallest of mistakes will screw you like they did me.

He is an incredible professor who knows what he is talking about. The lectures were a little lacking for online but he does mention you should supplement the lectures with reading so i guess that's my fault for not reading. The test and office hours are at ridiculously early times but he is always fair and consistent. Overall great professor.

Prof. Coburn is a great professor because he wants you to learn the material. He will go hard on you if you ask for handouts, extra credit, and answers. He is a professor that will challenge you, and make you work for all of your grades. Great professor. Can't wait to take the rest of the classes he has to offer. Be ready to work.

took dis dood 3 times, 3 A's like MJ in 96. Lowkey kinda a lot of stuff but he doesn't really read any of it. Never go to office hours bc its full of noobz who all ask the same question. b ready 2 wake @ 5:30am for dis mans tests n quizzes bc he is only awake at ungodly hours. Lowkey been slackin since were online

Tough grader, but fair and consistent. Expects you to be fairly intuitive, and put in work on your own time to fully understand the material. Doesn't hold your hand and spoon feed answers, you'll definitely have to learn if you want to pass.

He really knows what he is talking about. It will be a hard class to pass but not as much as structures 1. If you go to office hour he might roast you for not knowing something, but at least when you get out you will really know it. Watch out for his wording in quizzes and tests. Do the hw several times, this way you wont have any trouble in tests.

Dr. Coburn will make sure you know your stuff. Homework load is pretty heavy, but is manageable if you chip away at it and is key to success in the class. He will not respond to emails, you have to ask in office hours. The grade is based only on quizzes and tests and partial credit is hard to come by. DO NOT FALL BEHIND & BE PREPARED TO GRIND.

Professor Coburn is an excellent teacher, and he knows the material very well. His class is not easy, but you will definitely learn. During Covid, the lectures are videos posted every week that are informative and to the point. The tests and quizzes will be a breeze if you pay attention and do the homework.

Professor Coburn is excellent and knows his material very well. The main drawback is that it is an online class where your grade only relies on tests and quizzes which he does not give partial credit for. Other than that, the effort you give is what grade you will get.

Overall, a good professor. Though the semester was fully online, the video lectures do help to an extent. I just wish there were more supplementary lectures to help with examples and the homework, besides the limited office hours. STRESS A lot of it is learn by doing the work. He can be uncompromising with partial credit, but fair if you deserve it

Study your notes and the handbook before class to succeed. There is a huge amount of material to go over and if you start to slack there is no coming back. That being said, quizzes and tests are very straight forward, plug-and-chug style problems after you have identified the key figures.

Dr. Coburn is a great lecturer and I think he would be even better in person. As difficult as this class is, it was still very interesting. The main drawbacks in the online version of this class are getting little to no partial credit and having your grade based solely on tests & quizzes. Do AND understand all of the homework. Go to SI sessions.

Professor Coburn is really great structures professor. He knows a lot of structures and has worked hard to simplify it and make it easier for students. However, his class does require you to invest a lot of time to master the subject and will need to complete all homework in order to pass his quizzes and exams.

Professor Coburn presents the material in lecture in a straightforward manor and is easy to follow. However the material is technically challenging and no partial credit is given for the weekly quizzes. I wish I would have been able to take this class in person, I feel that I would have a better understanding of the material.

I have taken Dr. Coburn for ARO 3261 & 3271. He is one of the best professors in the ARO department and is very strong in the field of structures. Both of the classes can be a bit heavy on homework at times but all problems help to reinforce concepts in class. He is a bit of a tough grader and really makes you work for your grade.

Proffesor Coburn can be a great teacher but online classes proved to be quite difficult with him. While he does have office hours his office hour include all his classes so it can be difficult to get a thorough answer. The class relies entirely on tests and quizzes. Do all the homework and take notes on his online lectures.

Hard class but knows his stuff and wrote the books for all the structures classes that make the material several magnitudes easier to understand. the book for 3261 is a lot more comprehensive however, with the 3271 book being a little less helpful.

Since everything is now online, I haven't had to chance to sit in his class physically. He's a very knowledgeable Professor that knows his stuff, but if you have questions about the material you MUST show up for office hours. Do not expect a return email. Lectures are via YouTube recordings. No Asynchronous lectures. DO NOT FALL BEHIDE

I took Professor Coburn for the entire Structures Series and in all honesty, it's the field I feel the most prepared now that I'm entering the workforce. It's impossible to do well in this class without spending plenty of time reviewing and mastering the lectures and handbook. I highly recommend developing your own excel spreadsheets for the HW.

Never responds to emails. Office hours are a joke you have to fight your way through a dozen students to get in a question and he answers with a unrelated tangent. Zero partial credit. If your answers aren't his you get a 0%. The tests, quizzes, HW's and handbook are littered with errors. There are hard professors and bad ones. He chose to be both.

Todd Coburn is by far one of the best professors I have had at Cal Poly. His lectures are very engaging (for the most part even online even though they are pre-recorded), but he is very accessible during office hours and will stay on until there are no more questions left. His tests are quite hard but you will learn A LOT in the class.

Dr Coburn is a great professor. If you take his class you can expect to learn whatever he is teaching. The exams and quizzes are straight forward, for the most part. However the exams and quizzes can be graded harshly, especially in the online environment. There is little room for partial credit. If available I highly recommend attending SI session

Coburn is passionate about what he teaches and makes genuine strides to ensure his students obtain lasting knowledge. He is a tough grader; no partial credit for Blackboard quizzes or tests and your grade is entirely tests and quizzes (COVID Semester). He can be very intimidating and blunt at times. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. DO THE HW. ASK QUESTIONS.

I've taken Professor Coburn for all of my structures series offered at Cal poly Pomona and I can honestly say that among all of the aero curriculum, I feel most confident entering the workforce in structures vs anything else. He is a tough grader but you will defiantly learn. Make sure to absolutely do the hw and you will be alright. Ask alot of q

Incredibly difficult class, but Dr. Coburn does a very good job teaching and organizing the enormous amount of material to learn. One thing I didn't like was how he doesn't give typically give partial credit for Blackboard quizzes and tests, which sucks because questions are tedious and you can easily lose all credit for making one small error.

Coburn is a prof who is very passionate about what he teaches and knows it well. This class will literally kill you, but it makes you a better engineer. You get out of the class what you put in so go to office hours and ask questions on everything. Although, the quality of lectures could be better. Be prepared to put in the work you need to pass.

(during covid-19)This professor is very detailed in his work, and provides alot of info to his students in his lecture videos as well as the handy handbooks he published. He doesnt like to respond to emails, and tells you to attend zoom office hours. the online test are difficult since its given early in the morning, partial credit given is limited

I enjoy professor Coburn. However avoid this class at all cost. You're only graded on tests and quizzes with no partial. He tries to help but its limited time per student since his office consists of 15 people asking 15 different things. If you take this class DO NOT take it with other hard classes it takes up too much time. Good luck an email back

Get to know him he's a really cool guy. With that being said for the love of God avoid taking him if you can. If you get even a C in his class it's the equivalent of getting a doctorate that's how hard his class is. Their is little to no mercy in his class on exams and quizzes, and you literally have to know every detail in the class to get a C.

Coburn has a good lecturing style and well-made videos. The course introduces a lot of topics at a fast pace. Be sure to keep up with all the new lectures and finish the homework on time. Coburn has high standards for tests and quizzes--there is no partial credit for wrong answers in this online format. Overall, a challenging course.

Class was overall fine. Lectures on Youtube. Very minimal partial credit if any which I feel is unfair for an online course graded as 50% quiz 50% tests. No homework grade for an extra buffer. Learned the most out of any class this sem, feel grade doesn't reflect my knowledge. O.H. very frustrating at times as he helps 3 classes at once.
This is my first time taking a course with Professor Coburn, and so far he is the best professor I've had since beginning my college career. You'll really learn in his class.

He is a very tough grader in the virtual environment. For tests and quizzes, once you submit one answer you can not go back and change it! For some tests and quizzes, he will give partial credit and for some, if you make a mistake you get a zero! He genuinely cares about the success of his students. If you are neat and diligent you will do fine.

Professor Coburn is one of the Most Professional, and Most Passionate Professor's that I know. He drills you to work harder because it will pay off in the end. This class requires a lot of reading and a lot of studying. It is a lot of information to retain so best to start early.
Coburn cares a lot about the subject and a lot about the students. If you go out of your way to ask for help, he will go above and beyond to help you out.

Coburn is a challenging prof and can teach you a lot if you are willing to put in the work. I have taken him for 3 classes and this last semester which was online it seems like the effort put into teaching has drop significantly (tbf he used to put an insane amount). Be warned he now gives no partial cred, but a lot of time which I prefer.

I think i will always remember professor Coburn, not only because I had to retake his class, but because no one has taught me any subject the way Coburn does. I mean the guys a God of Structures and he knows everything about the subject. He cares about his students thats why he will let you fail 10 times just so you learn and understand his lecture
Do your hw and understand mistakes on quizes and youll be fine.

I have taken Professor Coburn for ARO 3261 and ARO3271 (Structural Mechanics 1 and 2). His lectures are very engaging and fun, and the material is top-notch. The course is homework, test, and quiz heavy but is structured very well. It is a difficult course as the material in-depth, but you will surely be a stand-out structural engineer afterwards.

For this class, you need a TI-Nspire or equivalent. Matrix heavy problems. Not difficult, but tedious. Lots of homework that you need to keep up with or else quizzes/exams are more difficult (BUT its not collected usually). There is a total of 10 Projects. Expect projects t be collected weekly, quizzes weekly, and 5 exams.

The class was amazing. Taught step by step. However, this online class makes it less interactive, and Professor Coburn is hard to be reached sometimes. This class requires you to be diligent and pay attention to details. He really prepares you for real life work. I wish he'd explain more on practical usage of FEA and design. More office hoursneeded

Structures II isn't a difficult class to understand as long as you complete every HW. For Coburn you need to buy his handbook or you will not do well on the HW/tests/Quizzes. The class is very HW heavy so make sure you don't cram. I took his class during COVID and he did not give partial credit on tests/quizzes so dont rely on partial credit.

Dr. Coburn clearly walks you through the basics of Finite Element Analysis, providing you a solid foundation for the more difficult projects and homework throughout the semester. The course was very organized and the lectures were very clear and concise. You will learn a lot if you put in the work.

This is an awesome professor with a great sense of humor, BUT as a virtual class, its a disaster because he doesnt give us partial credit on quizzes and some of the tests. This is essential for math and engineering so we can LEARN the concepts. I feel cheated because of this. I hope he grades on a curve; its the least he can do!!

Hard grader but makes you understand the information. He has created some very good video lectures for Covid-19 and has probably done the best at adapting an in person class to an online environment. Office hours are shared between all his classes but he will stay as long as is needed sometimes upwards of 5 hours. Solid professor be ready to learn.

Professor Coburn is a classic engineering professor. He is tough but fair, and expects all of his students to put in the work to master the material by themselves. During COVID he has become less accessible since his lectures on Youtube, and his office hours are very early in the morning, but he will answer any and all questions you have.

DO THE HOMEWORK! Expect homework and quizzes every week. As long as you master the homework and view all his lectures you should be able to pass. However if you want a high grade expect to spend hours reviewing homework, slides. Also make sure to double check all your work for tests since they are online and partial credit is hard to be assigned.

This was during Covid-19 Pandemic (asynchronous classes). Coburn really stresses the fundamental concepts of Structures. The video lectures are really well structured. The homework is not required but doing and understanding them is the key to mastering this course. My only issue is that office hours at 7 am and he doesn't respond to emails.

Students did not choose to be in the pandemic and professors are expected to help students at this particularly tough time and not torture them. Coburn is a great professor but his class is nearly impossible to do well in mainly because you have no way to make up for a bad quiz/test. Also you'll have to be up at 5am for exams. no points for Hw also

I've learned the most from this class out of all others so far in my degree, but one error will result in 0 points; it's an all or nothing on quizzes and exams. If you want to learn the subject well, take him, but be prepared to retake it in the future. I know I'm retaking it XD.

So Dr. Coburn, is a very interesting guy. In person he is amazing to talk to, is really engaging and does care that his students are learning. But he is an extremely hard grader. And he is not afraid to fail 60% of his class . This class is probably one of the most intense ones out there for Aerospace. Study all the time with trusted friends!

(COVID CLASS) Get ready to be up for 7 am office hours which are ridiculous. His lectures are all youtube videos with like no examples so the hw is really hard to do and worth no points. Very little partial credit on quizzes and tests. If he responds to an email, its a miracle. I took Wotring for 3261 and should have taken him again.

Aerospace Engineering at this school is known for following the motto "weed out the weak". Although extremely unfortunately, this professor is an echo chamber for that motto. He is the peak structures analyst everywhere he has operated, and because of this he is disconnected from the normal person's reality. You learn it instantly or not at all.

Dr. Coburn is a great professor, although I never had the chance to communicate with him in person and gauge his personality but people say he was good pre-Covid but if you take him online for 3271 you are bound to hit a wall. No partial credit, no homework points, no mercy. Probably the least forgiving dude I know. Get ready to struggle.

Dr. Coburn, from the get-go, says you can only pass if you do the work, pay attention, and study. You will have to work for your grade, but what you learn and the abilities you pick up in the class are invaluable and sets up a strong foundation for further structures/solids courses. This class is for those who want to master the material.

Took Professor Coburn online and he is one the best structures professors, but that being said he does have his faults. Lots of "optional" homework which will keep you on your toes. Exams are 50% of your grade while Quizzes are the other 50%. Communicating with him is extremely tough since he doesn't respond to emails :(

5 tests, 9 projects, 1 final project (no final exam), 1-2 homework assignments per week. The lectures were recorded in advance and posted online; typically less than 40 minutes. Textbook was occasionally useful. Easier than 3271/3261. Extremely well organized, the schedule was available from day one. Plenty of time to get the work done.

(COVID REVIEW) This has been the only class I have taken thus far that feels truly like a college level course. Up until now, I have always felt that college was just high school plus. Your only saving grace to do well in this class is a true passion for structures. This class will truly test to see if you are ready to pursue structures as a career

Took Professor Coburn Online, although his lectures were pre-recorded, they were still concise and easy to follow if you are up to date with the course content. Don't take professor Coburn if you aren't detailed and careful with your work.

Makes the class what you would think a typical online class would be with blackboard test and quizzes. Only thing I don't like is that it is hard to get partial credit since there is no way to show work

The worst experience at Cal Poly so far. Can never reach him through e-mail, have to go to his office hours at 7am, which combine students from all classes he teaches. Treats students poorly, barely gives any partial credit. Uses prerecorded YouTube lectures which are barely half of what supposed to be class length, never solves example problems

Coburn was a good professor in-person. However, once online classes began, the quality of his teaching and the course went down. Grading was based on 50% test and 50% quizzes, and he rarely gives partial credit on either. In office hours he would rarely answer your question directly, and when he did, it was accompanied by a 10 min unrelated story.

This is my 2nd class with Coburn. He is very intelligent, but his class is time consuming. 3271 is easier than 3261. The COVID version of this class makes section irrelevant, you will wake up at 6 am for quiz/tests regardless. Grades are quizzes and tests ONLY. Make and use excel spreadsheets. It will probably be different not online (post covid).

Preface, this review is during the pandemic ,online only. Dr Coburn is an amazing professor in-person. This semester was the first semester fully taken online and some of Dr Coburns lectures were IMO subpar from his usual quality. He was harder to reach via email, and his tests were unforgiving to small errors. Triple-check/quadruple check work!

Coburn is a good prof. I had him for 3261, 3271, & 4080. I credit him for getting me to a place where I was able to fend off the most difficult technical interviewers. His FEA class or any of his classes are only for those who have a passion for structures, if you do.. this is where you need to be. It wont be easy or always fair.. this is the way.

Professor Coburn was a challenging professor for the Aerospace Structures series, so I knew what to expect when I took him for Finite Element Analysis. He is the most qualified professor in the department to teach this subject and I highly recommend him. Just be warned, you have to dedicate many hours to study and do homework like a full time job.

I have had Professor Coburn for Statics, Dynamics, Structures 1 and 2, and now FEA (I would have taken composites if he taught it my year). The reason I came back isn't the absurd amount of homework, but instead for the incredible teaching he gives to you. If you put in the time, you will come out knowing you can do just about anything.

Great professor, but do not expect to be babied at all. If you actually care for the class and put in the work you will learn a a lot. Homework is optional but if you do not do it, trust me you won't pass. Busy office hours so show up early. We had 5 tests, no final test, 9 projects, 1 final project, 2 homework assignments and a quiz per week :D

Only graded on tests and quizzes. Partial is rarely given. If you make one small error you WILL get a 0% on your exam because it did not match his. Tests and quizzes are question pools you can get an easy exam or a really hard one. Not representative of ones knowledge just luck. Good luck getting in a question in office hours with 20 other people.

Professor Coburn is an excellent professor. His lectures are engaging and helpful. The exams can be a little tricky because of the wording, which may be confusing at first. However, if you understand the homework and study, the tests should be easy. I had to switch to online due to covid; the tests were a little more tricky online imo.

He is a phenomenal professor but his 326 class will take a ton of your time. The most homework I've ever had for a class ( I have since graduated). You will definitely learn from. Ultimately I had to focus on other classes because this class took too much of my time. C & B students, don't take too many classes when you are taking Coburn.

Homework load is manageable as long as you chip away at it (Around 2-3 assignments (12 questions each)) Quizzes are fair and usually easy as long as you did your homework. Tests, you could study and be confident and still trip up on if you're shaky on the concepts. Coburn doesn't expect you to learn to copy a process but more understand it.

There is homework to turn in and a quiz to take nearly every class so be prepared. LEARN to do the homework and understand the material dont just complete it for credit. Exams are simple but errors are common so be careful. Professor can be intimidating but hes really there to help reach out if you dont understand it or else you wont pass.

He is a very knowledgeable professor who is always willing to help in his office hours. The handbook will be your bible. He wants to see his students succeed, but you won't pass if you don't try on the homework and study for the tests. There is a lot of hw. Do not be afraid of the quizzes! People will try to scare you, do the hw and you'll be fine.

Lectures, you will learn. Homework doesn't require too much time in comparison to other classes. I have a love/hate for his tests. Though each question is never tedious, the challenge comes when you have to apply your understanding of each concept to those questions. His grading, hack and slash. Small mistakes will cost you.

I'll keep it short. 2 hrs of hw a week. He is funny, has VERY engaging energy, genuinely believes he is there to teach you and that you are there wanting to learn, and is VERY knowledgeable. Issues? Theory, derivation, and intuition are thrown out the window. You will plug, chug, and assume (quite boldly I'd personally claim) every 3 seconds baby.

Dr. Coburn is hands down one of the best professors I have had. His energy and passion for this subject is incredible. He is engaging and you will never leave his class saying that was a dry lecture. However, he is not a prof you take for an easy A. He really wants to make sure that you understand the material, more profs should teach like he does!
Knows his stuff, but gives almost no partial credit on tests and quizzes. Quizzes are at the beginning if class so don't be late.

A great lecturer, helps many students understand the material and concepts through many short and quirky examples. He is also very approachable during office hours and will help you with any problem. Make sure you participate in class because you get extra credit if you do. If it were possible, I think that everybody should take Dr. Coburn's class.

You will fight, and cry, and study, and work hard, and put in toil and effort with all your heart just to walk out with a C-. It isn't fair how hard you have to work to get a C, for other classes, usually this level of hard work gets people an A, but Coburn is harsh on his grading, he expects everyone to be an expert at structures. Study like crazy

Great teacher and he really knows his stuff. Gives industry insiders and has entertaining lectures. We were given a lot of pop quizzes so do your hw before coming to class. He grades hard and fair but you will learn alot. This is probablt my lowest grade this semester but i know more about this class than all my other classes.
Makes you practice the material as much as possible to get a better understanding of the subject.

Sets a high standard for his class and his students but gives many opportunities to earn a better grade. Nothing is easily earned in is class since he is a hard grader but if you pass his class you WILL know the material.

The Professor knows a lot about the subject and does his best to use the entire lecture explaining it. Tests and quizzes are reflected through the homework problems, and is very encouraging and inspirational to the students.

Coburn is a great prof! His lectures are the best but in return he expects you to know a lot. The hw is difficult but he provides you with answers (just answers, no work). Beware he feels no remorse taking points off for units/sig figs. Pop quizzes nearly every week. Overall he's a great prof and doesn't put you to sleep during lecture :)

Professor Coburn makes you work for your grade but it's fair because he teaches really well! He's funny and is very good at keeping the class engaged throughout lecture. If you actually want to learn stuff you can apply out in industry take Coburn! You will learn about structures, with a sprinkle of politics and life lessons!

4 Tests and 1 Final Exam. Not an easy A, but you will be forced to really understand the material. Pop quizzes are the sucking chest wound of the class. Exams could cover a variety of concepts. Be ready for all possibilities. I suggest taking him since he will most likely teach ARO 3271 too. Might as well get used to Coburnicus sooner than later.

This guy is so passionate and makes his class challenging but makes learning structures doable. You have to put in a lot of time and effort to learn the material but his lectures/teaching style/handbooks/slides are amazing. He's a very fair grader so I can't complain. In my opinion, Coburn is one of the best (if not the best) profs at CPP.

Coburn is a unique professor that makes learning simpler and entertaining. If you pass ARO3261 with a decent grade, ARO3271 should not be as bad. You may get the shaft every now but everyone does so do not worry too much.

Enjoyable, he made structures an interesting journey and dare I say inspirational. If you have that feeling structures could be a career choice for you then this is where you NEED to be. You must have the TIME to suffer through ALL the hw to ace the tests and quizzes or else run..! and I highly recommend recording his lectures youll be needing them

He is an amazing lecturer with plenty of personality. Sometimes gets sidetracked mid lecture but is quick to right the ship. I would recommend him to any aerospace engineering student that has the grit to learn and get better. You also have to realize that you must truly earn your grade in his class. It's not an easy A by any means.

Great lecturer. Expect to work for your grade. He is unspecific about his exams. It used be specific lectures so we know what to study, but now "everything" will be considered for each exam. Now we don't know what to study or focus on and can only spend a few days spreading ourselves thin in preparation for an uncertain exam. Hit or miss grade.
Make sure to bring everything needed for an exam(up to date class handbook). otherwise prepare to get a failing grade on the exam.

Very chill guy, unlike his grading, learn sig figs, he will find any excuse to dock points from your exam. But is he is humble and will admit fault and give back points and more (XC) when proven wrong. For FEA, learn to program your calculator as soon as possible, you will regret if you don't, especially at the end when it gets ridiculous.

Dr. Coburn is a great teacher. He breaks down the material in bite size pieces to make it easier to learn. The composites class mostly focuses on classic lamination theory. He teaches much of the basic practical topic you would need to know in industry.

Dr. Coburn is absolutely fantastic at teaching students. I have taken his entire structures series (326,327,329) as well as his finite elements analysis course (4080) and is currently enrolled in his composites analysis course (4360). He cares deeply about his students and always has an open door policy for questions.

Professor Coburn is awesome! The man knows his stuff. He does assign lots of homework but he teaches the subject really well that the homework is not extremely difficult but it is time consuming. You will learn the subject so well, he's awesome and funny!

Dr. Todd Coburns vector dynamics class is hard. He explains things very well during his lecture and is always there to answer your questions. The material is difficult, and you must put in work to ensure doing well on all of the quizzes and homework. He cares about the subjects he teaches, so he does not curve and expects you to master the material

Dr. Todd Coburn is a great professor and person in general. He is probably one of the best structural analysts in his field. This means he is a master of his material, but expects you to understand this material extremely well. He assigns a lot of homework, gives many pop quizzes, and 4 midterms. To pass this class you MUST put in a lot of work.

Todd Coburn is the smartest man I have ever met when it comes to Aerospace Structures. He is a literal genius in his field, but with that being said I feel he expects his students to be quick and to be a genius in the subject as well over time. But 15 weeks isn't enough time to be a master, so the class was insanely difficult in my opinion.

Professor Coburn is one of the best Aro teachers I've had. You have to do a lot of work to get an A. There are pop quizzes and the tests are fairly simple. But he's a tough grader, so you need to make sure you truly understand the material.
Is a master in the subject and teaches it very well. Sometimes he assumes you know more than you do, but only makes you feel a little dumb in return. Amazing professor.

If I could I would pick every description option for professor Coburn, I would. He is by far one of the best teachers I have ever had but also the hardest. Dude seems ego driven. Would not recommend. Also did not gain any experience or valuable knowledge.

The lectures are more than an hour long with non memorable information. Goes through about 50 slides and moves fast. You will have to go back on your own and read the relevant information again. 2 quizzes,definitely study for them;The labs could have been done online;I wish the curriculum was better;End of semester,he curved the class so the mean was a C;not showing up on teamwork days will hurt your grade;No one EVER got 10/10 on labs,always 9.6 or w/e or less;Right wing political and white privilege rants;His way or highway mentality

Professor Hudson is one of my favorite professors at Cal Poly. Hudson is very knowledgeable and easygoing. He gives great feedback for group projects and presentations. Tough professor but very knowledgeable. Hudson is very clear of what he expects in lab reports. He's knowledgeable and he prepares you for industry. He can be quite challenging with his quizzes so be sure to study the material diligently (based off the concepts over the experiments).

do. not. take. hudson. This class is designed to have people failing(curve), i unfortunately was one of the studetns that are failing. The material is easy to learn, but there arent many thing u can do to bump ur grade, failed this class by not doing the homeworks alone
Highly knowledgeable. Laid back, but not a free pass. Good professor

If for online classes, take Bhandari. Hudson is a cool guy but I don't understand him too well and his pop-quizzes can break your grade. He might also talk about climate change and politics often, so be prepared for that.

Professor Hudson genuinely cares about making his students good engineers who understand real world applications in addition to just concepts. I just wish there were more opportunities for points in his class, because if you mess up on one quiz it can shift your grade an entire letter due to it being 10% of your total.

Prof. Hudson really makes you understand how the labs work. We were put into teams for online format of 5 people. We got 2 weeks to write each lab report which was plenty of time and could schedule a zoom meeting with him at any time pretty much. Great guy and quizzes actually reflect what was done during labs.

Took Prof. Hudson for lab and lecture. A really great experience where I learned a lot. One of my favorite professors in the ARO dept since he's fair when it comes to grading and the amount of work he requires of us, and he explains things very well. He wants you to be a good engineer and is devoted to that purpose. I'd recommend him any time.

Professor Hudson's goal is simple: Produce high caliber engineers. His organization and clarity make inherently challenging subject matter easier, if not enjoyable. His industry experience adds helpful context to his lessons. Hudson wants students to succeed, take initiative, and ask questions. If you want to be inspired to be your best, take him.
Gives all the tools needed to succeed but makes you work for your grade.

Professor Hudson was one of my favorite professors. He is funny, and he knows what he is talking about. Make sure you really understand how the equations work for the tests.
He is a great teacher, but he expects you to really pay attention and ask questions. I would definitely recommend him to all incoming aerospace students. he is a great into teacher.

Prof. Hudson is amazing. He's worked in industry for years so he knows what worth teaching, he gives out pop quizzes but if you were paying any attention you shouldn't have a problem getting at least a 7/10. I only had him for the lab portion of this class and was within go was in his lecture the whole time. Take Hudson for controls!

Hudson has industry experience and goes about a practical approach when teaching Control Systems engineering. This is what he did in the industry for his entire career. His class is structured by 2 randomly collected HW assignments (out of 10), 4 quizzes, 1 midterm, and 1 final. From what I hear, he is the preferred professor to take for controls.

He's a nice guy and a good teacher, but this class is discouraging all the way through because he quizzes you on trivial rubbish instead of testing us on what really matters: and that's your engineering ability to solve problems. I feel cheated because the quizzes have too much emphasis over the lab reports. I would not recommend taking him.

Professor Hudson's main focus is system architecture and controls for aeronautics. Astronautics isn't his specialty, and most of his slides were borrowed from Professor Gonda and others. Still he did a decent job, and I will most likely take his classes in the future. He grades on a bell curve which can make the A tough. Has Industry background
Challenging professor but his classes are rewarding. You learn alot from his lecture and he really know his material.

Professor Hudson is a great and really knows his material. He shares a lot of stories of his field experience and keeps the class really interesting. he is very clear in his lectures and will make things clear if you don't understand them.

Cool guy, challenging professor. Class is curved with one midterm, one final, and three quizzes. Homework is optional but you should do it because it really helps for the tests. You can tell he loves his regular day job in the ARO biz. Shows in his teaching. Encourages you to ask questions. Tells u pretty much what will be on quizzes. Just go to class and pay attention. RC airplane project was cool.
he's a very good teacher and is really detailed. I learned a lot from him. He has grading usually by standard deviation which was pretty great for me. He is a challenging teacher but you'll have fun.

Great professor with a extensive background, and is nice like a grandpa! I found his class easy as a transfer, but most freshman, including those without prior knowledge of aero or engineering will find the class difficult due to the way he teaches, uses terminologies, and makes long exams. If you know engineering or aero, you'll really like him!

Is an incredibly experienced and knowledgeable engineer, but not a great teacher. Goes on unproductive side tangents frequently. Required to print every lecture, HW, etc.

He sucks but his class is easy to pass. Extremely unorganized, had assignments due in 2022& it's 2024. Had announcements for different classes in your section but again it's easy to pass that's the only reason I'd take him again

One of the tedious classes. Lots of project work, please quizzes or tests would be on stuff that we haven't really reviewed. Canvas was extremely disorganized and instructions were super unclear. Quizzes cover random stuff about this useless class. Lectures for all 2 hours and 50 minutes every single class. Has the workload of a 3 unit class for a 1 unit class.

This is a systems engineering class and there is a lot expected from you as far as homework / group activities. Dobbs has really great step by step instructions, and he is available to help you along the way. Just don't fall behind! If you can, be a team lead.

He is a really good systems engineering professor and has some good life experience to add to the lectures. He includes everything you need for presentations in Canvas, he offers extra credit, but it is a lot of work.

System engineering is a one-unit class with three units of work. Still, it's a great class, you learn a lot about system engineering through working on a huge group project all semester. A few presentations, tests, and quizzes. The leader rotates through everyone in the group. Professor Dobbs lectures the entire class, expect it and get used to it.

This class was one of many that were very disorganized. Focus on your group project. He throws in random assignments and lectures in between where you can't tell if you should take notes or if he's just telling one of his many stories he has. Quizzes and exams always felt so random, like "When did he teach us that?".

This class is INSANELY taxing (but not too hard). There are a good chunk of assignments that he didn't explain properly ,if at all. He is not reachable outside of class. Just be on top of your group projects and make sure everyone does there fair share of work and things won't be as stressful. His Canvas is very disorganized

Professor Dobbs is a very respected and friendly professor with lots of experience in the field of systems engineering. He loves teaching and although his lectures are long, there are filled to the brim with interesting topics and unique stories from Dobbs himself. The final exam and quizzes are based solely on things from the lectures and projects

Prof. Dobbs is an ex-systems engineer who spends the majority of lectures talking about past experiences, and very little about the lecture. The projects take an excessive amount of time, not because of the difficulty, but the terrible organization of materials and lack of instruction. Only take if you're planning on working as a systems engineer.

I took him for 1011L. It was a little disorganized as he hasn't taught it in awhile. The dullest professor I've ever had. Completely monotone voice and reads almost verbatim what he's presenting from his slides. Program Management is essentially a more in depth continuation of ARO2011, however, the topics covered in here are really helpful for formulating your designs in senior design. Nice guy. However, completely disorganized, lecture slides are cluttered and incoherent. Heavy workload. Prepare to spend 5+ hours on getting slides done with your group. Wasted more time for him to understand his mistakes, which he doesn't fix to spare the next semester, and you'll spend more time teaching yourself. You do not need 4200 for design

Like most of the Cal Poly Aerospace Department, Prof Dobbs is great. His lectures can get a bit boring, but that's to be expected when class is 3 hours long. He has a ton of real world experience that he pulls examples from during class to illustrate his point. There's lots of group work, but it's not bad if you have a good group culture.

Long 3 hr lectures, 2 projects, a report, quizzes, and final. Gives good feedback on projects before presentation. As long as you follow his slides and templates, you will do fine. Very heavy in the group work, so if you don't have a good group, it can be stressful.
Professor Dobbs is an awesome professor. The knowledge that Dobbs imparts on his students is invaluable. However it is time consuming, so be sure to clear your schedule.

Professor Dobbs is a good professor, but there is way too much work for a 1 unit lab class. His lectures are very long and take up the whole 3 hours of class time and his group projects are filled with busy work. There are 3 quizzes, 1 Final, 2 group Presentations, and one Team Project/Lab Report.

This class takes a lot of your time despite being a 1 unit class, but everything you learn is valuable. Professor Dobbs is very understanding and gives good feedback. He even gives reviews team works before the deadline so you fix whatever is to be fixed. Pay attention in class because not everything on the test is on the slides

Professor Dobbs is very knowledgable and has a lot of experience that you can learn from. There is quite a bit of work for a 1 unit lab but it isn't so bad since most of it is done as a group. He clearly wants his students to learn and is good at giving feedback.

Dobbs' class was a lot of fun. The projects are long, can seem like busywork, and can be confusing. But they are graded pretty easily and help you learn a lot more than you'd expect. Dobbs cares about his students understanding the material. My only complaint is that the lectures were a brutal 3 hours straight, which is made worse when on zoom.

Most of this course is done in a group. pray you get a good group. Dobbs is a great guy. caring about his students and helpful when you reach out and ask for it. Taking this class online sucks, but Dobbs tried to make the best of it. Much of his notes can be very confusing and a little lost ( a lotta sys is). talk 2 ppl who've taken this class b4.

This guy would take up a 8 hour lab if he was given the opportunity. Talks SO much, goes over the 3 hour lab time and sometimes doesnt even get to talk about the homework before the class is over. He's caring and he's a nice guy but cameras required at all times, all 3 hours is taken up, homework is a bit extensive, i wouldn't take him.

Professor Dobbs is one of the best professors I've taken at CPP. Try your best to absorb the information and be consistent with team meetings and work flow and you should get an A.
Great professor, one of my favorites actually. He teaches everything with passion and knows his stuff! 100% Recommended

Professor Dobbs' program management class is the same difficulty as systems engineering. The presentations are actually a lot of fun, and the group PowerPoint work is a relief from typical math-heavy courses.

I took this when covid hit, so half of our class was online. However, in the few months before covid, going to Dobbs' class was one of the the things I really looked forward to. He gives a lot of insight about what it's like working in industry and talks a lot about the projects he's worked on. Do your work and you'll get an A.

Professor Dobbs is very passionate about the subject. His lectures are very interesting, however are very long. It can be difficult to stay awake for the 3 hour lecture, which he uses all of. If you follow his format for the F-22 report and CoDR, PDR, it shouldnt be too hard to get an A.

One of the best profs at CPP. He cares about the students learning the material and gaining useful experience. Lectures can be long, but his anecdotes keep things interesting. Professor Dobbs is incredible. He really has a passion for what he does and has so much industry knowledge and experience. He is one of the nicest professors ever! Aro 2011 is a lot of work, but its pretty fun. His lectures can last the full three hours which can be hard to stay awake through, but he has some really interesting stories to tell. I have learned so much in his class.

Good Professor whos new to teaching, but has trouble juggling large classes. Everyone who will struggle or has in the class has no coding experience. Professor Yale was pretty chill in the beginning, but did not teach MATLAB very well. I could tell many other students in the class were having trouble. Made learning statics very simple and straightforward. He really cares about us as students and wants us to succeed. Very knowledgeable and has many years of industry experience.

I loved this professor! This was his first semester teaching but he does a great job. You can tell he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Going to his office hours was super helpful. One quiz every week, and one homework assignment a week. 3 exams and a final but they are similar to the homework problems so they aren't super hard.

For his first time teaching, he is a great professor. He's still getting used to the flow of teaching, the homework can sometimes be difficult, but the weekly quizzes are doable. Overall, I'm sure with time, he'll be a great professor as he does struggle with managing time well in class.

Despite some scuff here and there like homework content and difficulty due to the first-time teaching, he is generally a good professor. One hw due each week ranges from 4 to 12 questions. This was his first semester teaching but he's doing a good job. There's handwritten homework due every week and a quiz once a week Exams are homework problems so there's no curveballs. He's accommodating also.

Ton of experience in the Actual field of Engineering, and all of my questions regarding it were answered all the time. Just a boatload of knowledge. Would def take him again if taught another course, very knowledgeable, class is simple and straightforward, gives homework, but its very simple and easy, exams reflect exactly what is taught in class, just make sure to show up, attendance is mandatory.
Super chill and approachable guy. The class itself was more of a lecture on how to navigate through the ASCE 7-16. No labs, very easy HW, and two quizzes. Highly recommend taking him.

Not sure why her rating is so bad. Had her when she replaced Seong... she's definitely interesting but she's a fair grader. Shafahi is awful. This is the first review I've ever felt the need to write. what i like about him is his flexibility since he records his lectures you can attend class in person, zoom or watch later but your its better in person that way you can get extra credit. he has 2 projects and 2 test that he grades but even if you struggle with the tests you can definitely bring your grade back up with the projects and vice versa.

I had the pleasure of taking professor Olivas last semester. I can honestly say it was one of the best academic experiences I have had. He is not only highly knowledgeable in the subject but also genuinely passionate about teaching and engaging with students. He also provides extra credit!!!
Do not take if you do not know how to program
Great professor. Good lectures and a lot of examples done during class. The quizzes and homework line up in terms on material learned.

Nissenson is awesome. His class is very difficult and he's a bit of a tough grader, but if you are willing to work hard you will learn so much. He is super knowledgeable and very accessible outside of class should you have any questions. Genuinely, a really good person.
Stay away if you do not already know how to code through MATLAB.

This class is doable, but you need to carefully manage your time with the projects. Total of 6 MATLAB projects. I took it as an elective for my civil structural engineering master program, and I am glad I did. This class made appreciate the usefulness of numerical methods as a tool for solving interesting real-world problems.

One of the best professors at CPP. Clearly layed out course, quizzes that reflect secific topics of the class, and projects that do take time but are manageable. If you have to move around other classes to get Nissenson, do it

Pretty Solid Class, Highly recommend taking this class ASAP if you're part of the program since you'll need to know MATLAB in other courses. Graded by just 6 HW assignments. Don't be discouraged if you don't do well on the first 3, those ones are the hardest and it gets significantly easier after. He's also super helpful in OH's for going over HW.

A legend. He makes you enjoy learning thermal fluids. He makes sure you understand the concepts, and he is just fun to talk to. He is probably the most caring professor I have taken. Do your homework, study it, and you will be fine on the quizzes. He is also VERY accessible outside of class.

Coming from so many semesters spent with terrible professors, Nissenson was a refreshing teacher. He meticulously records all of his lectures and makes them available for you, he gives extra credit opportunities, and partial credit on all quizzes and tests. By far my favorite professor.

Nissenson is incredibly organized, records all his lectures to post online, and makes supplemental videos for every topic. Only downside is that he gives a quiz EVERY class. They are fair quizzes, and he is generous with partial credit. One of my favorite professors at CPP :)
He seems enthusiastic about teaching MATLAB. He's clear and the homework is easy.
This was an intro to engineering class so we went over the basics. nothing too much to need to teach. We did have a fun project with PI bots though.

He teaches a flipped class, which means you have to watch his videos before class. He spends class time doing a quick review, a quiz, and a group programming challenge that offers extra credit. If you already know how to program, this class will be a breeze.

All of his lectures in class are spent on weekly quizzes. You have to watch his online videos cause he never goes over new topics because the class is short. The class is a flipped course. You teach yourself, then come to class prepared. He gets very monotone at times. Probably one of the more lenient professors. Take him if you have no options.

Took Dr. Nissenson for his special topics course during winter 2016. Embraces the "learn by doing" concept. His teaching style mainly consists of teaching you the theoretical concept and part of the applied and then you learn on your own by tinkering with your assignment. Great guy. Super friendly, cares about you, I would love to have him as a grandpa or something. If you want to coast in machine design this is guy you should take. His homework and projects are complete jokes only taking a few hours each and where you learn almost nothing. Lectures are non existent, mostly flips through slides without going over the material. Tests are not very difficult but you have to learn everything yourself. Pretty terrible overall but you will pass.

Don't take. Cancelled class a lot, and we only met for lab a few times and only did three projects. Constantly brings up how he fails his statics classes. Spends an inappropriate amount of class time on irrelevant rants/tangents. Spent the first 2 weeks of class rambling about all the complaints we might have heard about him.
