Professor Ghaneh truly wishes us to learn the material, thus he makes the class hard. You really have to invest a lot of time into this class. Do the homework meticulously and pay attention to the lectures. As long as you improve on the quizzes and tests (there's two for both), you will not fail.

Ali will make you realize how invested you need to be to love what you are studying. He makes it clear that if you are not interested, he will have no patience for you. Study, study, study, and study some more. Ali will push you, and test your patience with his exams, quizzes, and tone. But deep down, he knows you can be one of the best engineers.

Take the class if you want a solid basis of the material, but don't take it hoping you will get an A. Tests are quite difficult but he will give you chances to improve your grade as long as you show effort and improvement throughout the semester. Lectures are challenging due to the material but he explains well and allows time to go over problems.

This major is hard and a lot of bad review reflect that. Ghaneh is a caring professor and has earned his respect. I think he teaches well, and during class time he is effective at answering questions. This class demands a lot of time outside of class, more than you would expect from the homework. If you put in the effort, you will pass this class.

Professor Ganeh is a widely respected expert in his field, but lacks the compassion, empathy and understanding of how students learn. As a professor he is arrogant, rude, disrespectful and rushed. His lectures are very quick, and impersonal, it often seems like he is under the assumption you have experience with the material as he does.

I had professor Ghaneh for both lecture and lab. He is an amazing professor, although he assigned very time consuming homework assignments but overall he taught the material very well and he was super understanding when it came to class requests/extensions etc.. I would definitely take his classes again for future courses!

The course is extremely difficult but the professor assigns ALOT of homework which is great practice problems for the students to really learn the subject. He grades really easy on the hw and exams, the only problem is his exams are difficult but he goes over what to "do" before the exam which is really helpful guidance.

If you want to learn and become an expert in circuit analysis, take Professor Ali Ghaneh. FYI if you don't have a solid understanding of ece1101, then you will struggle in other coming courses. We signed up to become engineers; Professor Ghaneh will teach you everything you're supposed to know and teach you how to think like a real engineer.

If you are looking for an easy passing grade do not take Ganeh! He assigns a ton of homework, and the quizzes and exams are the most difficult in the university, but it is great preparation for the future. People who walk out of this class with a C- are more prepared than those who got an A in another class. If you want to be prepared, take Ganeh.

Professor started tough, but provided opportunities to improve grades. Assigns all odd problems from book as HW, but gives full marks if you at least attempt the problems. Exams and quizzes were tough, but mainly because there are a lot of calculations. The professor goes through lecture quickly, but if you ask questions, will go into more details.

He is a very tough teacher but you will definitely know the subject by the end of the semester. There are 7 HW assignments and they are usually very long. 2 quizzes, midterm and a final. Tests are VERY hard! He starts the semester really hard but towards the end he starts going a little easier on his students.

Horrible professor! power point presentations with no examples, speeds through them, and asks you questions while you are lost. He waited towards the end of the semester to grade the lab reports. Stay away from this professor.
Ghaneh is super dope!

Professor goes easy on hwk and hard on midterms and final. Tries to trick you on exams. Like others have said, this class is hard. But, professor makes material harder and doesn't care about the students. Professor is difficult to reach out too. CHOOSE SOMEONE ELSE.
I gaurantee that you will get your ass handed to you on the midterm. Keep studying and practicing problems constantly and you will pass the class.

He might look very strict but he actually cares. The professor acts like that because there are many people who don't pay attention in class, but if you pay attention then don't worry. Pay attention and learn the material, stay late after class if possible and you can get many insights into the materials. He's not that bad of a teacher.

The professor might look like a strict guy on the outside but he cares. I think he's like this because there are too many students who don't pay too much attention in the class. If you pay attention and stay after class, he usually softens up a lot and you can ask him many great questions. Expect great times if you pay attention and learn.

In lab this professor is great, because you learn by making mistakes in the lab and you can always ask him for help if you are stuck. A good grade is attainable by showing up, paying attention, and following the lab report format. The Lab reports are tedious but there are only 5 to 6.

He's a good professor, he tells you everything he expects you to do. If you actually listen to him, then you'll be more than fine and you'll learn a lot in labs. He is very straightforward and he tells you what he needs from you. I learned a lot of stuff that I didn't know of in the lab. It was my first time working with lab stuff and it was fun!

Terrible lectures consisting of nothing but unenthusiastic reading off of a horribly-organized PowerPoint, not a single problem actually shown being worked out by hand. You will not learn anything from his lectures, and the textbook is unhelpful as well. Midterm is absolutely nothing like the homework. Avoid at all costs.

Spring Semester 2021 Pandemic Rating Your grade is decided on a few assignments that you practically have to teach yourself how to do. Took him near the end of the semester to give feedback on assignments. Lectures consist of him reading off of slides. Made me reconsider electrical engineering as a major. I don't recommend taking him whatsoever.

You do not learn in this class. His homework takes about 8 hours per chapter. He reads off the PowerPoint in an unenthusiastic way. Take someone else if you have the chance don't bother if he is the last one there. I was looking forward to learn about circuits but now I lost that joy

The course was supposed to be a lab, but it turned out to be a 3-hour lecture. No quizzes, tests, or final. Just lab assignments that he couldn't help us with. Not my favorite professor. His slides and handwriting are unorganized. I'm sure he did the best he could with the situation given. Grades weren't revealed until the very end. Good luck
He really tried to help under this special situation. However, I would not say that it is easy to get an A but it is also not something impossible.
The lab assignments are hard but he is not a tough grader. And he gave extra credit opportunity. If you do all of the problems, you easily pass with A.

He is not nice when you ask him questions. His expectations are high and hard to meet, don't be surprised if he gives you poor grades. His lab reports are long and take awhile to do. There is a final exam for this lab and it is very difficult and time consuming, don't expect to know how to do any of it. (Spring 2019)

Horrible!! Basically you wont get your grades or any feedback so you never know how you are doing. Class is just reading from Power point. Exams and assignments has nothing to do with the course book or even his power points. Some principles were not even thought or discussed in the class but they are in exams.

Absolutely horrid. Only read off the power points. Gave an insane amount of HW that had nothing to do with any of the tests. Always calls every problem easy, but when called out to solve gets lots in the problems then skips it and disregards it. When asked to explain problems if he does not have his notes he will try to skip it and say he can't.

Worse than his ECE1101. Just goes over PPT. Nothing feels like a lab class. Keeps trying to merge two sections together to save time. Waste of time and energy. His class will not just ruin your GPA but also discourage you as an engineer. I can honestly say that I didn't learn anything from his lab which will eventually get me back in the future.

He should not teach in CPP. Reading off the PPT and got lost. Late several times. Cancel classes for his computer issues. The midterm was way too hard compared with the HW questions. No office hours. Takes forever to grade. Never see my last grade. Yawning during the lecture. Haven't taken final yet. Fell very discouraged as beginning class.

Before covid, he would begin the class with a long lecture (30min to an hour) of what we would be doing that class. These lectures were way too long, and it felt like a massive lecture class. When online classes began, this behavior was only more exaggerated, since the lectures took much linger and had nothing to do with actually solving the labs.

Goes over powerpoint presentation of the textbook the entire class and does not let students participate in worked examples. He gives homework problems from the textbook, but his test questions are in a different format which makes it hard to prepare.

The worst. Lecture notes are from the book, he skims over them fast, so you dont quite understand how everything is working in a circuit. Gives an insane amount of homework. Gradings based on if you attempted it, so you dont know if youre doing anything right. Tests are insanely hard. Struggling in classes now because I still dont understand

Teaches by just pointing at a powerpoint and talking. Not good at explaining things at all. Exams/quizzes are extremely tough and he only made them easier because too many students were failing. If u end up with him just read the textbook and teach yourself. Also don't go to lecture cause attendance isn't mandatory.

This guy could not be any less helpful in lab. He reads his email in the corner the whole time. You are on your own, and if you ask a question, be prepared to work to get an answer out of him. Reports are insanely long, and then he grades each one in several seconds. Pro tip: get real familiar with the oscilloscope for the final.

Worst lecturer in my life. Flew through slides with complex calculations like we knew everything. Never wrote anything on the board. Expects u to remember spoken equations. One test, notified us about something he forgot to lecture on and then tested us on it. Syllabus changed constantly and without notification. Difficult tests. Universally hated.

Keep in mind this is the lecture. We had homework every chapter, only the odd ones, and grades the HW leniently. Sometimes quizzes can be challenging, so prepare yourself. Hes also really flexible with due dates dates and quiz dates and goes with what the students wish for. Was late to class several times, but hes genuinely nice and also funny.

Don't take this teacher. Labs are long and he doesn't help. He will not return lab reports until the last week of school, so you don't know what your grades are until then. This makes correcting your mistakes impossible. The final was difficult and we did not have enough time to finish. Try to take another professor if possible

Theres about 6 or 7 labs. The first 2 or 3, you don't have any lab reports, just do the lab and get familiar with the equipment, that was really fun. The lab reports are extremely tedious, extremely long (can be 20 pages 4asimple lab), and really time consuming when the labs themselves are quick. Lab final was crazy difficult, but curved.

He checks prelabs painfully slow. He mumbles his lecture under his face mask which nobody can hear or understand. You typically start working on the lab an hour to an hour and a half in. He disappears from the lab multiple times per lab about 10-20 minutes at a time. He changes parts of the lab randomly the day of. Besides that the labs are easy.

great lab prof! he lectures before lab starts so you understand the material even if it's been a while. answers questions during lab. was understanding if we couldn't get the parts and would get them himself sometimes. grades based on lab report. as long as you include all the required info, you'll get at least an 8/10. i've taken him multiple time

He wasn't bad but he would just read off of the slides which made the class boring. VERY heavy group work, almost all of it was presentations so pick a solid group. There were so many of these presentations we had to do, it felt like busy work. Lenient on due dates if an extension was requested though. He's kind and no tests or final, only quizzes.

Professor Yazdy was a good teacher, and although his briefings were slow and monotonous, he gave plenty of information to finish the labs and write the reports easily. Just make sure to ask questions for any unclear instructions. Also, buy ALL your supplies early enough to have everything ready by the first labs.

Professor Yazdy is honestly pretty good! If you sit in the back of the class be prepared to get closer to understand what he says. His lectures are straightforward to follow. He also provides demos on how to do the lab. Pretty much you can do this course as monkey see monkey do. There are lab reports on all of his labs however they are easy to do!

Professor Yazdy was a decent lecturer, however his briefings for each lab were very slow and difficult to hear. His directions were often obscure, so be prepared to ask lots of questions. His labs are also graded pretty strictly. Despite all this, he is a good teacher, and is open to helping you with your grade and work if you just ask.
class is boring, but nice guy. lot of group presentation and three papers to write. gives open book quizzes. overall easy grader, just a boring lecturer when he reads off his slides.

Lots of group projects in his section but they are all easy. Also has papers which, again, are easy. Overall, a good class, although when you ask for feedback, he is very indirect in telling you how to improve. For that, he goes from a 5 to a 4. Also a bit on the senile side but easy class.

You have to follow his rubric 100% perfectly to do good. However he takes forever to grade and doesn't let you know until about 6 labs in, and then its a struggle to make the points back. I got lucky he let me revise a couple labs. Class is fully graded on labs despite him saying there are 4 parts to your grade.

For in-person application half of IME4020. Yazdy is a professor you take when you don't care too much about the material. Just "lectures" from his corner and reads exactly what is on the slides, despite saying you can't read from your slides in your presentations. Messy with lots of assignments/presentations without canvas due dates, but all easy.

Nice guy who is there to chill and lowkey do nothing. Class mainly consists of group PowerPoint presentations which can be done in 30 minutes or so before class starts. The cases studied are pretty interesting which makes the class enjoyable. Not much else to say, best of luck!

He did not reply to emails AT ALL, and I had to contact the department coordinator in order to contact him. Also, he's very lazy and doesn't really teach in the class, constantly changes class schedules and his grading criteria is such a mess because he did not say what he wants AT ALL during the class. I even leant more with a tutor than with him
Not bad, kinda boring, but super easy which was nice

Professor Yazdy's class was real laid back. He would frequently go for walks through the hallways and get lost, sometimes for up to 20 minutes. This offered as a nice break from his monotonous lectures.

Wish I can give a 0. this professor is lazy and doesn't care about his classes and how he grades. You can have an A on canvas and end up with a letter grade or two lower as your final grade. His syllabus doesnt even state a grading breakdown everything is random and up to him. He also leaves class 3+ times for more than 15+ minutes.

Long boring lectures at start of lab, lab reports weren't awful. No lab manual, but I almost wish there was. Labs kinda confusing without clear direction. Got 9's and 10's on all lab reports, but still ended up with a B some how. Get a good lab partner who knows what they're doing, but also doesn't hog the board. Pre Labs are mostly ez.

Yazdy is okay for ECE4064, it isn't difficult. Two presentations, two short assignments, and occasional participation make up the grade. Grading is a bit all over the place, but if you put effort, you will get a good grade. The pacing is very odd in terms of when you present since you can present at the beginning and don't until the very end.

Lab reports are really easy. During the lectures before the labs, couldn't understand what he was saying, ever. He doesn't speak loud enough to reach the back of the class so we have to get up to hear, and he has a pretty thick accent so we couldn't understand his either way. Prelabs and lab instructions are good though so you can get by.

I don't get the high ratings. Boring and ambiguous with grading criteria; you can get a C for one project and then an A for another one that you applied the same effort. WAY too much group work for a 5 week class. Should allow students to grade groupmates since there are always those who do nothing and get an A for other people's efforts.

Took him for engineering part (Dolske for philosophy) in the Summer. He's chill. You'll enjoy in his part if you do the readings/don't "Fluff" the paper. Don't fail either engineering or philosophy part bc it is IME Department Policy that an F as your final grade for either part of the class is an automatic F for the entire IME4020 class.

Hes alright. Grading criteria is clear in the syllabus. Hes willing to help out if youre stuck in the lab. Sometimes his prelabs/notes are hard to read. Lab reports arent bad. Its basically just putting your results into tables and graphs and some error analysis. He didnt grade any labs until the end so make sure youre doing em right lmao

Professor Yazdy is a very lenient lab professor. The class consisted of coming to the lab and demonstrating that the lab worked and once you showed him that it did, you were good to leave. The lab reports were very simple and only required a few things which often leads to a 100% on them. Would highly recommend him for any lab that he teaches!
A Nice professor.

Yazdys portion of IME4020H was really good. Youre put into a group and have 4 total ppts to do, 4 quizzes but the lowest is dropped, and 3 short papers. I enjoyed his class and thought he was easy going. Im happy I had great group members they made the class so much better. Overall recommend, hes a really chill guy with reasonable deadlines.

I really enjoyed having Yazdy for this lab! It was such a straight forward class and he always answered any questions for clarification. Graded on 12 labs that were done using PSpice. Since the class was virtual he only lectured for 30 mins which I loved. His notes/explanations are very helpful. Definitely recommend! Such a caring and nice guy.

He gets angry at every little thing and treats everyone like children with no respect for anyone, hes enthusiastic about teaching he clearly does not want to be there. It was interesting to see him get in arguments with multiple different students during this class
Uploads blurry lectors from the zoom meetings. It is 720p but the video quality is worst than watching a vhs tape that has been ran 300 times.
Easy A. But the class is painstakingly boring. All you do is make PowerPoints and read off the slides and then write 3 papers over the semester. Take him for the A but be prepared to be bored.
The lectures are a little long and you might not succeed on the first few lab reports but once you understand what he expects the class should be fairly easy as he is also quite accommodating.

He does NOT know how to adapt to technology. I understand that Zoom is hard, but he takes his frustration out on his students. He has no effort teaching, actually put on a presentation read by an AI robot instead of actually teaching us. The class was easy but takes off silly points because he doesn't give perfects.
Took him for ECE1101L Fall 2020 all I can say he is amazing Professor! Helpful in Office Hours! Super Easy! Easy A. Awesome Lecturer as well! Would highly recommend anyone to take him.

I've taken Yazdy for 1101, 2200, and now 3200. Excellent professor who became even more understanding when we moved to online learning. Weekly lab reports + prelabs are straightforward, and he makes sure that everyone understands by providing extensive lectures. My Pspice license expried, and he allowed me to turn my report in 2 weeks later. Fun!

This class is meant to be a breeze and Yazdy makes it so. Overall grade consists of 2 presentations, a short quiz, your resume, one easy letter to a company declining a job offer, and in class participation. It's overall a bit of a drag considering it's once a week for 50 minutes, but it's a free A as long as you put in a little bit of effort.

Good way of organizing his lab, but the execution is less stellar. He says you can do the experiment at home, bring it for demo, and leave early, but he always takes so long doing whatever he's doing that you end up waiting for the whole time anyway which can be deadly boring. He's very friendly and willing to help though.
Lectures are good if a little boring. Homework is extremely difficult but the tests were not as hard. Not a bad Professor but the final project was hard. Grades lightly on it though.
Had a good time in this class. Made lectures not as boring as controls should be, knows his stuff. Always tries to answer questions and would correct himself if he was wrong. Labs only bi-weekly and

My main complaints are that the homeworks are a bit heavy (but with reasonable deadlines) and that not enough lab time was actually given to the project and instead went to lectures. It was his first time teaching 3250 so these are growing pains rather than things to worry about, would take again as he is a good prof. Open book + 1/2 page note exam

Dr. H is a good prof. Was his first time teaching this subject, but he taught it well. I know the bar is low, but he actually answers questions to the best of his knowledge, and writes out example problems on the board! (you may think i'm joking but after several years here, this is enough to gain my respect). Exams are manageable and fair

I had him for ME4391, He is a nice person but I would not recommend him as a professor. He is available to help you with the project he assigns but depending on how you make it he may not be able to help (based on the codelang/hardware). His tests are hard & he doesn't say what they are about, he just says you will not be surprised, I was surprised
He's super positive and always has time for you during office hours. Plus, he's just really cool and makes it easy to ask him anything. Totally the kind of person you want to have as a professor.

If you want an easy A you can take this professor. If you want to not fail your future engineering courses, DO NOT TAKE LAWAL. Strength of Materials is the basis of most engineering classes, and not only will you not learn anything, she makes everything a lot more difficult to understand by being disorganized and unprepared.

By all means DO NOT take this professor. The only thing you learn from this class is how disorganized a professor can be. Attending her lectures became pointless about halfway through and it was just better to read the textbook on my own to learn.

If a 0 out of 5 rating could be given, that is what this professor deserves. She is so lost in terms of the structuring of her class. There is also a research paper worth a good portion of your grade which is vaguely outlined and hard to see what she wants. Definitely take other professors if you can and want to learn.

Professor is lost when lecturing. If you have any questions about the material one would be better off googling it than asking the professor. Prepare for a lot of self studying. Professor also has to take breaks in between lectures as she is not prepared to lecture. Recommend taking another professor.

It might be because we are the first ever class she's taught, but she her lectures were confusing with her going back and forth to fix mistakes she would constantly make. Towards the chapter about sheer and moment diagrams a lot of my classmates including me were confused and lost.

Great professor. Homework was very difficult at times but there was a supplemental drop in session for help. Homework problems were much harder than lecture and test problems. Clearly outlines what types of questions will be on the test. Very helpful in providing test corrections when deemed needed. Amazing professor, strongly recommend.
Very helpful but be prepared to put in 5x the work for something higher than a C+. Homework heavy! He is very caring and tests are straightforward - easy to pass.

Only had Professor Lee for the first half of the semester but a great teacher. Always available to help you out and work you through the homework problems. Had weekly assignments that were to be completed by the end of class, no homework. Super clear on exams and what to expect. Would recommend.

Really enjoyed Professor Lee, brought a good energy to the lectures and taught in a memorable way. Tests were relatively easy as he would ask if we wanted certain questions on a test and told us exactly what we needed to know for the test. Some of the homework was difficult and could take a while. Overall great and easy teacher.

Took Yam Lee CHE2021 and CHE 2011. This man is carrying the chemical engineering department on his back. He is very caring and understanding of his students and is clear about exams. The class and the content are not easy but he makes himself accessible to his students and is willing to work with students to manage work load. Strongly recommend.

His lectures are good, the tests are rather predictable and he gives a lot of opportunities for you to improve your grade. The problem sets are kind of a nightmare though, you will rarely spend less than 5 hours combined on each of them

Combined grade. Weekly homework assignments/lab activities that aren't too hard, but don't procrastinate. He will help with assignments during class, in office hours, and through email. Very quick to emails!! Tells you exactly what to expect on the exams. Study for exams!! Group project and literature paper. Not graded harshly. Don't procrastinate!
Teacher was mid, only hard assignment was the first one. The tests are mainly homework problems.

I used to think Dr. Lee was cool until I took this class. Homework took HOURS to complete with no one to consult for help. The worst part of this class were the online tests, which had long, loaded problems and tight time limits. This course and the professor made me question if my career in Chem-E would be over before it even started.

(FALL 2019) Dr. Lee is a respected and knowledgeable CHE professor. Is very approachable and accessible outside of class- he will stay behind after the lab section if you have any questions, or you can attend his office hours. He was able to answer my questions about the course in a way that I could clearly understand. Overall, I think hes cool.

Prof Lee is a really nice guy. I get good vibes from him and he truely wants to help his students to succeed. That being said, his lectures are entirely just him talking, and he isnt very aware of if his students are following or not.

I was very nervous to take this class at first and did not know what to expect. The class is very Matlab and Excel heavy so get ready to follow lectures closely and study the methods taught! He is a quick responder if you have questions. The class is very manageable as long as you work at it!
He took his time to explain things in the lab, and made it easy to ask questions inside and outside of class.
My favorite Professor by far. Lectures are a little boring. Take home/ open note exams were nice.
The absolute best. I had him for CHE 1411L as well, and he was awesome.

Does not prep the class for any exams. You have 50 minutes to complete the exam & gives more questions than they can be answered. The lecture & lab were not in synchronization. He says that exams are curved with 4 or 3 additional points which does not do much to your grade. Not much of a curve but a dent in your grade. Go over the power points.

The lab and lecture have a combined grade. Do the work he assigns (usually one hw a week), it's not a hard class if you pay attention and do the example problems in class. Half of my semester was online due to coronavirus but Dr. Lee was very accessible and understanding.

If you take good notes, do the homework (maybe 2 hours per week), study, and start on the group project early then you can get an A. I didn't do the homework on time and didn't study for the first test which is very thorough, so I got a C+.

Pretty easy grader, HW is worth 15%. Rest of grade consists of a group matlab project, 3 exams, a final, and lab attendance. He is very available for help and explains things clearly. Lectures are somewhat boring but informative. If you do the HW the exams are extremely easy.

Avoid taking him for CHE 303. Lectures are super boring and scattered all over the place, and he doesn't show examples. You will just end up teaching yourself thermodynamics. AVOID. Makes this topic very boring
Absolutely the best teacher I have had at Cal Poly so far! Very helpful and will do everything to help you pass.

If you actually want to learn stuff you'll definitely have to do some independent studying; all class is just him writing equations on the board and yapping about random stuff. Despite that the class is very easy; all tests are basically open note. There are a couple of projects (this is where you'll actually learn stuff), but they are pretty easy.

Somewhat disorganized class, doesn't always make due dates clear and doesn't put assignments in canvas so it's difficult to gauge your grade. Lectures are understandable, tests are accurate to the lectures, and he's open to you petitioning for partial credit. ells a lot of jokes and enjoys socializing with the class. Overall would recommend.

This professor's class was disorganized. I never knew when homework was due or when the next test was. He doesn't put any grades in Canvas so I had no idea what my grade was all semester. His lectures are long and boring. He just writes stuff on the board without much explanation for 3 hours. Overall though it's an easy class with not much homework

The lectures are very fun, anything he doesn't cover in class you will read in the textbook. Homework is either problems that will be on the test or a summary report of the text, which again has content for the tests. This class is heavily group dependent, so get with people who will participate.

This guy is a terrible professor. However, his class is very easy. Tests are basically homework problems. Reports are only graded on format so you can make up numbers. Despite all this, his class is very fun. He can't go an hour without same something racist, sexist, xenophobic etc. He'll crack jokes at every opportunity he gets.

His lectures were not very well structured. Never updates canvas so hard to know what you grade is. Group reports/presentations. He would do midterm review/final review and then the actual exams would be totally different stuff/stuff not from the review. I often mentally checked out during his class.

Does not know how to use canvas. His class was frustratingly disorganized. You never know when things are due and if you ask him any questions his answers are so confusing and cryptic you would think its a riddle from a fantasy story. Exams are graded very weirdly. We only got to 2/3 labs and he somehow takes up 110% of the 3 hour class time.

This professor is great! Super engaging and had the whole class laughing, he was a great introduction to aerospace. There's some strange comments sometimes, but he's kind. There wasn't any fear to ask questions. Make sure to get a good group as they will make or break this class. Long written assignments and answers must be exact or no credit.

The class is relatively easy. Exams are easy, since the problems rely on basic equations (which he lets you bring cheat sheet for). The absolute WORST is the papers. These thing are brutal. I once wrote one that was around 70 pages long. If you do literally everything perfect for the paper, he still won't give you a good grade. Also quite sexist

Gave us random group projects often, but never knew what my grade was until end of the semester. Exams were kind of hard to study for because he'd do a exam review, then have problems not included during the review. Tends to ramble a lot, hard to tell what I need to note down as important info. Homework is kind of unclear in terms of practice.

The class isn't difficult. You work in groups and research many subjects. As engineers, we'll have no option but to learn to work in groups helping each other, being responsible, and leading a team; this is what I learnt the most of in his class. He goes above and beyond to help you understand calculations. Easy to get a hold off ANY day of the wk.

Royas is a nice guy but his class is disorganized and unproductive. He spends the first 30-40 minutes taking roll and collecting assignments. The 20-page lab report was graded by ignoring everything and just seeing how close you were to the expected result. Grading was arbitrary and not really reflective of individual ability but your groups.

Not very good at all. There is no clear format on how lab reports should be written, and he grades them HARD and is VERY picky on the formatting. Also seems to forget what he assigns. Very inconsistent and very disorganized. You will not learn much from him; recommend taking him ONLY if you want to just pass the class, otherwise take someone else.

Royas is kind of funny and his class isn't too hard. However, you won't really learn anything, you don't know your grade the entire time, he rarely puts things on canvas, and most assignment guides are from other professors, so you don't know what he wants. Also, he says a lot of shocking jokes? (I think they're jokes) so be prepared for that.
You won't learn anything but boy you're in for a great time.
