get ready for horrible time with this professor, any question you ask will be met with yelling and harsh criticism. he's not a friendly person. he'll make sure to help with as little information as possible. if you ever find another professor, please take that one instead. and if you do take his class, MAKE SURE YOUR PARTNER IS THERE FOR THE FINAL!
I do not like to get yelled at but if you can put up with it he is alright. I wouldnt recommend him.

He loves to play tough, but I believe he's quite chill if you catch him out of class. He actually tries to help you as long as you do some work and you know what you trying (AKA you didnt copy). Lecture is H E A V Y, but easy (IYKYK). Lab is tough, but you can form bigger groups and discuss/troubleshoot. Last class he will buy you pizza!

Just try your best. He will yell at you he will expect you to show up outside if class hours to demo. Just try and get 2/3 of all labs done. He will give you a C because he doesn't actually care. Just put up with the yelling and abuse. Don't take him too seriously. Expect labs to work for some and not others. Try and work on labs before class glhf

If you are unable to demo the lab properly the following week, you have until the end of the semester to demo and get late credit. The lectures are helpful, especially at the beginning because the labs are usually ahead of the lecture. He'll roast but don't take it personally. Don't be afraid to ask questions when you're stuck, it'll save you time.

This is not an easy lab so prepare to work long hours once you get past the first 3 labs. Make sure on the first day you partner up with someone who KNOWS how to code since there will be a ton of coding in the class. Prepared to get yelled at and at first you probably won't like him, but as the class progresses you start to understand his humor.

His teaching style is not for everyone. Ready to get yelled at though but he yells for your own good. Don't be afraid to ask for help, he is ready to help you out cause I asked so many times and got yelled at so many times, I find it funny though, he laughed it off most of the time. 3301 Lab has never been easy so get yourself a good coder.

Every ECE student will have to face this guy. Get ready for him to berate you on every little mistake in front of the class. Also, make sure to the grade to your demos. I would've got an A, but he sure that I missed some demos. Even though, I demoed every single time. Make sure you get a good coder as your partner. Good Luck!

He isn't too difficult. The labs are very time consuming so find a group of people to trouble shoot the code. Make sure to go to class with the lab already working or else he will make a scene. At times he is very rude but it is justified. If you watch his recorded lectures he gives you the code and information required to do the lab.

Beware who your partner is in this class, this professor is an inescapable hurtle for all ECE students, be sure to have your lab completely ready to go before having him check it off, he is extremely rude and overall a horrible Professor

The lab is hard, but you will learn so much with the applications covered. You will need to work on the lab outside of class if you expect to finish on time even if you understand the lab completely. He is a bit rude when you ask for help, but it is a bit of a facade so dont take what he says too personally, he wants you to succeed in the class.

This professor is very rude. Never ask him a question otherwise you will get yelled at in front of the class. He always comes to class with a terrible attitude. I have no respect for him since he seems to have non for his students. Avoid this professor if you can.

I mean look, I did learn a lot about the material. But something any industry looks for besides the technical stuff is respect, which is rare in this class. You want a professor that's HAPPY to guide you, not call your project garbage on tiny details until you get it right. Would I recommend? Maybe. For those who care about their mental health? No

He is definitely a hard ass, but he cares and wants you to succeed. His labs are very time consuming and detail oriented, but you will learn a ton really quick. Pray you have a good partner (software and hardware person), otherwise you are screwed. Overall, the guy knows his stuff and will make sure you get to know it too.

A tough class, but one where you'll learn plenty. Online format consisted of weekly labs, where we are given 3 days after the lecture date to demo for full credit. When you demo, you'll be given things to test with him and if one thing fails, you'll have to reschedule. You have to set a date with him 24 hrs in advance so try to do well to save time

Professor Pinai provided a true lab experience during virtual instruction by lending out hardware kits to each team. He gives roughly 3 days to do each lab, which is more than enough time if you have good communication with your lab partner. Pinai is really funny and often misunderstood by students. He cares for his students.

his 1st time teaching sigs&systems at cpp. curriculum wasnt organized on canvas so you have to go to lectures to learn. some hw graded for completion, 1 midterm online/asynchronous, one final based on questions he told us to study. cared abt students and asked if we were lost (we were). curved the class. you'll pass if you do all the assignments

Dont be fooled by ppl who gave him 5/5. He complained about his ratemyprofesssor score on canvas a few days ago. Like others said he doesnt teach code and has a final project where with 3 presentations and a 9 page long report. He said attendance wasnt mandatory but then questioned everyone who skipped during the last project presentation

Highly challenging course with intensive final project and frequent presentations. While lectures can be dry, the professor is accessible, caring, and clarifies questions when asked. You'll get minimal in-class coding, so expect extra work for final projects, 45 mins presentation as well. If you dedicate time and pull late nights, you can get an A.

Hates being questioned about projects and assignments that are unclear. Multiple students get lost due to this and seemly refuses to share vital detail of the project. Also tends to be sensitive regarding attendance and commentary about his teaching style when the whole class is struggling. Students have and will fall asleep in his class.

Had a midterm and a final project.The midterm was not bad we just had a hard question at the end but the final was tedious since there were progress report presentations, a final project presentation and a paper report.I feel like if the assignments were spread evenly throughout the semester it would have been easier but overall he is a caring guy.

It wasn't an easy A class, it was hard and his lecture can be boring but he is very accessible outside of class. He helped our team with our final projects, he gave us guidelines and so on. Even though the lectures are boring, he cares about his students and explain nicely if students asked questions. It was a hard class but doable.

Terrible lectures, he won't let you take pictures of his (useless) slides but he will talk too fast for you to take notes. you won't do any coding in class. 2 HW assignments, midterm, and a final project. He expects a lot for the project: 3 presentations, 9 page paper, GitHub, + the project. His grading criteria is not clear at all. Learned nothing
sucks at teaching and assumes this is the only class you are taking. also doesnt teach you any code yet expects you to fully code a machine learning algorithm for the final project

Ozer is a terrible prof when it comes to teaching. All of his lectures are very boring and he just talks about theories and then expects you to code a ml algorithm for hw when he hasnt even shown you a single line of code. He also has a final project where he requires 3 presentations, the last one being 45min long as well as a 9 page long report.

lectures quickly, i spent time outside of class filling in my notes. really knows what he's talking about, answers questions well. allows cheat sheets for (not pop) quizzes/exams. you can learn a lot in the class. the material itself is super interesting, just hard because it builds off physics2, integration heavy. curves heavily, nice guy!

His lectures are absolute garbage. Just reading from slides that are screenshots from the textbook. The saving grace is that his quizzes aren't absolutely horrible and some would say even easy, however, the material is very hard and you have to be motivated to teach yourself with youtube. Going to class is a waste of time

If you need the professor to walk you through every step then Kim probably isn't for you. He lectures super fast and there is a heavy chance you will probably have to learn a lot of the content on your own. There is a heavy curve at the end of the class so you will probably pass if you study but it will be quite difficult.

This professor teaches straight out of the textbook, so it's easy to follow even if things are confusing during lecture. Quiz and exam problems are pretty similar to problems covered in lecture, so there aren't many surprises. Make sure you work practice problems on your own without looking at the solution and you'll be fine.

Dr. Kim's analog courses are pretty tough and he makes you work for your grade. Simply sitting through lectures and relying on the homework will not get you an A. He makes you think on quizzes and exams, but never asks anything tricky or impossible. Takes a while to understand what he wants, but once you figure him out, you're good. 10/10 professor

This class was very conceptual, so it helps to read the textbook and not rely on lectures alone. Lectures were pre-recorded posted on BlackBoard weekly. 2 homework assignments, 2 quizzes, 2 midterms, and a final. He lets you use cheat sheets for each quiz and exam. Gives partial credit, so show as much work as you can. Dr. Kim is a great professor!

Let's face it, Dr. Kim's class is not an easy A. His quizzes and exams are quite a bit more difficult than the homework, so you'll need to work extra problems in preparation. Dr. Kim really knows his stuff and is 100% willing to help if anyone is struggling. Plus, he curves everyone's grade at the end of the semester. Solid choice for a professor.

Weekly quizzes, but they are not hard. His exams aren't that hard either, and you are able to use notes and slides from class. If you have his lab class, his lectures line up with it. Prof. Torousian cares about all of his students, and wants them to succeed even after college. He even provides projects they can do to boost your resume.

Answers any and all questions clearly, gives good lectures, only assigns optional homework, and has a sense of humor. Can occasionally come across as condescending, but is easy to look past. Highly recommend trying to get into his class before all the spots fill up.

Great professor who is always ready to ensure his students grasp the concepts. Although the lectures can sometimes move a bit quickly, he uploads his notes online. He is also willing to slow down and repeat any concepts if you didn't understand.

At first can be helpful goes through the steps and answers questions. Sometimes felt kind of intimidating bc he expects you to have prior knowledge. Graded on lab reports and a final. Lab reports done with lab partner and can leave early if you collect the data part.

He said he was going to make the labs harder and he did. He is caring and knowledgeable. The lecture itself can be challenging and this is an extension of it but for lab. Talk with your classmates and try to ask the professor questions. He's a solid choice regardless.
great professor, would definitely take again. He is definitely my favorite cpp professor.

Solid professor for lab. Grade is comprised of lab reports and a final. They are willing to go over topics and troubleshoot circuits with you as long as you ask. Lab reports can be a little tedious, however you work with a partner on them, and can leave early once you have all your data collected.

He was always clear about every lab and encouraged to ask for help if need be. Every lab he gave us was explained in enough detail to understand at the same time he'd be willing to help if something looked off. He is flexible as long as you put in the effort. I recommend him.

I think he is a very good professor. He knows his subject and willing to help. If you ask questions, he will explain very well. He is working in industry, if you ask any question about internships, he will help a lot. I enjoyed his lab.

His labs are not that hard. He's always willing to help with your labs, but sometimes he does not realize the lectures are always behind labs. He has clear expectations and guidelines on his syllabus. The only real gripe I have is that he does not have office hours.

Lab was a struggle for me since I struggled with circuitry but it really did allow for learning by doing. Prelabs must be done beforehand & sometimes include background lectures of the material. The material in lecture and lab do NOT coincide. Formal reports and the project should be done asap for the best feedback as his grading can be confusing.

This class can get tricky with so many topics crammed in a class, but Dr Chang made the material understandable and had very reasonable expectations. His online notes are horrible to study from so be ready to be in class and take your own. Learn by doing the hw and follow up with questions and you'll do just fine on the exams.

Very good lecturer and enthusiastic about the class. Homework is definitely a must because it reflects what is on the midterm and final well. Some concepts in the class are difficult to understand but he is very good at explaining. Helpful in office hours as well. Great professor!

This is not a bad 3, I just think more could've been done for this class. He was a fun guy to take but I think it was made a bit too light at times. Lab was reasonable and he always gave good feedback and advice when asked + the final project isn't too hard. Would definitely take him again just be aware that you'll get out what you put in

Every exam was open notes and open book. He gives all the solutions to the HW problems and is a very clear grader. Overall this class was very easy and he was a fun and engaging lecturer. He also cracks jokes every now and then and tries to make the material interesting.
Professor Chang is a solid instructor. He explains concept extremely clear. He also teaches you tips and tricks to make difficult concepts easier to understand.

I love how he always makes sure the class is following along. I like how he teaches both theoretically and mathematically, giving examples to show us how problems are solved. However, homework is unnecessarily harder than his examples, and it takes hours to do each week. Exams are easier and look more like PowerPoint examples. Exams are curved.

Great lectures with real-world examples. The two midterms and final exam were very fair, although his grading system can be a little harsh. Just do the HW without cheating and thoroughly study his lecture examples, and you will find his class to be useful and enjoyable. He's a solid professor with industry experience, would recommend.

Great professor for Mechanics of Materials. Has interesting lectures and posts the slides on canvas, although he goes a little fast. Midterms weren't too bad and final was fairy easy. Homework was tough but was a good tool to study for midterms/final. He curves slightly at the end of the semester.

Prof Pratt is a great choice for 4510. He assigns homework every week and it's tough but you can get through them using in class examples. Midterms/Final are manageable if you make a good cheat sheet for them. Gives good feedback and will respond to emails fairly quick during the week. Lectures are posted online so you don't have to write a ton.

The homework gets a bit heavy at times, but it's VERY helpful. The tests are something to get used to, so get ready to study. My only problem with pratt is that he doesn't give the curve until the end of the final, so you don't know your actual grade until later, especially since the first midterm has a low average.
Dr. Hormaza is a pretty good professor. She's not easy but I'd take her again. Would recommend for 3011.

Had her for electrochem, not thermo. Overall a decent professor who cares about the class. Sometimes gets lost in lecture as this was her first time teaching the course, but explained the concepts we learned well. I imagine she will teach this class better in the future. Midterm and read quizzes were hard but the final project will boost your grade

Don't understand these negative reviews at all. She's new and still figuring things out, but she's really nice. Some concepts you need to for thermo weren't taught in our prereq classes. It definitely affected this class, but that's not her fault. Would absolutely take Hormaza again and would recommend to anyone.

Do not take unless you have the time to TEACH YOURSELF using the textbook and homework. She treated the class as if we already knew everything and raced through the fundamental chapters. Only good thing was that she was very open to suggestions since she's so new. But you will learn NOTHING from her and it will hurt you in future courses.

What an absolute nightmare of a class. You have to teach yourself the material and the entire time you are treated as a six year old. If you have the misfortune of taking her as a professor, just study the homework. This is NOT the professor to take for a fundamental class

Took her during her first semester teaching and she has lots to improve on but did extremely well teaching and helping students during class. Was very open to feedback and improving on how she taught and the test reflected that. Would take again, even with the rough patches.

We were her first class so there was a lot of adjusting and figuring things out, but I think she did really great. The material is hard as is, but Prof Hormaza really wanted her students to pass and it showed. She is willing to work with you as long as she see's effort. I would recommend taking her!

Shes a new professor but her effort to listen to class feedback & try different approaches to teaching made the class easier. I can say she is one of the better Thermo professors. No curve, but does give fair partial credit on her exams. Lectures were useful to attend and did use hw examples to review the lessons taught. Exams were similar to HW.

This was her first semester, so it was a little rough, but I thought she was alright overall. She wanted everyone to do well and pass w/o making the class super simple. The quizzes and exams were hard considering the 50-minute time limit. I learned a lot though, and she's friendly! I recommend you take her.

Dr. Palomo is like Professor Snape in Harry Potter strict and tough at first, but by the end, you realize how much you've learned. Her courses are challenging, but they shape you into a better engineer. I believe she alone carries the reputation of the Environmental Engineering program at Cal Poly. If you're ready to work hard, take her class!

While she offers extra credit and manageable tests/material, her teaching style is disorganized. Her inconsistent grading swings between overly strict and lenient. The workload, especially in lab, is excessive for the credits - it should be a 3-credit course given the amount of work required in lab. Take this professor if you are a masochist.

Dr. Palomo is a one of my favorite professors since she really pushes her students to actually learn something rather than just teaching the info to take the next exam. If you listen to lectures, take good notes, and actually read the textbook you will have every HW and exam question right in front of you. If you dont, then her class will be hard.

I had her for the course CE5200/CE5300. She assigned A LOT of reports but grades leniently. I was also going through some personal things and she was very sweet and led me to some resources. It's a lot of work, but it's not difficult, and you can tell she really cares for her students.

Undoubtedly one of the most difficult and inaccessible professors at CPP. Homework is assigned like busy work. Grading for quizzes and exams is strict and oftentimes unforgiving. My (least) favorite is not being able to keep exams or quizzes to learn what you did wrong or how to improve. Avoid if you can. If you can't, good luck.

My 1/5 comment vanished last week, replaced by a 4/5 on Palomo's long list of 1/5 comments. Something fishy ;) Palomo's explanations cause a lot of confusion, gives dull lectures, lacks empathy, and is inaccessible for help. Steer clear of this professor, or avoid environmental option.

Dr. Palomo is a great professor and you really learn alot in the class. The structure of the lecture is pretty intense and requires so much time and effort so you will probably prioritize this class. I am currently taking it right now and I am currently overwhelmed and tired, but I have learned so much that I really do not care.
The only thing I ever learned from Dr. Palomo is that I do not want to be an environmental engineer

Do not take this professor. She never gives any feedback for any quiz or exam. Once the quiz/test is completed you never see it again, so you cant look back at other quizzes to prepare for tests because you dont know the questions or which ones you got wrong. I went to office hours and that didnt help either, one of the worst professors at cpp.
Avoid if it isnt a required class. Lot of work. If its required. Good luck!

Not a great professor. Puts up a facade of being inclusive and caring for her students, but has obvious favorites and is noticeably meaner towards Asian students. Expect a lot of homework and to work for your grade. Good luck.

This professor is the worst, she does not respond to emails, she straight up lies to you about giving extra credit. Anytime you submit an assignment even if its 100% expect 30 notifications of her leaving dumb comments like "??" and "So" all over your paper. She has zero care for her students and piles work on you as if its the only class you have.

By no means is she a bad person. That being said, she listens to the opinions and tries to make compromises, however it is not worth the effort. Additionally, she floods her students with work as if it is the only class a student has. Finally, never expect to be provided homework answers after completion nor testing material after completion.
Good luck if you take her

Please, on everything do not take her. Every time you ask for help she just refers you to the textbook and proceeds to read off of notes that you already took. She takes off a lot points on assignments for small reasons. PLEASE don't take her. Doesn't teach but expects us to know everything.

Lectures her own way and then assigns problems in the textbook that is phrased differently. Grading criteria is usually unclear. Open note quizzes/ exams but has enough problems to prevent you from having time to look at the notes once bc you wont finish otherwise. Feedback is only from office hours Im assuming. some ex cred opps, take advantage

taking palomo online for CE 4201 lecture and lab. sadly, this class is probably a requirement for you but if it is not avoid at all costs. she does not care/listen when students are overwhelmed. no empathy, extremely tough grader, and between lecture and lab its almost impossible to stay on top of anything for this class.
If you have another option take it, this class is not too difficult but its super-specific and annoying, and she goes out of her way to make things annoying for you.

Learn to do research just to find equations on online. Book Helps sometimes but not all the time. Make sure you save at least 20 hours for this class. Not a responsive professor so good luck! DO NOT TAKE!!

late add along with a few other and needed some catching up, tried working things out to hopefully be allowed to submit MUTIPLE assignments missing and elaborated on my reason, however, that was no good. Hand out take a large amount of time about 7 hours & she grades them. expect at least 20 hours of study form this class. not 3 units
Hardest class I ever took, unorganized and there's no point of even trying to talk to her.

I took her for CE 4201&3201. Like she's a nice person but as a professor she's not good at all. She expects alot out of you & then if you try to talk to her about something that doesn't seem fair, she'll "listen" but she won't listen listen. I dread going to this class since she is disorganized. She assigns too much in a timeframe & expects it done

Professor Palomo is literally the most confusing professor ever, she says something then does something completely different. Her schedule is all over the place and she doesn't care about how you're doing. Her exams are really hard and don't even think about getting partial credit. she's very apathetic. try to avoid at all costs.

Dr. Palomo as a person is nice and caring. As a professor, I'd avoid her. The class deadlines, the grading criteria, and lectures are all over the place. Her explanations aren't clear and it's impossible to get an email response. Office hours start >30min late. Be ready to read a lot. Group project. Quizzes/Tests are timed: zero empathy shown.

Very knowledgeable, funny, and insightful in career. Class is mostly making hand drawn site maps and some microstation work. Workload is very heavy at the end. 10 page paper as a final as well. For the drawings, FIND A GROUP TO WORK WITH, and have a person use a tablet with google earth (this will save you hours). He grades all at the last minute.

It really is an easy A if you just do the work but the work is very tedious since it only consists of hand drawing with minimal use of micro station. He also told us 4 separate times "this will be your last drawing of the semester" only to assign us a new one next week. Overall, DONT take him unless hes the only one that fits into ur schedule.

I felt like his class wasn't crucial to my learning. We barely worked on CAD and only did hand drafting, he switched the final the week prior. He also makes it seem that his grading is very strict and the hand drafting needs to be perfect but wont grade anything until the last couple of days. No email responses, office hours posted, or syllabus.
dont take the class, doesnt do well in teaching cad, and spends too much time teaching paper drafting. also assigns some busy work essays that are super long. still easy to get an A.
Any words that accurately describe this man will get this post removed, that's all I have to say.

You will have to take this professor in order to receive a CEM Degree at CPP. You learn hardly anything useful in his classes, and will spend a lot of time doing homework. He's conceited, rude, arrogant, and horrible with student feedback. Coming from a student graduating with honors, I hope the school will finally step up and get rid of this guy.

Considering the class was only 2 units, there was a lot of work. Most of it is easy and his lectures are solid. He's welcome to answering questions regarding lectures, assignments, and his engineering experience. Follow his instructions and getting an A is easy.

I think that if you take this man, he will give you so much feedback that it will help you outside of class. He honestly cares for you and is very understanding. The only thing that's tedious in this class is the hand drawings in the beginning.

Hes alright. Class is dumb easy, but explains things like hes teaching kindergarten. That would be great if he was teaching a higher level class. He also adds ridiculous 10 page papers weekly on pointless subjects (2x spaced). Ridiculous for a 1 unit class. Also did not learn much design (wasnt even cad was microstation)

I was scared of taking this class because of previous reviews, but take him you won't regret it. He teaches very well and is a respectable guy. He assigns one assignment weekly, but that assignment would take more than 10 hours to complete. It's not hard it's just very time-consuming. Don't miss class, your grade will drop by a lot.

Cool and serious guy, doesnt like it when you ask him questions but he is very clear in his lectures. It was weird being online with him because he always had his video feed on a piece of paper where he would write notes and would get blurry. So we never saw what he looked like. Assignment heavy but very similar to the exams. Recommend.
Lectures explain the homework clearly and the tests/projects are quite easy. Very helpful and reasonable teacher.

I loved professor Babikian! His lectures were awesome and hes very understanding! The work is manageable and he teaches really well. I had him for the online semester and I am so glad I got him! We do have a couple of 10 pages papers however, they are really helpful and if you pay attention in class and understand whats going on youll be good.

I think he is very knowledgeable about civil engineering. I took him this semester for both lecture and the lab. The first part of the class was really good, I learned how to do CE drawings. Then, when classes moved online we had one meeting and weekly papers. 5-13 pages each. He didn't lecture anymore, no lab component either (no CAD at all).

he is a tough professor who gives out a lot of work towards the tail end of the class. Most of the assignments are field assignments and he doesn't give feedback until the week after. At the very least I am more aware of what the built environment looks like, and there is minimal microstation afterwards

Alright this guy isn't joking when he says the work will be between 4-10 hours of work a week. The first 5 to 6 weeks are nothing compared to the final few weeks, the work load increases quickly. He leaves you to figure out a lot on your own unless you ask him. Overall, I had fun in his class just be ready to work.

As a starting professor for a starting civil engineering course he is pretty alright. Yet he gives out a lot of field assignment work which while an educative experience was beginning to look more pointless near the end. He went over micro station a little near the end. Overall hes not bad if you have to take him, but if you can choose another one

Babikian is an excellent professor:) You will learn a lot in his class, like MicroStation Drafting and Hand Drafting Best of all, youll accumulate more hands-on experience with on campus site fieldwork:)
Excellent Microstation/ Civil Engineering Professor:). I got more hands-on experience with the Fieldworks when going to different CPP sites.
Babikian is a solid choice. Although he takes a long time to pass back graded drawings (We didnt get it back until two weeks before finals week), overall he is amazing.

Babikian is the best professor. Dont listen to what others tell you. I had him in Spring 2019 for CE1001/L, and it will be a class Ill remember forever and I will miss this class. Point is if you do your work and not be lazy youll be fine.
He gets straight to the point with lectures. He lets you out early often because he finishes teaching.
He will work your tail off - but you will realize later that it pays off when you get a job from it. Rock solid.

Good professor. He definitely knows h is construction stuff. Class isn't that difficult, just be prepared to work when he gives you the inspection projects. One other thing, read through the chapters and tab your book...it will benefit you when you take the mid-term and final. Overall: Highly recommended!
be on his side, other wise you are on his bad list, " kiss ass" he likes it
chip on his shoulder, very hard to talk with. his exams are the hardest of all.

Great all-around guy. Fantastic lectures, actively involves his students. He would make sure everyone understood the material. Passionate about his teaching and what he does with his life. Always in good spirits. Liked you as long as you were putting in effort. He is retiring but he will be missed.

Tarek does not teach and expects you to learn everything yourself. Your grade revolves around a project which in the end does not matter if it works or not. You will get an A- if you at least have something and an A if it works. He has favorites and can be disrespectful at times but also understanding sometimes. Ride it out, it's an easy A-

I love this professor. He knows how to teach. He know what he is talking about. He comes from an engineering profession where he was a CEO and he wants the best for his students. Don't argue with him. If he says you're wrong then you're wrong. Take the criticism and deal with it like an adult. You have to work hard to get an A.

Dr. Tarek is a very caring professor. He really wants you to do well in his class. You work with a partner and you figure out how to do the lab like a professional engineer. He is from the industry, so you will be well-prepared.

Professor Tarek has the potential to be a good professor but he begins to get sidetracked and talks about things not relating to class and he expects you to learn everything yourself. Project is "easy", its easy because you will at minimum get an A- but he will grill you over the smallest things.

No assignments. No exams. Just the final project. It got really hectic, just hope for a good group. He did have a quiz once or twice but they weren't even graded. He'll give you a hard time if your group hasn't made progress/makes excuses.

no structure to the lab at all. spent many weeks talking about bronco space to recruit more members. gives very little guidance on how to complete lab. claimed we would end lab early but were forced to show up week 15 when we could have finished way earlier. very passive aggressive. shows useful info for matlab at very end of course. worst "A" ever

there are no lab instructions. he talks a lot about bronco space(a lot). if you really want to learn about Control System, do not take him, I repeat do not take him. if you don't care about the subject, it is an easy super easy lab.

Tarek is not professional or respectful, leaves class, and tells students he's on his "layoff list". He teaches stuff you already know. Have someone in your team who knows Arduino. You will either get an A or A-. Gets upset if you "talk back" to him. People love him or despise him, the majority of people who like him are his favorites.

The first weeks will be annoying, then you get used to it.Tarek is a pretty good lecturer when he's not talking about BroncoSpace. There's no way you'll leave this class without learning anything.The class is all based on a group project in the lab, so focus on that. Tarek himself is a pretty stubborn guy and pretty obtuse sometimes for no reason.

Class is very easy but if you want to learn avoid this professor. Class was a waste of time since he does not teach anything and spends class talking about his club. He gives no guidance on how to use the software tells us to just google it. Wish I chose a different lab professor since I actual wanted to learn about control systems but easy A.

Tarek is a tough professor that has high expectations for us. He only wants us to succeed but we have to work for it. Lab & lecture are combined and class is dedicated to creating an EFIS within a team. If you get a good team and put in the effort, youll do fine. Put every bit of info into your binder & notebook, he loves to see everything together

Prof Tarek is initially hated by many for his sharp personality and extremely high expectations, but as the class progresses, you conform to his standards, learn electronics and components along the way, and finish with a project everyone is proud of. My only wish was to be taught more before we dive into high level projects with minimal knowledge.

Dr. Elsharhawy is an amazing professor and really cares about his students. I had him for control systems lab and he is a great lecturer and goes above and beyond especially if you show you are willing to learn and work hard. He can be strict and intimidating at first, but he is really a great person especially if you take the time to talk to him.

Take notes and show some engagement in the class and its basically a free A. He is a "tough love" kind of guy which can be frustrating but that's just who he is. The class is not structured and basically show up and follow along if he wants to do a lab or lecture. You have to spend like $50 for a motor you use for like 2 weeks. Again FREE A

He combined lecture and lab. No homework ever. Sometimes a quiz but not graded. His lectures are super interesting. We finish two week before finals. The entire class was dedicated to a group arduino project: design a schematic from scatch, buy the parts, put them together, code them, test them, then present to him. He grills you only to push you.
Very easy class if you pay attention, a lot of group work and will really help you in the lecture with some light reading youll need to do before class. Great Professor

There's no homework and tests. Occasional quiz, not for grade. No structure at all, follows his own course schedule for the first half of the semester. Changes his mind a lot about what will happen next class. Takes things personally, plays caring dad/disappointed dad. Group project only thing graded. Attendance grade may depend on last day only.
Great professor, really cares about his students and makes sure that they are learning. Gives a lot of industry advice, provides great feedback!
all the reviews over here are written by the professor. he also will send someone to the discord group to say how of a good professor he is. Dont take it even if you have to.

He cares a lot about his student and understands that school isn't all a student has in their life. He is a very easy professor, but he doesn't seem to know what he wants from students when assigning readings. If you ever messed with an Arudino, this class will be a breeze.

You will be given a few topics to research and have to figure it out yourself. About halfway through the semester his lectures brought most of the concepts together and things began falling into place. If you show effort you will get an A-. He teaches what he has seen as practical knowledge instead of checking boxes of topics to cover.

Tarek's avionics class is one of the most stressful classes I have taken. The material itself isn't that hard but he expects you to research everything yourself. The class also involves a semester long group project. Be prepared to get roasted for not knowing specific pieces of information, but know that he'll grade nicely and you will learn a lot.

Tarek is strange. He makes you work so hard on everything. The material isn't particularly difficult, but you have to search for everything yourself, which makes in astronomically more difficult. His teaching method is literally to learn it yourself. If you get any sort of result though, he is satisfied and gives you an A. Hardest easy A ever.

You will very likely get an A in this class and learn along the way. The class is fairly easy as long as you pay attention and learn the concepts he asks you to BEFORE the next class. "Technical Independence" is his philosophy, meaning he'll give you a few topics to look into and you better have a passing knowledge of those topics next meeting.

Tarek Elsharhawy is a very unconventional professor. His course focuses on being "technically independent," where students learn to do their own research and teach themselves how to study topics assigned by the professor. He gives little instruction but will make sure you are heading in the right direction when it comes to your project.

Professor Tareks class is based on tough-love and technical independence. Right away, he assigns you and a group a project, and you basically need to learn 90% of it on your own and figure it out. It is stressful, but its a technique that works cause eventually you will get it done and feel great. Hes a fair grader and cares about his students

You will probably get an A. Unclear lectures. No slides. No textbook. No notes. Never answers questions. Make sure you're in a good group or god help you. Make sure you can code in C, Matlab and Simulink. Be ready to learn everything on your own because you're expected to be a full blown electrical engineer. Harder than 3090,3011,4060 and more

Ok, let me put it nice and simple for all of you reading this. This professor will make rocket science look like algebra 1. YOU NEED TO TAKE THIS GUY. Best professor I have ever had. Make his lecture confidential. But rightfully so. He is just great.
Great professor, encourages self improvement and self discipline. The whole class is tied to a single, on-going project, so be ready to work in groups the whole semester.

The most caring out of my previous professors. However, he has this philosophy called "technical independence." In other words, you are on your own with reading and understanding of the material. It is up to you to find out what to learn based on little resources. You won't learn much, but you will learn how to write a great lab report.

Although he can seem tough in the classroom, anyone who has called him or gone to his office hours can tell you he cares deeply about your growth as an engineer. I struggled to find a job after graduating; Tarek made time to meet me in person, work on my resume, and make calls on my behalf. Great teacher both in and out of the classroom.

Tarek is definitely one of my most favorite professors. Really caring, knows us engineering majors are overloaded so he lightens the load for his class. Forms his lectures around his experience in the workforce, truly embodies "Knowledge Applied." Great words of wisdom from his time being an engineer and CEO. Wish I could take him again.
Worst professor ever. Cant teach and set a moving target for final project.

Tarek is the elements of avionics professor and he's excellent. He explains things very clearly and brings real world examples into the classroom. He is always available to student 24/7. Cares about you learning the material he doesn't sugar coat things and tells you if you're messing up. One of the best professors in the AERO dept.
Gives lengthy, difficult group projects with vague instructions, and its based on luck if you get a good group or not. Professor's grading is kinda unpredictable.
Great person and professor, although the class is difficult. Has quizzes that are sometimes unannounced, and midterms/final were pretty rough. Gives a lot of partial credit for exams and quizzes.
Class is painful. Good luck. Textbook is useless to learn from. Watch his lecture videos on Canvas for review. Again, good luck.

Professor is a nice guy but he makes this class unnecessarily difficult. The midterm and quizzes were a huge part of the grade but they were difficult and the average was always an F. He will not curve. Avoid unless you want a painful semester.

His exams are worth the majority of your grade and exam average was 57%. Final average was a 70%. He does not curve. If you do well on the final he will change your grade to what you got on the final. He will change homework due date if you ask. He does not give any study guides and exams are not like the home work or class examples.
Explains concepts pretty well and does great example problems in class. Midterms were average to hard, and final was very similar to second midterm. Very nice and friendly professor overall.

He made so many mistakes during lecture and wouldn't even catch it until the students said something. It made the new topic difficult to understand. Went to office hours and he just confused himself trying to explain and expected you to pick it up right away. He did give as many points as possible for the tests which was nice.

I really enjoyed his timber lecture & lab. I learned so much and the experience will definitely make you stand out to employers. It is a lot of work and take time to understand outside of class but if you want to pursue structural engineering you need to take his class.

The class revolves only through group projects. If you are stuck with bad teammates you are SOL. Lectures can be very long, but mainly it is to ask to review your report. His grading style changes throughout the semester so it is hard to predict what grade you'll get.
The most practical class I've ever taken at CPP! By the end of this class, you will feel like you are able to design your own house! :D

You will really learn something in his class. if you choose an easy professor, then you are cheating yourself. you will regret when you get a job. my advice is that always choose a professor who is though on teaching and grading.

6 lab reports total that are 40 to 60 pages each in length. The actual workload of this class is closer to 6-9 credit hours which is quite frankly insane. The professor is a decent guy but is a very tough grader. He will also give very general advice and leaves it up to you to waste hours on end researching building codes. Take anyone else.

This was by far the most difficult lab I have ever taken. You will definitely learn a lot in this class but be prepared to put in the time. Ask as many questions as you need to and he will answer all of them and guide you in the right direction. DO NOT SLACK OFF IN THIS CLASS. These reports will take a huge chunk of time each week.

CE3501 is an extremely difficult class. However, professor Gershfeld is willing to go all the way back to the fundamentals to ensure each student understands the material thoroughly. He will not move on until all questions have been exhausted. If you come to class prepared to ask questions and make the most of his lectures, you will learn a lot.

Gives a lot of work for a lab. Total of 6 labs and each one is 40 pages long. also he is a tough grader and the guidelines he gives are not clear at all. he wont mention how to design certain things and he wont bring it up unless you ask him but that requires you to be aware of it in the first place. so if you dont include it you're out of luck

Cool guy but cannot make Timber Design feasibly learnable for the students. The homeworks are incredibly long and he will prob not even grade them at a certain point because he doesn't have answer keys. The tests are tough with no study guide. Don't waste time on his practice exams they don't even match the exams. Class avg is failing grade.

Great guy but not the best professor. He gives way to much homework for a 2 unit class. To do the HW you will need the book. HW can range to 15-40 questions. You'll have a quiz every other week. And youll also have a couple of group projects. Overall good guy but gives way to much work. Be ready.

Take his class for the easy A. If you took heat transfer, you're not going to learn much more than you did in that. He's lazy. Doesn't switch tests or projects from the year before. He is knowledgeable in industry, however, so that is a plus.

Amazing and funny professor. She isn't difficult but the class itself is just difficult w/ a lot of memorization. A lot of material to remember but she guides you through the labs if you need help. The only HW is for her lab due weekly. Her tests are based off her slides and you have to go to lecture to fill them in. Would definitely take her again
a sweetheart, and super energetic. the class is not hard, and a great way to meet engineers as a freshman and also get rid of a GE course.

GSC3210. Professor Perez is caring and approachable, guiding you through lab assignments and sometimes completing them with you. Labs are easy if you submit your work. Lecture was challenging, with many students falling asleep during the 9 AM class. The midterm and final had low scores with most people getting below 70%.
The best professor I have encountered in a while. Made learning clear, fun, and engaging. Do not even think twice before having this professor. Honestly great class.

Dr. Perez honestly made my senior year at CPP my favorite. She's an inspirational professor and our entire class would agree that she truly cared about all of her students. Her lectures were not heavy and were very informative. She discussed different ways for us to make teaching fun for our future students. Her class was honestly my favorite.

THIS WAS FOR GSC 2120, but this website didn't let me pick that option. Very caring and made the class easy. She cared about us a lot and even asked for our feedback several times. She just wanted to make the class easy/chill for us. Even asked when we preferred to turn stuff in.
Great professor, she mad the class very easy. Besides the final essay, all homework are very simple and light in terms of time usage. Just do your assignments and you will get an A.

Professor Perez is great! There is no final, just a final project. Her assignments aren't too difficult but, you do have to put in work and show up to class. I would love to take her again! She cares about her job and her students.

Easiest professor Ive had this semester. VERY lenient grading policy as long as you communicate with her. She cares for your well-being and academic success. Very clear assignments. You are graded on effort basically. Group projects that she explains nicely. Enough time to finish any assignment she gives you. 10/10
Very nice and generous. Cares for the well-being of her students. Would definitely recommend her.

Great professor! She really wants you to be excited about engineering. There is a little bit of busywork, but the majority of the class is interesting. She's always willing to offer a helping hand, whether it be about her class or not. I'm glad I took this class!
Doctor Perez is a great, caring teacher. You just have to also care to learn the material. Go to office hours and ask questions.

Dr. Perez is amazing, makes statics easily understandable. She cares about the student and makes sure to accommodate them if they are dealing with some things. Definitely brings the zoom lecture alive. She goes above and beyond what my other professors do like working out problems in class. She makes mistakes sometimes, but that's what is great.

Really fun, talkative, personable professor. Knows her stuff, breaks down a pretty hard subject for most lower division students into small digestible pieces. Loves to give lots of partial credit if she sees you're thinking the right way. Overall I really enjoyed her class.
Absolutely love her!
She's super nice and one of the easiest classes I've taken

On top of being a great professor, she's very understanding and compassionate. She has an easier workload than a middle school class. There are no tests or quizzes, only one or two homework assignments per week. If you need extra time for an assignment or if you can't make it to class, she will be very flexible. And she knows her engineering stuff!

She is the best professor you can have in the department. I've never seen a professor care so much about their students and is the only one who can properly guide us in the right direction to graduation. We love her classes and will always show up to them even if we're beaten down from previous classes. Everyone should have her as a professor!
Perez is an amazing person and is laid back. She gets the material delivered to you in an effective manner. She is the best professor. Would highly recommend to be part of her class. Love you Dr. P

I had her during the COVID 19, so I saw her teach online and in person. Attending lectures helps clarifies what she is assigning and you learn some cool things, but you'll be fine if you skip a few lectures. Everything is on Blackboard. There's a lot of assignments (time-consuming but easy). Easy quizzes. Pretty easy A if you do the work.
I love this woman! She's really laid-back, an easy grader and has a great sense of humor.
Shes really great and you can tell she really cares about her students.

Kind of absurd no one's rated. Perez is one of the few saviors in the ETM dept. A transfer new to SoCal, I understand why Perez values balancing class time with check-in time. An anti-social environment being a commuter campus, so the care she brings to dynamics and her students is sunshine on a cloudy day. Sad to have advanced beyond her courses.

In class, the professor made an effort to speak to all the students. However, she is late to class more often than she is on time. One of the requirements for the class is participation in the PolyX showcase, which is group work heavy. Difficult to tell how hard of a grader she is, as she has yet to grade any of the 20+ assignments on Canvas.

Get ready for the Poly x if you take her for the fall semester, don't know what she will make the class do in the spring. She does assign a lot of busy work but it wasn't anything too bad. Lots of extra credit opportunities and was always available for office hours.

This class has a lot of emphasis on the PolyX group project, I found it quite fun so long as you bring the passion into your group too. One downside of her class (or upside) is that she is often late for class, usually no more than 15 minutes and 5 minutes on average. Make sure to establish a healthy connection with as many people as you can!

Made us do PolyX showcase even though no other professors made anyone else do it and didn't even show up for it. Poster for PolyX is apart of your final along with 2 essays and she still gives weekly labs and assignments for 1 unit.

Has the weirdest things happen to her and randomly cancels class 15-30 minutes before the lecture. This class is very group heavy, pick a good group at the beginning!! One assignment you don't do can affect your grade by a letter grade, she assigns so many assignments...pick another professor if you can!!!

Lot of assignments which weren't pased out well through the semester. Didn't grade until the last week. PolyX project was required despite it not being explained well. Lectures were decent and she filled up class time well. She uses up all 3 hours of class time. Would often cancel class last minute (literally) or show up late by up to a half hour

Someone get this woman a lucky charm because how do you get a concussion and into a car accident in a month?! She canceled meetings like idk 5 times, made us do the PolyX showcase, and didn't grade anything until less than a week before the deadline for final grades (she ended up posting final grades 2 days AFTER the deadline).

The things I could say about this prof. Attendance is mandatory, but cancels class last minute & is ALWAYS late. SO many assignments, all busy work that she doesn't give directions to. Forced to do the Poly X project yet never even depthly explained it & was late 2 the presentation. I learned more talking 2 her TA than I did sitting in her 3 hr lab

She was great with how she managed a three hour class. There would be like three different activities throughout the class and all of them are done with your group. Make sure to get along with your group because you do all the labs with them. There's homework every week and is fairly simple and can be done within an hour or two

None of the assignments are clear and a lot of them feel like busy work. The professor is a good person but the class is not managed well and expect to randomly have eight assignments dropped on you. The class is not impossible if you need it for whatever reason but the biggest downside is not understanding half of the assignments.

Took her for upper division lab, she is an awful professor. Cancelled class 3 times last minute, always late to class and field trips that she organized. Always has an excuse but who's gonna buy it every single week. It is week 15, and there are no grades in yet so that's annoying.

She does not teach the homework she gives out. The class goes from building water filters out of water bottles and making marshmallow and spaghetti structures to advanced trigonometry and advanced logarithms out of nowhere. All assignments just feel like busy work that take so much time out of your day. Class goes from 0-100 then back to 0.
Teacher cancels class often, makes understanding assignments difficult. She forces students to sign up for the Poly X showcase although no other professor does. Muy Lame.

Attendance is mandatory but she's canceled class 4 times out of the 9 we've been supposed to see her. We've seen her teacher's assistant more than her. If you're in MEP-WiSE, the other professors assigned to the program are not participating in the Poly X Showcase unlike her. Also, you stay in the same assigned group for the entire semester.

His lectures are extremely quick and he's a super funny guy. If you don't understand something, just ask him and he'll help you. One HW assignment a week, an easy midterm, and a pretty easy final project. First half was VBA and then the rest is MATLAB. You can also ask him questions about the ME department and he's more helpful than any advisor.

Professor new, rushes over lectures and you must ask questions for beginners. Idk about coding, and this class pushed my limits a lot. Would do homework the day of, not recommended. 1 homework every week, 1 midterm, 1 group final. learned a lot about code, and could see myself using it in the future. Super cool MatLab stuff!! Good prof

There is a level of intuition he expects you to have that you don't fully develop until later in the semester. The lectures are pretty short and straight forward. If you don't understand the material, he will work with you until you do. Understanding the homework, makes the midterm is pretty reasonable. Course-load will not eat up valuable time.

Prof Mitri was a fine professor. Short lectures and homework is relatively easy if you can figure out the problems. He explains the content thoroughly enough and gives examples that somewhat help with the homework. One homework assignment every week, two midterms, and one final project. First semester half was Excel VBA and second half was Matlab.

Prof Mitri was a solid professor. The lectures were typically very short but I'm pretty sure that's simply because there wasn't that much to cover. But he still explains the content thoroughly and gives examples that provide some insight for the weeks homework. There is one homework assignment every week as well as two projects and two midterms

This man is amazing he goes above and beyond whether it's in the classroom or outside. He got his degree soon so he understands what it's like to be a student. He is down to Earth and is very fun to be in his class. 10/10

Really enjoyed this lab because of Fred. He is easy to talk to and explains concepts with ease. He gives great feedback on the lab reports and grades them in a timely manner. He also gives great advice on how to navigate the ME department. Highly recommend him for this class. Wish he could teach the lecture for thermal fluids.

I really enjoyed this class and learned a lot about thermal fluids. But I also walked away with a better understanding of industry practices, how to use Excel/formatting, and how to navigate Cal Poly Pomona's ME Program. Fred was very enthusiastic about the material, shared his expertise, and showed great interest in the success of his students.

She's very professional and straight to the point about the topics. Her midterms focus more on the concepts of her review packets rather than being the exact problems but the questions are still fair game. Study her discussion questions too. Take the EC offered. Know the basic steps for solving each topic for the final and you'll be good.

Great lectures, very organized class. She is super kind and knowledgable, she cares so much about her students and takes the time to get to know everyone. Her exams are very fair, just study lecture examples and HW problems. One of my top professors at CPP.

Dr. Kim is not just an amazing professor, but truly cares about her students. From the beginning she seemed invested in us and people and asked about our lives outside of school. She was always ready to offer helpful career advice when asked and to help us with Statics. Great teacher, great experience. She made me love Statics!

Very grateful to have had Dr. Kim for statics. Her lectures were organized, neat, helpful, and amazing reference tools. She took time to talk to us as a class and treat us as peers while also providing fantastic mentorship both in and outside of class. Study guides prepared us greatly for exams. I will continue referencing my notes from this class.

one of the best professors in the CE department, her lecture in class examples were very similar to her quizzes and exams, very fair grader but does expect a lot from her students. Homework was turned in at the beginning and was from the textbooks, she cares a lot about neatness, and grade was based 75% 2 exams and final 10% hw 15% quizzes.

Took him with another professor teaching the same course but professor was very chill. Everyone liked him a lot more because his lectures were straight to the point & made the topics easy to understand. He was also very funny. He points out what are on his tests so just remember to write it down & his tests are easy because you can argue either way

His lectures are next to useless, you're better off reading the textbook. The examples he does have no context behind them, so it is essentially him vomiting equations at you for 40 minutes str8 and it will not help you with hw at all. He tends to ramble as well, and this leads to him going over time in a 2 hour lecture class.

Dr. Ahmadi gives useful and engaging lectures. He usually spends the first 30 minutes of class going over important dates, Aerospace news, etc. The computer project is the hardest assignment, but if you start it early its not bad. If you can make it through 3011, 3111 is easy

This is my 1st time rating a professor here because he is THAT HORRIBLE! Haven't even finished the semester yet but this week within the span of 4 days, we have due: 2 hws, a project, & a quiz. Hes very disorganized, loves stacking you with useless assignments, lectures are useless, and hes flat out incompetent. Avoid at all cost!

If you are in the spot where you have to choose Ahmadi or Lin for Fluids; here's a basic sum up. Choose Ahmadi for better lecture quality, or choose Lin for a guaranteed pass. Ahmadi curves to a C, and Lin curves to a B. Fluids is an important pre-req, If I were to go back I would choose Lin, since I self-taught myself most of the material anyways.

Outdated, terrible grading system. Tests with no partial credit, homeworks that are actually decent but with basically no documentation of answers so you can't check your answers. Pointless computer assignment that encourages cheating and punishes you for not working with others. Class is difficult and lecture sldies prove to be thoroughly useless

One of the most outdated classes/professors. Lectures are horrendously long and always go past the end of class. He will not hesitate to move up a test with only one week's notice, syllabus is not accurate. Class average for all quizzes and tests were under 50%.

Ahmadi is the Dept Head of Aerospace at CPP. Despite title, he is one of the most disorganized professors at CPP. You'll take him or Lin, Both courses same (lin uses ahmadi material). Key info for projects worth large portions of your grade is found across multiple documents. its a hunt to find everything you need to get full credit on these!!

Ahmadi has got to be the most unstable grader at CPP. Spent hours on the Computer project just to get a 66%. Since the average was so low all the students complained to him. My grade went up to 94%. I AM NOT MAKING THIS UP! Tests are really hard to prepare for because his content is crammed with information. Also gives a negative curve at the end.

You can tell that he really wants his students to understand the material and succeed. He teaches the content of the class very clearly and organized. It is very easy to ask him questions about the class as he doesn't make any question seem like a stupid question and is always available either before class, after class, or during office hours.

He is very knowledgeable about the subject. The class itself isn't too difficult. The only cons are: his lecturing can be kinda boring (but you can always skip) and quizzes are definitely the hardest part of this class.

The most knowledgeable professor on Aerodynamics you will likely ever have. There is almost one homework a week and the two projects are worth a lot for this class. Often says a very inspirational speeches and makes you feel very good.

Professor is very knowledgeable, and cares about his students. Tough grader, one mistake and he will deduct points. His rants are enjoyable but sometimes go on for too long. The quizzes are hectic and you must read everything before hand to be able to answer the questions, and I mean everything. Tests are alright, not too bad.
The smartest professor at CPP ARO Dept. No wonder hes the chair. Call him aerodynamcis/wing theory king because he can literally calculate and explain without any ready slides or notes.

Very knowledgeable with great character, but this class is very frustrating. Disorganized, vague, and is the WORST at grading!! He looks at your work, takes it apart, and loves to deduct points and write criticisms for every little thing (dire consequences for a small mistake). 2 projects: both a nightmare! Quizzes/Tests were always EXTREMELY HARD!

Good professor and lecturer. Very understanding and works to help students better understand material. Some work is nitpicked for specifics, but it's standard. Definitely need to ask questions in class, read ahead, and practice concepts plenty to comfortably do well in the class. Overall, very caring professor, makes sure we get out work done.

Dr Ahmadi is a wonderful professor, with a genuine love for aerodynamics. His lectures are great, but he assigns lots of work at the end of the semester. The last three weeks of the semester we had a computer project due, two quizzes, a midterm, and a final. Oh yeah and HW sprinkled there as well. Great professor, but be prepared to work hard

Dr. Ahmadi is nice, respectable, knowledgeable, and cares about his students. The lecture slides are terribly organized and easy to get lost in. The end of the F20 semester (COVID Semester) was poorly planned, cramming two exams and a quiz into two weeks. He provides weekly homework guidance email tips, but not enough help for the computer project.

Dr. Ahmadi was deemed to be one of the best in the department pre-Covid but while doing school online he was always disorganized and understandably kind of demoralized. He is still very knowledgeable and works with you to solve your issues. Breaks down the material well and states his expectations clearly. Tough grader, but still your best choice.

Dr. Ahmadi is one of my favorite professors. He is very considerate about the workload he puts on students and will extend homework and assignments if necessary. If you have questions about a topic he will thoroughly take the time to clear things up. He genuinely loves aerodynamics and flight and you can see this in his lectures.
HAs a great lecture for each of his classes. grades harshly and be careful and look over your work to make sure grading is correct. If can take Dr. LIN

From what I have heard, Ahmadi is a great lecturer that uses the white board. But, he is a harsh grader. My friend said he got a 85% in a class of his and still got a C because he uses a true curve in the end. If you want to learn, then take Ahmadi, but if you want a better grade take Lin. Lin is a boring lecturer but is not a harsh grader like Ah

Pretty solid lecturer and nice guy overall. His grading on tests and can be pretty strict. Make sure you don't mess up early in the problem or he'll keep deducting points all the way to the end of the problem
Dr. Ahmadi really knows his stuff. All of his lectures are filled with useful information, which he's very good at highlighting. All of his tests are straightforward and fair.
Great professor, would definitely take again.
Very good lecturer. Learned a lot in his classes. His grading can be a little harsh on the homework, quizzes and tests.

Professor Ahmadi is a great lecturer, but be prepared to take extensive notes. To give an idea, this is the guy that has designed the curriculum for the entire ARO department. Take him if you can. The grading can be frustrating, but you will learn more with him than any other professor.

Nice guy, and decent lecturer. Could care less when it comes to students' concerns about grading though. I don't know whether his grader simply lacks a brain or is just following the old man's orders, but prepare to get nickle and dime'd on an arbitrary basis for EVERY SINGLE THING you turn in. Very frustrating. Take Chandler if you can.

he is clear his notes are really good ..dont ask questions most likely he dosnt know the answer and he would say "thats for graduate school" ..seems like we have a lot of work to do in grad school lol...and grading is really bad

Looks down on students who don't understand right away. He does not accommodate or help you out if you had some out of the class room problem. He once made the entire class retake a midterm on "rumors" that someone cheated, he never found out for sure. don't complaint to the dean because they are friends and protect each other.

This guy is Awesome. He makes everything clear and easy to understand. He is very enthusiastic about the material and makes it relevant to working in the real world. He is very demanding and you will learn a lot.
Awesome! Makes material clear and relevant. Not easy, but a great professor.

Avoids answering questions. If you don't get something right away you're screwed. Will assign extra work, to stop you from asking for help. Avoid for 461 at all costs. Almost did not graduate on time because he kept expanding my project last minute.

*Amahdi looks down at someone he likes taking the test and see they're doing the problem wrong* "Class now we all know..." He gives away the answer to everyone but hes really talking to his special student.

Great prof. Labs were amazing, lecture could have been tiny bit better, but overall solid. Quizzes are in forms of seminar for both lecture/lab.
