His "tests" are in the form on seminars where he'll ask you to solve a quick problem in front of him and then you can leave the lecture. I highly recommend this class!

Professor Oniciuc set my expectations low from the beginning because he was brand new to CPP as a professor and I figured there would be many growing pains. I couldn't have been more wrong. Oniciuc is one of the few professors who actually appears to care for his students and wants them to succeed. His labs are unique, challenging, and fun.

At first I had doubts about a new teacher, but this man exceeded my expectations. Of course this man has some improvements to make, but his patience is out of this world. He cares about students getting the concept rather then just wanting to mark off points. He can go a bit slower at times, but he is definitely one of the best teachers in CPP.

This professor has the biggest patience at CPP. He is one of the few professors in the ECE department who I don't fear will make me feel stupid if I ask a simple question. Some of his labs were confusing but it is understandable because it is his first year teaching at CPP.

All things considered - fair Prof. HW nothing too crazy, about 4 - 8 problems biweekly. 8 HWs in total. 2 exams - one was average difficulty, the other could be bit difficult if you didn't pay attention in class to his work (avg was 7/20). Final was more than fair, generous. Grading scale is accommodating and more than fair. Overall, not bad.

His attendance policy requires that if you're absent more than 5 times, that's 10% of your grade gone. 2% for each absence. And he doesn't care what the excuse is so don't bother emailing him. Tests were a bit difficult but doable. Homework was simple. No quizzes. He skews his grading scale. Lectures are well done.

He stated in class that attendance is mandatory and doesn't care about emails notifying him that students will be late. He even told one student that he wouldn't care if they had a flat tire. However, later in the semester, he cancels class when he gets a flat tire. Talk about double standards!

He lies; he falsely claimed that the test was easy. He gave an entire speech about how disappointed he was in himself for making the test so simple. Then, he assigns something that he only briefly mentioned once, significantly lowering everyone's grade.
Professor Akbari is pretty chill and easy going. He lecture from his own power points which are easy to follow, don't even need to read the textbook. Exams are fair and not too many surprises.

Off the bat very vocal about expectations being lax leaving class a bit disgruntled mid-sem when course took 180 turn. Retrospect, likely due to lacking student engagement. I trust future conduct of class will be more transparent/consistent. Wonderful professor/eager advocate for student success. Will have pleasure of taking again.

Had him for 3300 and 3300L. He's super cool and grades easy. Workload is super light. He's also very in-tune with the industry. You only get these types professor once in a while, so I was happy to have him

He is probably among the best profs left after the ECE department was restructured after COVID. He is a very understanding and caring professor who ensured that each student could confidently tackle the lectures and assignments. If a student was struggling, he took the time to help the student rather than make them fend for themselves.

Prof Van blerkom is a really nice dude. It's a shame I couldn't care less about microelectronics. He's very passionate about the material and does his best to explain. You're graded on a midterm and a final and in class assignments. Those in class assignments end up being 30% so be careful. He drops one and gives you an ec assignments so it's fine

Professor Blerkom's first year at CPP was okay for being his first year. The class grade is based on 2 midterms and a final. Homework is assigned but not mandatory. Each class consisted of lectures taken from the book, but I recommend reading through the book. He is a really nice and understanding guy and is willing to talk to you about anything.
She is a good teacher and has now started using microphones so you can hear her from the back. She gives good feedback and is helpful when you ask her for help.

You have to sit in the front in order to hear her. She calls people out a lot during lecture. Quizzes in the beginning of the class but normally she will tell you what the topic will be. There are two midterms and a final which are pretty hard. You gotta do a lot of extra studying. Good Luck!

Professor Yin teaches you what you need to know to pass the quizzes and exams. Everyone that says otherwise hasn't actually sat down and dived into the material. The class being boring isn't an excuse to stop paying attention, get your grind up lil bro. The daily quizzes account for 30% of your grade, don't get caught lacking. Read the slides.

Everyone's silent in class when she asks a question. Can you guess why? It's because she's beyond boring. I'd recommend no one to take her. I've never seen a class so quiet when a professor asks them a question. She will press you just for sitting in the back. The lectures were not good at all, useless in my opinion. Pick someone else.

Don't waste your time. An ECE professor that doesn't know how to use canvas or youtube...seriously. She doesn't know what she is saying half the time herself. Puts people on the spot when they ask questions and makes them feel incompetent. Quizzes aren't hard, they are just dumb and useless.

Class isn't too hard if you do 2 things: have an okay foundation in C++ and are can sit near the front to participate and listen. She explains concepts well, is open to questions, and wants you to understand as long as you speak up. Not as bad as everyone says, but if you do act up she will bite back, so just play it cool and things will be okay.

Not very friendly/accommodating/understanding of DRC disabled students since she didnt seem willing to extend time on Exams and Quizzes until after she talked with the DRC upset initially but they explained thoroughly

In my experience, she have been a good professor, despite what others said. Her lecture materials are easy to understand and accessible. She gives a quiz at the beginning of every lecture, it's usually easy. Midterms are significantly harder comparing to her quizzes. She does get emotional at times and get in the way of lectures.

The experiments in the lab are interesting and do a fair job supplementing the lecture. There is a quiz before class for the majority of the semester and can be tricky. There is a final project at the end of the semester and all work is individual. There is one report worth 10% of the grade but it isn't too difficult. Classes get out early.
SHE IS NOT A GOOD INSTRUCTOR, SHE IS EASY TO PASS BUT YOU WILL NOT LEARN MUCH FROM HER.
She is very sweet, and is helpful to a point, but her expectations are too high, and she doesnt explain what she is doing. most of it is copying and hoping.

Yin tends to be easy because of her exercises. She tries to teach but mainly just goes off the examples. She'll answer questions, but after a while, will get frustrated. Take her if you know how to learn programming by yourself
Pretty easy class overall. Lectures are not very important to attend. Group projects are pretty easy, and midterms and finals are all online. Nice and caring professor.

Super lenient professor. Exams and homework assignments are all online, you only have to show up for lectures and group presentations. Sometimes will give you extra credit for completing a group problem in class.

His class was extremely easy. Sometimes gave extra credit for showing up. Homework was extremely easy online. Exams are online on your own time and are pretty straightforward. Did not learn much econ at all but his class did not demand much time at all and he was a very nice and understanding professor. Only "hard" assignment is the group projects.

His class is very different from other professor in this course. Lectures are short, HW is online and real easy. We had 2 main group projects, all which are easy to complete. Final project is a group presentation and group essay report on another groups presentation. 2 midterms and one final, all are on online and easy. overall, easy class to pass
You have one group to work with throughout the semester, so choose wisely. The only thing that is heavy on work is the group projects; everything else is light work. Bro also got insane rizz

the class is all about 3 group projects, so make sure you pick some good groupmates. the projects aren't hard but can take some time so get started not too long after they are announced. he is generous on grading but that doesn't mean u can bs your work on the projects. the homework and exams were pretty easy and attendance was rarely taken

Class can be taken asynchronous if it is listed with in-person classes. There was a lot of canvas homework assignments. Midterms and final was online and not taken in-person. There was a group project in the end, but was not a deal-breaker for your overall grade.

Kept the lessons very simple and easy to understand. Also very approachable, easy to ask questions to and is very quick to reply to emails. Makes the class laugh every now and then, so you don't feel intense in the classroom.

Nice prof but didn't learn much. He wants you to pass. 3 exams and 1st question is given and worth half the exam points (hard to fail). 2 group projects and 1 final group presentation (15-20 min), about 3 HW's weekly with 3 ?'s each, very short weekly discussion post no need to reply to other student. Never takes attendance and posts the PP slides.
Class isnt too bad, video lectures explain what he is doing in class. Projects are not too bad either, mostly completed already when he hands them to you. Easy class, easy teacher.
He is not bad, he never takes the full allotted time for lectures, and he doesn't grade too harshly. He gives out very good study guides for his exams
You will end up teaching yourself. So, skip this professor.

Took his during the virtual learning shift. Has Q&A sessions before exams but otherwise you are on your own with learning the material. The exams are okay but the final was tough. At Least for virtual learning, exams are open notes.

If you are looking for an easy pace class, this is it. The class is fully asynchronous. Homework is credit no credit. Exams are decent. The minimum score you can receive is 50% so if you bomb a midterm you won't get a 0. The only downside is you learn mostly through PPT.

Now when everything is online he doesn't lecture, just sends a 15 mins presentation weekly and makes us read the textbook. He cares bc he gives minimum 100/200 on midterms, yes, but all the questions are mc, so small mistake can cost you 10 points. Still though, I expect professor to teach the class, not me teaching myself everything.

Chiang wants everyone to pass the class. Open note exams are hard since problems have twists (no partial credit, so procedure/answer must be right), but he gives minimum grade 100/200 if miss every problem normally (during the pandemic quarantine, minimum grade is 140/200). Only downside is group projects have short deadlines and are kinda vague.

Professor Chiang is okay. He is understanding and caring, and he literally wants everyone to pass his class (for real). He gives extra credit or sometimes gives full marks to all the class on quizzes. However, his. exams(open notes)/quizzes/projects are nothing related to what he teaches in lecture. It is hard, so choose your group wisely.

Prof. Eddin's lectures are all on his YouTube channel, so you can access his content anytime. A lab was done each week, & he made his grading scale so that you can still pass the class with a D even if you fail the midterms, as long as you do all the labs and final project. He's a very caring professor to all his students. I would take him again!
Simply the coolest and nicest guy in the ECE department at cal poly. The school is lucky to have him. His verilog classes are not difficult if you aren't a talentless idiot.

Eddin: - explains thoroughly, clearly, concisely. - gives many examples and is a very "hands-on" style with his lectures - very knowledgable in his expertise and is able to present his knowledge in an accessible way for students to understand the material. - he cares about his students! I took his 3301L class and watched his 3301 lectures online.

One of the best at CalPoly Pomona. If you actually want to learn something, take any of his classes. Highly recommend. Most if not all of his lectures are online and he is very great at answering questions.
If you want to actually learn something about ECE, take him. Great professor and one ALL cpp ece students should take at least once.

Very hard labs. Professsor takes too long to help. Very hard exams. Professor makes it sounds easy, but he doesn't realize how small errors which are hard to track can make it difficult to complete in time.

Professor Eddin is one of the best professors to teach at Cal Poly Pomona. He expects a lot from his students while going above and beyond for his students. His exams are difficult, but I wouldn't have learned from him any other way. If you have the opportunity to take Professor Eddin, take him over anyone else.

By far, one of the best Professors at Cal Poly Pomona's ECE department. The exams can be tough, but if you try your best, complete all the labs and complete the final or final project, you should be fine. Professor Eddin really cares about students grasping concepts.

This was the first time the course was offered so it wasn't the smoothest ride but was a great experience. The lectures were interesting but lacked hands-on activities; he's revising the course and addressing concerns the class had. This review will be outdated when the course is offered again, but he's a great professor and is worth the time.

Eddin is a great professor and the course is one of the more fun ECE courses. The course is structured such that you watch lectures on your own and then perform the lab only during class time. The midterms usually hurt people the most, make sure to prepare for them, he gives you a heads-up on them. There is a final project at the end.

3301/3301L Eddin was a top-tier professor for microcontrollers during the summer. This class required a good amount of work between the midterms and labs. Midterms were basically just more challenging lab projects. Personally, I liked this because it was more of an application to what you learn versus just memorizing stuff for a paper exam.

Professor Eddin is the cream of the crop at CPP's ECE department. He knows his stuff, wants you to learn, and gives challenging, but real life problems. No memorization of phrases, equations, or anything. Midterms are project based and final is a group project. Very fun, and useful course! This one got me many kudos in interviews!!!

If you want to just pass a ECE3300 without learning much, don't take this class. He explains the topics very well, but his assignments also ask a lot of your attention. His labs and midterms are no joke. That being said, you will learn A LOT from this guy. You truly do learn from doing with this guy.

This course is different than most in that the lecture and lab are with the same professor, and the grade for one is the same for the other. Eddin can explain topics fairly well and is willing to clarify if you reach out. Good prof overall. The grade consisted of 13 labs, 2 midterms, and a final projects and the midterms were like the labs.

This guy is one of the few professors who cares, and you can tell. This course can be quite challenging, but Eddin makes the material easy to understand with plenty of examples. He answers all questions and wants everyone to learn. Our grade consisted of 7 quizzes and a final; no midterm, and the lowest quiz grade was dropped.

I took him for the summer and he has to be the best professor I've had so far. He really gets to the point of the lecture and tries his best to get you to understand the concept. He's very reasonable when it comes to homework, quizzes, and exams. He really tries his best to make it simple for you to understand even the most difficult concept.

Great professor all around. I enjoyed the class and learned a lot. There are few quizzes and tests. And very few HW assignments that are collected. HW is pass or fail and he didn't grade many of them so I lost my A. Exams are easy, and quizzes are easy once you get the hang of it. But all around he is a great professor!

covers phasors, complex/real/apparent power, power triangle, phasor transform, review of nodal & mesh analysis, equivalent circuit theorems, etc. Great lectures, very clear & easy to understand; textbook optional. Very helpful & accessible both inside & outside of class, even to students not in his class. Best thing to happen to CPP in my 5y here.

My favorite professor in the ECE department (so far, at least). Very reasonable and fair. Also, I believe he is a good teacher and does a decent job understanding somewhat ambiguous questions. highly recommended

Took anas for 207 and enjoyed his class. He genuinely cares if the class is interested and involved during lecture. Would definitely take again. He doesn't give quizzes and doesn't curve his class at all but he tries his best to grade fairly and give partial credit. His midterm and final is very doable and average was a high C on both.

Prof. Pernalete is an amazing lecturer, giving lots of examples during lectures. Very caring and knowledgeable professor! Exams are based on examples you do from homework and in-class activities. A bit of a tough grader, marking off more than half of your grade per question if you get it wrong. But she's made me like and understand control Systems.

Really wants you to learn about the subject and increase your interest in it without just going through the material. Does lots of class examples and gives ample time to ask questions or clarification, grade consists of participation, a project, and tests which are all graded pretty leniently although there is no curve.

Good Professor, exams are easy if you practice off the textbook and classroom notes. She is all over the place while lecturing so it can be hard to follow sometimes, because she also speaks very fast. She doesn't care about the logic of your work you will get -10 or more if you get the wrong answer

She is the best professor I have had at CPP. Her lecture notes are thorough and she gives plenty of examples. Her HW was easy and just points to help boost your grade. All 3 exams weren't hard if you practiced problems from the notes and book since she gets all of them from there. She knows a lot about the subject which made it super easy to follow

She knows the content and has very in-depth lectures where she follows slides and writes content on the board. Most of the questions on the tests are taken from lecture or textbook examples so study them and you should be fine. Very reachable outside of class and content is turned in online.

This class was decent. Shes very nice. It was hard to understand when to meet on zoom & when to just watch previous recorded videos on canvas. When we needed to watch the lectures on our own time she was still on zoom during class time for questions. 1 midterm 1 final 2 CAs and 3 hw assignments. Exams are doable if you do problems from the book.

IDK how I felt about this teacher. minimal homework very disengaging online at least. harsh grader. the class content wasnt bad, but it didnt make me like controls. this class is good for you if you like self learning

A good professor to learn from. Hardly any homework, which means you would have to really focus in class and take notes. She makes notes on OneNote so I suggest taking notes during class so that you do not have to revisit the lecture. Also, the exam questions may be hard if you don't follow up in class and most of them are from the textbook.

I loved her lectures. The test was very much like the lecture examples however you need to pay attention to them and practice. She doesn't assign a ton of homework and she doesn't use powerpoint all is handwritten. If you get a small error on test -5 points. Allows Formula sheets that have to be submitted. Recorded Lectures and study sessions.

Theres not enough good things to say about Izadi, retired then unretired to teach statics and materials again. He is a great lecturer making sure everyone understands the basics of statics. Weekly to Bi-Weekly quizzes that allow for better retention of the material. He is one of the goats in the ME department.

I'm not gonna lie, this class was so hard. He also lowkey roasted me during an online lecture. He is a funny character though. Being in his class will alter your brain chemistry. The curve is beyond insane. I finished the class with a 52% and that was curved to a solid C. You have to do slightly better than average to pass this class.

I'm not going to lie guys, this guy is GOOD at what he does. Amazing lectures and made sure you understood the concept behind the material. Quizzes for 55% and Final was 50%, HW was 5%. Quizzes were challenging but if you did the homework you were fine. Final was challenging, but he made sure you were prepared with practice exams. C- was 47% avg

Take Izadi if you can. He's the most experienced professor here. He knows the material extremely well. He may yell or laugh at your work on the quiz, but it's because he cares and knows that you're capable of learning. If I could take him for every class, I would.
HES A GREAT PROFESSOR

He yells constantly during class . He makes you feel stupid if you do not know the answer to the questions he asks you during class. The midterms and exams are moderately difficult, not too bad. On the other hand it's impossible to get through a whole class period without getting a headache or being insulted.

Izadi is the best choice for statics, but there are better lectures online like Jeff Hanson. If you want an A and miss one quiz it becomes really hard, since there are not makeup quizzes and you have to be perfect on the rest. I got COVID and missed the first quiz making it really difficult to get an A. Possible to pass with a solid effort.

Anyone who says Izadi is bad still sucks on a pacifier before bed every night. This is the first class for ME that will push your buttons a little but if you actively listen in the lectures and DO THE HW then you will be perfectly fine. The quizzes and final are not bad if you study a bit. Best of luck!

If you take Izadi for anything, all I can say is good luck. If he gave decent lectures the class would not be so bad, but he is a terrible lecturer. He knows the content, but for the life of him he cannot convey it to his students in a good way. His class was practically an online one with the exception of quiz days because he always cancelled.

Do the homework, sample quizzes and office hours and you can probably manage an A. In my experience he has the problem of talking over students and kind of guessing what you are going to say and doesn't let you correct him until he's finished. Overall he is not a bad professor just ask questions if you can and don't slack off and it will work out.

He's a pretty good professor for Vector Statics. If you take him and want to pass, I recommend that you go to SI sessions and DO YOUR HOMEWORK!! Also, don't be afraid to ask questions and go to his office hours cause he likes that stuff. He also curved nicely, too!

This was an interesting professor. I didn't like his style of teaching, but he clearly knows his stuff. If you want to succeed, go to the SI sessions, do the extra credit, try to do the homework without looking up the answers, and watch Jeff Hanson on YouTube. He curves pretty good at the end, tough course overall though.

Class was formatted just like his 2141 class which I had him for as well. Majority of the ME department cannot even begin to compare to this man's teaching capability. ME 3501L references a lot of stuff from this class so keep that in mind.

God tier professor. Class is not hard as long as you actually try to understand the material since Izadi is very thorough in lectures. If you fail this class and think it's hard then be prepared for hell with later classes that are actually more difficult and have terrible professors.

You have to work for your grade, he explains the material clearly, he may roast you in office hours but it's worth it lol, do sample quizzes on handout, re watch lectures on YT if it still does not make sense, go to SI to get help and possibly 2% on your final. You will come out of this class full of knowledge or full of PAIN. Got A's in both.

I took him for both 2141 and 2191. You have to work very hard in his class, but you leave feeling like you've learned a lot. Be sure you study the handout homework questions. If you can solve the handout problems without help, you'll be mostly fine on the weekly quizzes. Be sure to attend office hours and SI sessions as well.

Get ready to put days and nights if you want A. anyone who received an A was either was retaking the class or knew the material already. His Lectures are heavy and he keeps talking with a thick accent and doesnt allow you a time to ask a question even if you raised your hand. He pretends that gave the option of asking with saying Is it Correct!!?

Izadi is that professor you have a love hate relationship with. You hate him when your taking his class, but then miss having him after. There was a review below saying he just yells at you and his lectures are hard to follow. For online, I would have to agree. His lectures would give me anxiety. You will have to work hard but you should pass.

Lectures are great, but sometimes very fast. If you don't learn the material, you will do poorly on the quizzes and final because they require absolute understanding of the concept. Grades on procedure. You must work hard to pass! Finished feeling confident in my knowledge on the subject. One of the toughest, but greatest professors I've ever had!

I've had him for both materials and statics and I can safely say hes one of my favorite profs. I find his lectures personally a bit hard to follow since he never really finishes his examples but there's plenty of online resources to learn the materials. He grades entirely on procedure and not correctness. HW is extremely useful but not worth a lot.

He genuinely cares about his work and students, but his ratio of speed in lecturing to his strictness about understanding what he teaches is difficult to manage. It's not entirely his fault as he only has limited time to teach, but because he demands specific methods to solve problems, it would help if he had more time for examples.

He's a decent teacher, but gets frustrated when people fall behind. It is easy to fall behind in this class because lectures are very quick and he gets frustrated when you don't know how to do something. His quizzes are most of your grade and they are extremely hard to do in the amount of time he gives you. Most of your grade is made up of quizzes.

His accent is not too heavy, but his muttering and stuttering is not helpful. He will raise his voice in an angry tone because he doesn't understand why the class is lost. He gives himself too much credit. He will often say that a subject is simple, yet he proceeds to do a poor job of explaining. Don't be lazy, and you'll get an A.

Professor Izadi stresses the importance of understanding the course material over just going through the motions to get the correct answer. If you do the homework diligently, and understand the concepts you will do well on the quizzes (I suggest practicing problems under a 20 minute time restriction to get accustomed to the pressure quizzes).

Lectures fast, lots of info, good professor IF you can keep up. Dont be afraid to ask questions, can sound condescending, but doesnt mean to be, ask during office hours when he's not pressed for time. Weekly quizzes, tough but fair, grades heavily on whether or not you understood the processes and concepts. Hw 5% if you dont have time, skip it

I selected the attendance isn't mandatory because his lectures are just pathetic. He speed runs through all of his lectures, and doesn't stop to help students, he just yells at us and gives no mercy fro his students. On quizzes he adds on extra little things, and gets mad when we don't do well on them. I would rather get taught by a fish than him.

Professor Izadi is easily the greatest professor/teacher I think I ever had. His youtube lectures are honestly amazing and were very vital to me getting a good grade in the class. A lot of people fail because they don't put in the time after class as this is their first real engineering class. I'll miss him when he retires

Easily one of the best engineering professors at Cal Poly. Grade consists entirely of quizzes, hw, and the final exam. His lectures are easy to understand, if you can do the hw fine, youll do well on the quizzes and exams. All his lectures are also on YouTube, so it wasnt affected much by covid. Always do the homework in order to understand it!

Izadi is a really nice professor for statics who really pushes you to keep on trying. He does a decent job of explaining the material but sometimes it feels rushed. Makes sure to conceptually get what is going on. He has a very generous curve at the end. I had a B minus quiz average and still ended up getting an A.

He's one of the best profs. Despite his age, he's really inspiring and makes you want to enjoy mech engi(at least for me). Stresses concept over recipe. You'll get exposed on the quizzes if you try recipe. The homework was long but in the end you'll do better on the quizzes and learn efficient techniques to solve problems. Final was fair. Take him!

Izadi is a fair professor. He's very passionate about teaching the class but can move somewhat too quickly during the lecture. Also, his lectures are very disorganized but he manages to cover all the topics he needs to cover for the day. He assigns a lot of hwk and most of your grade counts on quizzes given abt every week and a final.
Great clear and concise lectures. Helpful during office hours. Make sure to do all the homework. If you understand the homework youll get an A in his classes.

Stresses conceptual knowledge over formulas and recipes (gives you a formula sheet with the final). about 55% of grade is made up of quizzes given every 2 weeks. 40% of grade is made up of the final. Homework is useless grade-wise (worth 5%) but you better do it to reinforce the concepts

Took him for me 214 and again for 218. Truly a professor worth taking, its why his sections are always waitlisted. quizzes about every other week, homework as well. simply put, understand and master the concept of the current chapter, do extra problems and you'll do ok on the quizzes.

He teaches in a way that is understandable. Quizzes make up 55% of your grade and lowest one is dropped. Homework is worth 5% and is meant for you to practice. Final is worth 40%. He wants you to learn and understand the material, not just memorize some formulas.

Tough grader however he is straight to the point kind of guy . Lectures are clear and somewhat quick. Quiz make up half you're grade but if you master the material before quiz you'll be OK. Best advice is do more problems.

This professor teaches you what you need to know to become a good engineer. If you are distracting others in class, he will call you out. He wants you to focus on mastery, not memorization. He's blunt and to the point.

I feel like he genuinely cares whether you understand the material. His lectures go through material pretty fast but are very clear, precise, and he explains each step. The quizzes are very similar to homework. Overall I think he's a nice guy and good teacher.

Izadi made everything so clear, so applicable, and he made such an effort to be available to his students for questions and extra office hours. He does assign lots of homework, but it reflects exactly what will be on the quizzes. He deviates from the methods taught in the book and opts for less formula based learning and more actual application.

pros: seems to know what he is talking about, didn't miss any classes, straightforward grading, drops lowest quiz Cons; lacks the ability to easily convey information (aka bad teacher), when you ask questions he is arrogant, demeaning and interrupts you while talking which deterred everyone from asking questions, even when we went to office hours.
greatest person to ever walk this earth

Amazing professor. He is very knowledgable and he cares very much for his students. He makes sure his students understand the concepts being taught. It is a hard class, but if you pay attention and take the time to do the homework, you will get a good grade.

Hardest class I have taken so far. But the professor made it fairly understandable, the class was what I expected it to be. There is a quiz basically every week (55% of your grade) and a final at the end (40%), with 5% as homework. The curve saved my grade though, it is pretty generous

He is difficult to understand. Seems to know what he is talking about but isn't very good at teaching the subject. He told my class to give up and plan on retaking the class. It is a hard class, but he didn't help make it any more manageable.

best professor in ME that I know of so far, teaches what you need to know, feel lucky if you are able to get into his class. I was able to pull a B even though I dedicated sooo much time to dynamics in that same quarter. I felt I could of pulled an A and im sure you can too, put time into it though.

Izadi is probably one of the best teachers you will ever find. He knows his stuff and his only goal is to pass it on to you. He want you to understand it and not have to think about formulas. A must take for Engineering. BEST TEACHER!

Professor Izadi really knows his vector mechanics. He offers very insightful advice on how to solve problems that you cant get from the text. The class is basically broken down into 10 lab assignments worth 100% of your grade so if you miss a class, your not getting an A. You will have to know your statics inside and out to finish on time.

No quizzes were covered overall, but I learned a lot of useful content.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Sky is a great professor! There is a lot of reading from the textbook and taking notes, but as long as you do your best, you'll most likely get a good grade! She has no final exam, but she does have 4 review-heavy final assignments. Overall, I'd say the class was very informative and I learned a lot!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: In all honesty, Dr. Sky is an amazing professor and person; she is super bubbly! My only problem was that I felt overwhelmed due to the almost weekly note assignments and completing the reading on time. However, the workload does become easier. She is super understanding and not harsh with grading, so just communicate with her.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: One of the best professors on campus, you're in good hands. Her classes aren't hard, and the lecture isn't dull. She's very enthusiastic about what she does and will always hear you out. I plan to take her again for a different class if I'm able. If you're considering her, don't even worry.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great professor and her assignments weren't too hard. There were no tests but had a final a bibliography essay based on any topic. Had 2-3 assignments every week wasn't too hard. we had to read a chapter from the textbook and had to take notes on that chapter and upload them on Canvas. She did allow you to turn in late work but deducted points.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Sky is a wonderful professor! Since this course an intro course, we learned the basic foundations of linguistics. However, I learned more than I already knew. She posts videos about topics we discussed throughout the week in case we want to know more. She's motivating and really wants everybody to do their best. Would definitely take her again!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Sky is a fine professor who cares about her students and subject. This class has 3 simple weekly assignments: Chapter Notes, Summary, and a "Fun Stuff" discussion post. Midterm is a multimedia creative project and the Final is a reflection and portfolio. No quizzes or tests. Attend class, do your weekly assignments, and you will get an A.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: not a terrible professor, workload is not too much if you stay on top of it but overall a good professor she just lectures a lot but no need to take notes just pay attention. mostly everything you need is posted on canvas

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very interactive course: u spend most classes in discussion, and you have at least 3-4 wkly assignments but if u stay on top of everything u will do well. Dr. Sky knows her stuff and she makes the info relatable & enjoyable. It's a lot of work, lots of note taking and small assignments but she doesn't give tests and the midterm is a group project

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Sky is super nice and very chill. She has three weekly assignments which can be a bit tedious but are overall super easy. The assignments consist of taking notes on the readings which you turn in, an in class summary, and a "Fun Stuff" assignment due that consists of sending in a meme that reflects the class for that week. Overall, super easy

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Absolutely love Professor Valerie Sky! She brings so much humor to class, making it enjoyable. Her grading is super generous. Assignments might seem like a bunch, but they're a breeze with clear, detailed instructions. Plus, no finals, just projects and a few easy-to-handle portfolios. Getting an A is a given with her!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Reasonable amount of homework, no quizzes or exams, loooots of discussions and participation. Really try to read before class meetings because she asks a ton of questions, and if no one raises their hand it's either awkward silence or she starts calling on people. The hardest thing about this class is the mandatory attendance.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: You read a lot of interesting material. However, the grading criteria can sometimes be unclear. As long as you keep up, the class is easy.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great professor. Lots of discussions and group work but aside from that, the class is very easy. Overall workload was pretty easy. Hardest thing in the class was the final which was a group project. Would recommend her courses if you need to fulfill a few GE's. Would take again.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: One of the easiest A's to get. The first 2/3 of the semester is just watching movies and videos, with very few discussions/assignments thrown in. The last 1/3 is when she throws all the work on you. The midterm is a group presentation about a culture. The Final was the hardest thing, which was just a script for a game about IGE stuff, with ComSci.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: A great professor, and a pretty easy course. Be prepared to have lots of discussion and group work. Ms. Hwang seems to genuinely care about her students and put effort into teaching them, and if you put effort back into her class then you will get an easy A. I would definitely recommend for your Area F.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Most materials are given in class, so there's really no need to go out and purchase a book. She is really nice and actively encourages everyone to speak up.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: You had to read a lot and write some papers. Not too difficult just don't slack off.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She was honestly great overall, enjoyed how she wanted to include everyone and wanted to hear everybody's opinion. The only thing that was graded harder than others was her Midterm paper and the final group project, because they followed the IGE grading system. But overall as long as you stay on top of the discussions and faintly listen Easy A

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: An easy class for Area F GE, just be prepared to read (or skim and get a general understanding) of the weekly readings. She respects your opinions, encourages class discussions, and is passionate about the course. Group work can sometimes get annoying with slackers, but a great and funny professor overall.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Hwang is a very kind professor and will try her best to help you through the semester. That being said, there is a decent amount of reading and writing she will give you. 3 essays (4-5pgs each) along with lots of group discussions. All in all, a pretty solid and easy class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She is very very sweet and understanding. There is a lot of reading in this course, but it isn't overbearing. I recommend her.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: (COVID Edition) Took Dr. Hwang's class after having her last semester for IGE 1100. The number one thing that I loved about her was her personality. I would always enjoy coming to class every single time as she was very enthusiastic about teaching. I would always learn something new as she would ask students to share their own experiences. 5/5!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Hwang is such a kind person and you'll be able to tell that she genuinely cares for all of her students. The work is easy, so long as you read what you need to, discuss in class, and turn in your writings on time, you'll be fine. I can't express enough how much I recommend her class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: For a GE class I liked it. Professor is kind and smart and the assignments let you work with other students.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great class with a caring professor . She was very patient and understanding and took the time to meet with me to explain assignments

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took her for 1100 which is a great class. Professor is serious and smart and super interesting. She is caring and respects students who want to learn. Lots of group work and discussion and you are expected to participate but its totally manageable to keep up and worth it

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She is a woke white woman to a T. Brings up other cultures a lot to invoke in conversation in weird ways. She will pick on you in class. Expect to read 80 pages of random readings.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She is a good teacher gives way too much homework and isn't exactly understanding of your situation and is a really tough grader if you have friends in the class you could easily pass if you guys help each other out on the rrs and in class group work

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She's a very nice professor overall. However there's lots of participation expected. Talking out loud often and answering questions that will really make you think. Lots of reading and writing assignments. She's a tough grader on those don't expect an A on them. You can get an A if you do every assignment and put a little effort into them.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She was an alright teacher, expect to read 20-80 pages a week of random and mundane books and then compile 2-4 pages of writing per week as well as a few big essays and projects. She is a weird grader, She never gives out a 100% however an A can be attained if you complete every assignment, go to class, and pay attention.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: (COVID Edition) I took her for a joint class with Hyeryung Hwang. Overall, a very caring professor. She does seem to over plan the agenda and activities from the last class always seem to roll into the next. The zoom class itself is not hard, but she is a harsh grader on Reading Responses and Essays. If you want an easy class, take someone else.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She is tough, but worth it. I honestly think that if you don't like her, its probably because you're in school, but don't want to do the work. Reading heavy but the text is so so interesting. Mostly discussion based so you must participate.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The professor herself is very nice and emphasizes participation. Otherwise the class is pretty difficult, with biweekly 50 page readings. Most of the daily assignments are easy As but the Textual Analysis and Essays are graded tough, and she doesn't seem to follow the rubric at all. The readings themselves are somewhat interesting.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: As an English major, ENG 3000 is essentially your first real test in college, and it is no cake walk. While the workload and the demands she sets for class is extremely high, she really cares about her students and the progress they make, and she gives great feedback. Dr. Smith will make you a better writer but you've been warned: she's tough.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Really difficult grader, is not flexible at all in terms of assignments and work. Her instruction is not clear at all and her grading doesn't match the guidelines for her assignments. Do not take this class if you can help it.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This class was a pain but she really makes you a better writer and analyzer and she's super nice. I really enjoyed the class despite the fact that she is a VERY detailed/hard grader.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Smith is a genius. Her bi-lingual background gives her a distinct advantage when pulling from different areas of knowledge to apply in a classroom setting. She's also very sweet, funny, and she really cares about student success. Textbook use is mandatory. Whatever you do - do not show up unprepared or she'll pop-quiz the entire class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She is the director of the Grad Program, and she is rude! She doesn't answer emails in a timely fashion, and when she does answer, she is sarcastic and irritable. She doesn't give clear directions or feedback. She tells students that they're being vague, but she is the one who needs to be more specific. I do not recommend taking Dr. Smith.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Smith is an amazing teacher! She picks great books and she helped my writing so much. She's a tough grader but she gives amazing feedback. I learned so much from her class and I wish every teacher could be as great as her!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Awesome teacher! I love the novels that she produces for the class and the lecture engagements are always interesting. She challenges you to be a better student and you end up learning a lot from the class. Attendance is important and so is participation but that is what makes the class fun; is when you engage with the readings. Loved her!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: professor smith was really nice and easy going. she does take roll every class so make sure you show up and she has pop quizzes that i dont think she grades. Overally very nice and helpful. 1 midterm 1 final and 1 group project. No essays!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Fantastic course. Wonderful Professor. The works that were selected were unconventional and engaging. I would definitely recommend this Professor to any and all English majors.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Jensen is a great professor, she is very sweet and understands students. I never had the best English writing skills and she gave me great feedback to make my work better. You will definitely learn something in her class as long as you put in effort. She is always looking out for students and will look out for you if you ask for help.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: First off, the guy was in the Navy so that can tell you a bit about what kind of person he is, respectable at times, strict, serious, and intimidating at first. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Took senior symposium with him. Attendence required, 5 allowed absenses. Almost every text we read during class was by one author (Ana Castillo). Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I hate English classes but he still found a way to make it interesting. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's a washed up/wannabe writer/poet who wasn't talented enough to become a renowned author, so he just teaches at a mediocre school (which he also fails at). Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: First off if you don't want to read , do not take this class !! You need to read for each lecture ! Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Corley is a burst of sunshine that is felt by all his students. He doesn't care if you like, only that you become a better person. The parallels between him and Jesus are undeniable. His class is a good prerequisite for life. Do some work, be social, don't take it him too seriously, except when he is being serious, and you will enjoy it and learn.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He knows more about this subject than anyone I've ever met but seems to expect his students to know the same amount. Advice? Do the reading and participate, and you'll learn a great deal. Slack off, and you'll hate the class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He knows what he is talking about. However, he is very pretentious and condescending to his students. His discussions are very narrowly focused. The learning environment is structured vertically. I'd recommended taking anyone else available. You will learn more. Sadly, at the moment he is the only professor teaching American literature.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Prof Corley is certainly difficult, but he knows the material really well and makes his students think. However, he seems to have some weird philosophical ideas. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took Dr. Corley for a Master's-level English class, and he is often rude and haughty toward his students. I recommend that Master's students avoid taking his classes.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Corley is a really good professor. He knows his stuff. He wants what's best for his students. His class was difficult but extremely rewarding. I would definitely take another class with him again. He is one of those teachers that aren't too old that they don't relate to you and are extremely intelligent and know how to get the class to learn.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's very helpful but you cannot be scared of him. He doesn't bite.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: It takes a lot to make American Lit approachable but Corley manages it. Hes tough and likeds to drown you with reading but its all for a reason. He's an army guy so he has high expectations of his students and you can tell. He knows his stuff, hes grounded enough to teach it. Not too into discussion but I never minded listening to him either.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This professor gave daily quizes on a ton of reading! Even though the quiz questions were easy, the class was time consuming because of the daily quizes. You cannot be late or absent because of this. There's one final exam and one paper to write. I received a good grade in the course, however.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Lots of reading, but jokes alot and lets you out early sometimes

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Burton's class was pretty easy. The whole course is centered around the novel Beloved. Theres some discussion posts, a mini essay, and then a final essay and presentation. Her class is not hard as long as you read and listen to the lectures. She's really kind and approachable, just ask questions if you ever need help or clarification.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Burton is very kind. However, sometimes her class lacks focus and clarity. The lectures are just discussions about the readings, and sometimes the conversation gets convoluted. There are two pop quizzes, one take-home midterm, and one take-home final. It is straightforward if you read and take notes in class. Share notes with classmates.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She's not terrible, but she often lacks clarity. I've had her for two courses, and she's not difficult, just unclear and a little confusing. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Fucaloro is such a sweet and understanding professor who actually cares about her students. That being said, this course seems to be outside of her skill level. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The projects done in class are super useful for future teachers and the discussion boards teach you new things as well. You are given plenty of time to finish projects and the feedback is useful. Very sweet teacher willing to learn from her students as well.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Her class was easy but her readings outside of class were hard. She doesn't want you to use translate and to struggle through which is what makes it hard. She is super kind and makes sure you understand the content by the end of class. She's encouraging and doesn't make you feel bad for messing up.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She did not require the use of a textbook for the class. She taught the lessons via Powerpoint and all the lecture material ws avalable on Blackboard. She is very helpful and likes to teach.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Cravello is a great professor. His ENG 1103 class is based around a book that the class choosesYou write 3 essays related to the book. He gives amazing feedback and he is trying to help improve your writing skills with said feedback. He does like to engage with the class and wants us to engage back and not just talk and have us to listen

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Learned nothing new or improved my skillset of writing. An English teacher that thinks can change your "perspective" on the world but just genuinely will not. It is fairly easy but gets boring.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Want to learn something from a GE? Take Cravello. His strict feedback is among the best I've ever gotten. Austerlitz's difficulty is severely over-hyped by the prof and is a mix of self-fulfilling prophecy and inverse-survivorship bias from all the bad essays he gets. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is a good professor. After taking his class I can definitely say I am a better writer. The book read in class is very difficult and was the hardest part bout his class. I didn't think I would get an A but I did thanks to the embedded tutors helping me with my essays. Without their feedback I would have definitely gotten a C. Effort required!!!!!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: this class was overall pretty straightforward but I would recommend picking a different class if you don't feel like reading. the reading was 1 book and it was pretty difficult to get through but if you are up for a challenge then would recommend this professor.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Chill asf

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Cravello truly cares about his teachings and wants the best for his Students. The book Austerlitz is one of the hardest books ever, graded on 3 essays and a cover letter, if you can write essays well and receive constructive criticism you'll be good. Kind of a hard GE so if you want an easier writing class this professor ain't it.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Cravello truly cares about his students and was a solid teacher. The class is graded by three essays and a cover letter on the most boring book known to mankid, Austerlitz. If you're a good essay taker you should be chilling. I barely understood the last essay and still received a B-, just shows that passing is very doable. Good luck!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor is a good guy and seems genuinely interested in the topics he talks about and teaching. Unfortunately, the book that you read (Austerlitz, by W.G. Sebald) is the most difficult read you will ever do. Grade is based on 3 Essays + Cover Letter. If you cannot pace your reading, or if you cannot read difficult texts, do not take this class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: For the average student looking to get GE credit for English, this is a class for those who actually enjoys reading and writing. You are expected to read on your own and it's quite a challenging book to read. You also have reading quizzes from time to time and responsorial inquiries that evaluate your understanding. Three essays in total. Good luck

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: he has high standards for freshman students coming out of high school. he gives you essays that you have no experience in writing on. he said it himself he never gave out an A+ in his whole career of teaching. hes very sarcastic that can come across rude. respectfully, he should be more humble because not everyone can live up to his expectations.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took Professor Cravello's ENG 1100 class last Spring and he was a very balanced teacher. He is extremely caring; he's invested and likes to learn about each one of his students. He is extremely clear and concise on what he wants to see in your writing so if you follow his guidelines and enjoy english you will do well. Great guy!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I had the pleasure of taking this class in the fall. Overall, he is not a bad professor but can be challenging. The entire course is based on 3 essays followed by a cover letter. He is tough on grammar but never received a grade less than a B-. If you write your papers ahead of time and seek guidance from the LRC you should have no problems at all

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Cravello is not the hardest nor easiest professor. He has high expectations for students, but his demeanor can make students unmotivated. For written reasoning, he does not help students develop points nor is he encouraging. He pushes students to reason, but makes students feel like idiots if they think in another way or are just trying to learn

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This class is not as bad if you are a good writer however if you are not, you probably want to look for another proff. Really picky about grammar and will call you out on it. He likes to refer you a lot to the LCR which is not as helpful. Class is also based on 3 essays and some class discussions. Also does not like to give out A's so be aware.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The professor made you earn the grade. He was not a bad professor and his lectures were on topic. He is not a bad guy, just a tough grader. However he does not give a clear rubric for the writing assignments. You have 3 essays that are 80% of your grade. You also need to turn your camera on at all times during class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Prof. Cravello is very set in his ways. There is no room for your writing style, he wants a specific type of writer. He goes off topic sometimes, but he answers questions. Going virtual, Cravello was accessible. Beware, no A's are given.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: If you're looking to have a bit of a challenge... Cravello is the class to take. He's extremely knowledgeable and can be really funny. The best thing is that he does not sugarcoat so you know how to fix your mistakes. You have the same reading questions for ALL books and 1 essay per book (3-4). There is homework for every class, but it is not difficult and are typically not long. She gives extra credit. She also gave us linguistics book if we participated

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Kermad made grammar understandable and interesting. She is kind, caring, and always willing to help. Responds to e-mails quickly. She really wants you to succeed. Highly recommend taking a class with her if you get the opportunity.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Kermad is definitely one of a kind. Her class was hard, but it wasn't her it was just the subject that was a lot to take in. She really listened to her students and accommodated when it came to what was difficult, test taking and extra credit. She truly wanted her class to do well and pass.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I struggled in this class, but at no fault of Dr. Kermad. she is a wonderful professor, and gives her students the tools they need to succeed. I really wish I had been able to take this class in person, it was difficult to take online. if linguistics is your thing, I highly recommend Dr. Kermad.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Kermad is one of the most organized professors I've ever had. Her online classes are well-structured and interesting, and I feel like she assigns the perfect amount of work to really teach the material without being overwhelming. I've taken a few classes with her so far and definitely plan on taking more.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: One of the best professors I have taken so far. She is very organized and helpful when I need to reach out on email. It is a lot of work but not difficult.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She is one of the most caring/knowledgeable professors at CPP. The readings were short and very interesting. I loved the structure of this class. Your grade is basically your participation and major assignments. You have to put in work but it is still easy. All the classes she teaches are similar too so you'll really learn a lot about linguistics.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Liza is very helpful and makes the class interesting. She also gives good advice to both personal and academic lives. Answers emails fast but can sometimes get confused by canvas' complex design. We got some assignments missing but eventually she made them available. Difficulty ranges from 1 to 5 based on your english skills. Would 100% take again.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: she's very kind and always tries to make class fun and i really appreciate that. although english was never my strongest suit, she always gave me the chance to shine and i actually really enjoyed class and made several friends from this class. she was really engaging and inspiring, always pushing us to be better. i would take her again if i could.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Overall a really nice professor. She gives out a few assignments per week but it's manageable if done in a timely manner. Instructions can be confusing at times but she's willing to help clarify.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: 2nd semester with her. She's still just as great as my first semester. Just do the work she gives and youll for sure pass. not much work per week, but it will add up if you fall behind. she still doesnt do a good job explaining her requirements, but its still a very doable class!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Liza's class is great but she is a bit of a disorganized and person. She doesnt remember what she says and does a horrible job explaining assignments. her homework is pretty easy though. some journals, discussion boards, essays, quizzes.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Liza is really cool! If you like having discussions and talking, this prof is for you! she's really nice and easy to talk to. she does give a good amount of homework and essays though.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Class as a whole wasn't hard. Read a chapter on one of two books for the course, write a journal entry on your thoughts, and then have a quiz on the material. You'll have the occasional in-class essay or paper that you'll need to do, but if you follow the guidelines, you can get an A easily. He loves to tell stories so get ready to listen to them.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Overall, he was an okay teacher. He gives 3 major essays, multiple in-class papers, and then verbal quizzes. His grading criteria are pretty awful as the max you can get in the class without extra credit is 95%, assuming you get 100% on everything. He's funny but he doesn't really respond to emails until you email him a lot.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Mr. Carman's class was very easy as the majority of points come from journals, quizzes, and essays. As long as you do all of he journals and quizzes he will give you full credit regardless of the grade received. There are 3 essays that are simple to do since he basically tells you exactly what he's looking for. Don't expect to learn much though.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The class was overall boring,he mainly shared stories and for the majority of the time we went over his writing college program.The college program notebook was basic knowledge you learn in high school and it was a FILL IN THE BLANK.He also made us purchase two additional books which one was also basic knowledge.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This professor tells a lot of stories and assigns a lot of papers. The deadlines are due during mid terms and finals. You turn everything in at once at the end of the semester. You will need to buy 3 books and one of the are written by him. The English notebook written by him cost around $60. There is a quiz for a chapter of the book everyday.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Lot of papers in class and outside Have to read Good guy very funny

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Carman's class itself has a good idea of how it should be run, but there are too many side stories; It's like listening to my grandparents talk. Not to mention the fact that you have to buy his workbook for $64. It's only 30 pages, has spelling errors, and is common sense. This is one directly from the book: "1. You need to take college seriously."

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Mr. Carman is an extremely chill professor that I would indeed take again! He is nice and will listen to any concern a student may have and will help you enough to pass the class. This class is not difficult at all, unless you tend to leave the chapter readings to the last minute. If you know how to manage your time well you should be fine!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: As long as you do all the work you can't fail and he also offers ex credit for one grade up. He's very on attendance and does in person essay's that you can not remake. As well as, readings from textbook with journals, but it's all very easy. Overall, he's a very good professor and definitely recommend taking him.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Mr. Carman's class was easy in terms of what he wanted from you. We read one book throughout the semester, had short textbook readings, and kept a journal. There are in-class essays that are very easy and only 3 short essays outside of class that he gave plenty of time for. There were usually short and easy verbal quizzes after homework readings.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Take professor carman's course, you will not regret it. Very easy to follow along with his assignments he gives. He gives you enough time to complete them. I would take him again!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's super nice and understanding. Has lots of quizzes, but he gives out the answers. The extra credit was really easy and it boosts your grade by one letter. He has a lot of in-class essays that can't be made up, but they're really easy, and he's a lenient grader. He only gives his students an A, never an A+ on anything.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Overall, Jeffrey Carman is a great English professor. He requires students to own 2 books that are used throughout the semester. Every week you're taking quizzes, writing journals, reading, and writing essays. This may sound rigorous, but you'll pass if you keep up and follow his guidelines. He's also an interesting guy too for his stories.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Carman's class is easy to do well on. His guidelines are clear and you'll get an A following them. Make sure to follow them EXACTLY though. Classes are interesting especially when he tells stoties

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Loved his stories. You will need to buy 2 books for the class. Journals after every reading, quizzes in class, 2 papers, research project, in-class essays. Overall, the class was easy if you do the work.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Best English class I've ever had. Beware of pop quizzes (you have to read many different books). I actually enjoyed the essay topics we had to write about (plastic in the ocean, your opinion on ___, and etc.) He had so many funny stories to share to us and class was less than 50 minutes. Super easy A and will give out extra credit options to do

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He has a quiz every week based on the books, but you don't even have to read much. He lets you select a few quizzes for him to grade you on at the end of the semester. He mostly just talks in class about his life. The only thing you really need to pay attention to is the weekly quiz and occasional papers. They're not hard to write either.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is a good prof if you listen to his directions and advice before you do assignments. Quiz grading is lenient during online. If you ask for help, he will help, just as long as you follow what he says, you will get a good grade. Don't be fooled by my grade, it was a tough class, but you just need to ask for help.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Not too sure why the reviews on here are bad. Look at "Jeff Carmans" reviews those are 100% MORE ACCURATE. Super nice prof and you barely have any work. 2 reading books in the class but no textbook. Cameras required but it's only 50 min lecture. All the quizzes are answrd in the zoom chat so you can just wait for other answers. Jeff C First YR Comp

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Overall, class was opposite of helpful. The teacher talks a lot about himself instead of teaching. Also kind of demeaning. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: There is no teaching nor learning in this class. The class is very lousy, I didnt learn anything beneficial. Also pressures students to turn on webcams (made me uneasy). Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He complains about assigning too much work, but doesnt even grade it quickly or give good feedback. Theres no creative freedom, so if your essays dont align with his ideas, youll get a B max because he takes off arbitrary points.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is a great Professor! He made English super interesting with the assignments, and in class, we watched a lot of movies, so it was easy. As long as you do the warm-ups at the beginning of class, you should pass with at least a B.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I am currently taking Professor Carman online. The class is very easy and if you need help, he is willing to help and give feedback. Be prepared to read a bit and write a lot, but for someone who doesnt like reading - it is very easy. The writing is just a research paper, journals, in class papers, quizzes, etc. He is the GO-TO english teacher!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Overall, Professor Carman is really kind and cares a lot for his students. He always tells stories and jokes in class and wants everyone to do well. There is a lot of writing, but I don't think it is too bad.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Easy A if you put in the work! He's very caring and tells stories to make you want to learn, it is clear he cares about his students.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Quiz each week based on the readings but it's an easy A, plus he gives extra credit points on it. You do write a lot but he's not a hard grader. Mr. Carmen will help you if you ask him to. He really makes everybody pass his class by making sure you do his extra credit and making you go to the WC for his papers. Attendance isn't mandatory.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great professor. Really cares about his students. There is always quizzes for reading (are not that important for your grade). Listen to his advice and you will do well. There is extra credit, and a rewrite for one paper. Take his class, no regrets. One of the best CPP professors.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I love how often he cracks jokes. This man is here to help you - even after you take his class. Hes willing to help you out with your future classes, graduate school, and job! Hes passionate about what he teaches and definitely cares about his students. Just dont skip class often or hell fail you! Its an easy class though, so dont worry!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: this class was actually super easy bc writing is easy af for me. If you miss more than 4 classes, ur dropped from the class. for the papers go to office hours

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Carman is amazing! He gave excellent feedback on all my essays and really made me enjoy English. I would take his class again.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Easy to get an A if tries to do the work and tries to improve. He is very caring and nice to everyone. does have couple quizes about the reading, so keep up with the readings.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Mr. Carman is the nicest teacher in Cal Poly. There are quizes every time he assigns you readings.   Read Food Inc and Norton Field Guide. Not that hard. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: By far the best professor at Cal Poly, he cares for his students. Very understanding and will do everything in his power to help you get on track to pass the class as long as you talk to him. There are a lot of quizzes but as long as you keep up with your reading you'll be fine,provides many extra credit opportunities. TAKE HIM YOU WON'T REGRET IT!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: professor carman is, by far, the BEST professor i've had at cpp. he's super easy going. has a great personality. essays are graded easily. gives good feedback. is definitely willing to help his students. does several in-class reading quizzes but they are fairly easy. plus they aren't worth much of your overall grade. offers extra credit.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: One of my favorite professors thus far. He is super funny and talks the majority of the time. Beware of essays, although every english class obviously does. Reading is key in his class. Overall, he wants his students to pass and I learned a lot !

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: No creative freedom. If you talk about your own ideas on essays and they do not align with the professor's, have fun not getting an A on the essay. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This teacher likes to talk a lot and his stories do get pretty interesting. He does like to go off tangents, so if you don't like that then don't go for this teacher. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Mr. Carman honestly cares about his students.
