Easy A. And he wrote me a recommendation letter I needed. :) very nice professor.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Mr. Carman is a very caring man that wants everyone to pass the class therefore he offers many opportunities for students to raise their grade. there is a quiz after every chapter reading and at lease two sittings written in class every day. :)

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Fairly easy grader, almost every class session there will be a quiz on the assigned reading. Gives you a chance to rewrite 1 of the 2 main papers for the class. Wrote about 8 in class essays but they were all fairly easy to write.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Mr. Carman is a great teacher. As long as you put in the time and effort into the class, you will be more than fine. Be prepared to write a lot especially in ENG 130. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Carman is great, but the man is often disorganized and talks TOO MUCH ABOUT HIS LIFE. He's not a tough grader and though attendance isn't mandatory, you shouldn't miss class. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

A nice guy, but disagreeable in teaching methods.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I love Mr. Carman! Really nice teacher that loves to talk about his life when grading quizzes. You take a quiz from the assigned reading every class meeting. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's a pretty easy going guy. The only problem I had was he could care less about circumstances at home. No matter how bad he still made you feel pretty bad for missing class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Cool guy. Likes to tell stories about his life every 5 minutes. Quizzes every time there's class, but he offers a lot of extra credit points on them. Essays aren't difficult. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This professor is awesome. He is very understanding and helpful. He does tell funny jokes about his life experience. He is a huge fan of Springfield.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's a cool teacher and loves to lecture. He can seem a little weird at first, but has a lot of funny stories. Reading is assigned almost every class lecture.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: LOVED having him as a teacher. Very soft voice but EXTREMELY nice.. Everyday he writes out what will be happening in class.. Very helpful and wants people to participate.. they rarely do. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's a very easy professor. You have to do reading assignment every day and there is a quiz the next time you meet. The quizzes are EASY if you read (it helps if you have a good memory!) Let's you do a lot of extra credit. He's a bit boring but very nice :D

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Mr. Carman was the best teacher! He definately does tell a lot of life stories but they're all interesting. All he assigned were readings and quizzes. 5 essays total and all the topics were EASY. Offers a lot of extra credit as well!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Repeats himself constantly. Assigns readings everyday and then quizes on them. As long as you read, you should be fine. He also assigns a lot of essays, but they're all easy.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: very idiotic at times. Likes to repeat himself a lot. Takes up the entire class time by going off on tangents. He's a very hard grader. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Brown is a wholesome guy all around. Homework assignments are easy and only need to do 3 class speeches. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The best professor I have ever had. He's very kind, chill, and will always be there to help his students when they need it. Would definitely take his class again!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Lot of assignments: one in person speech, one recorded speech, a research paper, group presentation..., but overall great professor. very welcoming and understands nerves when it comes to public speaking.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is the professor that actually wants you to get a good grade. He is very helpful in essays, and gives good feedback. He is passionate about the books that we read. Prepare for some pop quizzes but they're really easy. Got an A.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Overall, Professor Brown is a caring and very fun professor! Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I love professor Brown! He's very clear on his expectations for assignments and gives the most helpful feedback on papers. I wish he taught more upper division courses because I'd definitely take him again. 10/10 recommend.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Brown is an amazing and caring person. He will give you constructive feedback!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is the best Professor I have ever had. If you show up and do the work you will pass. I learned so much from his class and he really took the time to give excellent feedback and he really cared .

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Good feed back on essays. Lectures are very constructive and fun. He responds quickly to emails.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Brown is so cool! Hes always so willing to help with any questions you may have. Hes a bit younger than other professors so he makes it easy to talk to him. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Ryan Brown is an amazing professor! He truly loves his job and makes a somewhat boring class as entertaining as possible. He's very funny and very relatable. Take him!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Legit the most understanding professor that i have ever taken. She truly cares for her students and loves her job. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This is a hybrid class, but I can tell you right now that this class is pretty much an at home class. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Nice professor and overall easy if you stay on top of things and attend every movie. Had a C for most of the semester as attendance was graded incorrectly. Was able to climb back to an A after putting in a lot of unnecessary effort.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The reviews for this class are true, truly an easy A as long as you stay on top of the journal entries he gives you and finish the discussion boards he gives about the film you watched that day. Midterm is a little painful if you do not like writing but its fine, and the final is easily doable earlier than the due date. Great professor, def cares

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The entire class lecture is watching a movie. You have to write papers and discussion boards pretty often but they are manageable. The final was a story board you have to draw.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Cooney is my favorite professor at CPP thus far. I have never felt more respected and had more fun in a class. Not only is this class relatively easy; it's well-rounded and executed well. I learned so much about film and history, and saw some films that are now my absolute favorites.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Fun class & easy A as long as you do your work. Watch a movie and write two 1-paragraph assignments. 2 page paper every few weeks. Grading is easy and course is fun. Just make sure to stay consistent with your work, as he doesn't grade most assignments until the last week.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Pretty easy A, most of the movies covered are older highly rated movies. Lectures before were a bit interesting. Communication was very slow, he would not respond to most people's emails quickly at all. Also his canvas page was very disorganized, and contained assignments from previous semesters

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Cooney is a great professor, and we watched a lot of amazing films in this class. I highly recommend this class for those who love the art of film. There is a lot of writing, but it is not hard at all. However, they are a bit time-consuming. The only problem is he forgets to post discussion boards, and lacks communication. TAKE THIS CLASS

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great class and professor if you need to fulfill a C1! Met once a week over zoom, discussed film topics, and watched a movie. Discussion board for each movie, 3 film responses, 1 midterm paper, a semester-long journal, and a final storyboard. Not a hard class but a lot of writing, and the professor is awesome!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's an ok teacher, but when you're just taking this class to pass a GE, its a pain in the ass. The movies are somewhat cool, but the workload in this class is waaaaaaay too much. I didn't expect to have to work this much for this class. He is also virtually impossible to reach outside of class. He absolutely sucks at posting the right thing to do.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This class is super easy. WE just watch one movie a week and write a few sentences. Only three film responses, an essay, and a project. He doesn't give very clear instructions and he rarely responds to you outside of class but it is not difficult so it does not matter.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Extremely easy class and he is really nice. You just watch movies and write a couple sentences on them. There's also 3 easy short film responses and a project.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Best class ever. Very easy, barely any homework. Take this class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Literally one of the best professors Ive had this whole semester! Super sweet and super invested in this class. You have to try hard to fail!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Prof Cooney is very passionate about film and it translates into his teaching and commentary. He truly wants everyone to enjoy the films we watch. It was an overall very enjoyable class, definitely recommended.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Cooney is super cool, nice, and funny! He really has a passion for film and wants everyone to enjoy the material. Only three film responses, in your choice of film, a pretty lengthy, but manageable midterm paper, and an entertaining storyboard final! Take this class!! It is easy, chill, and interesting, especially for a GE!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Cooney is passionate about films and makes class fun and interesting when analyzing films. The class meets once a week to watch and there are online journals, discussion boards along with film responses occasionally, and quizzes to make up general assignments. The final is a storyboard and is a fun project. Overall, it is an easy class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Cooney is a cool nice guy. The movies are hit or miss. It's was a good class to take online for COVID since you have a computer already. Quiz here and there a midterm and a storyboard for the final. I def recommend taking this class for an easy GE. The only thing was he responds to emails pretty slow so you would have to ask him a question in class

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Super easy class, you watch good movies, very few (and easy) assignments, no midterms, occasional quiz (I only had 2), and a storyboard final. Super laidback class if you want to have a good, stress-free time. The only thing though is he SUCKS at emails. Legit the whole class had to bombard him with emails and talk to him to get him to respond.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: super cool guy and fun class watched a lot of movies

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I had Cooney for virtual learning and the class was cake. 3 main assignments with a midterm paper and a storyboard final. You just attend class and watch movies. Some movies were boring, but some were actually good. At the end of each lecture you write 2-3 sentences on the movie really easy.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I had the honor of taking this class over Zoom for the Fall 2020 semester. Although communication with the professor was limited due to our current virtual settings, I could tell that he was really passionate about the films that he shows the class. Honestly, this is one of the easiest GE's I've taken and I recommend it.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The class is extremely easy. It' a joke. I took the course just for credit, but I came out with a greater understanding of films. I had a class once a week and u just show up in the zoom and watch a movie and then just write 2-3 sentences about it. we have to fill out movie film responses but its easy and it's quick and u only have to do three EASY

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I am currently taking Professor Cooney online. He is a very caring teacher who shows amazing movies. The movies are picked differently every week, he talks about it, and then we watch it. He will talk about it after as well. You just have to write short journals, discussion board, participation, midterm, and final. Very easy class and entertaining!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Movie choices are a mix, but it's up to the student preference. Professor gave excellent feedback on films we watch making us understand the concepts more. No tests, homework is assigned every few weeks revolving around a film of our choice. Final was super easy and fun.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Prof. Cooney is one of the best. Most work you will do is the 3-4 movie reviews out of the 15 you watch in class, a midterm comparing movies in class and outside of class, and an easy storyboard final. He does take attendance before and after the movie. Cooney does have peers in the film industry, so he really knows film!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He was a nice guy. He showed great classic films that are enjoyable and interesting. It's very little homework but sneaks up on you, easy grader. One problem was he showed a couple of movies that had very violent and graphic scenes like rape and didn't warn us despite saying he would, several people cried those entire film and it really sad.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I recommend!!! Easy class, you just watch movies and write discussions every 3 movies. DO NOT PROCRASTINATE! I did that and had to do all my discussions the day before our exam. Movies we watched were interesting and attendance does matter! You sign in before and after class. 10/10 For our exam we had to do a storyboard which was fun!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Every film selection was very well throughout and well picked. I've gained a few favorite movies from this course. He's a very fun and laid back professor who's obviously passionate about his work. Class starts off with background on that week's film, then the film itself. Don't take advantage of him because he gives a very relaxed workload.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Cooney's class was very easy, but tiring. Every time there was class, there was a film. They were interesting, but tiring. Of these films you need to write three 4-5 page essays that were very specific on aspects of the film. Although it was a class I was lazy to go to, it was very easy and would still recommend it.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Movies in every class. Write 5 reports on any of the 15 movies (will tell you what he wants on it). Recommend to complete the 5 reports for the first 5 movies then relax for the last 10. 2 attendance sheets at beginning and end of class. Final is a storyboard then present within small groups and choose the best and present to class. Easy A. Take it

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This is probably the best area C1 class. We get a little lecture on film elements and watch a movie every class, then we can choose to write a report to turn in the next week (watch like 10 movies, only need to write on 5). He is very caring and will help if you have any questions or issues. Attendance is necessary and recorded twice each class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is the easiest professor I have every taken, if you like to watch movies then take this class. You have to write five movie reviews by the end of the semester and make your own story board. Very simple and he tells interesting stories about celebs and what he is working on.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Got him for a film class, we watched films and turned in discussion papers every week we watched like 10+ movies but only 5 papers were mandatory. You can tell he's passionate about films, super fun class however its important to attend or notify him in advanced if you can't or else you will lose points and potentially fail. Watched amazing films!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: good teacher

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: TAKE HIM!!!! 5 essays, plus a final; none were hard. Super super easy.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Nice guy who is clearly both passionate and knowledgable about film. All the movies selected were relevant to the course and provided a good introduction to film studies. He started each class with an hour lecture then played a movie, stopping occasionally to provide commentary. Not much work and extremely doable!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Understood most kids were taking the class as a GE and conducted it as such.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Take him if you want an easy A. We watched about 9 movies and were required to write about 2 for credit. The movies weren't bad. The final project is a storyboard; you make up a movie and use specific terms. He gives no homework. Lectures are boring, but use the time to do work for another class. He's got a great personality

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This was basically a movie class with Prof. Solano. One of the best classes I've ever taken period we watched such amazing films and I learned a lot about all the work that goes into filmmaking. We were graded on 3 papers for whichever movies we wanted to write about and there was one final storyboard project. A great class and an easy A.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The class was about Film and American Culture, but rather than showing an actual film that might be educational, Solano chooses to show documentaries about those films that will put you to sleep. In the end, he shows American Beauty as the final movie, and that's about it. Very boring lectures.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The greatest teacher at this school. He actually likes his job. If you're an A-Hole, he still sees good in you. You'll learn and just show up and do your work and you'll get an A as well. If you are very stupid and lazy, you'll get a C-, if you get an F, drop out of school.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took this class during the fall quarter, on Fridays only and I gotta say he is by far the best professor i've had. He's really clear on what he expects. Its an easy A if you are willing to participate at least once in class and do the homework! We watched a movie each day and discussed it afterwards. Used for one of my GE's.
It's a super easy class, and the teacher is very cool. No homework and tests are open-book and open-note. Very understanding and is very open minded with his students and their schedules.

I wouldn't recommend taking it if this is for a GE course, he makes no sense. He gets upset when students don't understand, he will try but it honestly doesn't help. The work is easy but so pointless, he has it set so complicated and claims the tests are easy but the average is around 60%. He curves at the end of the semester though.

Dropped him on the first day of class after he went 20 minutes over and made up copy an excel sheet and work data. Speaks very fast, is not helpful, wont record zooms. do not suffer take the easy way out and drop the class.

You can tell this professor is never prepared for his class. He uses the "Socratic" method for teaching which means he can just talk without any prep. Also he is very condescending. He will bring in guest speakers and tell them they are wrong even though he has no idea what he's talking about. He somehow made a easy class harder than it should be.
Would stumble over his own explanations and argue that correct answers were wrong at times.

Great professor. My small class of 8 allowed for personal interaction. The class was conducted via an Excel sheet, making it unique, and I retained a lot of information even after the semester. It wasn't too difficult, as we worked well together, and asking for help was easy. He genuinely cares about students' learning and comprehension.

Yes,sorry to break it to you,but college is hard.GROWUP!We are adults,and college requires resilience.I prefer a professor who is tough on us and holds us accountable rather than one who just reads prelecture material.I took Roman last year,and I learned the most in his course.Dont take him if you're looking for the easy route.Hes a great professor

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR NO MATTER WHAT!!! If you enjoy sitting in a classroom listening to a washed up professor talk about how great the things he knows and does are then be my guest. Be ready to randomly be told the most important parts of the class for about 2 minutes with no follow up information. Very sassy guy with a zesty attitude.

DOnT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! He jumps into the topic as if we already know it. He's not good at explaining problems and his handwriting is not comprehendible. He does a lot of midterms and the class averages would be 50s. He does not curve the test at all but I've heard that he will curve your overall grade (not sure yet bc this sem isnt over yet)

Canvas page is very disorganized and is barely used. Participation & homework graded by Google & Excel Sheets (very chaotic & not structured well). Loosely answers or doesn't answer student's questions. Thought this would be an easy GE and introductory course. I highly encourage you to look for another professor for this course.

I believed this professor was chill in the beginning but slowly started realizing how rude he truly is and how he cannot teach. He complains about students not doing work but locks the columns (since we work on sheets) which doesn't allow them to work on it. He has an extremely high ego, can someone please humble him.

This professor is VERY DISORGANIZED, there's literally no structure to his lectures. He does not prepare you well for his tests and although it is communicated with him he does nothing to change it or help you. Awful attitude as well. HIGH EGOOO!!!
Rushes students when taking tests, comes in late, does not teach. Unwilling to answer students questions and shows no interest in students excelling in his class.

This professor has an out-of-control ego which is why sometimes he'll refuse to answer students' questions. He doesn't explain the course concepts well at all, we never look at any examples in the book, and he'll usually only go over topics once. I've taken two exams so far and the material on there was barely gone over.
Today seems to have been the last straw for a lot of us. DO NOT TAKE HIM.
Giant ego, no ability to teach.

Horrible professor and refuses to repeat formulas when asked for help. The Excel/Google sheets he uses are no help at all. Forgets this is an intro/GE class not a graduate level course. Dont take for your own mental health.
DONT TAKE HIM.

Professor connects the texts to useful, real-world application. His lectures are dense, but if you understand the basic gist of what he's saying, you'll be fine. Note that this class size is very large for that of CalPoly, so you won't get as much attention as you'd like.

Lectures explain close to nothing and he does not go over what will actually be on his tests. The homework he assigns does not relate at all to what is going to be on the tests. Continually brags about his past students and the canvas is very disorganized.

DO NOT take a class from this professor. Absolutely no help, lectures were ridiculously all over the place with no structure, and the professor barely knew what he was doing at most times. He can come off very rude at times as well. Literally take any other course. I think we all only passed this semester because more than 70% of people dropped
no

very disorganized, no clear course planning. doesnt give useful assignments or homeworks to prepare you for midterms. hes definitely a likeable guy just not a competent professor. if you talk to him and participate heavily you will pass if he remembers your name. definitely look for a different professor for frl 1001.

Summer Session, lots of information and a very long class but he understands and cares for students. If you do not attend the lecture I can imagine you pass at all but show up every day and keep up with him in class and you shouldn't have any problems at all. Easier if you have a PC and have ForecastX with Excel. Definitely recommend!

Grading system is weird. Grades with rankings. Top 10% gets an A, next 10% B and so on. Professor is knowledgeable in economics and finance but does not lecture fully according to book. Lectures don't help with the HW. Lectures help with the exams, so pay attention. Participation matters. Professor has a very strong character.

Very unorganized. Top 10% of students get an A, next 10% gets B & so on. 2 Midterms, 1 final, weekly HW about 40-60 questions. He uses google sheets for you to enter in things he asks which is the worst thing i've had a professor do. You cannot miss class & expect to pass. Just get your name recognized & you will be fine. Makes his own exams.

He is an extremely disorganized professor. His lectures just jump all over the place and they're not interesting. He keeps bragging about his old students... He is also very condescending at times. I would not recommend him.

Professor Garagulagian seems a little young and like he is not very well versed being a professor. He does not respect student presenters, he interrupts presentations very often and criticizes you through the whole thing. Also seldom posts on canvas, he is very disorganized and goes back and fourth on assignments. No clarity, no direction with him.
Class is moderate. The notes are done on google sheets, so i recommend you pay attention to what he talks about in class/zoom

Put in the work and you'll pass, this is a hard class and he understands that. He wants everyone to pass and even offered us internships. Very passionate and funny guy. Gave us points just for filling out stuff even if it was wrong. His Exams were quite different than I've ever seen, but relate to the lecture material if you kept up.

Let me say this, he has been like no other professor I have overtaken. There isn't a lot of homework, most of it is just reading. He writes his own tests but are not too difficult. Makes an excel sheet for the whole class that gets updated every class meeting. Keep up with what he says, participate a lot! A prett chill class that teaches you a lot.

Probably one of the worst professors I have ever taken! He would get angry at us thru ZOOM and start yelling. He wants everyone to participate yet his lectures are all over the place & hard to follow. The notes he writes down are horrible. He would threaten us saying that only the students that would participate would pass even if they fail exams.

Professor G is a very caring, and passionate lecturer. He will assign a lot of homework, but if the class agrees it is too much, he will cut out a lot of the assignments. He wants you to learn and loves questions. You will learn A LOT about personal finance if you put the effort in. (Fall 2019)

Okay, so let me tell you. Not fun. However; only like 10% of the class actually "passed" until he curved the grades. I was part of that 10%. After he curves almost everyone passes. Where ever most people end up getting scores at becomes a C. Most people got ds and fs so they became c's. His class changed my life. I can do the impossible.

HORRIBLE! Save your self time and find a different professor. He is condescending and rude. Makes you feel like you stupid for not understanding and he doesn't lecture at all. Just rambles and confuses you more and more each class.

He's a pretty easy professor. His midterms and final were very straight forward and simple. You will be required to buy cengage for the textbook and homework. There was a lot of homework though so make sure you do them weekly to stay on track.

He really wants you to learn, he is funny and kind. His tests are hard and do not make any sense but it was a fun and entertaining class. I loved listening to his lectures. If you were there in class and read beforehand, you will do fine!

OK professor, as long as you do your work and participate in class you'll get a good grade. Lectures can sometimes be interesting He uses cengage for homework which is extremely tedious and annoying. Also you get a lot of homework. Would not take again for that sole reason.

Had a great experience with Roman this summer. When you meet him he comes off a little strong, but he's not your typical professor. He really cares more about you learning the material than performing well on a test so he pushes you to read before hand to have better discussions in class. If you like to participate and learn he's the prof for you.

Roman was an interesting guy. His lectures were a bit messy as he did not even know some of the functions he was teaching us. It felt like he was learning along with the class too and never really tried his assignments himself. Overall, it was a difficult class made more difficult by his lack of knowledge in Rstudio.

Roman is super funny and smart. He doesn't baby you, he expects you to come up with solutions yourself, using critical thinking. I would say his class prepares you for the real world more than any class I have taken. Get ready to do presentations. He comes off tough but he is really caring and wants you to pass/succeed in life. Great professor!

He's a fair professor. He teaches clearly with applicable examples, and welcomes questions which is great because finance can be very hard. He expects participation, so make sure to raise your hand frequently, even if you think it might be wrong. He may come off a little rough at first, but he's actually pretty chill as the class goes on.

Roman gets a tough wrap due to his passion for his students. While the class is difficult and he does expect you to work to succeed, Roman is very fair and makes himself available to help his student is whatever they need. Expect to carry your weight and show up to class or you wont do well. Would take again for other classes. Thx Roman!

The first day of class he comes off as aggressive but he definitely grows on you. The way he teaches is different from most professors, you absolutely have to read the chapters he assigns if you want to do well in the class. He starts every lecture assuming that the students have already read, and class focuses more on examples and problems.

Overall he doesn't care. Always talking about his other job. Lectures about being smart and prepared, but makes us buy a book with a CD that is compatible with Windows XP. Expects us to come to class at a random hour window to learn program. Gives quiz on program with no access to the program to practice. Quiz every week, many F's on quizzes
Avoid at all costs. Talks down to students.

Very knowledgeable about the big picture of finance if you are not a finance major. I was kinda lost at first but began raising my hand and asking questions. Ended up getting a B in the class and i actually left understanding what i was doing. Comes off strong but hes actually really nice to you if you are paying attention during lecture.

FRL 300 is a tough class regardless, Roman teaches via Socratic method aka asks students questions and to engage. Tests are moderate but if you attend each class even if you don't participate he most likely will not fail you. He seems rude at first, but then you realize that's just his normal tone of voice and he is actually a pretty chill dude.

I have always passed every class although some have been challenging. I can't even call Roman a teacher because he does not teach. I am so sad at the outcome & will have to retake this course again. His test were very difficult and everything that was in the test he didn't even teach us... DONT TAKE HIM

This class was hard because he is not very clear on what he is saying and writes all over the place. You need to read (on own), participate a lot, and prepare to study on your own. No study guide. Wish he was a bit clearer on topics so that everyone can follow along without no problems.

If you are willing to read the chapter ahead of time like he asks as well as pay attention during class, you should have no issue getting an A or B in this class. Subject matter is hard by nature but he really helps you understand the functions of finance. Does not go over HW in class but if you go to his office hours he'll break it down for you

Horrible teacher. Glances at the textbook and knit-picks topics to talk about. Impossible to follow his examples on the board because skips steps (hes a smart guy but a bad teacher). Yells and picks on the class for not knowing things. His tests are nothing like the homework. Inadequately prepares you for tests. Would avoid at all costs.
The ONLY good thing about him that he curves
Avoid him he doesn't know how to teach and he keeps screaming at students in the class. It is useless to come to class or skip it you wont learn anything.

Do your homework, study the PowerPoints, understand the case studies and read the textbook. Took her for FRL301 & 440. She gave me an A & A-, respectively. Don't ask easy questions that you can look up. Put in the effort to ask good analytical questions.
Do your homework and study the lectures

One of the most difficult courses in FRL. Three written reports, one presentation, and bi-weekly quizzes. At times, it felt like it was too much material and work that was due. Strict strict grader, so be sure to double check your work. If you have no choice, I'd recommend as 4401 classes fill quick. Although you may learn a lot, it was tedious.

Updated for 2023: Took Wei Yu for FRL 4401. She might be the strictest professor I've ever had in my life. She offers zero leniency with assignments and when approached with questions needing help, she says for me to "learn for next time" as if we have another chance to redeem ourselves for this assignment. Took a big hit to my grade because of it.

She does the best she can despite the time constraint she has to teach a difficult subject. She posts videos and uses iClicker to supplement learning. She also gives really generous curves! I did a lot better than I thought I would because of her.

She's not the worst professor, but I definitely wouldn't recommend her. She's almost sarcastic when students have questions, and her speedy lectures don't make the material any easier to understand. She requires an iClicker which is how she takes attendance (she'll provide you one). Homework, iClicker, and 3 exams make up your grade.

Her accent and speedy lectures make it difficult to understand the material. I had to go to a tutor to understand the material and even went over some homework questions with her during her office hours. Still received a D+ (my first ever) which dropped my 3.5 gpa. Wouldnt recommend taking her.

Great teacher, always on time, clear, and concise. Gave reviews before exams. Advice: DO YOUR ONLINE HOMEWORK some of those problems were on exams. Overall a great teacher. I would love to have her for the rest of my FRL classes!
Easy teacher, but very strict with grading. Do not slack in this class for at all if you want to get an A. Received an A- for a 92.8% and she said the A was at a strict 93%.
she is active and really intertest in teaching and responding and also nice.

Hybrid class but exams are not online. Will need scantron and fina.calc. His lectures are not very helpful especially if you try asking questions; he will get irritated. Take someone else if you need to pass. The only good thing is connect hw are not tedious. Be prepare to self learn and good luck with the calc.

Teaching style should be unacceptable at this level of education.Utilizes a scanned PDF form of notes from 2013 full of errors TELLS YOU TO CHANGE HIS LECTURE NOTES!!! No questions he immediately gets an attitude. Practice test for his exams don't help. You will have to learn from another professors lecture videos available on YouTube, waste of $.

He taught online but he didn't know how to use technology very well. He would read off of PDFs but sometimes there would be mistakes and he wouldn't be able to change them, he would just correct them by saying what it was supposed to say. You're going to need a financial calculator, ~$30. I learned nothing. Only survived thanks to the curve.

Extremely tough professor. He makes a ton of mistakes on his own lecture slides and doesn't fix them. Plus, he overcomplicates the chapters. If you sadly get this guy I recommend youtube as an alternative.

I self-taught myself for most of the tests but he does provide the tools to do well in his class despite his lectures being dull and unorganized. He wants his students to do well and tells us what problems to practice for the exam. His study guide is also pretty identical to the exam and also gives a generous curve

Exams are the only grades that matter, that being said, I highly recommend you attend class even though it is optional. He teaches everything that will be on the exam so if you just listen to him you can score at least 80% just by attending class and using that information on the exams. Solid Choice

This professor may not be the best one but his course is definitely manageable. Your Hw is an average of 10 questions on connect and its not even a lot . The test are manageable, he provides lecture notes and study guides for exams. He curves exams which is a plus. I honestly didnt attend most of his lecture but I would read and teach myself.

I was hesitant to take this class because of previous reviews but it turned out to be doable. Professor Sohrabian is by no means the best professor as he seems to lack compassion and care for his students; however, he grades on a curve which is one of the few positives of this class. If this class is one of your few options, it's manageable.

I was worried whenever I signed up for Sohrabian class, specifically because of his bad reviews. Turned out I made the perfect choice! Prof Sohrabian class was not bad at all, he provides study guides, and gives lots of hints on what to expect for exams. He's a cool guy, and loves to joke around. His curves are amazing! Highly recommend!

He doesn't know how to teach, but the material is basic and easy chapter 1 wasn't that hard, but yes you have to teach yourself. Its not that bad just do a few problems and understand them. Tom 301 with Nguyen was more difficult than this class. He also curves. Homework is easy, and just participate and he will give you a point each time

Well the bad news is, I'm not sure there are any finance professors that are better than him. lectures are quick and easy but take notes for quizzes! weekly assignments are not hard just do what you need to and you'll be good. Never interacted with him all semester but seems like a caring and nice professor. the class was not bad and I enjoyed it, you will too.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: You get weekly quizzes based off his online lectures and a research paper based off the three books you read throughout the semester. His class is very easy and he responds right away with any questions you may have.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is extremely knowledgeable about his subject, down to the tiniest details. His lectures are pretty enjoyable and feel like story time. You're screwed if you miss his lectures, though, since he doesn't publish his lecture notes. He also makes some pretty funny jokes sometimes, and he's extremely friendly and easy to talk to.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Down to Earth and knowledgeable professor. Easy A, no textbook, homework, or reports. 3 exams 45 questions in 50 minutes in class on paper using a scantron based on lectures. 3 film quizzes each 10 questions based on the film he tells you to watch outside of class. Exams are not cumulative, fill out the study guide each lecture for exam preparation

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Delgadillo's class is very reasonable. There are three exams and a final paper which determine your grade. Class is very lecture heavy, but he does a good job at addressing everything for the exams. It is important to take notes as he does not post anything on Canvas. As long as you show up to class and pay attention, you will do well.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Show up=easy grade! Awesome professor

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Delgadillo seemed like a nice enough guy, but his 3340 class was severely lacking. He does speed lectures with no breaks, and in an American Institutions and Ideals class, he spent literally 2 minutes on Jim Crow. I will admit that the structure of the class seemed very easy, but I wouldn't recommend him to any history majors.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Delgadillo's class consisted of three online film exams, and four exams throughout the semester. While lecturing, he does talk quickly but he made learning history informative and fun. Take good notes and listen carefully to what he says and you'll do well on his exams. I recommend taking his class!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great professor. His lectures are very fast-paced but are entertaining. He gives 3 tests of equal weight (including the final), all of which are multiple choice and easy to do well on as long as you take good notes.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Good class with a good professor. We never met but he was helpful in emails if I had questions. Everything was on BB: weekly homework and tests. Remembering history is difficult for me but the tests are fairly easy if you know the information. Mostly just busy work.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is amazing! Take him if you can for HST 2202. All you need to do is show up everyday for class and you are pretty much set. He hardly assigned any work, and the exams are only based off what he goes over in lecture (no textbook) so just take notes during lecture and review them before class. He gave us three film exams but very doable.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: If you miss a lecture, you better have friends in the class. I'm not a history person so I sometimes dozed off when he talked. I did miss a few points on the exams because of that. There are 3 exams and flim exams. Those are mostly your grades. This is the class if you want to get a GED over with. Just pay attention closly to his lectures.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: One of the better professors at Cal Poly, it was only a GE class for me but Professor Delgadillo made it enjoyable. If you skip lectures you will fail the class. Also provides plenty of extra credit opportunities which was nice!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Delgadillo's class was one of the most interesting I've been in. He is very knowledgeable in US History and it shows through his lectures. Very little homework is given, just study for the tests. Only complaint I have would be that he does not post any of his slides or lectures in any circumstance. Be sure to attend class to get points.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Super chill professor. Gives you participation points for showing up to class. Take good notes in class and you will pass the exams!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's really cool. Very knowledgable of the subject. Easy and straightforward class. Allows an index card for exams. He talks hella fast tho so watch out lmao

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Amazing professor! 3340 is pretty much all lectures but the lectures are great and he is not a boring speaker. He can talk little fast at times. There are 3 tests and a paper due at the end of the sem but its not super long and an easy prompt. Good extra cred opportunites. The tests are very easy if you pay attention in class. 1000% reccomend.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Charles was a great teacher. He had lectures every day and kind of went fast so you just need to make sure you pay attention. Also he only grades based off of the 3 exams and then your key terms you turn in after each lecture. If you base your notes off the key term list he provides you, the exam will be easy.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Delgadillo is an amazing history professor. I hated history but, he made it so easy to understand without overcomplicating lectures. There't no homework expect for a couple of movies you need to watch. Exams are straightforward and entirely based on lecture. He lectures from memory for the entire class so COME TO CLASS and you will pass.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great professor but his microphone is so annoying. Was only graded on exams and some small film quizzes and some attendance points.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Charles is a great lecturer and provides clear instructions for the 1 big course essay. If you're not headed in quite the right direction, his feedback is super helpful and there are 3 separate days where he reviews your progress. He's really cool and a proponent of the class Discord, so it's super easy to get in touch with him. 10/10 class

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took this class asynchronous but the structure was simple there was a discussion board and quiz every week and a lecture video. He was a really chill professor and his grading is straight forward.The assignments cannot be made up so if you forget to do one you cannot go back and do it.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took this course fall of 2021 as an Asynchronous course. The class was very straightforward, very easy, and enjoyable. Class set up is simple, all lectures are podcasts with short multiple choice quizzes every week. There wasn't any worksheets but there are 4 essays, with your pick out of the 5 essay prompts that there are to choose from.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The class was asynchronous and entirely graded on multiple choice quizzes with some extra credit. He will answer emails pretty quickly. His lectures are interesting and if you take notes in them you should pass the class pretty easily.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Delivered content in the form of recorded lectures and reading. Presented in a way that was easy to remember for weekly quizzes. Honestly felt like busy work, but was useful information. Would take again.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's such a good professor! Although it seems like the exams are enough to make you drop out, its okay because the answers are in the lectures which was really easy if you actually take time to listen to them. Make sure to also do the 4 main essays in order to pass the class. Overall he seems organized and put together.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I believe he is the best history professor in CPP. There is nothing to regret taking him. Lectures are amazing, engaging, and AWESOME. He makes me becomes more into history even I'm in STEM major. Easy A class, just need to read(watch) the materials once a week (1-3hr) and you can get an A. Quiz will be each week (100% course). TAKE HIM

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: For Professor Charles' class, there are weekly 15 question quizzes. They're not that hard, I would usually leave about a couple of hours to get through the content then take the quiz using memory. He has people respond to discussion prompts and then to others' responses to the prompts. He also offers extra credit. A very easy class to pass.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: There are weekly 15 question quizzes. They are divided to 5 questions from the lecture( recorded podcast), 5 questions from the textbook, and 5 questions from a primary source(either movie/ reading). Not that hard, as long as you keep up with everything. He offers extra credit as well. Very easy class to follow.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Easy online class you get a article/movie each week with a textbook reading and a podcast. Then every week you take a quiz on those things. 15 question and you get 30 minutes. No final. Gives extra credit for voting. Also each week you have a discussion board on article/movie. Super easy :)

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took Prof Delgadillo for HST 2201 Fall 2020. Fully asynchronous. He was super easy. Just weekly quizzes and discussions. No essays. No midterms. No final, just a quiz. Would def recommend! :)

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: the class was easy. No FINALS OR MIDTERMS. but you have quizzes and discussio every week. every week you just have to take 15 question quiz on the reading or movie and write a discussion and reply to a discussion. very easy class. I recommend having a group chat to help with the quizzes and help for reading. the prof has a discord to ask questions.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Lectures, straight forward and simple. 4 exams (3 mid-terms 1 Final), all graded the same way, no difference between a mid-term and a final. 45 MC questions per exam, 3 movie exams (few questions after you watch a movie), and a very simple project (took me 2-hours of prep time). Take notes, or if you can remember his lectures than you'd be fine.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Good teacher. Their are 4 exams,3 film exam and Cartoon Project. He gives you a study guide but its still not enough. You have to study all your notes LITERALLY. Lectures are oral so get ready to write. Film exam are easy, take notes so you can remember what is happening. Interesting movies not boring. Gives 2 extra credit. Test multiple choice.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: he's a very animated professor and fun to listen to. he cares about his students and will work with you on grades. however, if you don't show up to class your grade will reflect that as tests are lecture based.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Not a hard class. His lectures are good and interesting and i don't even like history. Just show up to class, take good notes, and its and easy A.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is one of the very few teachers I have had to offer multiple extra credit opportunities. His class is lecture heavy and you have to go otherwise you will not pass, he does not post lectures on blackboard. All the assignments are really simple, he really tries to make the class interesting for his students.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Does a good job for the most part. His problem is that he begins even handed, but gets toward indoctrination later in the semester. Conservatives, moderates, and liberals beware, take the class for the GE, keep your head down. He is a cool dude, just horribly biased. Easy class, even for stem majors.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's interesting and at times fairly funny, not afraid to share his views. He lectures by speaking not power point so be ready to write until your hand bleeds. Each lecture gave about 5 questions on a 45 multiple choice test so if you miss get someone to fill you in. Course: US history 1877-present

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Delgadillo was very engaging with his lectures. The lectures consist of listening and taking notes. There are powerpoints, but not much on the powerpoints. There are 3 tests, 2 film exams, a cartoon project and a final. The exams are all multiple choice besides the short answer films. He talks really fast but you will get used to it.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Charles is very knowledgeable about history. He provides a study guide w/ key terms that will show up on the test, so it helps to take notes with that nearby. You only present once on a political cartoon and provides 3 points for being in class (given by writing a key term of his choice for that lecture). He is very good at answering questions!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Slides are all pictures and he does not post them, so you have to show up. Lectures fly by and are pretty entertaining, and he's pretty funny at times.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He does talk fast at first then you get used to it its like nothing he's amazing clear organized criteria if you show up to class you'll pass EASY test gives flashcard that gives you more confident going in pretty easy going highly recommend tbh he is willing to work with you try to get better grades. trust me his slides are mostly pictures.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He talks fast in lectures but it makes you pay attention more during the lecture. Really fast course and one easy little cartoon project. No pop quizzes or homework. Just the tests and the three movies to watch and write about

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This prof was cool! You only present once, not hard, you just analyze a political cartoon. Class is not mandatory BUT he offers free points every class by having students write a sentence on a key term he chooses. There are 3 films we watch on our own time + questions to answer on it! Make sure to study for exams because points are worth more!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is awesome.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He speaks very fast, but if you show up to class & take good notes you'll get an A in the class. His two papers are only 1 page double-spaced. Two midterms & Finals are super easy, you just have to know the vocabulary. He's very nice & will answer questions in class if you ask him to. If he knows your name & face in a positive light you're set.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: All the information you need for the test/ study guide is given to you during his lectures. His lectures are all pictures, which makes it easy to understand since you dont have to copy off a screen. He allows an index card for the test and gives you extra credit opportunities. He replies to emails very quickly. I highly recommend you take him.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He lectures with images, so make sure you stay awake through his lectures so you can get the notes. Attendance non-mandatory but he lectures verbally, so there's no point skipping if you can't find someone to get the notes off of. 1 cartoon presentation which is approx. 3 min: super easy. 2 film analyses: only 1 page double-spaced! 3 exams-MC.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Since there's no reading, make sure to show up to the lectures and take good notes as they'll be on the exam. His slides are all pictures and he talks really fast. Also do the key terms as they are easy points. Exams were all multiple choice. There are two film analyses and make sure that your grammar is on point for these papers.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He talks really fast and his slides are mainly pictures. There are two film analyses (check your grammar), a political cartoon presentation, and key terms after every lecture. DO NOT THINK YOU CAN SKIP THE KEY TERMS. They are easy points and there IS a time window. He will let you skip ONE. You can bring a 3"x5" index card as a cheat sheet.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: His lectures were really interesting, even tho you have to pay attention b/c his powerpoints are only pics, but thats what makes it interesting is that he talks a lot & its not just words you copy down from a screen. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: All of the power points he uses are primarily pictures and he tends to speed trough the lecture which makes it challenging to take notes.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He tries to make the class interesting, and is somtimes successful. Grades consisted of 2 papers, a political cartoon presenting project (very easy), and the midterm and final. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The class was pretty interesting and funny at times. There are about 4 essays, a cartoon project, 2 peer reviews, and easy extra credit. You don't need the book unless you don't take notes or pay attention in class. He also doesn't post the lectures online and it's all pictures anyway.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great professor overall. Not very tough at all and doesn't give a ton of work. Only 2 essay assignments during the whole quarter and he will help you with anything you need. You'll also need to to a 2-3 min presentation (it's easy and most people get A's). 2 essay exams but they're also easy and he will give you the topics ahead of time.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Delgadillo is a good professor. Make sure to attend all his classes and study the midterm assigned topics. I was heavy penalized for an assignment but still managed his class Make sure you are decent at writing before taking this course because it will mostly consist of written exams. Individual presentations last for the entire quarter!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: great guy, lectures were long but he gave us fair breaks and a fair grading scale for the final, which wasn't cumulative. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: great professor, easy to follow lectures, the essays are very important, there is 2 big essays and the midterm and final are 2 small essays, if writing isn't your strong suit ask him for advice and he will grade you easier as the grading criteria for what he wants is a tad up in the air. overall loved this class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This was for senior thesis, but for any history majors reading this: I cannot recommend Dr. Lewis enough! He was really kind and understanding of any life situations that got in the way of your weekly 3-page requirement. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Lewis does great work covering sport developments over time. He connects sports to culture and how it shaped societies over time. Definitely recommend!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This was my first class with Dr. Lewis and he made it amazing! He is super helpful and will actually give you solid feedback on your papers. He is a bit heavy on the reading assignments, though they all serve a purpose in learning the topic. He is always available to reach via zoom or email. 10/10 recommend

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Lewis is great! He is a slow grader BUT when you get your work back, he leaves corrections and a paragraph or two on what you could improve on. He actually takes the time to help you become a better writer. He is always available and super helpful. 10/10 would take him again

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Lewis is one of my favorite history professors at CPP. I took his asynchronous class and I enjoyed it due to its flexibility. 4 papers in total all regarding the course and were fairly easy, the midterm and final were papers. He is really kind and was overall accessible and grades fairly, put in a bit of work and you will succeed!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This is for the senior thesis course, so my experience could be different. However, Dr. Lewis is really a kind soul who is more than willing to help you or get you in touch with people who can. I couldn't recommend doing a senior thesis with him, he's really an asset when you're writing.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Lewis's discussions are so fun! He genuinely enjoys talking to students about the topic, so the weekly in-class discussions were always a blast. The workload is not very intense, just some weekly reading and a final term paper. I highly recommend this course to anyone, history major or not. It is pretty easy and actually interesting.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He definitely knows what he is talking about, but if you're not a good writer don't expect an A in this class. There are 4 papers in this class and he will grade them heavily so be prepared. Weekly work is easy to keep up with. Take him if you love to write and learn about history.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Insanely knowledgeable about European and world history. Hes also very nice and understanding about situations. He does grade the papers hard but it pushes you to become a better writer.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: A majority of your grade in this class is based on how well you do on the essays, midterm, and final exam. He's a tough grader, but gives very good feedback and explains how you can improve. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Not an easy A like most courses taken for GE credit. Grade is dependent mostly upon a few essays that he critiques thoroughly. Wish I would have taken a different class that would be less time consuming and less harmful to my GPA.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I've taken a few classes from Dr. Lewis and I've enjoyed them all. Definitely take him in-person if you can! He's insanely knowledgeable on European history and cares so much about his students. His online classes have weekly discussion boards and a few papers, but they aren't too bad if you watch his lectures and read the assigned novels.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Prof. Lewis is one of the most caring professors at Cal Poly. Always very accommodating and understanding. Have had him for Euro hist. as well and he made it very interesting. A bit quirky, but he's always ready to listen and help with whatever questions you may have!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Chris Bates is the man! His lectures are amazing. He tells you exactly what he's going to quiz on. It's so clear as long as you show up this class is easy. I've learned so much about California, he makes it so interesting and entertaining. Best professor I've had at CPP.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Christopher Bates was definitely one of my favorite professors during the semester I was in his class. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I admit he is a great professor and clearly enjoys what he teaches, however I would not recommend this class if you worry about grades. He grades everything LAST minute... Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is a double-edged sword, and that's why you'll find conflicting opinions on this page on how good he is. I would not recommend him if you stress about grades.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Bates is an absolute delight to have as an instructor for this class; his lectures are consistently engaging. I can confidently say that 100%. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Best professor ever, super caring and awesome lectures. 100% deserves the amazing reviews and I highly suggest taking History of California if you're thinking about it, very cool and very interesting.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Bates was my favorite professor this semester! I enjoyed his lecturing style & he always made class interesting. His weekly quizzes are super easy & open notes. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Bates is awesome. He does take awhile to grade things. His lectures are informative and in depth. Despite his health issues this semester, he attended classes fairly regularly and even brought cookies on the last day.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Bates is one of few professors I wanted to write a good review on such that others can find him. Nonetheless, I have great respect for him.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Prof is a good professor but he gives a lot of homework. He uses webassign and there were times when some of the questions didn't fully align with the lecture/section. Dr. Lee is a very clear and cut professor. The class is lecture heavy and can get boring at times however, as long as you pay attention and do the work it is impossible not to get an A. You can also always ask for an extension to homework and the tests reflect what you learn.

Ryan is a very sweet professor and cares about his students. His lectures are thorough and recorded so if you miss the information is available to you. His students matter to him and he cares about mental health. With each section there is a homework assignment. His tests are easy as long as you have done the homework and understand the concepts

This is one of the most amazing math classes i have ever taken. The professor has three lectures a week, but they really helpful to understand the material. IGNORE THE BAD REVIEWS HE IS THE BEST PROFESSOR. Honestly the best class, lectures are recorded if you miss, and his hw is set up so you get many tries to get 100 so it helps to prepare for exams. Honestly he's one of my favorite professors this semester. He posts the lectures if you miss and they are so easy to understand he walks you through the examples. Super easy kinda feels like khan academy. Homework through this one website you have to purchase. You have unlimited trys though to get 100. 3 exams + final. TAKE HIM

My class was turned online during its running course. I must say for those who have had a negative experience, this is only because of yourself. Strongly recommend him. Put in the work and will pass. Exams straight out of lecture. Transferring online he gave us more homework, but with unlimited attempts so you can get an A every time. His class is whatever. I don't know why he has good ratings tbh. Theres better professors out there. His exams are very hard and they were even harder online. Save yourself the time and take someone better, or expect to teach yourself the material.
Professor Lee is nice but he doesn't teach well. I had to teach myself the whole semester. Our class got switched to virtual, but I felt like it made his class even harder. Take someone better :(
Don't take him, there's better professors out there for statistics.

I have always hated math and never understood it. Prof lee made my semester very easy. His way of teaching the material is way better than most professors and I would definitely take his class again. Easy quizzes and light homework. Highly recommend .

Had the utmost greatest experience with this professor. Makes the course easy to understand while being quite comical. There are three exams and one final. Ryan is an AWESOME stats professor! He prints out the blank notes for the lecture and gives it to his students so he can save them the hassle of printing! Professor Ryan Lee is a great teacher, I was able to get good feedback on what I needed to do to improve. He helped me during the math lab and I would definitely take him again. All you have to do is show up to class and listen to his lectures and do the . assignments. I would definitely take this class he's super funny and nice.

Yes ofc any BussCalc class WILL BE HARD to some extent. But choose a professor who will make it easier for you! (aka Prof Lee). I came into this class with 0 math skills whatsoever. Ryan is a great professor. It seems like he really cares about the success of his students and goes out of his way to help. The course's HW and textbook come w/ your required purchase of WileyPlus. I hate Wiley, but its nice to have online HW. 2 midterms and a final. Office hrs are crucial.

Great professor, he had online homework that was bundled with the textbook. He seems to really enjoy helping students both in and outside the classroom and is very accessible via office hours.

Easiest stats teacher you can get. Online textbook & homework so all you gotta do is buy the WebAssign code. Don't buy the actual textbook bc the WebAssign code comes with an online book. I've never failed a class until I took this one. It's so hard because the exams are worth so much and she goes very fast. Also, the homework is too much.

Be prepared to make this class your priority class since 70% of your grade is based on 3 exams. Winwin is an amazing professor. Her class isn't necessarily easy, but she gives you every opportunity she can to make sure you succeed AND learn the material too. WinWin was genuinely a professor who cared about her students and the material she was teaching. She encourages questions to create a dialogue with her lesson plans. She was always open to questions about the homework. The coursework itself is challenging and there's a good amount of hw but it's great test prep. She wants everyone to do well.

Best math teacher I've ever had. Would not have succeeded in this course with any other professor. She simplifies the material, explains every question she receives thoroughly, and was super funny. It's a difficult course, but if you do the work, show up, and spend a couple hours reviewing before any quiz/test you'll pass.

This class was one of the hardest for me this semester. Her lectures are GREAT, you need to come to class and complete all the hw to be prepared for the exams. Professor Nguyen is awesome. It's not an easy class but if you study beyond the hw and use her study guides for the exams you'll do well. I participated in Winwin's calculus class in the previous fall semester & admired how organized she is compared to other professors. As a Calc retake veteran, Uyen is the only CPP math professor who is extremely organized. Don't be fooled, her course is not a free pass. Very professional, and amazing at breaking down material.

Winwin is probably the only Calc professor at Cal Poly that cares about her students. She gives extra credit just because. If you ask for extensions she will give it. Business Calc is tough no matter who you take it with. Winwin emphasized that algebra is crucial for this course so brush up on that if it's been a while. She explains what's expected for quiz and tests by providing examples that will be similar to what she is testing you on. Seek tutors if you are struggling and don't give up.

WinWin is a great professor! This class is tough but doable. Theres a weekly assignment, and a quiz every couple weeks. Sometimes she goes fast over the material, but is always willing to clarify. Ask questions, and do not miss class. 3-4 quizzes and 3 exams only, aside from homework. If you need to take this class, take her!

If you like to bum around and skip class, you won't pass. She will respond bitterly to you if you ask for help if you aren't one of her daily-attendant students. Sweetest professor ever and provides great notes. She compromised with me a lot when I e-mailed her and is very understanding. So glad I took her! I really appreciated that she took notes with us, it's easier to follow along that way. prof is SUPER SWEET! she repeats a lot of her expectations to prepare you for quizzes and exams. i recommend taking this class if you can keep up with a fast-paced prof bc she quickly explains as much as she can (usually two lessons per lecture). Difficult subject in general but she helped us pass and was an amazing prof.

Professor Nguyen is the best! Math is not my best subject, but she really cares for her students. She is really easy to contact, she responds to emails fast and is always willing to help during office hours. Her lectures were easy to follow and I am not afraid to ask questions during class. I would 100% recommend others to take this professor.

Professor Nguyen is the best, take her! Bus calc is super hard on its own, she makes it understandable, does not belittle anyone for their confusion. She truly cares for her students, our understanding, and our grades. You have to put in work for this class, but if you attend class, and do the weekly homework, you should pass.

Course itself is challenging, but any math course is challenging. Professor Nguyen is honestly one of the few amazing math teachers. Understandable lecture. Ask questions & she try's her best to help. I would not get the textbook for online course. Everything is explained on her lecture/slides. Easy hw/quiz/exam ONLY if you study & practice.

Great professor. She really does her best to help students when they need it. The course itself is VERY CHALLENGING, but as long as you study for the final and tests, you should do fine. Definitely would recommend her. Sometimes shell give extra credit points for participating.

Professor Nguyen is an amazing professor! She's extremely accessible & is very responsive to her emails. If you have a question about a concept or math problem, she helps you break it down step by step & helps you identify where you made your mistake. I could not have passed STA1200 without her patience and quality of teaching. Highly recommend!

Lectures are done via Zoom. The lectures take up the entire time block for course with mandatory attendance. Follow by homework that is extremely tiring because it has a lot of parts to answer. Participation
She is nice and caring. She answers every question patiently regardless of how obvious the answer may seem. Highly recommend.

She has an accent, but you get used to it quickly. Homework is due every monday (online) there are a couple quizzes, 2 mid terms and 1 final exam, which she provides study guides for all. She wants you to do well and won't move on until everyone understands. I'm not good at math, but she taught in a way where i was able to understand. Take her!!!

She is honestly an amazing professor who obviously cares for all the students she has. She's available outside of class often, and would drop things just to be able to help you. She's honestly an absolute gem, and is the sole reason I'm remotely passing this class with a C, especially with all this wacky online stuff as of late.

Very good professor. Has an accent, but this is not an issue. In addition for caring for her students, she also makes sure to take time in making the student understand. Homework is online with a set date that it is due, so make sure to check that periodically. Also, make sure to study properly before the exams!

Simply amazing! Never had such a connection with a professor. The work is easy to understand just as long as you attend lectures and participate. Asking questions is mandatory in order to fully understand. Just as long as you participate and interact with her, you are in for a very joyful experience.

Great professor. She really cares about the students and always provides study guides that are pretty similar to the exams. Ms Nguyen is really good teacher. She is willing to help struggling students who need practice problems during office hours. Trig is never fun like this to me.

Winwin is sweetheart and best math professor I took in CPP so far. She provides exam reviews with exercises and keys to practice before taking exam. Prof. Nguyen is an extremely nice person. Always make sure you understand before she move on. 3 quizzes( drop the lowest one), 2 midterms and one final.
