Ms. Nguyen is a very caring and funny professor. 3 exams, a couple of easy quizzes, and homework assignments which are due every Monday. Sometimes she'll extend due dates and postpone quizzes or exams, which is very helpful if you use the time to study. I would highly recommend taking her class!

Excellent teacher! class require group work and she encouraged us to talk and engage with us incredibly and effectively. she did review session before quizzes and exams. very caring teacher and I'm so grateful to be in her class. Thanks for all the help and encouragement.

You will need an access code, all your hw will be on line. Very nice teacher, makes sure her students are on the same page before moving on. She gives one week to turn in hw. Need to study in order to pass the class, I recommend you take her.

Do all hw and sample tests, show up to class, ask questions, you'll be fine. very sweet professor and is very caring. explains concepts well and is open to helping anyone with questions. however, he doesn't grade homework and takes a long time to grade exams. hard to get feedback unless you ask him during office hours or during class.

Fernando is easily the best math professor I've ever had. He explains things so clearly, is very kind, and is extremely knowledgeable about math in general. Genuinely one of the best math professors I've had. He really wants to make sure you understand the material and is passionate about the subject. The work was very manageable. Garcia is a solid professor who is a really nice person. He has an accent since he is from Argentina but it is nothing that you can not understand. His lectures provide all the information you need to succeed. He also drops your lowest midterm grade so he wants you to pass the class. Great dude!

Probably one of the best and nicest professors I've ever had. He would have office hours often and would answer any question. He was very invested in helping students learn. Solid guy from Argentina. Very good at teaching calculus if you can get past his accent. Don't expect extra credit, the syllabus reigns supreme. Office hours are packed but he will make time for you.

Was a good professor and made the concepts clear to understand. Not much homework, mostly assigned practice problems and online problems every week. By far the best professor I've had at this school. His lectures are very intuitive and easy to follow. He is really great at clearing up any confusion students may have about the material. Very accessible during his office hours. He's honestly so sweet and helpful.

Extremely professional, answers questions thoroughly, creates fantastic, in depth lectures, assigns fair amounts of work, never missed a single day (excluding strike), and always willing to help. This is the kind of professor I wish every professor was like. 10/10, make sure you get him.

Lectures are extremely helpful and lecture notes are posted on Canvas. Weekly homework assignments may be tedious as it requires different approaches or long calculations. Exams are around the same difficulty as the in-class problem sets. Grading on exams are very generous and there are additional extra credit opportunities that are free points.

Easy lectures but weekly or biweekly homework. You can use your extensions up to 4 or 5 times with no punishment. He gives problem sets (psets) once per week/two weeks and gives extra credit if you do study guides for midterms and the final. Overall easy professor.

Yao is a great professor. Calc 3 is very demanding and time-consuming, but if you put in the work and effort, you will be well off. Do the study guides! Calc 3 is a DIFFICULT course, Yao is a great professor and forgiving on occasions when it comes to grading, but with the new common final it is essential that you put in the work, go to class, go to office hours, complete the all the hw, and study if you want the best chance at passing or receiving a high grade. One of the best math profs at cpp.

I took him Fall 2022. He's a great professor, provides notes that you cant print out to follow his well-done lectures. I didn't buy the textbook, and I never needed it. A great professor, if you really want to learn the subject, this is the teacher to take. He is really likeable and very charismatic. This is a difficult course, so if you want to pass, you will have to put in the work.
Great professor that would answer any question. Study guides for each exam and final. Also uses a free website for homework so no need to pay for Pearson.

Higher on the workload level with the amount of homework we were given, not hard work however. He was deathly afraid of COVID when I took his class, so we took a few exams and quizzes at home online. A regular calculus class to me since I took AP calculus in high school, but I heard his teaching style is kind of wacky from other students so beware.

One of my favorite professors for mathematics. He makes the class super straight forward and tries to give as much partial credit as he can on midterms. Only work was classwork and homework with no quizzes. The workload was fair and was not stressful. Very easy professor to talk to.

I really enjoyed my time in this course. Professor Jiahui Yao knows this subject really well and is really nice. It will not be an easy course. Before the final, I had a B+ (around 88.5%). To start off, Calculus 3, is, without a doubt, more difficult than Calculus 2, which makes this class hard by default. However, Professor Wilson is a very fair grader and works hard to help his students in and out.

For tests re-do the psets and the study guide and the examples on the lecture notes and you can probably get at least a B. He gives a good amount of partial credit so write something on exam even if you aren't entirely sure, not curved. Find examples outside of class, he has a yt channel called glass of numbers with some good ones. Worth taking him

Yao himself is a really nice guy. He's pretty chill and seems like a cool dude. With that being said, his teaching style just wasn't it for me. We would do like 1-2 problems max per section(sometimes not even explaining the full thing) and would move on. Two tests and final dictate your grade so you have to study super hard for them or it's over.

Bi-weekly quizzes and test heavy grades. Exams, quizzes, and the final are the majority of the grade, but 7% for homework isn't something to scoff at. He's helpful and a great teacher with a great personality. His grading is very fair as well, giving credit for your work. One thing, no curves, but he gives enough points for work on exams to make up

I found Prof Yao's lectures quite difficult to keep up with. His tests are extremely fair (if you do the study guide) and he is a very fair grader. He's happy answer questions anytime.

Yao was a pretty chill dude who is approachable to questions during and outside of class. His lecture notes are color-coded and gives class time to work in groups on study guides, homework, and any other assignments. His tests are fair with no surprises, although he expects you to work for it. Definitely take him.

Professor Yao's class was great! His notes were amazing (color-coded and neat) and he can be easily reached through office hours or email. Homework and study guides were difficult sometimes, but he does that on purpose to get us to prep for exams, which were the best designed exams I've had; two midterms (25% each) and a final (35%).

Uses Webwork for most hw, with unlimited attempts and 3 possible extensions. Lectures are color-coded and thorough, with reminders of basic concepts so we understand the more advanced ideas. Tests don't usually require tedious calculation, but you have to know the set-up. Office hrs 3 days/wk. He's caring and works hard for his students to succeed.

Although he was organized and you can understand the lecture and notes, it was the homework on MyMathLab and the exams that were very difficult. The lecture and notes didn't fully prepare me for homework and exams.
Homework/study guides were difficult but prepared you for the test well. Tests were extremely well crafted.

He's nice and easy to reach but I would not take him again. His class is well organized and he explains things decently well but his homework/classwork (he gives so much work) and exams are pretty hard. During lectures, we go over like one problem maybe two problems max a section and then move on, which is really hard to learn from.

I got by without the textbook. Very organizes! Notes are structured and Blackboard is easy to navigate. Gives study guides for extra credit. Has a YouTube and Instagram account. The first midterm was very easy. Compared to high school AP tests, his are much easier.

Such an amazing guy, his lectures are clear and easy to understand. His tests are not difficult at all. He really cares about his students and is super easy to get a hold of. Take his class if you want to understand the material and pass easily at the same time.

Professor Jiahui Yao is a gem. He makes calculus 1 so easy. I highly recommend everyone to take his class if can. Yao is so great because he explains everything step by step and in a organized way. He clearly has lecture plan and care about his students performance. I think he does give out extra credit as well. Only down side is lots of hw.

Yao is very friendly and likes to crack some jokes in his lectures. The class is lecture / difficult like any math class but he tries his best to spice it up a bit. His class consists of hwk packets due abt every 2 weeks, 2 midterms, and 1 final. Also, if your final test score is higher than a midterm, it can replace one lower mid term score.

The class itself can run a bit dry, however, the professor tries his best to make it somewhat interesting. He knows how to make a joke and actually makes his notes legible and organized. His tests are very fair, do the study guides and read your notes and you should be fine.

Perhaps it's just me, but Yao (or Wilson) runs a very difficult class. There are extra points to boost your grade, but the three tests (two midterms, one final) are difficult and dictate the majority of your grade. I love him so much I had to create a page for him at CPP. He is very clear with his lectures and well organized. If you just pay attention in class the hw and tests will be a breeze. His lectures are neat and they are my best notes that I have taken in a math class so far. He has a sense of humor and is really chill. I recommend!

Professor Thach is probably one of the best math professor/teachers I've ever had. He explains things very clearly, and he is also really generous when grading tests. My grade is because I'm simply not good at math. Anything else, he's just amazing! Love him, he's funny too.

super hard professor. I went to office hours and he straight up made fun of me and I felt so stupid. I would recommend you to take someone else.

Hurry and register for his class before it's full. (Even if the class is full, he most likely will still accept you if you're on the waitlist because he's that awesome). Amazing professor and really easy to connect with. He really wants you to succeed and is always willing to help and make sure you understand the material. Tough class if you don't like math. Be sure to attend, overall would take again for a math teacher.
Legit one of the best professor the college has to offer. He's so cute and smart. If you don't understand the lesson in class, then you can catch him at office hours and he'll help you.

Now let me first say his class is really challenging. A lot of time need to be spent working on homework and reviewing the lecture. Best calculus professor hands down. He cares about his students and makes sure you understand every bit of detail. ATTEND HIS LECTURES. This professor was easily the best professor I have had. He goes over multiple questions per exam during his lectures and will state when he does so. Best math professor ever. If you put in the work and consistently come to class this shouldn't be a challenge for you. Professor Gupta makes asking questions very easy and is always available even online to help with assignments. The expectations are very transparent and he wants nothing but for you to succeed.

This is a tough class no question. with that being said, he is tiers above any other professor ive had and ive had MANY great professors. He goes above and beyond and really does everything he can do to make sure you understand the work. Put in the time needed for this class and he will make sure you succeed.

This is clearly the best class I've taken at CPP so far. Prof. Gupta makes understanding Calculus concepts a breeze. His class was pretty hard, but he made a strong effort to make sure everyone understood. Always holds office hours or will stay behind in class to help explain. As long as you pay attention and ask for help when needed, you should be fine.

I generally suck at math but Professor Gupta was very supportive in making sure you are able to understand the topic being taught. Whether you needed clarification during the lecture or later in the day he was available and willing to help. 100% take this class.

I am terrible at calculus, but this professor helped me pass the class and actually learn the concepts. He is truly one of the best professors I've had and I would be delighted to take his class again. He is extremely responsive, caring, and funny. If you have a tough time with calc, please take this professor because he will help you SO much.10/10
He is one of the best professors that I had in college and although this subject is hard, he has office hours pretty much everyday. Take him.

one of the best professors that I have had so far at CPP. His lectures are very in depth and he explains everything very well. This professor was the best I have ever had. This is my second time taking the class and he made this class much easier to understand. He cares for people to get a good grade. Business Calc is a difficult subject but Professor Gupta is great. His lectures are very clear and he truly makes an effort to provide many resources to help students pass the class. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very straightforward class. The professor's online book was set up well which makes getting through simple. The workload for the class was very manageable. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Prof. Wallin-Huff is a great professor. She has her own online book, which is used for class. There are weekly assignments, w/ some weeks being a little tedious. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor huff is one of the best professors. We used her online book to make 1 question and to reply to 2 people. Our hw was inside the online book (questions) Nothing too much. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took this for elective credit however was quite satisfied with the class. Weekly assignments and discussions were a little bit of a pain. Exams are long but you can retake as many times as you can. Semester project is pretty cool depending on which option you pick. Professor is fun and caring.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Prof. Wallin-Huff is very kind and made it clear what had to get done. Two exams, a project, and weekly homework assignments; very simple class structure. She does not grade that hard so it was a really easy class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This class was very easy. Theres an easy weekly quiz, and short writing assignment. There are 2 exams and a final project at the end of the semester. Slight work. Recommended!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She is extremely nice and does not pressure students to memorize every detail of the textbook. Her philosophy on learning is something that all students will agree with and love. She talks with great interest during her lectures, drawing your attention even if you didn't initially have any interest in music.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Huff is amazing and the sweetest person. She's there when you need to communicate with her; she's very understanding and responds to email quickly. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Took this for the 2nd 5-week session. It was very fast-paced, and due dates were very lenient. Each unit had a pair of lectures, a response, and a quiz. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Her class is really fun, and really organized. She's really cool, and an easy grader. The content in the class is interesting even from someone who is not a music major. I'd recommend taking her class to complete the upper division GE for something easy.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: It was a fun class to take! She gives interesting video lectures and makes the topics easy to understand. The quizzes and 2 exams are easy to pass as long as you take the time to watch the video lectures. There is one project, but it was not too difficult to complete.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Prof. Huff enjoys her job, and this carries over to the lectures each week. Each week there is a quiz and a reflection assignment, but those are not difficult. There are two tests, midterm and final, along with a final project. The final project has many options to suit your strengths and weaknesses. Great class overall.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Really easy class and nice professor! Really enjoys her job!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Can honestly say she is an amazing professor and human being. You will enjoy her class, her topics are actually connected to history and technology.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took Music Appreciation with this professor and I can truly say I left this class with a greater appreciation for music. I would recommend this professor. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Honestly, this professor was not difficult. Her materials are fairly easy. She assigns one thing each week, which isn't a lot. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Overall great choice to take if you're looking for a class to take for this requirement. Content easy to learn, and there is extra credit chances throughout the semester. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Awesome professor. I only talked to him through email, but he responded quickly and was more than willing to answer any questions. The assignments were easy and enjoyable. If you've ever played a type of music before, the class will be a breeze.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Took him for an online class and he was super organized and quick with grading. His recorded lectures were very informational and straight forward, included examples and demonstrations. He was very accessible outside of class and an easy grader. Amazing professor!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Graulty is exceptionally patient and cares for his students. If you are communicative, he understands and will give you the necessary time. His classes go at the pace of his students. He is genuinely a great professor, and I really enjoyed his class!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Took for credit in Spring 2023 asynchronously. Straightforward and structured class with very manageable workload. Fairly quick to respond to emails. Weekly quizzes, discussion posts and includes one midterm, concert report, and brief composition project. Beginner-friendly for those new to music and lenient grader.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Class can boring and has a lot of busy work, but it's not a difficult class. A lot of the answers for the tests are found in his lectures and some of the readings. Two tests, one final, and a 6-7 page paper on a unique instrument of your choice. Lots of reading of different texts and summarizing them. Textbook may be found online somewhere.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I enjoyed the interesting lectures. Very insightful! Easy to pay attention when music history is important. Great professor!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great professor. The class is all about the history of music and can be very boring at times. 6 reading responses with a few having you read 30-40 pages. no quizzes, 2 midterms, and a final, all are easy if you show up to class and pay attention to lectures. Knowledgable and easy to talk to. Never went to office hours but talked after class a lot.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Super easy course and nice professor. Tests were online and he dedicated a day to going over possible test material. 2 tests online and a research paper as the final. Few short readings and responses.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's a really nice professor. There were only 2 tests and a final research paper. There are occasional readings and responses but they are only 300 words. Super easy course and a cool professor. His notes are posted to Canvas and attendance was not mandatory.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: 2 midterms, 1 research paper, one final, all online. Easy A class, professor is nice and going to the lectures are not mandatory.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Shiotsuki is caring and nice. He makes sure all students are on track and provides a lot of information about music. His exams are all based on the book, lectures and homework. His lectures can be very long and bore sometimes but they are insightful.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Shiotsuki is a very kind and flexible professor. He lectures for quite a while and really seems to be enthusiastic about his teaching. His midterms are based on a few amount of homework and some of the lecture material. So even though his long lecturing can be tiresome at times, at least keep a few mental notes on key bits of information.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: His lectures are easy to understand but the slides have few words. He does post class recording. Tries to answer any questions with a clear response and is helpful. Exams are not multiple choice but they are easy and basic knowledge of the topics will get you a good grade. 3 exams and 1 paper. Overall a great guy who sometimes has a monotone voice.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I really enjoyed taking this course. I am not a music major, but I am happy I chose Professor Shiotsuki. He is very much into his lecture and at times it may seem boring, but if you give it a chance you can learn a lot about the subject.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He's really kind and his lectures are really interesting. Just make sure you pay attention to all his lectures, take good notes, and remember the songs he puts on blackboard and you will be fine for the exams. There was a textbook but I never used it and I got A's.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Took her for MU1000. Despite being a GE course, she's a very passionate professor and has easy-to-follow lectures. I learned a lot from her course and I almost wish she was a STEM professor the way she broke down the more complex units later in the semester. If you're looking to learn a bit more about music theory, this is the professor to take.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Pretty easy class. Not too much homework and exams were a breeze, however lectures can go by slow sometimes. Shes a kind and funny professor.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She was really nice and class wasn't too hard.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took this class asynchronously and it's been pretty easy. He gives out 1 to 3 lecture videos a week and there's a pretty easy weekly quiz. There are also the occasional discussion posts, which are easy to write. Just watch the lecture videos and take notes and you'll get a pretty good grade.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Was in my phone the entire time during class and knew what was going on all the time. Easy A and the assignments r hard to mess up but the final is kinda messed up. 2 essays of random topics that he will pick for u is the final. If ur looking to complete a GE requirement then take this class

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Gravelle is passionate about what he teaches and makes learning enjoyable. However, quiz questions can be confusing due to oddly worded answers. But seriously, you learn a ton in his class, and it's a really good GE option. Overall, he's great! We did discussion boards, lecture quiz, and a final concert report

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This is my 2nd time taking a class with Dr. Gravelle,and I truly enjoy his lectures! He's friendly, funny, kind, helpful outside of class, responds to emails fast. He'll set up office hours with u outside of class if u need, he truly wants his students to succeed! I learned so much about music theory from him, he's amazing! Open note midterm/finals

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Buzz Gravelle is an amazing professor. I already had taken AP music theory in HS so I dealt with a conflicting way of answering his prompts/tests to how he preferred, but he knew generally I understood the class. Very engaging, very charismatic professor. Take him as a music major and you will have a strong foundation, and someone in your corner.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Amazing, friendly, patient, and kind professor! Cares about his students & wants them to succeed. VERY helpful in & outside of class, responds to emails fast, cool lectures, updates grades fast. About 2 to 3 quizzes each month. For MU1201, if you have little music theory background, this course might be a little bit challenging and fast for you.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I was not interested in this class at all. The work was easy and all you have to do really is show up. If you would like to take an in-depth class about classical music than this is it. While Professor Gravelle is passionate about what he teaches it was still an incredibly boring class to me.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: We were online MW and then in person on F. There usually were weekly assignments/ musicianship quizzes, but often he'd give half credit for the quizzes just for being there. Midterm was open note. He calls you out to answer questions, but even if you don't get it he explains and walks you through things pretty well.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This course is relatively easy if you understand music. Attendance and participation matters! If you dont dont participate he will call you out. His lectures are very informative and he is always willing to help students outside the classroom. The only downside is that he doesnt update grades so you never know if youre passing or failing.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is really cool! His class is always fun to be and I cant wait to be in his class again next year!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Music Theory 1 was my favorite class. I'm a huge music nerd and have been listening to it all my life, but I've never had formal training (learning to read, etc), so this class was really difficult for me. However, it was an incredibly rewarding experience, and I loved every minute of it. Prof has a great sense of humor and a library of knowledge.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: If you are a music major, he is a great professor to attend. While he is tough, he is motivated and works hard to help you understand. His theory classes (which are also GE's) may be hard to those who don't study music. His ego can get in the way of his teaching and make him annoying at times however. He is strict on attendance.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This class was bad in my opinion because I was just taking it as a GE but if you were actually majoring in music then it might be a decent class. The professor gets way into detail with music. You have to attend a concert that he approves of and do an essay about it and it's due on the day of the final. The final is multiple choice and TWO essays

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very tedious class filled with discussions. However, teacher is very nice and clearly dedicated to music. She tends to notice things that were copy and pasted or "using outside knowledge" so be careful if you use AI or Google because the discussions need to be things that are in content of the book.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: A great professor overall, be specific regarding Discussion Boards to get a higher score, those are vital when it comes to grades. Attend office hours as well to know the lesson and video lectures.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Grade is based on 3 exams and one report, with an additional extra credit assignment. No homework, however there are ONLY exams.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very kind professor and is genuinely passionate about music. Homework assignments are small but will build up if you don't keep up + study well for exams. Has a concert report and extra credit assignment that are both very easy. Didn't take attendance but will be hard to learn without the lectures.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Really easy if you have even a basic knowledge of music. Lectures that you should take notes on, but not hard if you set aside a few hours to cram it all. She doesn't proctor tests. She grades by 3 tests and a concert report, but they're not hard if you have your notes with you.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Only homework for the semester were discussion boards, about one every other week. The only other grade were 3 tests, all 50 questions, and very specific and based off lectures. Very easy overall, the extra credit and music report bump up your grade an entire letter.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: she was nice and accomodating but as someone who doesn't know anything about music, this class was rlly hard so be prepared

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Maldonado was an okay professor, she was nice and very passionate about music. Just that her class was heavy, you will have to do discussion boards every week. There is a textbook that is require to buy (renting it is cheaper), make sure to attend every lecture and take notes. Every exam requires a scantron and is only 50 questions each.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She's a cool professor in all honestly. Very lenient and very understanding when it comes to deadlines. The class overall consists of discussion boards, a concert report that is mandatory, and then an extra credit. The concert report and the e.c. combined are worth a lot, so that is a +. The tests were dummy difficult, so rely on quizlet and allat.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Maldonado is the sweetest professor I've ever had. She is very clearly in love with what she does and gets excited about teaching. Her class was super easy and consisted of turning in notes, doing group projects, and a final presentation. Absolutely loved her and the course she taught.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Too much material. Definitely hard for just a ge class. If you skip class it is kind of hard to keep up. Most important thing would be to go to the review lectures before midterms. Very easy to get a bad grade in this class. It's mostly memorising so it isn't too difficult, but you definitely need to study. She's an awesome professor though.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very easy upper division elective if you need to take one. She is very kind, but you need to show up to class or else she will take role and dock you big points. Her class is pretty straightforward with very little work for an upper division. She is super respectful of her students and loves engaging us, but her lectures are mostly YouTube videos.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Mrs. Maldonado is really caring; however, her class is really hard if you miss any of the lectures. The only thing she puts in the grade book is the tests and the final essay. She randomly calls on students to give her the answers from the homework and goes over it in class but other than that, she doesn't give you a grade for the homework.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very easy A class. The exams are multiple choice and it's usually defining terms. There's is a report where you have to o to two concerts and document it, this is probably the hardest part of the class. Recommend!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Honestly I had a hard time in this class, but I'd still recommend it. Exams were pretty hard, but you should be fine as long as you go to class, pay attention, and do your homework. The two concert reports are only 2-3 pages, and the extra credit assignment is nice.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Don't take her, tests hard, class average was at 60% for all exams. No curves and no study guides, rambled during class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Awesome Professor in my opinion. I had no prior music knowledge; just pay attention in class and you'll be alright!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She is passionate about what she teaches and is understanding of students. There is no homework, just two 2-page reports and a midterm/final. The material is very informational and history-based so it's easy to search things up if you don't know the answer. You don't need music experience, and the class is very easy as long as you pay attention.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Absolutely loved her, I actually did not show up to class, most of the class is on quizlet. She only grades two reports that are super easy and 3 exams. The exams are super easy with quizlet.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: You have to make sure to pass the 2 concert reports, 2 tests, 1 final . At first glace you would think this class is easy, no. Music is hard to learn so pay attention in class and understand what you are learning. It helps to make study guides from what you learned in the previous modules. Know how to read music for most of it is on the tests.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: EASIEST CLASS EVER! shes a very kind person and it is very clear how passionate she is about what she teaches in her class meetings. her classes are easy to follow, just be sure to take some notes. no hw! 2 concert reports(super easy, just follow her outline), 2 mc midterms, 1 final. no music experience needed to pass the class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor was very caring and nice, she's very passionate about her job. She always recorded lectures to upload online (just remind her sometimes she forgets), 2 concert reports, 3 exams (2 exams, 1 finals), homework is optional but you should probably do it if you want to pass, and an extra credit opportunity; it's also a point based class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She was a wonderful teacher and you can feel her passion through her lectures. I will say, having previous music knowledge made the class extremely easy but I can say for people that don't have that privilege to just pay attention to lectures and practice. Music is almost an entire different language so don't expect yourself to be perfect!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Nice teacher, definitely cares. I passed everything but the tests were insanely difficult. Did not understand a thing, and I played some instruments for years. Felt as if this was too advanced for a beginner music class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: you could tell just how passionate she is about music and its history. she seemed so happy during our zoom calls whenever some good classical music comes up. i always felt bad though since i slept through most of her classes. she grades only on concert reports which is about a page and a half of words. easy class!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Maldonado is so kind; she incorporates so many interesting topics in the course. Tbh, it was such an easy course; the course consists of journals (don't procrastinate on the journals). There are 3 projects (it's broken down into groups, so you only have to do 1 slide). The 3rd project is on your own, super easy. There are two reports.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Maldonado was great and super nice!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The switch to online classes made things difficult for the professor which was the root of many of the issues I had with this class. From not knowing which screen she was sharing to having errors on the tests, it sometimes made things difficult. The class itself isn't too hard.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Prof. Maldonado was very sweet, unfortunately we were not able to have class in person, but she made the best of it. She does take attendance almost every class in the first few weeks. There is not much homework, but it is necessary to study before tests. She loves what she does, and you can definitely tell through her work with her students.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very caring, and passionate professor. PowerPoints uploaded on blackboard for reference. 2 essays, 2 midterms, and 1 final.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very nice and sweet professor! I had no prior music knowledge but I passed the class with an A by studying. Pay attention to the test reviews! Keep in mind that the 2 workbooks for this course is $125 from the Bronco bookstore (they do not sell the set online).

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She really cares about her students and it is clear that she loves what she teaches. She is always there to help her students and although there is a lot of clapping involved, it helps those who have never learned anything related to music.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Maldonado is such a sweetheart! She is so filled with joy to teach about music and she makes the class really easy. Plus she shows A LOT of youtube videos during class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I only recommend this class for those who have music theory experience.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: great professor; class is easy as long as you take notes and study. lectures can be slow at times but overall very interesting.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Attendance is mandatory and checked by randomly calling on people. An absence is -5 points. There are 2 midterms, 1 final + applied exam (play rhythms on piano), and 2 concert reports. Extra credit is offered by writing additional concert reports. Clear and concise lectures. Easy professor if you have prior musical knowledge.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Sweet professor. Very enthusiastic. Would definitely take her again. Super caring/understanding. She's been teaching for a while & you'll definitely learn a lot from her class. Participation, concert/museum report, group presentations, journals, assignment, final presentation. One of the most inspirational professors.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Super sweet lady but if you have no prior music knowledge please hesitate to take, the exams are very difficult and you have to learn how to play piano. Textbook is very expensive.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She's a very sweet woman and it's obvious that she has an intense passion for music and sharing this with her students. Although her class does tend to be boring. You basically just show up to class to hear her talk about history for an hour. She has a few extra credit opportunities. She checks attendance randomly. 1 absence -5 points

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: $100 textbook required for class. No homework. Grade is dependent on two midterms and the final. Took it thinking it was going to boost my GPA, but boy was I wrong. if you have knowledge in music, you'll get an A, but if not be prepared to study long hours for the midterms and final.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: In this class you learn how to read music and play the piano. I had no background in music before this class but she did great at explaining everything and gave time to practice in class. The midterms/final were easy just have to pay attention during class and take notes. We practiced for applied final during class USED BOOK ARE OKAY FOR THIS CLASS

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Two midterms (m/c), two concert reports (attend CPP's or any others' concerts), one final (m/c). She tells you exactly what to study for. She's sweet & passionate about music! She does attendance randomly and each absence is a 5 point deduction, so don't miss class. Plus, you learn a ton in one class meeting, so it wouldn't be smart. E/C too!!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: You don't have to have any music background to join this class. she will teach you the basics but the later portion of lectures get more difficult so pay attention. you need to buy the books because you'll use them everyday. you don't really need to do hw because she'll go over it in class. exams are reasonable

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: A very sweet, and caring lady. She's extremely passionate about music. There are 2 midterms, and then a final, the usual. Also two papers to write in which you have to attend 2 live concerts, but they're easy points. Also has extra credit during the test that is pretty easy, it's just memorization. Just study and the tests themselves are easy too.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Maldonado is a very sweet lady. She's honestly so caring. There are 2 midterms and 1 final (the usual). She does not collect homework, which is to complete problems in the book. So I would recommend buying a used copy and save yourself about $50. She understands that music is hard and if she sees you trying, you'll pass!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She is very nice and loves her subject, which makes the lectures nice. I had her 2 hour class but she always released us 20-30 mins early. She tells you exactly what you need on the test and goes over everything in class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Such an adorable and kind woman, she loves what she does and radiates gold in her aura. A very welcoming class and homework isn't mandatory, it just makes for great practice! She's so understanding too! I got a C but I have dyslexia and couldn't read music so well.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: A Maldonado is the cutest lady,so passionate about music. Showed us interesting pieces of music and put a lot of character into her lectures w personal stories. only 3 tests on material (not cumulative) so make sure and study. She tells you what to know and it is pretty accurate. know the songs for extra credit and MAKE SURE YOU ATTEND PERFORMANCES

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Such a great teacher!!! I'm a freshman and she definitely made my first quarter of college great! I looked forward to learning more and she made it fun and exciting to learn all about music!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Fun class!! The class actually enjoyed learning about music history. She makes the class laugh. Group project was fun. Easy grader and captivates the entire class. I took other courses of hers (MU 425 & MU 101). I Highly Recommend!!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I personally love her, she's enthusiastic and very helpful if you just ask. After a couple weeks she stops taking attendance but I recommend attending all classes or you WILL get behind. Learning music for the first time is just like learning math for the first time.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This was an easy class. She rarely takes attendance, but there is a journal which is how she checks you've attended. There is a booklet ($22ish) she asks you to buy, and comment on in the journals for credit. There are no quizzes or tests, the final is a project (which is easy). An easy synthesis class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very sweet woman and extremely passionate about her subject and teaching. I loved her!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very sweet and nice lady. Loves music and tells you everything to know for the tests. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very enthusiastic and loves music. Enjoyed the class...no essays or hard tests, all multiple choice and extra credit was offered. 4 tests, all easy if you come to class or have the book. Attendance isn't really a big deal, takes roll SOMETIMES

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I found the class difficult, I felt like she went through all of the material too fast. She calls a lot on people, and requires you to do a lot of work in the books. Her tests are kinda hard. You have to pay attention in her class. It is not an easy A at all.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She's not a bad teacher, she has way too many kids in class so it's hard to learn, and she doesn't seem to comprehend that people are at different levels of learning and rushes ahead, and her need to have the class clap ALL THE TIME is irritating, but she's nice and explains music terms pretty clearly.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She is kind of boring but she's so sweet and tries to make class interesting. She tells you what you need to know for the midterms and final so it's pretty straight-forward. You have to attend 4 concerts also for this class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very vague, boring, nothing to do with music, very religious class all she lectures on is sections of the Church, Popes. DO NOT TAKE!!!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Class was fun and work was not too difficult. She helps out her students and is very animated/passionate about music. Recommend!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Song is very enthusiastic, which helps if you have her for an early class. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Take good notes on the lectures and ALL the readings he makes you read because they will be on all the quizzes. Great professor!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Chadd is SO funny. Easily one of my favorite professors of all time. His class is easy if you put in the work.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
