I recommend participating during the class discussions because it really makes the class worth while. Overall, really liked the class and Professor.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The material is interesting but the class is pretty dull. Dr. G has a monotone way of speaking and its difficult to engage with her lectures but shes one of few philosophy professors at Cal Poly. You just kinda have to get through it. Make sure youre doing the weekly reading otherwise youll trip yourself up. Good luck!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Loved this class ! Professor G made the material clear and gave us real life examples to help us soak in for context. She quizzes weekly so definitely take time to read her assignments. The final was optional which we all loved! I would definitely take her class again.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Although you are gonna read a lot for this course this prof really tries to make it understandable as possible, so that does mean going to the classes. She's very caring to all the students especially those who don't understand, if you have a question she'll keep trying to explain it until it makes sense. Grades fairly and is genuinely passionate.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She was a great professor! Her class was very hard for me in the beginning because of the large papers she made us read, but I found a way around it. As long as you read the first page of the articles and have an idea about the concept, the rest will flow easily. I was fascinated by how smart she spoke. She made me love philosophy.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Everyone told me not to take a philosophy class! this professor is so smart and explains the material in a simplistic and articulate way that makes you think. 25% of the lectures may feel very boring but you will heavily appreciate the other 75%. I honestly believe taking this class changed me as a person. I cannot recommend this professor enough.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Gasdaglis is very nice and provides clear material during lectures. Everyone warned me about taking a philosophy course because it might be boring and useless, but I really enjoyed taking this class. You are expected to write 15 journals by the end of the semester and you take 3 midterms and the final exam. There are pop quizzes!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Gasdaglis is an amazing professor who keeps boredom out of her classroom with often fascinating discussions and engaging lecture that takes input from the class (I'm not a philosophy major btw). She assigns reading almost every class and then quizzes you on it next class but her quizzes are relatively easy if you merely skim the readings.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Reading quiz after most readings. Very lecture heavy and boring. Hard to stay awake in class. Monotone professor.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took Professor Gasdaglis for PHL 204. It was her first quarter teaching at CPP but it was also my first quarter as a freshman at CPP. I really enjoyed her class and she made it super interesting. She didn't require a book. You do have a good amount of reading and probably a quiz after the reading but it's interesting. Would recommend her.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: honestly don't take this professor. I went to office hours since i didn't understand the concept of an assignment we had to do and felt that it was rushed and she tried to rush me to answer even though i was completely lost when she taught it in class

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Overall, this course was easy if you want to get some credits. However, Professor Reardan assigns a DISGUSTING amount of homework. There were weekly quizzes based on the homework, two midterms, a group debate, and a final. This course provided more stress via assignments than my actual major courses.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She never let anyone finish their questions. If you didn't say the exact answer to a question she would put you down. She's such an incredibly harsh grader. "I'm better then you" vibe. I missed a class due to a doctors appointment and when I told her before hand she gave me no opportunity to make up the work I missed in class. I hate her class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Overall an easy class although there is a lot of homework quizzes, the midterms are just like the study guides. She is an easy grader but assigns an assignment after each class. In addition, each student has to participate in a group debate.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: she has an "in class activity" every lecture so attendance matters! 25 or so homework assignments, 3 papers, 3 quizzes, midterm, group debates, final, 2 e.c opp. seems like a lot of work/difficult but if you follow and understand her lectures, you'll get at least a B. she's always there to help out if you're confused on a concept. highly recommend!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She's insightful and understanding. Lots of assignments, but most are pretty easy. In total there were 20+ Homeworks, a small in-class activity almost every lecture day, 3 papers, a group debate, and some tests. Make sure to pay attention in lectures as most of what she writes on the whiteboard will be on the tests word-for-word. Solid choice.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This Professor will talk over the class time about the basic lessons, but then give a test about different things while weighing her tests and quizzes a lot in class. You have to repeat what she says or she will fail you.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Instead of coming out of class mind blown I always came out in relief that class was over. She grades her homework & tests let alone in class activities so harsh and nitpicks every little part of your assignment. She is the most passive aggressive prof I have ever come across & she gets agitated when you answer a question incorrectly.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Reardan challenges students to answer examples and gets very frustrated when they get the answer wrong. Grades her assignments and test very strict. She is also very good one telling you what you did wrong, but doesn't say how you can do better. She can either be all over the place on the whiteboard for notes during lectures or lost in thought.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Reardan's lectures are very good and engaging when the class participates. This was definitely one of my favorite in-person classes this semester. The whole course was rly cool but there was a bit more homework and papers than I initially hoped. It's by no means unreasonable though. I definitely would recommend for Children's Lit!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Tests are take home, but can be time consuming. She takes a bit to grade, but not anything terrible. Automatic 8/10 for turning in an in class activity. Goes over plenty of examples, but sometimes she can lose train of thought. Super helpful and understanding if you reach out.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Positives: goes over a lot of examples, posts lecture videos for the course Negatives: exams are time-consuming and stressful (and she takes a long time to grade them), assignments are often posted late, she gets frustrated when people answer example questions wrong, she sometimes lashes out at students

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Basically, she gives out A LOT of work. Sometimes forgets to post assignments and needs to be reminded. She's pretty nice, but feels like this class is not worth the workload. Second exam was only 2 weeks after the first one, so seems pretty unfair. Easy grader for the most part. There's definitely better professors to take.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Reardan is a great professor and teaches very clearly in her lectures. Instructions are always given for assignments and she usually gives helpful examples. She is a very fair and easy grader. She can be a little unorganized sometimes but as long as you keep up and pay attention the class is very easy!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Reardan is an easy-going and straight forward teacher. However, I find her online class to cause her to be a bit disorganized and constantly posting things later than she announces which can be frustrating. Just make sure to constantly check in and be on top of your work in that case.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Reardan is THE BEST professor I've had at CPP so far. She is so sweet, caring, & smart. I took this class only for the credit, but I actually ended up learning a lot! She assigns a lot of readings and some are difficult, but they all give you a better understanding. Take good notes, it really helps with exams. Participate in class discussions!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Her class is extremely boring but she manages to give good notes, she lets you know whats going to be on the test and if you read the notes and do the homework you will be fine!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Good teacher. Very kind. A little boring. Speaks and explains things clearly. Easy grader. Need book for HW and readings(recommend renting). One debate in small groups (can opt to have it outside of class). Mostly just lecture and practices.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Reardan is a kind person. The more you participate the more she likes you! Her lectures can be repetitive so it's fine if you miss class as long as you know the major points. Try not to miss in-class writings! Lots of reading! She gives you all of the exam questions before the exam and picks a select few off that list. Overall, fun class!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The class was overall fine. You have to teach yourself alot. If you get D or C's on the test you'll basically get an B in the class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: There aren't pop quizzes but there are quizzes after every reading hw that she assigns. Her tests are based on her lectures, so make sure to write down notes and pay attention to them. She is a little disorganized while writing notes but it's still okay. One group project. 5 books needed are reading hw but aren't used that much. (share w/someone)

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This professor is incompetent. She constantly contradicts both herself and the textbook, often stating that the book itself is wrong. She assigns a ton of homework, rarely collects it, and randomly assigns poorly timed quizzes. She is incredibly disorganized. She grades very harshly and includes things she mentioned only one or two times on exams.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Reardan is a nice professor, but her lectures are extremely unorganized, making the material much harder to understand. In addition, she challenges students to find answers themselves instead of helping them directly. The class grade is made up of 3 tests, attendance, a bunch of quizzes based on daily readings (which get annoying), and a project.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Grades according to lectures. Gives study guides before each test. One group project. Overall Reardan's class was very organized and easy to pass. However, it does take her a while to grade assignments. She also used Tophat instead of Blackboard.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Her lectures are long, and kind of hard to take interest in. Her tests are not as difficult, but the way she grades essays is strange. She would say I did a fantastic job on an essay and give me only an 87 on it with no feedback. I was so close to getting an A (1.6% more) , but she refused to round my grade up. Her grading cost me a spot on the DL

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Reardan is one of the most caring professors. She teaches with such passion that captures your attention. Philosophy can be quite difficult but she makes it fun and interesting! The books used and read are somewhat difficult but she explains it so well!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She was alright. Made class mandatory. During every start of class she would give us a code to enter into this app (you have to buy it) in order to mark you present. Then she makes you take a quiz about the reading she usually assigns. Class is very boring I'm always having trouble staying awake cuz all she does is talk and talk. Kinda rude too.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Neverrrr taking her again. So much reading, quizzes almost every day, unrealistic amount of questions on her exams (a lot of people didn't finish and she blamed it on us), and her lectures are way too messy. Didn't learn anything meaningful.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very nice person, but the material is hard. Expect a quiz every class. Lots of homework (not graded but it will be on quizzes). 3 papers, 3 exams (final cumulative), 1 debate on topic of choice. Material is not useful for later in life (Fallacies, constructing definitions, etc.) Average exam score was between 50%-60% for each of the 3 exams.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Shes an easy teacher and is very forgiving in terms of lost points. Show up to class because she does random quizzes and if you do, you'll be able to pass her tests with little to no studying. Share a textbook; lots of short reading and its not worth the money.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This was my favorite class of the quarter. Dr. Reardan's lectures are very interesting and get right to the point. We have quizzes almost every day after a reading is assigned. Most of them were not graded, but you should always be prepared. There's a group project and two midterms and a final. The final isn't cumulative. It's a great class!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Good teacher, she knows her stuff. Can be quite boring at times but what class isn't? Oh, and its not like deep level thinking if that's what you thought, its more stuff like sentences and arguments and stuff. Quite easy if you use 10% of your brain and think and memorize some stuff. Shes quite nice and learns your names.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Unorganized initially but improved by week 3. Gave (at the time) daily reading quizzes which aren't hard if you read (short) and her exams are essay, but pretty reasonable. She lets you have notes and gives you the questions in advance so if you take notes on her lectures and read, you'll do fine! Class was pretty easy and straightforward!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: No Comments

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: No Comments

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: No Comments

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: NOT LOW EFFORT. For a GE class the effort I have to put into this class is blasphemy! Might as well change my major to philosophy with all the NEW knowledge im learning. Stay away if your looking for a good time. If you have him on your schedule. GL your spending all your time and efforts into his class. GG Drop out NOW

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Stowell is super funny and I really enjoyed his lectures. He's clearly devoted his life to philosophy which makes the lectures interesting, but also made him quite jaded and cynical. Work wise, the class was light with study guides almost identical to exams and quizzes based on the most boring reading ever, but I still got by only skimming through.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Took him for Religions of the World for C2 in Spring 2023. He is a nice guy and makes the lecture a lot more interesting. You do need to study a bit and his tests are not that difficulty if you study. You do have some projects as well but not so difficult either. Would definitely take him again.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very easy to get an A (as in straightforward, not low-effort). Readings were a slog in contrast to the great lectures, and the assignments are nearly impossible to fail if you read the textbook chapters, which are mind-numbingly dull, which I cannot emphasize enough. If you are predisposed to this (e.g., goths, masochists) maybe you'll enjoy it.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I don't know if it is the class or the professor but the class was a grind when it needn't be. You are expected to figure out the prompt to essays which are meant to be as tricky as possible which is a terrible idea because if you are off a little bit then you are docked heavily. A B is attainable but the stars will have to align for an A.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: All previous ratings lead me to have false expectations. He's a tough grader but then fails to provide any context as to why you received the grade you did (claims you're vague then is vague himself). And so much readings.. If you're looking for an easy going class, I wouldn't suggest taking this professor. Oh and he doesn't respond to emails!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Textbook readings are required but i never read a single page, powerpoints from class is a summary of all the required readings, and some example he gives in his lectures ends up on the tests and homework. So as long as you pay attention in class you should be fine. Great professor btw, very patient and always provide help to those who asked.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took his class in Fall 2020, and I came back after graduating to say that out of all the classes I have taken, his class was my favorite. The reading and lectures are thought-provoking, and it might sound strange, but you feel a great sense of satisfaction just by learning the subject. Highly recommend this class to anyone.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great professor overall. He teaches with a passion and makes sure his students understand the material. The material is a bit difficult to understand and does become a bit much towards the end of the semester. As long as you read the textbook and take notes, you will be fine. Only graded by exams and essays but there are extra credit opportunities.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Easy going class, read his readings and you will be fine for tests. This class opens your mind and you definitely learn about other religions. He isn't strict, and he seems to care for his students. I would totally take him again if I could.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great professor, really opens your eyes to the world to be able to critically break down anything we come across in life. Few things were graded for the grade. Nice, caring guy though.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took this class in the summer. Every week was a quiz but he gives two chances and one discussion board. His midterm was kinda hard. Quiz was heavily based on textbook. Textbook chapters averaged 70 pages long sometimes longer.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The asynchronous class basically was you reading a book and then answering a question that he has at the end of the chapter. The quizzes are 2 attempts and multi-choice with answers so you can retake and do better. Midterm was easy even if you don't read the book and the final was as well. He won't grade until the end of the summer so its a gamble.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: The most based professor I've ever had. Encourages fulfilling discussion about philosophical concepts. Will often reference the textbook during lecture and on quizzes and tests. His teaching style can make it feel like there is a "method" to studying philosophy, which there is. But if you come into the class with an open mind it should be no sweat.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Really enjoyed Stowell's class this semester. His lectures were engaging and knowledgeable, both on Eastern and Western traditions. He likes to offer commentary on current events and on some subjects he mentions, which I personally enjoyed and found quite funny. Makes lectures especially engaging and entertaining

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Tough grader, try to answer everything to best ability. Took online summer, lecture videos and one assmt per module. Gave final essay instead of an exam(mite b diff for other semest). Graded AFTER the class concluded and there were so many points he took off that did not make sense to me but I could not argue about it since class concluded :/

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: A bit existential and negative, says some weird things about political issues. Otherwise fine, keeps his own opinions out of the actual tests and assignments, lectures aren't too bad if you take notes. Tests are easy. Experiential project is just about your own opinion so real hard to fail. Wish it was a bit more discussion-central but oh well.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great Professor. Great Textbook. Great class. Highly intelligent and not quick to make judgements.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: There were three papers (midterm and final) that are kinda long. One was an argumentative essay, and the other two had various questions from the chapters(#1, #2, #3 etc). There are quizzes (2 attempts per quiz) that are based all on the readings, powerpoints, & lectures. I was not interested into philosophy, but this became my favorite class since

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Stowell was great at explaining philosophy, and was enthusiastic in doing so. For his class, you need to buy a book to understand the sections and for the quizzes. Readings are long and difficult, but are worth the read. Great teacher overall, recommend truly.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Stowell is nice and you can tell by his lectures that he genuinely enjoys teaching philosophy. Before the quarantine I enjoyed the class. But after, he became satin himself with the unreasonable amount of work load he assigned to a GE class. Literal break downs from what he expects from the assignments and not being clear on them at all.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Stowell is the kind of guy you can have a deep conversation with any day of the week and you come out of his class feeling like you've learned something new. It was easily my favorite classes on campus and I'll never forget how great of a teacher (and guy) Adam Stowell is. If you want to take Intro to Philosophy, look him up.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Stowell is such a great guy, my favorite professor this semester. Lot of reading, but youll do fine even if you cant always keep up with it; just try your best. He has a dice system for quizzes and my class only took like 3 this term so we were lucky lol. Theres one paper and its pretty easy to do well on. If you like to think, take this class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Passionate and exciting professor who can be quite funny. His class, quizzes, and tests are straight-forward and he reviews the exams afterwards. Lectures a bit unorganized, sometimes with a PPT or just written on board. Attendance is taken. Does his best to answer theoretical questions but often argues back to his original point.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Stowell was a funny and interesting professor. He is super passionate about philosophy and does his best to help us to understand the lectures. This semester we had 2 midterms, 1 essay (3-5 pages) and a final that was lengthy. Overall, the course was challenging if you are not as interested in philosophy. There are readings + quizzes.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Stowell is extremely knowledgeable and attempts to make class a little more fun with his jokes. There is a lot of reading involved if you want an A. The semester consists of 3 tests and 2 (3-5 pg) essays. I barely read half of what he assigned, but I did well on essays so if you're not good at either, you might want to enroll elsewhere

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: You do have to study for this class. But if you pay good attention to his lectures and take notes, half the work of studying will be done for you. His lectures are engaging and he enjoys students participating.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: There are 2 papers and 2 midterms and that determines your grade. All the other posts are outdated. If you mess up on any of these, you're done. He's a good teacher, but his midterms are super hard. The midterm is worth almost 50% of your grade. Study Hard, attendance is optional.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is very passionate about philosophy. Doesn't assign much homework, but you have to pay attention in class. He gives out quizzes when he wants but he is fair. He uses the textbook all the time. If you don't have the book, you will most likely fail.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Literally, the best professor I had. He's super funny and understanding. He helps out if you ask him questions and makes sure it's completely fair. He let's two attempts per quiz on blackboard and gives you a study guide on the questions that will be on the midterm and final. A good amount of group projects. Show up, makes everything extra easy.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Not gonna lie, I thought that the subject (Philosophy) was hard to understand, but as long as you ask questions and reread the material, you can't go wrong with him. When it comes to final grades, he is fair and reasonable.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: class at first is hard, but he helps you adjust to philosophy. He gives you everything you need to succeed (midterm/final study guides) and the essays are easy and fun (got to write about movies!) The textbook is a must! I really enjoyed the topic and how he presented it, hes funny and sarcastic. Not an easy A though, do your work and youre good

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Please please PLEASE take this professor. You won't regret it. He is SO FUNNY and makes going to class enjoyable. He gives a 10 question quiz about every week. He lets students roll a dice and if it lands on a 1 or a 6 you automatically get full-credit. There is a free point question on all tests and you write 2 essays. Study and you will pass.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Prof. Stowell does a really good job of explaining all of the concepts, terms, thought experiments, etc. There's a lot of reading to do, which is what the quizzes are based on and there are only a couple of assignments (1 hw, 2 papers, 5 quizzes, midterm and final). He is a cool professor, very approachable, and would take another class with him.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This professor is great. From the way he discusses the subject with passion to the way he makes jokes to keep everything light. It's not hard to pay attention in his lectures because he makes them so interesting. The workload is not bad at all, and his sense of humor and good looks are just perks when it comes to him being a great professor.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Absolutely loved this professor. He made a subject that could tend to get hard to follow, easy to understand. He was always willing to help with any questions you had and extremely friendly. He's also very funny and pretty cute.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Really great professor who knows his stuff. The book isn't 100% mandatory, but it will help a crap ton more if you get it. Other than that he has a really great personality and sense of humor and his workload is low with only two essays and a few quizzes.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I highly recommend this professor. He is funny and helpful, you really understand the material and do not get bored.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Dr. Garcia based all her classes on student discussions. Almost every answer to the questions we had were "what do you think?" or "how do you feel about this?". I took the course because I did not have background on the material, not because I wanted to form an opinion on concepts I barely understood myself.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: A truly passionate, and caring professor. Do not be led astray by other reviews, he does not penalize for missing class and thus many people do not show up (take advantage of it). It is obvious that missing class would lead to a worse grade bc he is very lecture-reliant. If you show up you will get a good grade he will always make time for you.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Avoid this professor, "attendance isn't mandatory" but if you do not attend class he will grade your papers with more criticism than those who do go to class(verified). He is not understanding and has no empathy for students. He should rewrite his syllabus and state what he expects from students because it is misleading. AVOID!!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: One of the best professors I've taken. No textbook needed, he uploads all the papers and powerpoints. His canvas is very well organized. The only thing is that quizzes are based on the paper or pages of the textbook he uploads. The 5 reading response papers are simple. No harsh grading on anything. He is a very optimistic and engaging professor.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Reading materials are hard to understand and super vague about concepts, but this professor alone saves the entire course. BB is well organized, post detailed summaries after each class, accessible whether during office hours or not. Easy A if you simply want to fulfill your graduation requirements, just do what he asks you're fine.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: 4 Reading response paper, no midterm, final was a reading response too. Participation credit can be solely done on discussion board (he leaves feedback which is good to keep in mind for reading response) every week to avoid online discussion. Quizzes every week on the reading, reading in my opinion was rather difficult and confusing at times.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He knows when students are disinterested in the class or are not getting the concepts. the more you participate and ask to explain the more lively he becomes. I highly suggest you take it. Not super heavy on work but you do have to read to pass. everything is provided you just need to show up and put some effort.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Good prof. Material is provided so no textbook. Lectures are BORING but is informative. Mainly about AI and other types of intelligence from robots. I was bored in class, but he is passionate about what he teaches and you can tell he is. We just need to give him a better resource. No midterm, Final is either essay exam or formal paper-you choose

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Ross is a nice guy, accessible during/after class and is cool. Prints readings for class (no textbook). The lectures are okay, mostly from older version prints (1970's-1990's). Lots of talk about AI and Robotics, so not really a Cog Sci class in the sense most are expecting. But he is good! Can take Final or write a Term paper. No midterm! :D

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is not the best in my opinion. He is a tough grader, but does give feedback. Lectures are not interesting at all. There is no textbook, and he prints out the reading material. The material is all from the 1980's-thus is boring and outdated. I expected new material for this class. Random quizzes, so show up. Final is a formal paper or an exam.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Ross really knew what he was talking about and made the class really interesting. However, that being said, don't take this course if you have little to no interest in the scientific community, how they do research, etc because you'll be bored. He prints the reading for you and if you do it, the quizzes easy--you just summarize it.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Nouri is a nice person but his teaching style did not work for me. His examples were physics based and hard for me to follow. Avoid this professor at all costs! Aweful professor, should be fired
Terrible Professor avoid at all costs

I studied and got the homework down so well, but the exams would be completely different. He didn't give us solutions to exams until 2 days before the final. This class is insanely hard. When asking for help, he does not give it; he lectures you on life and how you should do better. Horrible professor, can be either nice or rude out of nowhere. Took a quiz I got a low grade on, asked him what I did wrong in a polite way, gave me an unnecessarily rude response back. Homework hardly helps with tests, and his teaching style is hard to learn and prep from. Avoid at all costs.

If you understand physics at a base level you will be perfectly fine. he is one of my favorite teachers, he wants you to really understand the topic. Do not take 3180 w/ Nouri under any circumstances. I sent multiple emails over the semester, and he responded to none of them. That he wrote.

The class is mainly done through online videos. Lectures were only there for him to briefly talk about the lab. Homework and quizzes were extremely easy. This was during the pandemic so be weary if it is done in-person.

I loved how he took time to work problems out on the board instead of just clicking though a powerpoint. He knows his stuff, and wants students to succeed. Helpful and encouraging in office hours. Tests are tough but as long as you keep up with the hw, you'll be fine. Nouri def gets more hate than he desires.

So much undeserved hate. Favorite professor. Wants you to succeed. Brutally honest, which makes people upset(other reviews), but he's right. People that don't do well are the ones that aren't used to or willing to do work and learn. He spoon feeds you the lab at the start of class. If you pay attention it's easy to understand. Absolutely recommend.
He wants you to learn the material and will make you work for your grade. He seems chill and very interested in this subject. Exams are heavy and homework can be too.

Professor Nouri did his best with this class but unfortunately it was not enough. He himself is a nice person, but his ability to teach this math course is lackluster at best. He was one of the worst teachers I have ever taken. No HW bc WileyPlus had issues Quiz on some Mon Comprehensive Final: too many ? & not enough time Lectures w PPTs & post recordings on YT but I didn't really attend Does not respond to emails

Professor is unresponsive, won't respond to emails at all. He couldn't figure out how to access the homework, so he cut it all together. He couldn't figure out Wiley Plus so we never had HW. We got a total of 7 Quizzes. 2 Midterms + the Final. The median score on the final was a 39/100. I got the highest grade at 76/100. During lecture he basically just reads off his slides with some explanations for example problems or certain concepts. Quizzes and Homework every week that are never too long or difficult. Must pay attention to his lectures to understand the methods he wants you to use, but overall nice and is open to answering questions in class/office hours.

Hard to give a good feeling for professors who haven't done online classes before. Beginning of the class was copy pasted lectures from the book and not much explanation. As it went on the lectures got a little better but it is clear online teaching is not where he shines. I feel he is a lot better in person.

Nouri's class was a total disaster. He was very rude and people have left his office in tears. Exam one was an absolute disaster, class average of about 60%. Just try to take the other professor if you can he reads of the slides word for word, gives quizzes without notice almost every class. Very hard to reach out too most likely won't respond to your email. Seems nice but is not a good professor.

He speeds through lectures he never stops to let students interact except for "does anyone have a question?" after he just rushed through 3 concepts. His voice is monotonous, if you want to feel engaged and learn don't take this guy. He is not a good teacher

Nice guy who seems to know his stuff, but not too accessible or straight-forward; he gets jumbled up often as if he has never taught or talked to students before and has gone-back on his word a few times. Tests are not too similar to the homework, they follow the lecture concepts which are not elaborated on greatly in an understandable fashion.

Seems nice and lectures without tangents, but he is hard to contact and goes back on his word. He said on the exam 1 that you could redo wrong answers for some credit back.
