Physics E&M is a hard class, but Dr. Waung made it enjoyable. Provides his own set of notes, his explanations are clear, and lectures are easy to follow. Provides study guide & solutions prior to exam, and the exams are similar to in-class examples and the study guide. Homework is reasonable. Super friendly and funny. Definitely take his class!

Wonderful professor, very helpful office hours and curves the exams greatly. Homework assigned once a week, due the next week and the problems are from the textbook. Course was difficult but the professor did what he could to help us (had extra office hours before finals). Highly recommend you take his class if you can.

Definitely the best physics professor at CPP. He has great lectures and is very funny, and he is an extremely fair grader. He has one of the most generous curves that I have ever seen in any class. Very kind and caring professor

Hands down best Professor i've had for Physics. Has crazy good curves on exams. There were 4 tests total including final, even curved on the final. Final was pretty difficult but thats a given since its Physics. Definitely recommend to take and professor is such a sweetheart so he's very approachable.

I absolutely loved this class, it was my first time taking physics and trying to grasp the material was tough. He is incredibly patient and wants you to succeed. He curves and that helps your grade but do the hw and its similar to exams! Go to class to, he provides the notes physically and online. Has demonstrations and videos for some concepts too

Professor Waung is very caring and understanding. He cares for his students and is pretty funny as a professor. There is a quiz almost every week however he curves them. There are only 2 lab reports and he cares a lot about neatness and spelling. Overall, this professor's review relates to his course, and I would 100% take him again!

Professor Waung is great, he cracks some pretty funny corny jokes sometimes, and is a sweet guy. The class is simple there are about 10 Homework assignments for a total of 10% and 3 midterms each with a weight of 20%, lastly the final is 30%. The curves are also crazy good, he curves so that a C is whatever the average was for an exam.
funny and great professor.

He tries to make the class engaging, and I enjoyed all of his puns. It's a lot of fun and he's clearly passionate. Tests give partial credit and the homework is both useful and has corrections posted. Study guides are great.

He always had his lectures structured by every minute and he always knew what he was talking about. He would give us heads up every once in a while whenever midterm season would roll around again. Homework is necessary in order to have a chance to pass this class, only 1 hw due at the end of the week.

A very nice teacher and gives generous amounts of partial credit. The homework and study guides are ok. For midterms he allows one note card and four note card for the final. The best thing about his class is the amount of Dad jokes. The only thing I didn't like was that the lectures are a bit tedious. Class taken Spring 2024

Professor Waung is an excellent lecturer that genuinely enjoys teaching students. There was a total of 10 homework assignments, 3 midterms, and one final. Difficult exams, but he curves them fairly generously. Also gives a little extra credit. Take him if you want to learn physics and are willing to put it in the work to get an A.

I hated this class so much, but Professor Waung made it bearable with his clear lectures, organized class, and the insane curve for the exams and final course grades. Might be your best option for this class, would definitely recommend.

Excellent Lecturer. Most of grade depends on exams. Exams are fair. Not an easy A, only about 10-20% of the class gets an A. It's very doable, and %80 of the class seem to pass. Fair, fun, and challenging course. One of 5 of my favorite lecturers at CPP

This is one of the best lecturers I have ever taken. He is very clear and methodical in all of his steps, and would respond to any question until the student understood. It was a very nice time learning with him, as you can see his knowledge and passion. The exams were difficult, but were heavily curved. If you are not afraid of difficulty, I rec.!

He is great. He is very understanding and always accessible if you have any questions. You have 6 quizzes and 2 labs which are all curved. Labs are fun if you have a good partner and know how to use excel. Take notes while he lectures the theory because thats what your quiz will be based on. Also, make sure you know your calculations for your labs.

The tests in the course are heavily curved, which is clutch. There is homework given weekly. He gives out reading assignments. Available during office hours. Does expect a little knowledge of a topic before going into the lecture because reading assignments are given before a lecture. Really good professor though.

He's a great professor, explains the labs thoroughly, will help and advise if your having trouble. There's like 3-4 quizzes (a week after the lab). There are 2 reports, and gives the opportunity to have extra points on the reports. He's awesome, take him.
Very nice and caring professor. His office hours can be very helpful and he wants students to succeed.

Professor Waung is a great prof. He teaches at UCLA and CPP. He has great lectures and gives lecture notes. The content is hard, but he lets you have a notecard for each test and 4 for the final. Weekly homework from textbook. 4 "midterms" (tests) and 1 cumulative final. He makes a lot of puns/dad jokes, but he lectures well and answers questions.

Class is fairly easy. Most of your grade is based on lab quizzes. They are curved, easy and open notes. Make sure you take notes during his lecture since they will help you on the quiz. The rest of the grade is based on the lab reports. He's pretty picky when grading the lab reports so make sure you ask questions if you aren't sure.

Very clear on expectations for the class. Provides helpful guidelines for labs and an important lecture before every lab that covers most of the topics that will be quizzed on. Very helpful during the labs themselves, and is very passionate about this topic.

Ray is an extremely likeable guy for as much of a whooping the class gave me. I'm very bad at physics but if you took it in HS unlike me and are good at it for SURE take this class. He breezes through topics and teaches kinda assuming you have a basic grasp of the concepts coming in. His tests were hard but curved pretty generously.

Great class to take. The class consists of 3 exams and 1 final. Study guides provided and curves are extremely generous. Notes are also provided but I recommend going to class for best results. 1 short assignment every week for 10% of the overall grade. honestly probably your best bet for physics 1510.

Waung is a good choice although his teaching didn't click for me. His lectures provide the formulas but he doesn't explain why (which is crucial for physics). Not to mention the surface-level coverage of each section. His exams are hard because of this very reason. His curves/partial credit are nice but don't justify self-teaching.

Professor Waung understands how difficult Physics in general is to learn, so he does his best to make it possible and entertaining at the same time to do so... and he nails it! Midterms and final exams are definitely reminiscent of his lectures. Although there are few homework problems being assigned weekly, they are extremely helpful for prepping

"GOAT". If that online class I think easy A+++++. But in person you have to study to earn good grades on EXAM (3 midterms) 1 FINAL. They all HARD! But he curved a lot!!!. His practice problems for midterms and final not really help, I never do it but still good.REMEMBER GO OVER ALL THE HOMEWORKS, MIDTERM AND FINAL TOOK EXAMPLES FROM IT

Take good notes during his lectures at the beginning of class and maybe watch an organic chem. tutor vid on the subject and you'll be good for the quizzes, he wants you to understand so don't be afraid to ask for help if you need it. 2 lab reports and he can look over them in office hours. Great professor all around, probably the best for 1520L.
Most of your grade is going to be dependent on the exams which are tough b/c of the subject. He does curve the exams. He is very caring, nice, and cracks jokes/puns during lectures.

While he doesn't teach the concepts super well and his lectures are quite boring, he provides lecture notes that are clear and easy to refer back to. His grades rely on difficult midterms but don't be alarmed because he curves HARD and is pretty generous with partial credit. Waung is the GOAT.

Prof. Waung is a nice man who is willing to help you with anything you don't understand. This felt more like an asynchronous class with how the professor showed his own prerecorded videos for lecture. As others have said you're better off watching the lectures on your own. The class itself is curved to about a C+ average.

It says synchronous but it's actually async outside of exams. Calculus is barely used. Homework is time consuming.(3-4hrs/wk) Read textbook for concepts and watch lectures for examples. Exams are like lecture examples but more complex. Expect low grades but curve boosts you a lot. Concepts take a few times to understand, youtube helped a lot.

Very available and helpful through both office hours and email. 3 Midterms, but the questions were from the recent chapters. Homework about every week except for test week, and allows the use of a flashcard per midterm. Lectures were from prerecorded lecture, which is nice because he will explain extra in chat but the not great video quality. Puns

his lectures are very boring but extremely helpful. I failed the first two tests, and when I started watching the lectures and taking notes, I instantly got an A on the last midterm. Hes a sweet guy who only wants the best for you but the class and tests are difficult so you do have to study. I would take him if you can.

This class is more of an async than it is syn. The lecture videos are prerecorded on Blackboard and consist of him writing on the board or walking to the other side of the room and stare at the camera 45% of the time. He provides blank lecture notes and midterm/final review, which best reflects these exams. He would be a great in-person professor.
He curves the grades, but the tests are hard and I don't like his lecture vids. He teaches like a robot. He's super caring and nice tho

I would highly recommend Prof. Waung. He's so kind and wants everyone to do well. His class is organized and straight forward. He explains material very well and is always happy to explain topics you may not understand from your lecture.
very organized even though it was switched to remote learning. lectures are very clear and very understandable. exams can be a bit difficult. but he provides helpful study guides.

Hard exams but decent curves would definitely recommend self-studying on youtube. in zoom meetings he plays the same lecture videos he already posted, so you do not have to attend. Class is graded on 3 midterms (20%) 1 final (30%) and ten homework assignments (10%). Use the study guides he puts out before the exams!!

Prof. Waung is a great lab instructor. Class is graded based on 2 reports and some quizzes. Most of the weekly assignments are freebies just make sure you study for those quizzes. Lectures are prerecorded and not that clear quality or exciting but just listen and take notes. Overall, not tough but fair enough.

This class was graded on 2 formal lab reports & 6 quizzes. We still needed to turn in the other labs but just as calculations. His quizzes were a little tricky at times but still doable. He was a tough grader. He took points off for every little thing but theres extra credit opportunities for the reports. He wants you to pass. He loves physics!

Professor Waung is nice and understanding but his class is really hard. Exams are difficult but the curve is pretty good. During online learning, I do not like the structure of his class because you just watch a pre-recorded video. I would have learned a lot more if he actually lectured over Zoom and did examples with us.

Class is graded by 3 things, exams, 10 homeworks, and the final. He curves the exams which benefits more towards people who earned a low grade. I didn't like how he just replayed a pre-recorded lecture during the Zoom meetings which is why I stopped going. But his videos make sense. His grades exams & homework by the following week. Very organized.

Professor Waung is a nice prof. who cares about his students and wants everyone to do well. Exams can be challenging, however he does curve so you will get a grade boost. Make sure to pay attention in class, take good notes, and review the material and example problems. Make sure you also do the sample midterm problems that he posts.

Highly recommend! Physics has always been challenging for me, but he's extremely fair and understands the needs of his students. I really appreciated all of the help/availability that he gave to each of his students. One of the best science professors I've ever taken. 10 homework assignments, 3 "midterms", 1 final. Grades on a curve.

Taken in Fall 2019 for PHY1510 with him. Excellent choice of professor. PHY1510 content itself is not meant to be a very easy subject. Unlike other professors that make the hard subject harder than what it already is, Dr. Waung makes it simple for to understand. I hope he can teach the lecture part of PHY1520 in Fall 2020, then I'll take him again

(LAB)Highly organized. Very involved, makes sure everyone is on track. Only 3 lab reports which are easy. About 10 quizzes on prior week's lab which are also very easy. I've never heard a clearer lecturer, it made a great supplement to other classes' lectures. Keeps cough drops on hand for sick students. Quirky but charming, he grows on you fast.
Highly recommended. Unlike regular physics professors, he makes the subject as simple to understand as possible, which helped me learn a great chunk of physics.

Dr. Waung is the best and professor I taken for physics. I highly enjoy his physics jokes his office hours are very helpful. He gives a lot of partial credit even if the final answer might not be right. He curves a lot too, which is very generous and helpful. I learned a lot from his class taken in Fall 2019.

Professor Waung was a pretty good professor. He is very knowledgeable on the subject. Class is based on 10 HW assignments, 3 midterms, and 1 final. HW is pretty easy and manageable. He has fat curves on his exams. However the class is lecture heavy and he tends to go kinda fast.

Homework is from the textbook, there are 10 homework assignments. 3 Midterms and 1 Final. Midterms are similar to his sample tests, homework, and in-class examples. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, go to class and take notes because his lectures are great. Also does small physics demonstrations which is cool.

Dr. Waung makes this difficult subject as simple as is possible and really tries to set everyone up for success with multiple examples and his willingness to answer questions. His tests are very similar to his homework and lecture examples. Study these and youll do alright.
Good teacher with great curves.

Great prof, silly physics puns all the time, hands out ricolas to our class of 105 people, quirky, tests make up 90% of the grade but he curves hard because as he says, "At UCLA where I graduated, we curve hard." Can be boring at times, but covers material well, allows notecard on tests, he wanted the average of the class to be C. Overall fun class
Amazing professor- very organized

Raymund is a great, organized professor. Before each lecture he maps out the dates of the next exam and when homework is due. All homework is posted on blackboard & solutions are posted after. He also posts sample problems and solutions before each exam for practice. Exam answers are posted the night of, so you can compare & don't have to stress.

Waung is a solid choice for PHY132 . He made the class so much easier than other normal physics classes. He will teach you a subject, and then present sample problems and teach you how to solve them. Graded by 2 midterms, homework and final, but if you can do the homework and exam review then you should be able to get at least a B on the exams.

Waung is one of the best physics professors you can take. He gives clear lectures and is a very nice guy. He only tests on the material that appears on the homework and practice exams, so as long as you understand and practice those questions you will do well on the exams. He gives hints on each question and gives a lot of partial credit.

Dr. Waung is a really simple and nice professor. I had him for a lab and I learned so much in his small 10-20 minute lectures. He has about 2-3 quizzes and a few lab reports. Most were simple and straightforward. The only con (but we are in school so) is that you need to do the lab correctly because he checks at the end of every session.

He is a good choice. Physics is not easy especially for me but I was able to understand most of the course without an issue. He is a great professor at explaining and doing example and plenty of them. He doesn't use any powerpoint just on the whiteboard.

Had him for 133 lab. Learned more during his first 30 minutes of every lab than I do during other professor's lectures. He's a bit of an awkward fellow, but he grades fair and simple. The course had about 3 lab reports, 3 quizzes, and 2 "free" labs which aren't graded. Easy B for sure, achieving that A is totally within reach. LAB MANUAL NOT NEEDED

Fair grader. If you understand physics well from YouTube or from high school, you're set for the class. You can self-study and pass. The exams are pretty fair and she provides lots of examples and notes. The homework was kind of a lot, but it wasn't too crazy.

Amazing professor, incredibly helpful in the recitation class. She explains everything very well and thoroughly and is very kind. If you're taking physics for the first time, I HIGHLY recommend take a recitation class with her, it helped me greatly. One worksheet per week related to the topic in lecture, pass/no pass class.
Even for a recitation class, she's very helpful and she knows the physics. She thoroughly explains how the physics works and helps you through the problem. Overall, her course is extremely helpful.

I only took for for recitation but she actually made it enjoyable to attend class as its easy to skip. Every week there was a new packet based on a new chapter from lecture. Shes very patient and willing to walk you through everything if you're genuinely lost. She never made me feel stupid and overall a very sweet professor

Cheerful and very knowledgeable about the topic. Gives great examples in class that can be used for the homework and are usually referenced on the test as well. Is caring, kind, and eager to help anyone that has a question. Pacing in class is great. Tests can be difficult so make sure to study up and don't wait. Would 100% recommend.

I had to go to her office hours each week and take 1510A with her to pass. But I'm a first-timer with NO physics knowledge/background. You won't need to put in this much effort if you have experience. Quizzes weren't bad, exams and hw were brutal. Lectures were very organized, grades fairly, gives extra credit. She genuinely wants to see you pass.

I took Pan's recitation course (PHY 1520A). In this, she was extremely helpful and instrumental to my understanding of the material in the main course. She was able to explain every concept from the ground up, making her an exceptional professor.

Physics was never my strength before but Dr. Pan made me fall in love with this subject. She gave the best lectures with useful examples. Organized lectures, decent workload, quizzes, and homework were online, and 2 midterms and 1 final were taken in person. The final was not too difficult if you understood the material. She's also a fair grader.

Jun Pan is easily one of the best professor on campus. Lectures are nice and organized though you'll need to write fast because she erases her work. HW and quizzes are all online and don't take very long. There are a total of 3 exams, first 2 are very easy while final's a bit more challenging. Just pay attention to notes and you'll be fine.

There are weekly online quizzes and homework assignments and three exams. Attendance is not necessary, but her lectures are good and help for the exams. One thing is that she doesn't post her lecture notes and it is difficult to take notes unless you have a tablet to write on as she moves quickly.

Professor Pan was so nice and easy to talk to. Her tests were relatively easy with the fact that we were able to bring cheat sheets and use those during the test. All of the assignments and quizzes were online, only in person tests. Her lectures really helped if you went, if not stay home and do the homework, you'll still be fine.
Solid professor, easy to pass. A4 cheat sheet for all tests, easy tests + online HW = free C. Only went to class for tests and passed with minimal effort, take her even if it is an 8 AM

I got a C- because I didn't try at the end. But she was the best professor to take physics. I was never good at physics but she made it easy to understand and follow along. She had a recitation class that helped me in class and on test. I would recommend her 100%.

Attendance is not mandatory, but you need to be there to learn the material. Clear lectures and helps review the labs so you have all of the correct answers to study. Less than 10 hw assignments throughout the semester plus a few quizzes and tests. Interesting and not too difficult if you have good attendance and take good notes during the lecture.

Very nice and approachable. I had her for both lecture and recitation and she guided me through a lot of problems that I struggled with. Definitely better than the last time I took this course. I feel like thanks to her lectures, I will pass. Though the homework can be difficult since a lot of them are multi-step, but it definitely prepares you.

Professor Pan was a breath of fresh air. Her assignments were the same format every week (aka easy to keep track of) and she's an incredibly fair grader. The only thing I would say is make sure you pay attention and attend every lecture to take full advantage of her class and understand the homework. Highly recommend.

Personally, I don't know if it's just me, but I had a hard time staying awake in this class. I don't know if it's her voice, or her teaching style, but I could not stay awake. Not to mention, while the first exam was very easy, things started going downhill from the 2nd exam, and proceeded to get worse with the final. However, she is a fair grader.

Lectures are decent. Homework is difficult but not too long thankfully. First two exams are relatively easy, be wary though, the final exam is difficult, so make sure that you have a decent grade before taking the final exam.
Professor Jun is an okay professor, not very personable. Her lectures are long and she does have an accent, be she speaks very clearly and answer all students questions.

there should be more professors out there like dr pan. no more than 10 hw questions every week, short quiz which is mostly graded easily, good lectures with lots of example problems, 2 exams that are not that hard, but mostly conceptual. just take good notes and do everything on time, and get help when u need it.

Great teacher. You will do well if you attend lectures. Homework every week. Can be hard at times but a week is plenty of time. FRQs on tests are very simple, but the MC's are quite difficult. Pre and post test worth 1 percent extra credit for grade. Super easy weekly quizzes which you get 2 tries on. A is attainable but have to do well on midterms

Dr. Pan has a bit of an accent but it gets easier to understand over time. This was my first time ever taking a physics course and she was great because she explained everything clearly and worked out her examples well. Homework can be challenging but it prepares you well for the midterms and final. Overall a good learning experience.

I had this professor for lab and she is amazing. One of the best teachers Ive ever had. Yes she has an accent but shes easy to understand. When my physics lecture was torture, she was the peace for me in physics. She is a good teacher and wants you to succeed.

I really liked her class. Physics in general is a very difficult subject, but she explains it in a way that is really helpful and easy for the students. She gives really helpful feedback and responds very quickly. I even sent her some of my labs before I turned it in for her to check. Overall, you can really tell she cares about her students.

Had her for Spring 2021. Online hw, must purchase access code. Lectures are optional, but helpful. Dr. Pan is a very smart woman, and wants her students to succeed. Homework is similar to exam questions. She is a fast grader! her exams are straightforward. Physics can be a difficult subject in general, so just try your best and you will succeed!
She is an ok professor. Although her classes can get boring at times. You must pay to do her homework. She cares a lot for her students can get generally good responses during office hours.
When I took Jun Pan for PHY1510L in person Fall 2019, shes a solid choice. I dont know about how she is as a professor teaching online due to the pandemic.

quizzes given every Wed but theyre group ones! online homework can be looked up as well + written but just learn ok. lectures are easy to understand so go to class + has quiz solutions. Dont just look at powerpoints. Midterms ez. Final was hard!! Everyone failed n she didnt curve. Cheat sheets for tests allowed. Iclicker+$40 for online hw
She is a really great professor. She provides you with all the resources you need in order to pass. A passing grade is a 65% so it is manageable. I did the bare minimum that is why I received a C.

Lectures aren't anything to write home about, they are powerpoints that get right to the chase, they do the job well. You have to purchase the online homework, but there is a free textbook. Before every test, she gives a practice test so you'll be prepared. Plenty of practice with weekly quizzes and a fair amount of homework. Good choice overall.

She has an accent but it doesn't deter you from understanding the material. She is helpful with the labs and if you run into difficulties just ask. She provides handouts for all the labs, just follow her directions and you will be fine. She has 4 quizzes, one after every 3 labs, they are relativel straight forward, mostly summarizing the labs.

Shes soo good i would do recommend her if you put your work. Her class is not easy but she helps alot as when you ask her for anything she explains and most of the time you dont need to ask anything because she does her job right ! Grades are kind of hard to gain as her exams are graded based on percentages and not points. Highly recommended

When I have questions she will answer them fully. She will post slide shows on blackboard but I still recommend attending her lecture because she shows many examples that will appear later. Labs were clearly explained as well and I always finish a minimum of 1 hour ahead. Pay attention and you will get an A. Her homework is hard though.

Jun Pan is a very good choice of professor in the physics department, and does her best to make sure you really know the material by the end of the course. Her tests can be a bit challenging and vary in difficulty but are nevertheless doable and she grades more than fairly. I would recommend!
Shes honestly so simple as long as you keep up with her hw. Shes generous and the tests are just like the hw or sometimes even simpler. 10/10 recommend.
Honestly shes really hard to understand Bc of her accent, but also Bc she mumbles and talks really fast. She doesnt do a great job at explaining and she just starts doing problems out of nowhere

at first I wasnt sure how I felt about her class but then I realized it was structured in a simple way. each midterm has 8-10 concept/multiple choice questions ( sometimes with a few problems to work out) and 2 problems to solve. Before each test she tells what those two problem consist of, the examples she uses are directly from the textbook or HW

She goes VERY fast through her lecture slides and kind of yells at you when she lectures; really hard to follow. Tests are easy if you have taken physics before, but her class in general should not be for newbies in physics. She really cares about her students though, and will help you out a lot in office hours. Nice person, but would not recommend
great professor, helps inside and outside of the class. I used to hate physics a lot but she make me want to minor in physics!

She is very loud and clear, and she is always willing to help you understand the material if you're lost and explains it in a simple way so that you won't have to be a physics major to understand her. She grades her reports fairly, just DON'T FORGET UNITS! Whatever you don't understand from lecture, you'll definitely understand after lab with her

She actually reads reports and gives good criticism. It's not an easy A, but it's not too hard to pass her class. Very lecture heavy. At least 1-1.5 hours of lecture before even starting the lab. The labs aren't too hard, and she's there to help. VERY accessible out of class, and she's happy to share about her background.

Cool and fun professor, engaging lectures, and you must attend them. They are labs, so partner up and be there every day. Easy grader on labs tho took a while to grade. Easiest imo for all 1510L professors from what I heard, take her if possible, NOT Grainy. 1 presentation, 1 lab report, and 1 final with report, data, and final test. Great prof

Labs were interesting, and she explained them very clearly. Her enthusiasm made the class a lot more fun than I thought it would be. You will use a lot of google sheets for data gathering and analysis, so get ready for that. Overall good lab class, her grading is pretty reasonable and clear. You're guaranteed a pass if you go to all the labs also.

Explains the labs in ways that will make you (or at least me) intrigued. Very reasonable prof. Workload is light, lets students leave as soon as they finish their labs. Would definitely take again if offered for another course.

Phan is great. She is super nice and explains labs well. You have 2 weeks for all labs and even more, because you submit an editable sheets link so if you do the lab before she grades then you're fine, just make sure to submit the link on time. My only criticism is that she has graded one lab so far and we have done 8.

Professor Phan is easily one of the best lab teachers. Unlike other lab teachers she cares more about learning than having perfect results. You get two weeks to analyze lab data. Every student has to do a presentation of one of the labs. The midterm was pretty hard and the final is just doing a lab with a short test. (Class taken Spring 2024)

Super cool professor. She'll have you keep all lab data and post-lab (graphs, etc) in a notebook (she let me use a binder). There's 2 weeks to do post-lab (not reports). After one week of doing the lab, a group will do a presentation on the lab and you can fix your data as you wish. Her lectures are short but very detailed and intriguing.

Very good lectures before performing lab and has a clear grading criteria. Canvas page is organized too. No formal lab reports but you have to analyze your results from lab. Most weight is on your lab notebook, but watch out for the midterm and final. She really expects you to master the content, but it's not too hard to get an A on them.

No lab reports, only data sheets, calculations, midterm, and final lab. We get an extra week to make corrections if needed, except for the final lab. Only complaint is that she is a big yapper and can overexplain things but her lectures are great and she's super helpful if you are confused. Super chill and a solid lab professor choice.

Prof. Phan provided great lectures before the experiments which were super helpful in doing the experiments. During the labs, she is very approachable and is willing to give you tips on getting to your results. In addition, if you have further questions she knows how to help u bridge the lab and lecture material so that it is easier to understand.

She was a great lab instructor for my 1210L. The grading was pretty straightforward but a bit strict with having our weekly lab data and quizzes (you always had a week after to correct). She lectures a bit in the beginning of class so the labs are pretty straight forward. Even if you have questions she is very approachable and will try to help you.

Goated professor. 2-3 hours of solid work a week will get you a B. Minimal effort + easy labs, just follow the lab guide and her clear criteria. She lets you make up every lab "report" for full credit - no actual lab report; just a data and calculations section needs to be submitted + her in-class lecture notes.

i loved prof phan. my group spent lots of time just talking to her throughout lab and she was so sweet. very thorough with lectures. will give u the procedure step-by-step at first then kinda throws u into reading the lab manual after break (spring or thxgiving) but grades p easily and if u do everything ur guaranteed to pass per her scale

pretty straightforward lab. She has very clear grading criteria, but the work isn't too bad, so there is nothing to stress about. She doesn't make you do full lab report write-ups. She also has a fun end-of-semester project which is pretty straightforward.

She was okay; wasn't really a fan of the prelab lectures which were a bit hard for me to understand. Half of our labs weren't graded until the end of the semester but she ended up giving them all 10/10. She graded the first few labs a bit harshly. The final was absurdly difficult and tanked my and many others' grades. Allows 2 weeks to submit labs.

Professor Phan is a phenomenal prof. She explains each lab before we work on it, and is always available for questions. Lab works do take long, so do not wait last min. There is one presentation but it is not too bad. However, beware that the final is very difficult, so prepare adequately beforehand. In general, I definitely recommend her class!!!!
I took her over the fall, lets just say all of her labs are vague, and there's a final lab that she doesn't give you enough time for it, if you have no better options take her.

First and foremost, getting a good grade in this class is not a difficult task, especially if you have a cooperative lab partner. The professor will deconstruct the lab for you, explain it thoroughly, and is always open to answering questions in regard to the lab. However, be aware, as she will not do this for the final lab.

She allows submission up to a week after the due date to get a higher grade if you didn't get all the points. The reports are very straightforward and easy, so there is little if any homework. She is very good at giving feedback to help you learn what you didn't include or can work on. If she is available take her. She is the best lab professor.

Genuinely cares about your learning. Almost every assignment is done in the same preassigned group. Lectures are informative. A lot of different assignments/due dates but all easy work. The content is simple. She fell far behind on my grading and ended up giving me 100's on every ungraded assignment in the last week.

GET A GOOD GROUP. There are 12 labs and a 4 part final for a 1 unit class. Her class is so incredibly unorganized and hard to manage. Students would complain and try to figure out her lectures and she would basically give vague passive-aggressive answers and move on.

The most unorganized organized class I've ever seen. Her course on Canvas is a maze. A bunch of work for a 1 unit lab (and a final exam), and takes centuries to grade work. There are lab reports from the first two weeks of class that still haven't been graded over 3 months later.

Professor Phan is ready to lecture. Her lectures are great, easy to understand, and they're organized, she posts them for you to revisit too. I would recommend finding friends you know who are taking the class to group up with, or someone who is dependable. Do not underestimate this course! The workload can be overwhelming for some people.

Idk what others are saying, this class was VERY organized and clearly structured on Blackboard. Prof. Phan is truly the best lab instructor for 1510; she's amazing. Attendance is mandatory (per CPP's rule), and you need to attend synchronously or asynchronously, and fill out a Google forms with some basic questions. She also makes a class Discord.

The lab class is asynchronous, but you can attend live. Filling out a google form each week is your attendance for the class (can't miss more than 2 classes without being auto-failed). Follows the lab manual. MAKE A LIST of all the assignments that are due including attendance because it can get confusing since not everything is on the calendar.

Because it is a lab class online I can understand how things can get confusing. She's oddly organized but disorganized at the same time, there will be hidden things that will be due that you had no clue even existed. Luckily she allows late work all the way to the end of the semester which is nice. Overall not bad but takes a bit of getting used to

She's a really nice professor and her grading is really lenient. Everything is group work besides quizzes. She's really chill about everything. Only issue I have with her is her quizzes which are so hard for no reason. They're worded so weirdly and it's the reason why I'm borderline. The class has mentioned numerous times her quizzes are bad.

Took her Fall 2020 during the pandemic. Everything is groupwork with the same team members. Her quizzes are pretty bad, it's the sole reason why I'm at a 92 instead of 100. But other than that, if you do the labs you're good to go! Every other week we have to film a 5 min video, and every week we have data to turn in/lab report.

Hands down the best lab professor I've ever had. I had her for the online semester and the class was just adapted so amazingly well and intuitively. She is super passionate about the subject and all the assignments are very clearly laid out. Do be careful though, her lab quizzes can be really come out of left field, but that's the only downside.

Professor Linh was very passionate about the subject. I feel like she would have been a great professor on campus, but online she is kind of hard to understand. Her class consist of collecting data, working with group on data analysis, and then compiling it all into a report. Then she quizzes you on the weeks material. I was lost most of the time.

This class was very fun and I learned more from it than I did in the lecture. She is a super awesome professor who will help you with anything! She grades super easy and is really good at explaining things. 10/10 would recommend.

I honestly learned more from her one class a week than my three class a week physics class. She tries to make sure everyone understands by going from group to group and explaining what she's trying to teach and what we may have done wrong. The lab assignments were easy to do once she explained them and she mainly graded your lab notes. Chill class
tells you what to do and then you do it. i enjoyed her class and didn't have to think too hard about it

She is a great professor. I learned way way way way more in her lab than in the lecture. She would give feedback to every single person on each of the labs. She wanted us to understand the concept and be able to explain it. I would highly recommend Professor Phan to anyone. She was great to talk to and really caring.

She is SUPER cool. You really cannot fail this class. I stressed so much over lecture but NEVER for this class. As long as you do the experiments and fill out the data tables, you'll pass the class with a B. No papers. She's a very lenient grader. I am taking her again for next level physics lab, happily!
Easy. Just record everything in your lab notebook. No lab reports required except for 1. A small presentation is required but it's just you saying presenting your results.

Very fun and interesting class, she has a short lecture before each lab to show you what you need to know to do the labs. Each lab was pretty easy, and you can normally get out early. There is only one formal lab report and that's your "midterm". Overall it is a fun and easy class. Just study for the final lab, she tells you which lab it is.

She is very nice and sincere. She doesn't require a lab report for every lab except for the last lab of the course, it was the main weight for your grade. Overall, she is good at explaining the prelab and during the lab. Don't hesitate to ask her questions.
She is a great lab professor and is helpful. She explains each lab and expectations very clearly.

Good professor. Lectures are thorough and concise. Although, there are instances where there is some confusion during lab as to proper procedure. She grades based on data taken in a student's notebook. The grade consists of the notebook, "optional" quizzes, and 1 formal lab. Easy to get along with and I highly recommend this prof.

Final exam was 30% of our grade and significantly more difficult than anything in the lab or lecture usually. To make up for it, all labs are super easy and you get points based on participation and turning in a write up. Basically impossible to fail, very hard to get an A.
Give this guy a full time job

He is a chill and intelligent lab instructor! He does not seem to look at the lab reports, but make sure to follow his instructions he asks for and you will get a good score.The finals is the most difficult part of this class.

I don't think he even looked at the lab reports: if you submit something then you get full credit. But, even if you get full credit the entire semester, the final exam will bomb your grade because it's completely unfair. It doesn't reflect what we learned in class AT ALL. No preparation for the final whatsoever.

He was chill but the final is genuinely unfair. It's obvious the only reason we have a final is so he gets a nice distribution of grades because he can't let everyone end with an A. The "study guide" for the final he gives you does not help. It is very frustrating and honestly if you can take someone else you should.
While the labs were all easy, the final was an insane spike in difficulty, to where the labs will not prepare you for it whatsoever
Unnecessary difficult. Too rigid.

Roy is a great prof. He wants to get out of class asap, so he will help you to make sure you do the lab right. His labs were easy, got full credit on all of them. However, that final is no joke. Luckily it was online, but I spent all day on it just to not even finish it. You can pass the class without the final, but if you want an A, good luck.

He is a very easy grader when it comes to his lab reports. His lectures are very simple but he won't explain anything he doesn't need to so make sure you ask questions if you're confused. Make sure you study for the final, probably the only hard part of the class.
Very easy grader for the labs. The only thing to watch out for is the final, because it will dictate your grade in the class.

Professor Roy is very clear on what he wants for his lab reports. During online lectures, he would make the lab assignment at hand very understandable and clear breaking down the equations and theorems as a class. His labs are not difficult; however, his final is the hard part. Do each lab and you're basically guaranteed to pass. 10/10 recommend.

While Aaron Roy is chill in terms of grading lab reports. He does not read em, he literally just gives you full credit just by doing it. He does give a lab exam at the end of the semester. The lab exam is really hard! It consist of 10 questions that are all calculations which are problems basically. The problems were much harder than lecture. Study

Aaron Roy was possibly one of the best professors I've taken at Cal Poly Pomona, he is fun, helpful, and easy to get to know. It's very easy to create a good student-professor relationship, making it easier to get help when needed. He's also very relatable. Your grade depends on your lab reports and the final, which is difficult but not impossible
Easy grader on labs! nice and helpful! beware of his lab final very difficult. Make sure to study for his test well in advance!
Doesn't have HW. But easy doesn't mean good. Expect to learn most of the stuff on your own.
5/5, amazing lecturer, very didactic. Tests are difficult but he will keep you engaged and learning during the lectures. Highly recommend if you actually want to learn.

He is an amazing professor! He cares about his students doing well. He gives study guides that are almost identical to the exam and final. You must attend his lectures because he doesn't post anything on blackboard. He goes through the study guide with class. Very nice professor outside of class and extremely approachable!

Professor Modak is new, and tries his best to teach PHY 1520, which is not a terribly easy class to teach. As such, quizzes and tests are adjusted based on class performance, giving ample opportunity to both learn and get a good grade. His office hours are very helpful if you are confused on a topic or problem.

This guy is literally the goat. He made the class super easy to learn and he went straight to the point for each topic. Quizzes and exams are literally just like in-class examples with a couple numbers switched. If you want an easy A in 1520(which is rare because all the other teachers teach horribly), take Modak. Highly recommend.
Super nice guy! Maybe a little too nice. Easy pass but won't learn much

Professor Modak was an amazing professor overall! I enjoyed his class and found it pretty easy. Since it was this professor's first year teaching this course, he was a bit messy; however, towards the end, he got it together. He really was passionate about teaching physics, and I believe he did his best to teach everyone this course material.

I think he's new to teaching, so it seemed like he was figuring out what level of question was appropriate. Exams are 65% of ur grade, everything else is hw/videos. Exams are short, but 1 incorrect frq is 20% of ur exam grade. Exams r curved and u get to bring ur own formula sheet. Gives partial credit. Drops lowest 2 quiz out of 7.

For the ones curious about physics, Dr. Mo has been an amazing professor who really knows his stuff. If you have a strong PHY 1510 foundation, his lectures will be surprisingly intuitive as he relates many E&M concepts to Newtonian physics. He'll also happily sit with you during office hours to answer all of your questions.

Dr. Modak is a very passionate professor. His lectures can be a little unorganized at times, but he is one of the few professors who put in effort to make sure all his students succeed. His exams are pretty easy and he gives a lot of time to work on the homework.

It was his first year teaching, but he did so well. He does have a slight accent, but you can understand him. He cares about his students' grades and will help you no matter what. He gives you problems related to his quizzes and midterms. He goes through his PowerPoints and does board work. I recommend taking this class with him.

He truly cares about his students and is possibly the friendliest professor I've met. His lectures are engaging and conceptually thorough. Constantly available, being quick to answer emails and open to scheduling sessions outside of his office hours. Tests and quizzes closely reflect homework. Timely grader. Passionate and endearing.
his first year teaching in the u.s... he changes his mind on criteria faster than i can blink... lectures and assignments are an absolute mess... i'm cooked... im so cooked...

Professor was chill and would explain things in a very digestible manner, even when lecture and lab weren't in sync. He was understanding and was always willing to help if we had questions in our lab setups. He wasn't the quickest grader, but he graded fairly

I enjoyed this professor's class. He was very caring and willing to help his students. He is easily approachable and not too harsh of a grader. If you show up to class and make sure your lab reports have everything he asks for, then it'll be an easy A.

Professor Jasso is a very thorough and considerate teacher; he clearly explains each lab before starting, and is very helpful when answering questions. He also outlines each item that needs to be present on lab reports, so there's little confusion with what to include. Just make sure to come having read the manual, because the later labs get tough.
He's great, labs are easy when you do them correctly so e
Very easy class as long as you complete the labs properly. He gives clear instructions on what he wants and is helpful if stuck.

He would go in depth into the lab material before class which helped a lot with the lab and lab report. He also would walk around and give great help too anyone that asked. The lab reports were a little tough to get all the credit but there was no tests.
Professor Jasso is a stand up guy, as some may say. He makes learning fun. Its difficult to say that about a lot of teachers. Enough said.

I had him for Lab. KING. ICON. BEST PROFESSOR OUT THERE. So caring will help you out with everything. no quizzes or final. He helped my group out with every lab and answered our questions. best lab class and professor ive ever taken. I actually understand physics now wooooo

Prof. Jasso is not a bad professor if you want to do well. This class is not that difficult, however if you want to actually learn the material I wouldn't consider him a good choice. Other than that its fine.

Took him for the lab in fall 2020, during covid. Course was run asynchronously; he gave us videos of people doing the labs, it was our job to record data and do the analysis. He would give us docs on how to do the analysis. Overall class was pretty organized. Never went to office hours but he seemed pretty helpful the one synchronous class we had.

Video lectures didnt reflect HW and tests. Quizzes & exams are MC based off HW, still hard tho. As someone who finds physics DIFFICULT Im able to pass but didnt understand all of it. Helps us by curving grades & does his best to have us succeed. He knows his stuff but I didnt like his teaching style, Im sure it wouldve been easier in-person.

He's a super charismatic guy, very nice to talk to, but his online teaching method is not working at all for me. It's all prerecorded lectures that are SUPER fast paced with vey few examples of how to apply things. Equations are tossed around, but you never know what to use until you google it yourself. Good in person I'm sure.

Took professor jasso during virtual semester. lab procedure were on youtube and he uploaded his own pre-lectures to give more context behind the labs, questions to do, formulas, etc. which helped a lot. not the toughest grader but make sure you and your partner double check data and questions. no zoom after 1st week, became his office hours

A cool guy, that treats you like a friend more than a student. Very approachable - do not be afraid to negotiate back your points! Make sure you follow his exact lab write up format, as he docs points heavily for bad format. Also make sure you find a good lab partner.

Very cool and approachable. He really was very helpful and answered all and any questions especially if you stayed after class. Cared that the students understood the material and graded fairly. Do the homework, look over the examples he gives in class and study what he says will be on the tests.

He's all theory. A bit inexperienced so he made mistakes on the board fairly frequently - but they didn't often interrupt the lecture or confuse us. I loved that he almost NEVER used numbers. He really taught us how to use relationships to solve problems. I took him in the summer and though I DID put in work - I ended up with over 100%
I had him for two classes and was able to pass both. I'm freaking out that he isn't teaching 123. Take him if you have the chance.

Pay attention to his lectures, write the stuff he puts on the board down. They're super useful when doing the labs. He's pretty silly too, but you gotta pay attention to his sense of humor. You might think he's serious when he cracks a joke.

An engaging lecturer who knows what he's doing, but he certainly isn't the professor for everyone. The exams are very difficult and have the opposite procedures of the optional homework, so you have to study it extra hard. The smallest mistakes will get points docked, and you won't know your grade until the end of the semester. DO THE HOMEWORK

This was one of my favorite classes. Every lecture was very interesting and interactive. Quizzes were fair, if you didn't review the recommended chapter you wouldn't be very prepared for it and vice versa. Exams were fair as well imo. I didn't have to take lab though so I had a different experience than most.

Amazing lectures I genuinely like his dad humor, however this class is deceiving, the content is still hard. Quiz on most Mondays if you spend 10min skimming through the first 4 chapters you'll be fine. Homework is the study guide for the midterms and final, sometimes it's the exact same question. Final is not cumulative.

His grading made 0 sense throughout the semester. He was a funny professor, but approaching him always felt scary. He graded labs super tough and it was impossible to raise your grade. would not take again

He is so chill and during lectures he just did examples. Gives a quiz per chapter but its based off the book so just read and u should be fine. Easy exams and final they were just based off the examples he did in class. And if u took ap physics before u will still pass this class without doing any hw I promise. He made this class rlly easy to pass

Interesting lectures and homework is not required but recommended to do. He gives weekly quizzes and two midterms. Overall not too hard but you need to check your grade in his office hours since he doesn't put it on canvas. Gives moderate curves.

No exams, just a couple of random quizzes that are NOT mentioned in the syllabus. He refuses to use Canvas to input grades so you won't know your grade til the end of the semester. Super tough grader, will purposely look for something to mark off on your lab report. An O.K. class to take if you know what you're doing.

Professor Vandervoorts style of lecture was a breath of fresh air and I made it a point to attend every class. Homework is not graded but its great study material for exams. Friday activity and exams are only thing on the grade. Exams were very fair. Would typically only be 3 questions, randomly from each chapter in the unit. So study up!

He was the only professor of this class during the Summer, and this class would be probably the hardest class I have taken and even though I did learn a lot, he was an EXTREMELY hard grader and docks off points for smallest things. The average grade of this class is C+ and I worked with a tutor and passed with B. Only recommended for physics major

This class was a very hard class when its supposed to be an easy fun class. The teacher does give you good notes to write down but the formal, semi formal, and the exams are very hard. His grading is very harsh because he wants everything very specific, and if there is one small mistake, you will be marked off many points. Do no take his class.

Definitely what I would consider a tough grader. However, following his teachings and ensuring you go over the homework, lecture problems, and anything noted in the syllabus assures a great grade in this class.

Very good lecturer, his tests are exactly like his homework/ activity problems. You wouldn't have to touch the book if you go to his lectures which are very easy to follow. He is also not that serious during class and cracks jokes from time to time.

Honestly, one of the best professors in the physics department. He talks very loudly and sternly kind of like a dad giving a scolding at home, but if you look past that, he doesn't play mind games about what's going to be on the exams. The exams are the exact same if not extremely similar to what's taught in lecture or given as homework or activity

Everyone obviously has different experiences but for me, prof vandervoort was awesome. I found his lectures entertaining. Allowed a flash card for exams. He is very lenient with grading. He WANTS you to pass. He will give u as many points as he could. This class can be hard, yes, but thats when the effort comes in. Dont fall behind on reading.

Think Walter White, but if he taught physics, and you get Kurt Vandervoort. Honestly rated lower than he deserves. Entertaining lectures, weekly quizes. The exams are tough, but could totally be worse. Gives some free questions where u basically just plug things in. Tests are based from the OPTIONAL HOMEWORK, except a whole lot easier.

Do yourself a favor, avoid. Lectures were mathematically condensed, but even though being hybrid, he's so old school and hated uploading lectures regularly. So if you missed something, you were screwed. Exams were based off hw and he only gives out solution during office hours or sometimes in class. Class was also very exam-heavy (50%+ of grade).
Such a difficult grader. He would mark points off on the labs for the smallest things. It's almost like he tries to look for something to mark you off for. Don't take him.

Teaches well but you'll have to hit the books in order to pass. Grade relies solely on quizzes and tests, but he lets you have a 3x5 card with formulas on tests. Tells the occasional joke too and they're honestly not half bad.

This class is very hard. His lectures are very helpful, make sure to take good notes. His exams are VERY difficult and he gives you an index card for help. Be sure to study, study, study. His homework is just like the exam. The homework is very hard too, but Chegg is always there to help you understand. (Fall 2019)

He straight up told the students in our class that we should do problems on the exam right the first time and that we have no excuse for making any small mistake. Has no respect for students, it's his way and ONLY his way. The WHOLE class complained about time constraints and other issues on exams and we were interrupted every single time we talked

Complete terrible especially over zoom! took him for the summer and grades so harshly. He expects us to know what to do with barely any background knowledge. I'm sure he is a nice person but he is a terrible professor.

Let me clarify what kind of student I am. I have 3.91 GPA. I have only gotten 2 B+s ever, and I am a junior going on to become a senior. He does not write what he wants in the syllabus. Docks you off for things he didn't teach you he wanted. Sends personalized angry emails, is rude, and is very poor at helping his students. AVOID. AVOID. AVOID.

Took professor Vandervoort over the summer and it was a waste of my summer. I had him for both lab and lecture. He seem to lecture better than his labs, more than his actual lectures. He very specific when it comes to grading. He doesn't use blackboard and gives optional homework. Would not recommend
very bad class try to avoid

Good Teacher. I dont know why people rate him so poorly. I am taking his summer class and he explains things very well in his lectures and his tests are not that bad. There is some challenge, but that is to be expected. Do the homework to study for the tests, go to class, and PAY ATTENTION in class and it should be an EASY B.

He is a good teacher but as a person he has some major flaws. Whenever you ask him something he usually answers really quick, without a lot of explanation and in a demeaning manner. Tries too hard to be funny during lecture and often makes me cringe instead of laugh. If you can learn outside of class, take him.

Grade is made up of lab reports worth 10 points each. He gives a quick 5-10 minute lecture before the lab starts. He is willing to help you out a bit if needed. He expects quite a bit from his lab reports, as you can't just put two things down for the conclusion and get full credit on it. Easy B+ to A if you show up and do a concise lab report.

He's very good at explaining things in the lecture. But you have to show up to understand what's going on, as his quizzes (10 Q, one after each chapter) are concept based and need 10-15 minutes to study for if that. His final is exactly like the mid-terms. 4 questions, one from each chapter. They are very similar to the optional homework problems.
Great professor. I rate him a perfect 5/7. Explains stuff clearly yet isn't boring. He's cool.

Difficulty between a 4 and 5. Exams questions were always harder than all the homework problems we had. Kept lectures entertaining. Some quizzes were piece of cake while others were mega difficult. Office hours I found not helpful, and had to seek outside help to pass. Overall passed. Still perplexes me, no calculators in a physics class......

Superb professor. His lectures are clear-cut, and he's great at explaining and breaking down difficult concepts. Mainly uses chalkboard but displays diagrams on screen. Homework and exams are based on notes and book. Gives you answers to homework and exams, afterwards. Available for help during office hours. To top it off, he's hilarious.

he was pretty interesting in class and had fun demonstrations. no homework just suggested problems that you should do for great practice for the midterms and final. he lets you have 3x5 cards for the midterms and the final. tests are easy if you do the suggested problems.

This professor is so overrated. Her quizzes were super hard, and she is a very tough grader. If this is your physics class don't take her.

Lab groups of 2 and once a group of 4. Gives lab report templates so they are easy. Four open note quizzes that are easy, just copy the prelabs. for the labs, she gives a lab handout so you can just fill it out as you go throughout the lab. didn't really do a great job explaining every lab and how to do it, but she is open to answering questions and very helpful during office hours. would recommend

Class was generally easy. Most difficult part were her quizzes. An easy trick is to just write down all of the answers for her practice quizzes because she slightly reuses the questions. She grades on the smallest things in the beginning but then gets easier as the semester goes. She's a good teacher and I would recommend her.

she assigns way too many assignments for a 1 unit lab class. She lectures for so long before the actual lab and makes a simple lab procedure seem so complicated by not explaining it well. She's nice and willing to help, but get ready for a lot of homework for this class.

Lectured for very long in the beginning of class but did not explain experiments. Class was alright, the lab reports were like worksheets and pretty straightforward but its usually a lot longer than if you did it by the book. There were quizzes for some reason but they were alright too. Overall it was pretty manageable, just make sure you have a really good lab partner otherwise its doomed.

Her worksheet-like lab reports were straightforward. I was usually able to turn them in early on the same day the experiment was conducted! Pre-labs were online, fast, open-notes, and 3 attempts. There were 4 in-person quizzes (open-notes). Pre-labs and Quizzes were

Such a caring professor! Physics is a difficult subject for me, but Prof. Nazareths teaching made her lab a bright spot in my week, even when everyones bleary-eyed at 8:00 AM! Taking a lab fully online is difficult and I know that. Professor Nazareth is very nice and knowledgeable about physics. She's knowledgeable and experienced - two things that I feel are extremely important, especially in a lab class. Very willing to help students. Show up, work hard, and be respectful you'll do great. Overall, a very good choice!
Professor Nazareth is such a caring professor. She will literally do anything possible so you can learn the material.

Professor Nazareth is a pretty good professor. The lab itself wasnt that hard if you read and followed the steps. She has her own lab sheets and theyre pretty self explanatory. idk what these people are saying, Julie does not make you excited for Physics. Her class is mandatory attendance too. if you miss a lab you're kinda screwed. You will learn a lot and have a great time. She makes you excited to wake up early for her 8 am class, and she loves her students! Prelabs save time during the lab and help you feel prepared. Her website is extremely helpful and is found at cppedujjnazarethphy132Lhtml

She gives very clear and understandable mini-lectures on how to perform the lab at the beginning of class. If you're ever stuck or unsure during the lab, she is readily available to help. She is very particular about how she wants lab reports put together. Details, details, details. However, I HIGHLY recommend office hours for any clarification she is VERY helpful. If you're the kind who WILL have questions to ask on the homework, don't go to her - she isn't very helpful and is almost intimidating about it. She's really a very good teacher who really cares if you get it or not. She's also very clear on what is expected of you and even though physics is the worst subject I've ever taken, she made it tolerable!
This teacher is one of those that will make you feel unintelligent if you ask a question. She is not very flexible and does not curve anything.

NO PRE or POST LAB WORK, NO LAB REPORTS (everyone gets 100). Only partner work in labs. Very funny, but sometimes hard to understand during pre-lab lectures. Really nice guy but only grades 2 midterms and attendance which is done by physical iclickers. If you do bad on a single midterm its hard to come back.

Prof Rhee I my favorite teacher so far at CPP. I've taken him for 1510, 1510L and 1520L and he was great in all of them. His lectures are very informative but his homework can be challenging. However his tests are not bad

Stand up comedy with a side of physics. If u have physics experience, this class is a breeze,didn't rlly study. but if you have no physics experience, this class is hard, study outside of the lecture. Dr. Rhee is a fantastic professor. He's very passionate, a solid teacher, and knowledgeable. Tests are heavily curved but he makes EVERYTHING about the course clear. The difficulty of the course has to do with how difficult physics itself is.
makes the lab very very very easy. all partner work, and no lab reports.

LOTS of extra credit (even on HW, make sure you finish it) and huge test curves. Pacing is quite fast, 15 chapters in 1 semester. Basic concepts in class; HW is harder than content covered. best physics professor hands down!! Go to lectures if you want to pass this class because the exam are very difficult. The homework problems sometimes are harder than the exams. Exams are curved. Highly recommend this professor!!
He curves everything. His lectures move very fast but he is willing to help outside of class. He has stated numerous times that he will try to pass as many people as possible. Very good professor.

(Note: I took physics already). Professor Rhee doesn't lecture much before lab (good if you know the Physics already). Provides graphs/formulas we need on the board. overall solid professor. Great professor. He lectures a bit before you start the lab and will show you how to do it step by step. If you are confused or have any questions he will definitely help you. Professor Rhee is beautiful in his brevity, lecturing briefly at the start of each lab. The lab is mostly up to you, but he provides assistance to everyone, if they need it. Two quizzes but they're more like midterms, so make sure you study for them. Dr. Rhee is very professional, lenient, and accessible outside of class. Had a career as a researcher so he can likely answer most of your questions about industry.

He doesn't mind spending the whole lab walking you through it if you don't understand. At times he does make you feel dumb but doesn't do it intentionally, but he is funny so that makes up for it. He is a great professor, he warns everyone how much stuff needs to get covered by the end of the semester so he goes really fast but he does his best to work out examples in class and will even give answers to some future exams in his lectures. Taken online. It was a difficult class and I didn't learn anything. I find the subject interesting but I didn't like his lectures. I would've taken an easy GE to fulfill the requirement had another class been open.

Very straightforward lab professor with no reports or outside HW needed. Briefly goes over the lab at beginning, and then you collect data and check it off with them once the data is good for full credit. There are two tests to distribute the grades with the average set at a B.

bro has immaculate rizz, super funny and overall a really good lab professor. show up to lab every week and you will get a free 60%. just make sure to save the lab worksheets because they do help you prepare for the two midterms that your grade depends on

Extremely efficient at delivering information. Gets right to the point with all of his instructions and is willing to help during labs. To the point and very clear. show up, do the labs and pass the class. its simple. he does not allow for homework, you must finish the lab in class for credit. there are two exams with the soul purpose of dispersing grades. All curve based. STUDY for it though its harder than he says.

Rhee is a very relatable professor and cares that you know the material. He has a great charisma. Classes were interesting but sometimes hard to follow. Don't fall behind. If you don't understand something at the beginning you're going to have a hard time at the end. He didn't show up to his own office hours. Decent professor. Go to his office hours if you need help on labs and he basically gives u the answer.

Like he know how to get the material across but the execution isnt the best. Lectures can drag on at times, but there really was minimal hw each weeks lab. Not the best class, but youll definitely get through it without too much pain compared to some other profs Ive heard.

Professor Rhees lectures are hilarious and he is always available for students. Exams are based on lectures with some questions from the LT (textbook).

Prof Rhee is a good person and tries to be as fair as possible. However, the class can get pretty confusing at times and feels rushed. As he says, it gets harder as time goes on so try to not fall behind and stay above the curve.

Very nice guy, but sometimes unclear. Test questions are often confusing but he is very open to receiving questions and will sincerely try to explain the correct answer.

He is a really passionet guy about the subject and really funny. He helps when you need help and although yes his tests are hard, they are not impossible to pass. An extremely nice guy. he will help you outside the class and are very knowledgeable about the subject. the class is very easy and you will learn alot.I got an A in his class but will take this class again just because it is so fun. Tests and final are easy, i didnt even need to study.

Pros: Very nice guy, and seems very knowledgeable in Physics. Gives a very good lecture before lab, just follow the exact formats and provide exact information and you'll pass. He is very open to questions.

He is a good professor that explains the concepts of the lab in a good manner. He tells you what you need and how to get it for the max points. Not harder than what everyone thinks, follow his rubric, take notes on his little lectures he does and just do the report. His office hours are sometimes helpful but sometimes will confuse you even more, have a friend help you out during lab reports and you'll alright.

Idk why this professor gets such bad reviews. I loved him. Before each lab he lectures for a bit about the theory behind the lab and why you are doing the lab which made 1510 easier to understand. Prof. Smith grades lab reports very strictly with docking off points as small as not putting the lab in the correct order he wants it (data, analysis, conclusion). Not terrible, pretty much what I expected
