Teachers should be teaching their students, and he doesn't even do that.

He is ok for in person classes, however with the shift online he has done absolutely nothing to provide for the class. He just gave us lecture notes and problem sets and just told us to take the notes in little by little. Without a formal instructor I was left to learn by myself, and I didn't really learn at all. Chegg is your best friend for tests

Rainey was very passionate about his lectures. Although there were times when I was a bit lost during lecture, but he mostly answered my questions. He didn't give out an exact study guide, which made it somewhat difficult to pinpoint on what topics to study for. Be sure to do the homework, it can definitely cushion your grade.

If you can avoid taking this prof for lab, then do so. I followed his lab instructions exactly as he said and was failing all my lab reports. I would reach out to him after every report for clarification, and he would get very annoyed and would sass me. I was always very professional with him, but his feedback was not. Avoid him & your frustration.

Rainey gives you a chance to miss one lab and make it up. He's not very clear about what he wants in his "informal" lab reports so I lost a lot of points just trying to figure that out. They are informal, but his grading seems kind of random. You'll also skip unneeded parts of lab and get out early every day. Figure him out soon and you'll get an A

I wanted to like Dr. Rainey so bad,he is a cute old man but the class is very hard! The class is based 80 percent on exams and 20 percent on homework. Nothing is online, and the exams were always EXTREMELY HARD! I would study for hours and would still get a 60 on the exams. When you ask him for homework help he literally just reads off his copy.

His class is very much based around doing derivations of equations. Almost every example given in class was just showing how to derive from one equation to another. Wasn't very helpful in class, exams had nothing to do with lectures or homework, and he spoke very monotone. Would not take another one of his classes. Only needed textbook for homework
He grades his tests really hard,top scores for our session were in the 70's and 80's. Speaks clearly, answers questions, but a little boring.

You can't miss any lectures in his class. The midterm did not match anything in the book nor the homework. You can't reinforce the lecture by studying the book or doing the HW. He seemed nice, but the class was very large so there was much one on one interaction.

Great professor! Lectures are very easy to understand, but I might be biased as most of the course was review for me. Most of the homework is optional, so you only need to do what you need to so that you understand. Exams were pretty straightforward, and he tells you what they will look like beforehand.

One of the best physics professor. Only reason I got a B is because I didn't studied for the first midterm. The second midterm and final was very easy if you just spend a couple of hours each week studying. Weekly quizzes that aren't too bad. Very engaging lectures. Study guide make you over prepared for test. Trust me study for the first midterm.
Prof. Botana was a good guy. Recommend

I took this professor for 1510A or the physics recitation, and it really helped a lot, he dives deeper into the problem solving aspect of the class to make sure us students understand which steps to take when we are given specific problems. If you struggle understanding physics would highly recommend this class.

Professor Botana always tries to make class exciting and more interesting. I liked his style of having slides and clicker questions that weren't graded to help with understanding. Homework was not mandatory, so you can complete it as you see fit. Homework was a great help in studying for quizzes and exams. He just wants to see everyone succeed.

He is a very fair grader, he tries to get as many points from your work as possible, he can be disorganized with his lectures but his tests and quizzes are very fair. His activities are very useful as well, a lot of practice can be done in the class.

He's an understanding guy and wants his students to be successful. Build a relationship with him based on participation and attending office hours. He's a lot more understanding than others say, and definitely wants you to see the gift of physics. Take it seriously and he'll take your grade seriously.

Took him for a few upper div physics classes during the pandemic. His workload is very demanding but he cares that students do well and he cares when students take interest in class(es). He is also a super likable guy and patient when answering questions (in office hours or during lectures). I definitely recommend him.

Prof is very patient and understanding. Overall solid choice for lab (lectures might b another story). Show up to his office hours if you don't understand something. Sometimes doesn't reply to emails. He is strict to you following his format. And, do his extra credits.

Would not recommend if it is your first time in physics, felt like I barely learned anything from the lectures, I learned more watching Michel Biezen on YT for HW / Midterms. Lectures were pretty much straight off the PPT and did not do much for me. Not a terrible choice as he sometimes curves but would not take him again.

very nice professor. straightforward lectures - he talks, you learn. lectures were posted online to watch later, attendance not mandatory except for recitation - rec. attendance is 10% of the grade. one midterm + one final half your grade, so be ready to study when the tests come. homework is straightforward, one assignment a week. very good prof

Professor Alcalde makes physics 1510 a really hard class if you have never taken physics before. If you took AP Physics 1 or 2 at a relatively good High School and passed the AP test, this class is definitely an easy A. If you took regular physics expect a challenge. He also tends to overcomplicate the material a lot.

At the beginning it seemed like he didn't know what he was doing but he eventually got it together. My lab partner and I finished experiments in < 1 hr and finished the lab reports in 30 mins. His expectations for reports are low so getting a good grade on them is super easy. Follow the lab manual and the slides he posts and you're good to go.

If you didnt take (and understand) physics in hs or have never been exposed to it, I do not recommend this professor. His assignments on flipitphysics have due dates that creep up on you so keep up with it. He's pretty lenient and wants to compromise so just ask and he'll deliver. Uses clickers to account for participation. PPTs are wordy.

He is an amazing professor and makes physics bearable for non-physics majors. He sometimes gets sidetracked, but he's funny and wants to help you succeed. If you follow what's in the syllabus, writing lab reports is a piece of cake. He even will skip sections of the lab and he emphasize the important parts, so you only do useful lab work. TAKE HIM!

He was really good for 1520L. He will give you a B in the class as long as he sees you trying in the course. My only complaint was that he would lecture for the first hour of the lab when we could be using the time to do our lab, but he wanted to give us insight, so he had the right intention. Also, labs were only to be turned in on paper..idk why.

Professor Christensen is really caring and nice, lectured for a little bit just deriving eqautions for the lab, very easy grader, as long as you have graphs, data, and percent error you'll get 9-10/10 every time. Sometimes gives pop quizzes off Lab manual just to make sure you know what your doing. Wish I could take him again for 1220L.

Professor Christensen was a great choice for lab. He was always available for help throughout the experiments. He even omitted parts of labs since his lectures did take quite a bit of time to get through. However, he does get sidetracked sometimes. He is a lenient grader on reports. Make sure to read beforehand since there will be 3-5 pop quizzes!!

I highly recommend him, ignore the bad ratings. He does his best to explain the lab and what you need to do during the beginning lecture, and he is available the whole time to answer questions. He also tries his best to simplify labs to give students an easier time. Several times he makes parts of the lab not mandatory so you can leave early.

He was very unorganized and did not seem to help at all. Our whole class was getting very bad grades on the labs (my average was around 75%) and we were all surprised when we got good grades in the class. He did ensure that everyone in his class passed but he wasn't the best educator. Very nice man.
Easy grader, funny guy and gave me a B. Love you Walter. Incredible Titanic lecture.

COVID ONLINE REVIEW. If you want an A, take this Professor. As long as you complete the weekly labs (experiments are shown via YouTube videos), he will give you full points. Pros: easy grader IF labs are complete, no quizzes or finals; only weekly labs. Cons: he doesn't teach at all and you have to learn everything by yourself.

He only emailed us twice. 1.) Syllabus 2.) When someone asked if we had to do the Spring Break Lab. He was useless as a professor and I'm glad that I was able to ask classmates for help because he never held a single lecture. Perks: no mandatory lecture, no quizzes, no practical. Be prepared to teach yourself. Overall he was an easy grader on labs.

(COVID Edition) First things first, Professor Christensen's Lab was asynchronous for Spring 2020 despite saying it is synchronous. He did give us instruction on the syllabus as to how to do the Lab Reports, but his syllabus had the wrong time and wrong manual to purchase. If the syllabus wasn't so clear, I'd give him a 1/5.

Highly recommend him for those of you're not into physics or have a hard time understanding physics, take his lab for an easy A!! He's an engaging professor with a passion for helping students. Basically, if you do your lab reports and show up to every class you'll definitely pass and very likely to get an A!

First day of class the room was full. Last day of class less than half of the students came to lectures. If you are coming to get credit then go for it because he curves the grade and you get a C but if you actually want to learn physics I would suggest going to another prof. He's a chill dude, he just doesn't teach well unless you already know PHY

This class was an easy A because he tended not to grade any of our work. He didn't know the material and was not prepared at the beginning of class with knowledge about the labs we were doing. When asked a question he would half explain it, get side-tracked or cut himself off and never finish answering it.

DON'T TAKE if you want to learn physics. Lectures are SO unorganized, you will cry. I learned nothing in 16 wks, & I was at every class. Assigns homework, but won't return it until too late. Offers extra credit for quizzes & correcting exams. He curves exams so nobody fails. You're guaranteed a C, but anything higher you'll have to teach yourself.

350 characters are not enough to explain how horrible he is. How should I start this? Lectures are very unorganized and keeps on jumping off topics back and forth. If you have a question he won't answer your question. Exams have nothing to do with HW at all!. Oh, he has a grader that grades exams and HW and all of the grades are multiples of 5's

He's the guy you take for the easy "C", if you put in a little more work I you will get "B". He doesn't use mastering physics (well for my class he didnt) if you want to learn don't take him. He tells you exactly what the mid terms are going to have (2 total) so the only learning I did was the night before the midterms filling out my cheat sheet.

He is a very nice and caring professor. He will try the best to explain everything to you BUT no matter what you ask him your question won't probably get answered. His lectures are messy and hard to understand. He guarantees a C for curve. Lots of pity points. Only about 10% of the class got As.

His lectures are unorganized and very hard to follow. If you're going to take this class and you're aiming higher than a C, you'll be relying solely on the book. The tests are much harder than you'd expect them to be, so doing well requires effort. It is virtually impossible to fail the class, however, as the lowest grade he gives on tests is a C.

If physics isn't your forte and you just need to pass, definitely take him. A lot of pity points all around, hardly any homework, everything you need is already on his power points so attending class is hardly required. If you're a physics major, don't take him. His lectures are convoluted and unnecessary.

Pretty much what u read about unorganized and directionless lectures is accurate. Formulas are presented but not shown how to apply them. I learn nothing going to lecture and find myself lost and clutching my text book hoping to make it work. Great person and really fun but teaching style is crap.

He basically guarantees you a C in the class but the hw and the tests are completely unrelated to what he teaches in lecture. He's super unorganized and makes up examples in his head. He says "make sure you get all of this down" then erases the board right after, people just sigh and put their pencils down, whats the point of even going to class?

For the sake of your own sanity PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS MAN! He is seriously THE ABSOLUTE WORST! Okay so lecture is a complete mess, he doesn't define terms and doesn't explain when certain formulas should be used. He just puts examples that he makes up on the board and draws arrows everywhere. Then he says "get this down" and erases right after!!

If you're looking for an easy A you wont find it here. BUT, if you're not too into physics he's still an engaging professor with a passion for helping students. At least in my class the lecture was all exam based but he gave many pity points for the less science savvy students leaving most students in the C range. Think outside the box and study.
Awesome teacher! very helpful and he knows his stuff!

Honestly not the worst professor of the options, lots of lab reports, but he cuts some parts out. Will explain the lab and give example calculations sometime before and after the lab to help with the reports. Accessible through office hours and answers emails on canvas.

Credit where credit is due, it is actually difficult to fail his class due to is grading methods, and he does care for the students despite his demeanor in class. However he is a very tough grader. As long as you put a decent amount of effort, you will for sure pass. However if you want an A, prepare to put in some major time into the reports.

Run from this professor. He's the worstexpects you to know everything, offers zero help, and treats students like garbage. Labs are insanely harder than lectures, and he grades like he's trying to make you fail. It's a complete nightmare. He doesn't care about you or your success. Avoid him if you value your sanity and GPA. PLEASE DONT TAKE HIM!!!

Ozer is a nice guy who cares about his students. A bit rough on the edges, his teaching style is a little different, at the beginning with having students try the work then telling what they did wrong. It made him seem more intimidating as a professor. Be prepared to spend a significant amount of time to complete the work and correct things.

Warning: DON'T TAKE HIM. Ozer always gives vague answers when answering questions about labs. He will dock you down points for the slightest errors in your lab reports. The only way to communicate with him about general problems with labs is through Canvas discussion boards or office hours. Wouldn't recommend this class to anyone

Take literally any other lab instructor for this lab. Gives horrible feedback and the workload is insane considering its a 1 credit class that's supposed to be supplementary to the lecture. Talks to students like were dumb and should already know how to do everything. If no other instructors are available just wait until next semester to take it.

Please do not take this prof, especially if you are an architecture major. Physics is bad enough in general for me but there is so much work for just a 1 unit class. If you do have to take him, make sure to balance things well as you need to do multiple final lab reports for the semester and he has to review them before they are submitted.
is a demanding and tough grader but doesn't teach much and gives vague instructions/feedback/'answers to questions.
Please skip him. Not good at giving instructions and assigns things due on the same day and at 11 am. Sucks at giving feedback as well. I wished i had just taken someone else.

the entire course is group work which is fine, if you and your group are on top of it. 1 credit but the workload feels a lot more like 3 credits sometimes. grading criteria is incredibly hard to figure out. you have to see him to revise solo lab reports but you can only do this in person and has 1/wk limited office hours.

3 big group assignments due each week MINIMUM, if you don't work well with your assigned groupmates good luck. Grades harshly with no clear criteria POOR feedback, answers questions rudely and vaguely, very few office hours + hard to reach. If you aren't already comfortable with physics this class will be INCREDIBLY DIFFICULT.

His grading can be annoying at first but you will eventually pick it up after a few reports, which require a lot of work. He can be a little rude sometimes. This class relies heavily on team work, there were many reports where it was just me and one other partner finishing a report which was frustrating.

His feedback is usually not very helpful/enough to understand what is expected. Grades aren't terrible, but don't expect an A, especially considering your grade is highly dependent on the work of your groupmates. Expect to put in a lot of legwork, before and after, for the labs, as lab reports are expected to be semi-professional, so don't be lazy.

Grades semi-harshly on lab reports, but you'll get used to them after a few weeks. Office hours are available for more extensive feedback on lab reports. Quizzes are not difficult to do if you pay attention in the labs.

Take other professors if possible. Its not difficult to get an A if you understand the lab and what he wants, but his class is a hit or miss. There are 3 quizzes and 13 labs worth 5% of ur grade each. He SUCKS at giving feedback for lab reports, but even then he doesn't give terrible grades for work, usually. He expects you to know what he knows :(

Not a terrible professor, lab reports are a bit of a struggle because he does want a lab report that looks and is professional. Tests are dead simple if you pay attention and follow the examples. That's also why he's unforgiving with the test grading. Take this professor if you're out of options, it's more than possible to make it out with an A.

Please do not take professor Ozer, the professor is barely any help in the classroom. His comments of feedback are vague and he expects you to know physics as he does. He grades very very late and therefore it makes it impossible to get full points on each lab. Save yourself the money and stress and take another prof. Also there are pop quizzes.

WORST teacher at Cal Poly Pomona. I really wish the Dean of the Physics Department would actually look into this professor considering test averages and grade averages. I understand physics is supposed to be difficult however, when your teacher is cutting you off when you're practically exclaiming for help on labs, there should be something done.

Nice lab and easy to do. Just attend labs every week and do the reports on time and you'll be fine. He grades very slow, but holds office hours to provide feedback for your lab reports, so just attend one or two for feedback and you can get a feel on how he wants you to write the rest of his lab reports. He's also very lenient on grading as well.

Takes very long to grade work, feedback is poorly written, and doesn't give you a clear criteria of what he wants in your labs. Only good things are that he's not a very tough grader and lets you do quizzes in groups.

Overall, the professor tries his best to be accommodating and has altered the course a couple times to try and make it work better. His quizzes aren't terrible considering you can work in groups, but sometimes it they can be hard to understand. Lab reports are graded a bit harshly with no rubric or example report, so no room for improvement.

This professor is the worst physics lab professor I have ever taken. He does not have a clear grading criteria at all. He just tells us to follow the procedures on the lab manual and does not care to give up an example of what the labs should look like. He doesn't respond to his emails and is very hard to reach.

She's really nice! The free response portions of exams are really similar if not the exact same as problems done in class. This was our case even for the final. For the final the multiple choice portion felt more difficult than the others imo. She's also really strict when it comes to turning in homework on time.

Rosie really cares and wants her students to succeed. Attendance not mandatory, but in my opinion helped understand material better. She always stayed after class if you had questions and always tried to clarify without being condescending. The only tough part were the exams but the practice exams are very helpful. I would def take her for phy 1220

Her lecture slides and example problems/solutions are posted on Canvas. Quizzes are available online for ~48 hrs and done outside class, and are simple. Exams themselves are decent difficulty, but very similar to the practice exams she posts. HW is given through Expert TA weekly. She's generous w/ curves too; one of the easier physics classes.

had her for both lecture (PHY1210) and lab (PHY1210L). she really cares about her students and wants you to succeed! labs had 1 report a week (easy 10/10 if you follow her format, gives feedback to improve), lab quizzes were open note. lecture class allowed a formula sheet, class lecture on slides accessible on canvas. would recommend!

Not sure why she doesn't have better ratings, but she is one of the best professors I've had at CPP. She cares and wants you to succeed. She's always willing to answer questions and provide any further assistance you need. Only 2 exams and a final which you are allowed a 1 formula sheet (3 total for the final). You want to pass physics? TAKE HER!

Great professor! Physics is not an easy subject, so you do have to spend time practicing problems outside of class. The class average is 60% but honestly, tests weren't that difficult. You just have to study. She gives you points for writing down the given variables and drops the lowest test score. I found her lectures easy to understand.

Helps with lab if you need it. She gives her own data sheet which is easier than the lab manual. Lab summaries are super easy if you follow her format. Labs never take too long but they can be hard if you don't follow it. She never asks for too much, she wants you to have an easy lab experience and have fun learning physics.

She's a sweet professor and cares. Her notes have examples problems and people stop showing up for lecture. She goes over the example problems that are on her lecture notes which already provide the answer. Has practices exams which are similar to exam. 10 mcq and 2 frq. It can be hard. HW on expert TA. She has an accent so listen closely.

I do suck at physics, even though i took AP physics in hs, but this class was very hard. 70% of grade from 3 exams, some homework and quizzes which were easy. She cares a lot about her students, but definitely study more than you think you need because a lot of exam material is changed from the practice exam to test conceptual knowledge

Rosie was my favorite professor I have had for a min. I usually dont write reviews, but I think she really deserves one. She is incredibly nice, goes out of her way to answer questions with detailed explanations, and genuinely cares about her students. Do yourself a fav and take her class. The goat p much

Her labs were not as stressful as I expected. She demonstrates how to do the experiments, gives notes on the board to help with the assignments, write five paragraphs about the experiment (not that bad), and we usually get out of lab an hour early. She also gives feedback on your reports if there is a mistake.

she is very nice and knows what shes talking about, but is sometimes hard to follow. if you take good notes, do the homework, and use the resources the school has (tutoring, study groups, office hours), you'll be fine. class is all lecturing, but she is a generous grader on tests.

She is super caring. You can tell she really wants everyone to succeed and even for the people who don't have this major. She drops lowest quiz grade and will give extra credit to people who complete homework. She offers a lot of help to all students and she teaches very well. She has an accent but I think it's still clear enough to understand.

Rosie cares for her students soooo much!! She does her best explaining concepts and formulas multiple times so we can grasp it. Sometimes she would get a little too detailed and it was a little confusing but she will clarify if you have any questions. Weekly homework is short and very helpful. She gives out study guides for each exam!

While Professor Nawpar is incredibly caring and supportive of her students, it felt VERY difficult to succeed in her class. The majority of your grade will depend on how you do on 2 midterms and the final. Collectively, those were worth 70% of your grade. Class average on exams was 60%. Make sure you give yourself time to STUDY!!!

She has a very thick accent that makes it a little hard to understand, would recommend getting a tutor. Online hw, 10 questions per week. 2 exams and a final. The first two exams are tough because it's only 20 points in total. Class averages lower than a B on the exams. If you want an A, you need to work hard for it. Go to lecture or get a tutor.

Professor Nawpar makes physics possible. I took her for 121 and loved her so much, I waited for her 1220 class. She only teaches 1220 during summer but it was so worth it! She is very clear about what she lectures and electromagnetism itself is not easy. But Prof Rosie makes it possible for us by being thorough and clear about everything. Take her!

Definitely would take this professor again. She is kind and cares about her students. The subject material is not the easiest in the world but she is always available to help when you need it. Quizzes were all online and the homework solutions were on youtube. As long as you put in a decent amount of work you'll pass.

She is honestly a really good professor. She is a good lecturer and always is asking if her students need help. However, the course material itself is really hard, so you do have to develop the discipline to study often. Overall, she is a good professor and you can get a good grade in this class if you study.

Physics in general is difficult. She as a professor is great. She breaks down the formula, which can be confusing but makes sense when applying it to the problem. She is a good teacher and does want you to understand physics. I would take her again.
Overall she's great the test are difficult but thats bc physics is a difficult class just study and you'll be fine. SH explains really well and her notes are helpful!

Not the worst. Generous when rounding final grades. Grade mainly based on exams. Quizzes were easy and taken at home online. Weekly HW. Exams were pretty rough for me but I managed. She provided practice exams and answer keys which were helpful; usually at least 1 of the practice questions were on the exams. She's pretty nice and caring.

Professor Nawpar was very easygoing when it came to lab. She was very helpful when needed and graded lab reports in a timely manner. All her quizzes were online and very straightforward. Great lab professor overall.
The previous ratings made me nervous but she was great! Rosie teaches very well and tells us far in advance about quizzes and exams. Do your homework and the practice exams and you should be fine.

Great professor. She is really caring and wants all her students to succeed. She works out problems on the board during lecture and one of those is always on the exam. Weekly hw, 4 quizzes, 2 midterms, and a final. Exams are hard but you can make a cheat sheet. Rounded up my final grade. Generous when grading free response questions on exams.

Seeing all the previous ratings, I was skeptical about taking Rosie. However, she is better than I expected. She is very nice and is willing to help as much as she can. Tedious homework once a week, straightforward quiz every 3 weeks, and 3 exams. Exams are difficult, but study the practice exam and lecture problems. Key to success is to practice!!

Very straight forward with lectures and homeworks. Her exam free response questions are very similar to the lecture examples and homework. Clear lectures and everything you need to know is in the powerpoint. Caring and nice person. Some people had hard time understanding her but it wasn't that bad for me. Write small so sit in the front.

she is a little TOO thorough during lectures, and it just confuses everybody. tbh i think i wouldve been better off learning off of her ppt's and the hw. she gives partial credit on exams, curves, accessible outside of class, allows formula sheets-make sure you have a good sheet for exams, study ppts, and hw,, and you should be more than fine.

This class was not an easy class because it is very exam heavy, do well on the two midterms and final and you will have an A/B. Her lectures are confusing because she does have an accent but after a while it's easier to understand. She isn't the best at explaining things so make friends in the course!! Do the homework!!

Prof. Nawpar lectures were full of information, one homework and one quiz every week, the exams are super hard so be aware and study well for them. She allows a cheat sheet for each exam, try to write some examples. The (practicing exam paper) that she gives is useful in multiple choices. she's super nice and understanding.

She is okay at explaining but not super clear. But she is the nicest woman and wants to give you as many points as possible. There are online quizzes every week that are easy and one homework assignment every week but you have a ton of tries. the class was doable but there is a lot of self teaching

Overall good class. I took her lab without any physics lecture and was able to get through it easily. Sometimes, she has a harder time explaining parts of the lab, however, everything is in the lab manual. Very predictable assignments but sometimes forgets to remind us about quizzes. Quizzes are based on lab manual and the labs done in class.

If you want to learn find another professor. She doesn't know how to explain and nothing she explains makes any sense. She's a really sweet lady and she tries but teaching is just not for everyone. Her accent makes it so difficult to comprehend anything she explains and she just lectures straight out of the book so it makes no sense.

During class she went over exactly what you needed to do to solve for the lab data which made the labs clear and easy to complete. Labs only took 1-2 days to complete. As long as you put in effort and follow directions, you should get an A on every lab report. The quizzes were easy and straight forward.

Quizzes and homework were rather easy but counted for a little portion of grade. Professor is EXTREMELY generous while grading, always giving partial points on exams. Her lectures are directly from the book so the book will not be of much help. Professor is super sweet and wants you to succeed in her class.

1 lab per week, 4 quizzes per semester. Quizzes are short and straightforward. If you read the manual and do the labs, you should do pretty well on the quizzes. She explains the labs really well. She describes how to obtain data and exactly where it goes. 10/10 would recommend taking her for lab!

1 lab a week. The labs are 1 week ahead of the lecture, but everything is in the lab manual so its no big deal. The labs take some time (4 hrs) to get the data and fill out the lab manual. It isn't too difficult, but it does take some time to complete each of the labs.

She has an accent, but most of the time you can understand what she's saying. She gives lectures that cover the week's chapter but leaves some stuff out, so you have to read the book if you want to know it all for the test. There are quizzes every week on the past week's chapter, so beware of that. Overall she wasn't a terrible professor.

We have one paper due every week with data and a report. It was pretty easy however my classmates always had to clarify concepts with each other or her during office hours. You can do one makeup lab if you miss some. You will need the lab manual in order to do the labs. Also suggest going through the lecture link she gives with the video data links

Even though she had an accent, the lectures were ok. I suggest just memorizing formulas and when to use them (it gets easier after velocity lol). We do ExpertTA where each week you have homework containing 5-15 questions (search questions on youtube if you have trouble). When clarifying concepts though I ended up turning to my classmates.

1 lab due per week. She is a fair grader, as long as you show effort in your lab report. 1 quiz for every 3 labs. The answers to the quiz are in the Lab Notebook you must purchase for the class. Despite this being an online course, professor nawpar showed she is caring and understanding. If you have trouble, just ask!
Overall she is an ok professor. Her accent can be hard to understand at times. Classes can be boring but she tries to encourage her students to participate. There was Lab reports due every week.

(COVID Edition) Took Professor Nawpar's Introduction to Physics Class. I've learned HS Physics before, so I know I am capable of learning the content. HOWEVER, Nawpar is very hard to understand and does not explain the content well. I'd have to find the answers to the homework online because she couldn't explain it. Best to take someone else!

By far the best professor in the godforsaken STEM department. Super caring and understanding. He wants everyone to pass his class! Always willing to help and an easy grader. No prelabs or weekly quizzes. Just turn in the labs and do the final at the end.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Class was pretty engaging if you wanted it to be but overall was a smooth course all around. Very minimal Homework, One Project, and 2 exams. Need more professors like this teaching GE's.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: HE KNOWS HOW TO TEACH!!! I COULD NOT RECOMMEND HIM ENOUGH. This class is the most I have ever learned in my entire life. You will succeed if you follow directions and try hard. Yes he is strict, but for a reason.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Honestly, fire professor, the tests weren't that bad, the questions came from his lectures, articles(which are sometimes very boring), and his mandatory "fun" videos. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: If you have any resemblance of study skills and an interest in the topic, you can survive. 5 quizzes, the lowest scoring quiz will be dropped. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: As long as you read the mandatory articles and watch the mandatory "fun" videos as he calls them, you can pass all his quizzes easily. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences

Then, you find a newspaper article that relates to the topic and write a two page paper on the article and give your thoughts. Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: one of the best professors i've taken, really kind, really cares about his students, super friendly, replies to emails, super helpful, would definitely take him again!

Comment: Mrs Demerson is not a harsh grader and lectures are interesting but she goes through lecture way too fast. You have to do one group presentation and a research paper and only 2 exams.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Not hard to pass. You must follow up with the readings because the tests can be slightly difficult at times. Also, missing class affects your grade a lot.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I took DAN 4490 as a GE. This professor is extremely rude/insulting. If you're a dancer, you'll probably get her lingo but I am not. This GE is simple enough but I personally think this class is absolutely useless and this professor is even more so. She has been very disorganized with classes and ignoring urgent emails. Go elsewhere

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Took this class for GE D4 and it was the weirdest classes I have ever taken at Cal Poly. She made us watch very unusual videos and do weird exercises in class. We had to read a lot and there was 1 quiz and no tests. The final was a group project. She is very vague when it comes to the group projects and is a tough grader for the papers.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: LiteraLot one of the worst teachers I have ever taken. She comes to class just to waste your time and by the end of the year you learn nothing. The grades you receive on the papers are purely based on luck. Her grades do not correlate at all. Take someone else I insist.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Contemporary Dance (textbook style) was very interesting with her. You can tell she's a true dancer....the work load is CRAZY! If you take her prepare to be writing a paper every week starting midterms.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She is a great teacher. I liked her. She made my Choreography class fun. She gives the class a topic and is very general, then we have to interpret it through our movement. If you have her for Choreography, be creative.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: she looks like a nice person but once you get to writing the papers you are doomed...she is a very bad grader, in my opinion DO NOT TAKE HER !!!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: One of my fav. classes at Cal Poly!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: My experience with this professor was affected because of the students. He was unable to control some students who would ask some really trivial questions for the first hour of class meaning we lacked time to watch movies (saw 5 but he was planning on screening 10). You make 2 shorts, 1 3 min. no dialogue, 1 5 min. with dialogue, A easy with effort

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This course is specifically a 3 part integrated arts course. Emma is hardworking and passionate when it comes to educating the students. She can come off strong, however she is caring and motivating . She helps you get in depth with yourself and reminds you to always try your best.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Taken Spring Qtr 2017. Literally the best dance teacher you'll have. Funny and sarcastic but keeps it real. Pushes you out of your comfort zone in a good way. I had the opportunity to dance in a side project of hers, so she is definitely observant of her students.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Emma was one of the funniest people I have ever met. I only had 2 sessions with her but every time I was cracking up. She is so nice, and I think she truly cared about each student in the class. She is awesome at dancing and at her job. But, do not get on her bad side because she will call you out and make you feel so stupid in front of everyone.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: She is a fun dance teacher. Didn't have many sessions with her, but she was entertaining. Sometimes she talks too much and we didn't get to dance a lot. Easy class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Taken Spring Qtr 2017. Very knowledgeable and will teach you life lessons. Group project we did was making up our own skit, and we had to cover topics he discussed in lectures (the main character, theme, conflict, etc.)

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: You watch clips of movies every class. But it's more than just movies, Professor Fossum truly shines in his knowledge and expertise of the creation of movies and his behind the scenes information. He tells you all about actors and actresses and paints such vivid pictures of his life. If you have the opportunity to take this professor please do.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Professor Fossum is amazing. Hes super passionate about art and artists and the way he lectures isnt really even lecturing. Hes just sharing his knowledge about artists with the class. We watched amazing movies/clips every class period. I learned so much and gained an appreciation for art/artists/movies in his class. Def take him if you can!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Very engaging and interesting teacher. Took this class to fulfill a GE requirement and I definitely don't regret it. He shows some good films and is really passionate about what he teaches. Definitely take this class if you have a chance!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: One of the best professors at CPP. Professor Fossum is really passionate as a teacher and with the subject that he teaches. He has experience in acting and with movies, so he knows his stuff! We only had to write 1 three-paged paper on a film and during class we fill in a worksheet containing questions about the films. Take his class if you can!!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I LOVED this class! He's so funny and picks pretty good movies each week. I took his Friday class you'd think 4 hours would kill you but his lectures never get boring. No midterms or finals, just one really easy term paper. Don't be late, he absolutely hates that and will call you out to the class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Lou is an amazing teacher. If you're taking him for TH 423 (Liberal Studies) and wish to become a teacher, remember everything he says!! He will tell you everything you need to know to make your classroom fun. Seriously, TAKE HIM if you want to be successful!!!!!!!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He says he really cares about teaching. He talks about himself a lot and really tries to make you like him. Always brags about himself. Easy class. Few group projects and a paper. You're pretty much guaranteed an A as long as you show up.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I have never had a teacher like Lou. He is the most universally respected figure around Cal Poly, gives incredible lectures on interesting subject matter and leaves you with lasting thoughts about important topics. Only teacher I can say changed my way of thinking multiple times throughout a quarter. Always looked forward to class with him!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: If you ever have a chance to take Fossum, take the chance!!! He is extremely passionate about what he teaches and he's funny too. NO homework, only weekly "quizzes" that you fill out throughout the class as you learn the material with extra credit on every single one. Your only version of a final or midterm is a 3 page paper due towards the end.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is the best Professor I have ever had. The class is simple. Show up, watch a film, and answer questions on a quiz every week. The quizzes aren't hard at all. Just pay attention and the answer is there. There is a term paper where you evaluate a film of your choice and that's it. Very fun class and I wish I can take it again.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Lou is a great professor and is really passionate. He really wants all his students to pass, also the class is super easy with one term paper & quizzes each week.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Just do the mid-term paper (super easy), he tells you what he wants, and you get an A. ALL the movies were very entertaining and the class room itself is air-conditioned and is like a movie-theater. JUST DONT: Be late, Be absent, and Be on your phone.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is an awesome teacher. This class is one of the best class I have taken. If you don't do the term paper, you won't pass the class.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I recommend class. The lectures are interesting &you can tell he genuinely loves & cares about what he teaches. Films shown aren't boring. There's a weekly quiz- 5 questions &very easy. 1 extra credit question is on each quiz. No midterm, there is a final 3 pg essay. DON'T BE LATE (he hates that) &attendance is mandatory. Definitely bring snacks.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Thanks for Professor Fossum, I was able to manage taking 20 units this spring and receive all A's. His class was not difficult but I did learn a lot and I now look at film from a different more creative perspective. 1 paper, quiz every week (took the 4 hour Fri class), and mandatory attendance. Great professor, very passionate about his subject.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: One of the best professors Ive ever had. He's really knowledgeable and has a lot of interesting stories to tell. Just listen and follow to his simple rules and you'll be fine. His paper assignment was easy as long as you had what he asked for. Great class

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Awesome Professor. Clearly tells you how to ace his class. Great movie choices

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This guy is a character. He loves what he does and after you take this class, you'll never see movies the same way (in a good way). All you do is watch movie clips and answer 5 questions at the end of the day. NO TESTS EVER. No need to take notes either. The essay final is respectfully easy as well. Bring snacks to class! Don't be sleepy either.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Whether this class is a requirement for you or you're taking it for GE, you will have a good time and pass the class without much effort. Prof. Lou is very passionate in teaching! He used to be a Hollywood actor. You will not look at films the same way after taking his class. Strongly recommended for everyone!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Never in my life have I had such a passionate teacher. His enthusiasm incorporates the entire class into his material. Weekly quizzes at the end of lecture and a final essay which is easy if you paid attention the entire semester.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Such a fun class! I highly recommend it! He really enjoys what he teaches and makes you enjoy it too!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: He is a fantastic professor!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great professor! If I had the time to retake the class, I most definitely would; even if I wouldn't get extra units. Both the material and the professor are EXTREMELY entertaining. First week is terrible only because it's silent films. But other than that, it's an INCREDIBLE class! Take it!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: I was looking through my transcript preparing to graduate by this year and saw his name and brought back so much good memories. I was a freshmen when I took his class and I remember looking forward to his class each week. I did not expect to learn and enjoy this class as I did. It truly is an amazing experience i will take on FOREVER!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Best "general ed" class I have ever took in my history as a college student. Prof. is passionate and as entertaining as the film/clips shown in class. DO NOT use this class as time for napping, you must pay attention to everything shown/told or you would miss important info. DON'T SHOW UP LATE, unless you wanna be humiliated in front of the class!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: EASILY ONE OF MY FAVORITE CLASSES, IT RAN 4 HOURS BUT THEY FLEW BY. WE WATCHED FILM CLIPS AND FULL LENGTH VIDEOS AND THE FILM WAS A PAPER ABOUT A FILM. PROFESSOR FOSSUM IS SO ENTHUSIASTIC; I MEAN NOT MANY PROFESSORS WILL TELL YOU SUCH INTERESTING STORIES ALONG WITH SINGING & DANCING! :) GREAT CLASS

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Great prof. Very fun and keeps the class interesting. Gives info to survive the real world. Need to keep a journal, 1 paper, and a 1 final group skit.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Wow! This teacher is just one of those rare teachers who come along and make school an enjoyable part of life. He was from the get go at the top of his teaching game, giving his students the empowerment to take education not as a means to just get a degree but as a means to learn. Also, his class was fun and entertaining.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: This professor is awesome. You will never be bored in this class because every single clip or full legnth feature he shows is wonderful. I highly recommend you take this teacher.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: WOW! Easy, fun, great class. Well worth the time. No homework (minus a 5 page term paper on a movie, which was CAKE), great class time, awesome teacher, really knows what he is talking about. Take this class!

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: You will never forget this teacher! He shows clips and full length features to a class of 90 and everyone is entrapt in the films.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Did a really good job considering this is his first time teaching and he was very knowledgeable about the material.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Class was taught in conjunction with another professor's class; Allowed other professor to teach the majority of the class and did not participate much in lectures. Allowed other professor to judge student's work to standards that have nothing to do with theater.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Does not inspire creativity in his design classes.

Colleges: College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences
Comment: Jeff is super funny, and easy to learn from. He is down to earth and simple enough that non theater majors can understand. Not to mention he's super attractive.

I like Brownfield's lectures, and I think she's a good professor. But she will make the class way harder than it needs to be. Quizzes are not open note. She has an all or nothing late policy, so if you don't turn things in on time they won't be graded at all. If you want to avoid Type A strict professors, choose another if you can!

One of the most patient and understanding professors I have had. She was great at working out any issues, even if it was only in regards to a single student. She cares about your success as a student. Her lectures were organized and she offered plently of opportunites to ask questions. No midterm or final, instead quizzes throughout the semester.

She is a good professor. Knows her stuff and assignments are pretty decent. Not terribly difficult, just stick to the curriculum. Quizzes are the only type of test, no final or midterm. However the quizzes are harder than you might think, definitely need to read the textbook and pay attention to the lectures. Take notes in class! She is enjoyable.

Her class is difficult and you must study really hard for her tests sbut she is a great professor and really wants her students to pass and cares for her students. She is always willing to help out and she responds to email quickly.

Nothing but lectures and for the midterm we didn't even get a study guide. If you mess up a single assignment (there are only like 2) or flunk a single test, your grade is screwed. The lectures aren't very fun or entertaining either. Offers some extra credit but it's really not enough.

There is no one else on Earth i'd want teaching my GIS course. He is well-respected in the industry for a reason. He loves to teach, but will not make it too easy for you. However, with the right attitude, you can gain a ton from him.

His lectures were clear and instructions were easy to follow. He gave plenty of time to complete assignments and ask for help. He created a fun, safe classroom environment where we were never hesitant about asking for help. He begins class immediately so be on time for every meeting.

You take this class because you have to, but he can be insulting and discouraging and gets mad when you do not participate in class. if you are at Pomona, you will have to take this class just try not to take Kim
Do Kim is my favorite professor at CPP URP. He's taught multiple classes. He's not super difficult, you just need to complete your work with good effort. Very approachable if you need help.

Dr. Do Kim is my favorite at URP. He really knows his stuff and he's funny. You can go up to him and ask all your questions and he's always available to answer. He gives a ton of feedback and really helps you grow. I've had him in multiple classes and as an advisor. He knows bs when he see's it so be prepared to put real effort into your work.

Professor Kim is a nice person which is why I feel bad for rating him so low. He demands a lot of participation, in my opinion, TOO MUCH. He wants us to reply every five seconds and its annoying. Also, he talks down on his students a lot and its pretty discouraging. Overall, keep the work and youll pass, its just hard to sit through lectures.

Do Kim calls himself the "GIS god" for his skills in the program that he teaches, Arc GIS. Who gives themself a nickname? Narcissists do, and Do is definitely one of those. His pastimes include belittling students for asking questions and saying the phrase "Am I correct?" after every sentence. You have to take the course, so do the work before lab.
DO KIM is the best teacher of the URP major!!! The classes are amazing if you pay attention and be respectful. He's an all around great person.

Professor Fonza's course on the Ethnic communities and Urban planning was like a gift to me. I learned so much about American history and Urban Planning history. She's a warm yet challenging professor. She calls on students randomly but, in the end, I gained confidence and learned how to be a critical thinker.

Professor Fonza stimulates critical thinking and enhances your awareness of the environment. This course encourages you to think creatively and explore perspectives that you may not have considered previously.

URP1051: Her class was via Zoom & she took attendance at every meeting. We had to do reading every week & watch videos before every meeting where she would ask questions & call on us at random if no one answered. She offered plenty of extra credit opportunities. Her quizzes & exams were open-note & non-cumulative.

The material for this course was not too hard to grasp. A relatively easy course to pass as long as you keep up with readings and hw. There is a quiz just about every week. The professor, however, is not easy to get in contact with outside of class. He was not good about answering emails in a timely manner. Not a very personable professor.

Teaches how to write professional proposals, will give a template to follow YOU MUST USE IT or will be docked points. Always willing to answer questions and help you understand the city of your choosing. You will be writing proposals every other week, using the articles from that week in your proposal. Always ask questions, ideas, or how to improve

Quizzes are related to the book or lecture, every week your quiz will be online or in person he will let you know. By studying and memorizing is the only way to pass the class. He answers questions, help you understand the material, and will tell you what you need to study for the midterm and final. Overall don't be scared for asking questions.

quizzes only, memorization is all he cares about as a teacher. only teaches half the work, students read majority of info on your own, lectures and 'video lectures' are super vague and not helpful. classic bad teacher syndrome pretending to be 'helpful'

Huge on attendance and will mark you down for being late. Doesn't give constructive feedback unless you ask him for it. Sarcastic responses when you ask him questions, not welcoming at all! Take someone else if you can.

The material for this course was sometimes daunting and the professor did not have a way of keeping students engaged during lectures. You will have to go back and do a lot of re-reading and studying to grasp the information being thrown at you. The professor was kind and answered emails quickly, however.
So-Ra Baek is a great teacher, she gives good lectures and examples of what she wants from you on your papers. If you don't understand something, she's happy to further explain.

Very understanding! I had a group that never helped me so I had to do most of the work by myself. She allowed to to present to her privately in her office hours so i could have an extra day to organize. She gives back great feedback too!

I love Professor Baek, shes very caring and she does her best to explain assignments. Shes a lenient grader and Ive never gotten below an A in her classes. Her lectures can be a pretty boring, but I dont mind. She lets us out of class early all the time since we never use up the full 3 hours.
This professor is amazing. I love her lectures. Highly recommend.
Dina is great

I wouldnt say her class is dificult, just heavy loadwork sometimes. She really pushes you to bring out your best work and gives good feedback on all assignments. she takes participation seriously and it is a part of your grade so show up
Shes a tough grader. I've only had her for lectures and I really enjoy her. She's caring and likes to get to know her students.

Professor Abdul Karim is one of the best teachers, especially if you're into design. She knows so much, gives detailed feedback, and seems to really care about her work and about how you do in class. Would take this class again (URP 2010 and URP 2020 sequence). Lots of work but learned a bunch.

I had prof abdul for two semesters. She definitely challenges you to bring your best work. Sometimes its hard to juggle especially with the remote learning. But I have to say shes supportive and understanding. Its just shes meticulous with the work she expects. So be prepared. I learned a bunch.

The Straight forward lectures. Attend and youll be ok. Assignment arent hard but could need time. Depends on your familiarity with acad and photoshop. Wish there were more demos to cover more details on the softwares. Still worth the money.
Some experience with cad helps. Assignments are straightforward. No readings required. Would take in-person classes with her. Shes approachable and chill.

Had professor Dina for lecture and lab. She demands more but offers support. Expect to learn the softwares. She is flexible and willing to work with you. Reached out to me about a missing assignment I had.

Dina is a nice professor and she cares about her students, but shes a really hard grader. When she gives feedback before projects are due, she doesnt have anything negative to say. But when the project is due, all of a sudden she has so many bad things to say. She expects work to be done every time you meet up for class, so be sure to keep up.

I know that the material of the class is intimidating and sometimes her feedback is hard to understand. Therefore always communicate, ask questions, and participate. Being creative while realistic for the project is the best way to go. Being able to communicate visually is important to her.

She teaches mandatory classes so you are stuck with her. She's very strict but likeable at times. Be respectful to her and she will respect you, but she gives blunt and vague feedback so she often conveys a tone of not respecting you. You need to participate in discussions. No books are used, it's all discussion and group projects. Deal with it.

Had her for lecture and lab, she pushes you though to do more, which is a plus. I will say this-Prof. Dina is a good teacher -her communication can be better in terms of feedback it lacks clarity. Whether being graded individually or not, urban planning is a collaborative job, so it makes sense, but some people just suck

She's a tough grader when it comes to analysis. You literally have to be the most "WOKE" person out there about buildings if that's even possible. She's passionate about buildings, spaces, and everything that comes with it. But you literally have to match that energy into assignments for a decent grade. Also, she doesn't reply to emails on time.

Always willing to help, answer questions, and work one on one with you so you understand the content or programming you will be using. She gives great feedback on what is good and does not make you feel dumb when asking questions. The grading is fair and with group project especially if you end up "doing it all yourself."

Love Prof. Lambrou! She is super caring and also very nice about late submissions. I had a situation with a group not doing their part and she was super understanding and gave me a good solution to save my grade. Can't wait to take more URP classes with her going forward!!
Nicole is awesome. She will give step-by-step tutorials for design software, and gives great ideas for your 2010 and 2020 projects.

Absolute blast to learn from, and her design tutorials are incredibly helpful. She recognizes that students in 2010 and 2020 are new to the profession, and is kinder when it comes to design and presentation critiques.
Great Professor. Will teach you software.

Professor Nicole is a great person to learn urban design from. She tends to always give excellent critiques to your work and is always excited by new ideas and designs. She is definitely a professor that you will want to take as she fosters growth and nurtures potential. Some tasks can be demanding but they tend to payoff in the end.

If you do the readings and participate, and show up with some progress each week to get feedback on, this class is great. We talk about heavy topics (not just climate change but how it's affecting people in different ways), but you learn so much (including how to deal with climate anxiety!)
Good feedback. Group project with a client, in an LA neighborhood. Feels like a studio

Engaged students really well in her lectures. Somehow is able to make learning about really depressing content (climate change and social inequalities) really inspiring. I wish I could take more of her classes.
Took her class with another professor. They didn't have a clear consensus on what they wanted and how it was graded. Required so I couldn't drop it.
Really good professor. She is very direct and tells you what she likes and what she doesnt about your work
Does not reply to emails. Students deliver all the lectures. Do not take her classes.

She is such a lovely person but unfortunately it is all time pressed presentations and chaotic conversation without any structured learning. She is passionate and has an interesting career with many accomplishments but I did not feel as though I learned much. It was all students teaching other students with constant busywork. She needs to organize.

Do not take a class with this professor, she is an amazing person but has no organizational skills. She often enters class unplanned and you will often not have time to present your work on the day you are supposed to. Her class was mostly students teaching students, we had maybe one lecture, and I didn't learn much throughout this class.
One of the best teachers I have ever had is always willing to help and very caring to students. Truly cares about students and Planning.

Great professor. She truly cares about your interests and always provides good feedback. Every presentation will be met with questions, but none that are meant to make you feel like you are doing something wrong. I would love to take another class of hers. She is funny, passionate, and a genuinely great planning professor.

One of my favorite professors. She's extremely caring and wants all her students to pass. I have had her for multiple classes and it was always a pleasure. I would say responding to emails isn't her best trait but besides that, she's an excellent professor and it's easy to pass her class! just show up and do the work

I would avoid the urban and regional planning programs at CPP so long as Shawnika Johnson is still employed there. She was the worst excuse for a teacher I've had throughout my entire education. She ruined my experience in the MURP program and had me questioning whether or not I even want to be involved in this industry. CPP should be embarrassed.

The class is mandatory but nothing she has taught is relatable. This class sounds like a high energy MLM scheme. Must attend class. Grades area all over the place with zero feedback. Expects to read her mind and magically it will be up to her standards. Stated first day of class no one will get an A. Avoid!

Let me clarify- she is hilariously bad at this job. WORST. PROFESSOR. I'VE. EVER. HAD. Doesn't respond to emails. Isn't present for office hours. Gives out last-minute assignments. Doesn't know how to use Canvas. Required three textbooks that we don't use. We instead watch Youtube videos for most of class time. Awful in every way. Avoid!
She is amazing in every way. She is one of the few professors who actually care about her students' well being especially during the covid pandemic.
Tiwari was a great professor! He was very engaging with the students despite our lecture being on zoom. He is very passionate about urban planning and made the class super enjoyable.

His lectures were entertaining & informative. He offered great feedback on assignments & involved the rest of the class when it was concerning our final turn in. This collaboration was helpful & got you moving in the right direction. Quizzes were relatively easy & open notes. He seemed passionate about planning & community development.

Tiwari is often absent, with very little notice. Lab assignments are easy to complete but the course otherwise is nightmare. His lectures are unorganized and usually devolve into tangents about Keanu Reeves. He works at several schools, best evidenced by his inability to grade assignments in a timely manner or be reached outside of class.
Best teacher ever! Loves planning and is always willing to help if you have questions!

I'm surprised he doesn't have a urban planning podcast. If you're passionate about urban planning then you'll love professor Tiwari. I've never skipped a class because I always looked forward to his lectures. Had him for both 1040, 3310, and 4750 and the work load was very doable and educational if you're a URP nerd.

Tiwari is one of the best professors in URP at Cal Poly. Definitely knows his subjects very well. You can talk to him about anything, even if it's not planning related. get used to his jokes sometimes only he understands them.

Tiwari is an icon. I have had at least three courses with him and wish I could have more. I learn so much about topics I love and he makes it super easy to take his courses. There is a lot of research and writing to be done, however if you like urban planning then you'll be glad to do it. His classes are always chill and so is he!

his class is always entertained by the jokes he throws from time to time. He is a caring and kind professor. His homework isn't that difficult but you have to read and actually study for his quizzes because they could be challenging.
The topics that he covers are super boring but he is such a great lecturer that he makes it interesting. Although there are a lot of readings, some are pretty interesting.

Many people like him, but his classes require tons of reading and quizzes. Mostly solo work. He knows his stuff but is not great at teaching it. He unknowingly assumes you know all the background that he knows on the topics. Funny but get ready to read. His lectures are okay and funny but reading the book is most important.

My favorite professor from my undergrad career at CPP. Prof Tiwari is a genius so you better try to soak in all you can because such opportunities seldom arrive. He's super chill and wants to impart knowledge as opposed to establishing authority.

The way the professor handled his modules and dates of releasing assignments were at random and sometimes very late. The communication with the professor was poor with getting a response back from them was very late and took days. Assignments given with a simple and loose explanation on what the assignment actually is supposed to be. Do not take !

General content of class was easy. But the class was unorganized and and their really wasn't a syllabus. All grading was done the last week of class and we didn't find out our final grade until it was published on Bronco Direct. However, he was responsive to emails but class was just very unstructured. Wouldn't take again.
Learned nothing in this class. Ghosted us for 2 months and then posted all the assignments for those 2 months 3 weeks before semester ended. No clear assignments or grading standards. Awful class.

Took this professor during Spring, there's just a lot of reading/video material. Not all of it is required to answer the discussion posts. Read and write a 1-2 pg discussion. He posts these kind of late though and it's hard to get a response back from him. Like a ghost. But, still a great professor and I enjoy learning about regenerative studies.
